The text of all streams together never exceeds `max_bytes` (4096 by default, `0` is no limit) and a line longer than 400 characters is cut. After exit code 0 the result has the last 5 lines and the field `digest`; after a failure of `cargo` or `pytest` the field `diagnostics` lists the first errors with file and line, and a response that leaves lines out ends with the hint "more: next": `next` returns the lines left out from the output file without running the program again. The `exec` record carries `exit_code`, `signal` and `timed_out`.

```nurt
run ["npm", "run", "build"] cwd: "/srv/app" show: errors tail: 40
```

## Exit codes

A program that exits with a non-zero code is not an error of `run`: the code is a field of the result. `assert exit_code: 0` turns an unexpected code into `E_ASSERT`, and `E_TIMEOUT` reports a program stopped by its limit.

## Detecting changes

Files that a program changes are detected only in the paths named by `watch`; the default is the working directory of the program. `track_changes` selects `scan`, `events`, `auto` or `none`. A change made by a program is recorded in the journal, and when its previous state could not be kept it is marked irreversible.

```nurt
run ["./build.sh"] cwd: "/srv/app" watch: ["/srv/app/dist"] track_changes: scan
```

title: scheduling
text:
# scheduling

## Creating a schedule

`schedule.create` takes a label and an action, which is a pipeline, and one of the times `cron`, `every` or `at`. `timezone` selects the zone in which the times are read, `max_runs` and `expires` end the schedule, and `enabled: false` creates it paused. `run_now: true` starts the first run at once.

```nurt
schedule.create "backup" cron: "0 3 * * *" action: (run ["backup"] cwd: "/srv")
schedule.create "health" every: 5m action: (http.request "https://example.com/health" |> assert count: 1)
```

## Missed runs and overlap

`on_missed` decides what happens to runs that were due while the service was stopped: `skip` drops them and `run_once` runs the action once at start. `overlap` decides what happens when a run starts while the previous one still runs: `skip` drops the new run, `queue` waits for the previous one and `parallel` starts both.

```nurt
schedule.create "sync" every: 1h action: (run ["sync"] cwd: "/srv") on_missed: run_once overlap: skip
```

## The service

Schedules run only while `nurt service` is running. When it is not, a schedule is stored and `schedule.list` reports `active: false` for it. The next run and the state of each schedule are fields of the `schedule` record.

```nurt
schedule.list state: active
```

## Controlling schedules

`schedule.pause` and `schedule.resume` stop and restart a schedule without removing it, `schedule.remove` deletes it and `schedule.run` runs the action now, outside its times and run limit. The first argument is an `id`, or `all: true` for every schedule.

```nurt
schedule.pause "backup"
schedule.run "backup"
```

## History

`schedule.history` lists past runs with their result and the journal operation of the changes they made. A change made by a scheduled run can be undone like any other change.

```nurt
schedule.history "backup" limit: 10
```

title: text-editing
text:
# text-editing

## Reading ranges

`read` with `lines` returns a range of lines, `last` returns the end of a file and `around` with `context` returns the lines around a position. `lines` produces one `line` record per line, so later stages can filter them.

```nurt
read "/srv/app/main.go" lines: 10..40
lines "/srv/app/main.go" |> filter text ~ /^func /
```

## Searching

`search` takes a pattern and a path. `mode` selects `literal`, `regex`, `syntax` or `auto`, `case_sensitive` and `whole_word` refine the match, `context`, `before` and `after` add surrounding lines, and `output` returns matches, file names, counts or the files without a match.

```nurt
search "deprecated" "/srv/app/src" glob: "**/*.go" context: 2
search /oldName\(/ "/srv/app/src" glob: "**/*.go" output: files
```

## Replacing

`replace` changes text in the files of a search or in the files named by `in`. `occurrence` limits the change to one occurrence, `whitespace` selects how whitespace is compared and `template` enables the groups `$1`, `$2` in the replacement. `expect` stops the change with `E_ASSERT` unless the number of replacements is the given one.

```nurt
search /oldName\(/ "/srv/app/src" glob: "**/*.go" |> assert paths: 12 |> replace "newName("
replace "colour" "color" in: "/srv/app/docs/a.md" expect: 3
```

## Inserting and removing

`insert` adds text before or after a line, a match or a node, or at the start or end of a file. `remove` applied to `line` or `match` records deletes them. Both keep the encoding and line endings of the file.

```nurt
insert "import \"fmt\"\n" in: "/srv/app/main.go" line: 3 position: after
search "debug_print" "/srv/app/src" glob: "**/*.go" |> remove
```

## Several changes to one file

`edit` applies a list of changes to one file as a single write: all of them are applied or none. A change that does not match fails with `E_NO_MATCH` and the file stays as it was. `write` with `mode: append` or `mode: prepend` adds text without reading the file first.

title: unix
text:
# unix

## Permissions

`attributes` changes the mode, the account and the group of an entry, the times and the extended attributes. `recursive: true` applies the change to a directory tree. `info` reports the mode and the account of a path, so a change can be checked with `assert` in the same program.

```nurt
attributes "/srv/app/run.sh" mode: "0755"
find "/srv/app" glob: "**/*.sh" |> filter mode != "0755"
```

## Services

On Linux `services` reads systemd units, and `scope: user` selects the units of the current account instead of the system units. On macOS it reads launchd jobs. `start`, `restart`, `enable` and `disable` change the state of the input services; they need the rights of the administrator for system units (`privilege: elevated`). `start`, `stop`, `enable` and `disable` are undone by the opposite command, `restart` is irreversible.

```nurt
services name: "nginx" |> restart
services scope: user
```

## Packages

`package.install`, `package.remove` and `package.upgrade` call the package manager of the system. `manager` selects `apt`, `dnf`, `pacman` or `zypper` on Linux and `brew` on macOS; `auto` selects the manager found on the system. Installing and removing packages needs the rights of the administrator: write `privilege: elevated` (`package.install ["jq"] privilege: elevated`); without them the command fails with `E_PRIVILEGE`. `undo` removes a package that was installed, or installs the recorded version again.

```nurt
package.list outdated: true manager: apt
package.install ["jq"] manager: brew
```

## File names

Linux file systems distinguish names that differ only in case. The default volume format of macOS does not, and it stores names in a decomposed Unicode form. Two paths that look equal can therefore be different entries on one system and the same entry on another. `find` with `case_sensitive: false` matches names without regard to case.

## Links and programs

`create` with `type: link` and `target` creates a symbolic link, and `hard: true` creates a hard link. A script is started through `run` with its interpreter named in the argument list, so the result does not depend on a shell.

```nurt
create "/srv/app/current" type: link target: "/srv/app/release-12"
```

## Named pipes and device files

`create` with `type: fifo` makes a named pipe, and `type: device` makes a device node. Both are available on Linux and macOS; on Windows they fail with `E_OS_ONLY`, and the message of `fifo` names the `\\.\pipe\` namespace of Windows named pipes. `mode` is octal text (default `"0666"`, reduced by the umask). A device node also takes `kind: char` or `kind: block`, `major` and `minor`, and it needs `privilege: elevated`; without the rights the call fails with `E_PRIVILEGE`.

```nurt
create "/srv/app/events.fifo" type: fifo mode: "0660"
create "/dev/app0" type: device kind: char major: 1 minor: 3 privilege: elevated
```

Both are journaled as created files, so `undo` removes them. `info` and `list` report `type: fifo` and `type: device`; a device node also has `major` and `minor`. The parameters `kind`, `major`, `minor` and `mode` conflict with other types (`E_PARAM_CONFLICT`), a device without `kind`, `major` or `minor` is `E_MISSING_PARAM`, and a number outside 0..4294967295 or a mode that is not octal is `E_INVALID_VALUE`.

## Conditions and several changes

A script that adapts to the system uses `when` and `exists`, and writes the changes of one task with `steps`, so that a failure in a later step restores the earlier ones. The constructs are described in [language](../site/language.md); the commands that administer accounts, mounts, kernel parameters, the firewall, the network, the clock and power are in [administration](administration.md).

```nurt
when exists "/etc/nginx/nginx.conf" {
    steps {
        replace /worker_processes \d+;/ "worker_processes 4;" in: "/etc/nginx/nginx.conf" expect: 1 privilege: elevated
        services name: "nginx" |> restart privilege: elevated
    }
}
```

title: windows
text:
# windows

## Paths

A path is a quoted absolute text with `/` as the separator on every system: `"C:/proj/app"`. A backslash is not a separator in a Nurt path. Relative paths are allowed only with the call parameter `base`. A path that is valid on another system but not on the current one fails with `E_PATH_FOREIGN`.

```nurt
list "C:/Users/dev" depth: 1
info "C:/proj/app/readme.txt"
```

## Reserved names and files in use

Names such as `CON`, `NUL` and `COM1` are reserved by the system and cannot be created. A file that another process holds open cannot be replaced or removed: the command fails with `E_IN_USE`, and `open_files` names the process that holds the file.

## Links and the registry

`create` with `type: junction` and `target` creates a junction, and `type: link` creates a symbolic link. The registry is addressed as a path with the prefix `registry:` and works in `list`, `find`, `read`, `write`, `remove`, `copy` and `move`.

```nurt
create "C:/proj/current" type: junction target: "C:/proj/release-12"
read "registry:/HKCU/Software/Example"
```

## Services and packages

`services` lists services with their state, and `start`, `restart`, `enable` and `disable` change them. `package.install` with `manager: winget`, `choco` or `scoop` installs packages through the package manager; the installation is recorded as irreversible. `windows.cim` queries CIM classes.

```nurt
services name: "Spooler" |> restart
package.install ["jq"] manager: winget
windows.cim "Win32_LogicalDisk"
```

## Encodings and command interpreters

Files in code pages such as 852 or 1250 are read with `encoding` and converted with `convert`. Programs of the command interpreter or of PowerShell run through `run` with an argument list, for example `run ["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-File", "C:/ops/task.ps1"]`.

```nurt
convert "C:/legacy/readme.txt" encoding: "utf-8" line_ending: crlf
```

title: Administration, packages and schedules
text:
# Administration, packages and schedules

## List the services

List the services whose name matches a pattern.

```nurt example
services /nginx/
```

```text expected
nginx
```

## Restart a service

Restart a service.

```nurt example
services name: "nginx" |> restart
```

```text expected
nginx
```

```bash
systemctl restart nginx
```

```powershell
Restart-Service nginx
```

## Enable a service at boot

Enable a service so that it starts at boot.

```nurt example
services name: "nginx" |> enable
```

```text expected
nginx
```

## Query WMI classes

Read a CIM class on Windows.

```nurt example
windows.cim "Win32_OperatingSystem" properties: ["Caption", "Version"]
```

```text expected
Caption
```

```powershell
Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_OperatingSystem
```

## Read a registry value

Read a value of the Windows registry as a path.

```nurt example
read "registry:/HKCU/Software/Example/Mode"
```

```text expected
Mode
```

## List the installed packages

List the packages that have a newer version.

```nurt example
package.list outdated: true
```

```text expected
package
```

## Search a package

Search the package manager for a program.

```nurt example
package.search "ripgrep"
```

```text expected
ripgrep
```

## Install a package

Install a package with the package manager of the host.

```nurt example
package.install ["ripgrep"]
```

```text expected
ripgrep
```

```bash
apt install ripgrep
```

## Upgrade the packages

Upgrade all packages of the host.

```nurt example
package.upgrade
```

```text expected
package
```

## Schedule a daily job

Run a backup program every day at 03:00.

```nurt example
schedule.create "backup" cron: "0 3 * * *" action: (run ["backup"] cwd: "/home/user")
```

```text expected
backup
```

```bash
(crontab -l; echo '0 3 * * * cd /home/user && backup') | crontab -
```

## List the schedules

List the active schedules.

```nurt example
schedule.list state: active
```

```text expected
backup
```

## Pause a schedule

Pause a schedule without removing it.

```nurt example
schedule.pause "s4"
```

```text expected
s4
```

## Run a schedule now

Run the action of a schedule once, outside its time.

```nurt example
schedule.run "s4"
```

```text expected
s4
```

## Show the history of a schedule

Show the last runs of a schedule.

```nurt example
schedule.history "s4" limit: 10
```

```text expected
s4
```

## Find a program for a task

Search the programs and packages for a task.

```nurt example
program.search "ocr pdf" limit: 3
```

```text expected
ocr
```

## Stop a service

Stop a service and wait for it to exit.

```nurt example
services name: "nginx" |> stop grace: 10s
```

```text expected
nginx
```

```bash
systemctl stop nginx
```

```powershell
Stop-Service nginx
```

## Disable a service at boot

Prevent a service from starting at boot.

```nurt example
services name: "cups" |> disable
```

```text expected
cups
```

```bash
systemctl disable cups
```

## Start a service and wait for it

Start a service and wait up to 30 seconds for it to run.

```nurt example
services name: "postgresql" |> start wait: 30s
```

```text expected
postgresql
```

## List the services of the current user

List the services of the user manager instead of the system manager.

```nurt example
services scope: user
```

```text expected
service
```

```bash
systemctl --user list-units --type=service
```

## Query the running Windows services

Read two properties of the running services through CIM.

```nurt example
windows.cim "Win32_Service" where: "State = 'Running'" properties: ["Name", "State"]
```

```text expected
Name
```

```powershell
Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Service -Filter "State = 'Running'"
```

## Install a package in a given version

Install an exact version of a package with a chosen package manager.

```nurt example
package.install ["nodejs"] version: "20.11.0" manager: apt
```

```text expected
nodejs
```

## Remove a package

Remove a package with the package manager of the host.

```nurt example
package.remove ["ripgrep"]
```

```text expected
ripgrep
```

```bash
apt remove ripgrep
```

## Upgrade selected packages

Upgrade two packages and leave the others unchanged.

```nurt example
package.upgrade ["openssl", "curl"]
```

```text expected
openssl
```

## Schedule a job at an interval

Run a cleanup program every six hours.

```nurt example
schedule.create "cleanup" every: 6h action: (run ["cleanup"] cwd: "/home/user")
```

```text expected
cleanup
```

## Schedule a weekly job with a time zone

Run a report every Monday at 08:00 in a given time zone, at most twelve times.

```nurt example
schedule.create "report" cron: "0 8 * * 1" timezone: "Europe/Warsaw" max_runs: 12 action: (run ["report"] cwd: "/home/user")
```

```text expected
report
```

## Resume a paused schedule

Resume a schedule that was paused.

```nurt example
schedule.resume "s4"
```

```text expected
s4
```

## Remove a schedule

Remove a schedule that is no longer needed.

```nurt example
schedule.remove ["s4"]
```

```text expected
s4
```

## Locate a program

Show where a program is installed and its version.

```nurt example
program.find ["git"] versions: true
```

```text expected
git
```

```bash
command -v git && git --version
```

title: Archives and network
text:
# Archives and network

## Extract an archive

Extract a compressed tar archive into a directory.

```nurt example
archive.extract "/home/user/dl/data.tar.gz" into: "/home/user/data"
```

```text expected
/home/user/data
```

```bash
tar -xzf /home/user/dl/data.tar.gz -C /home/user/data
```

## List the content of an archive

List the entries of an archive without extracting it.

```nurt example
archive.list "/home/user/dl/data.zip"
```

```text expected
data
```

## Extract only some entries

Extract the entries that match a pattern.

```nurt example
archive.extract "/home/user/dl/data.zip" into: "/home/user/data" only: "**/*.csv"
```

```text expected
/home/user/data
```

## Create an archive

Create a ZIP archive of a directory.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app/dist" |> archive.create "/home/user/out/dist.zip" base: "/home/user/app"
```

```text expected
/home/user/out/dist.zip
```

```bash
cd /home/user/app && zip -r /home/user/out/dist.zip dist
```

## Compress a file

Compress a file with gzip and keep the original.

```nurt example
compress "/home/user/app/app.log"
```

```text expected
app.log
```

## Decompress a file

Decompress a gzip file.

```nurt example
decompress "/home/user/app/app.log.gz"
```

```text expected
app.log
```

## Send an HTTP request

Send a GET request and require one response.

```nurt example
http.request "https://example.com/health" |> assert count: 1
```

```text expected
200
```

```bash
curl -fsS https://example.com/health
```

## Post JSON

Send a JSON body with a POST request.

```nurt example
http.request "https://example.com/api/items" method: post json: {"name": "item"}
```

```text expected
200
```

## Send a request with a header

Send a request with an authorization header.

```nurt example
http.request "https://example.com/api/me" headers: {"Accept": "application/json"}
```

```text expected
200
```

## Read a page as Markdown

Read the main text of a web page as Markdown.

```nurt example
http.request "https://example.com/docs" as: markdown
```

```text expected
example
```

## Download a file and verify its hash

Download a file and verify its SHA-256 hash.

```nurt example
http.download "https://example.com/a.tar.gz" "/home/user/dl/a.tar.gz" hash: "sha256:9d3c"
```

```text expected
/home/user/dl/a.tar.gz
```

```bash
curl -fLo a.tar.gz https://example.com/a.tar.gz && sha256sum a.tar.gz
```

## Check that a host answers

Send four echo requests to a host.

```nurt example
network.ping "example.com" count: 4
```

```text expected
example.com
```

## Resolve a name

Resolve the IPv6 addresses of a name.

```nurt example
network.resolve "example.com" type: aaaa
```

```text expected
example.com
```

## List the network interfaces

List the network interfaces of the host.

```nurt example
network.interfaces
```

```text expected
interface
```

## Extract an archive without its top directory

Extract a source archive and drop the first path component of every entry.

```nurt example
archive.extract "/home/user/dl/src.tar.gz" into: "/home/user/src" strip_components: 1
```

```text expected
/home/user/src
```

```bash
tar -xzf /home/user/dl/src.tar.gz -C /home/user/src --strip-components=1
```

## Extract without overwriting files

Extract an archive and keep the files that already exist.

```nurt example
archive.extract "/home/user/dl/data.zip" into: "/home/user/data" on_conflict: skip
```

```text expected
/home/user/data
```

## List the entries that match a pattern

List only the JSON entries of an archive.

```nurt example
archive.list "/home/user/dl/data.zip" glob: "**/*.json"
```

```text expected
json
```

```bash
unzip -l /home/user/dl/data.zip '*.json'
```

## Create a Zstandard tar archive

Pack a source directory into a tar archive compressed with Zstandard.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app/src" |> archive.create "/home/user/out/src.tar.zst" format: tar_zst base: "/home/user/app"
```

```text expected
/home/user/out/src.tar.zst
```

```bash
tar --zstd -cf /home/user/out/src.tar.zst -C /home/user/app src
```

## Compress a file with a chosen algorithm

Compress a log with Zstandard at level 9 and remove the original.

```nurt example
compress "/home/user/app/app.log" algorithm: zstd level: 9 keep: false
```

```text expected
app.log
```

```bash
zstd -9 --rm /home/user/app/app.log
```

## Compress the old logs

Compress the log files that are older than seven days.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/logs" glob: "*.log" depth: 1 |> filter modified < ago(7d) |> compress
```

```text expected
nothing_matched
```

## Request only the headers

Send a HEAD request to read the headers of a resource.

```nurt example
http.request "https://example.com/a.tar.gz" method: head
```

```text expected
200
```

```bash
curl -fsSI https://example.com/a.tar.gz
```

## Save a response to a file

Save the body of a response to a file.

```nurt example
http.request "https://example.com/data.json" save: "/home/user/dl/data.json"
```

```text expected
/home/user/dl/data.json
```

## List the links of a page

List the links of a page that lead to the same host.

```nurt example
http.request "https://example.com/docs" extract: links same_host: true
```

```text expected
example.com
```

## Limit the time and retry a request

Fail a request after five seconds and retry it up to three times.

```nurt example
http.request "https://example.com/health" timeout: 5s retries: 3
```

```text expected
200
```

```bash
curl -fsS --max-time 5 --retry 3 https://example.com/health
```

## Resolve a mail exchanger

Resolve the mail exchangers of a domain through a chosen DNS server.

```nurt example
network.resolve "example.com" type: mx server: "9.9.9.9"
```

```text expected
example.com
```

```bash
dig @9.9.9.9 example.com MX
```

## Ping with a short timeout

Send one echo request and wait at most one second.

```nurt example
network.ping "example.com" count: 1 timeout: 1s
```

```text expected
example.com
```

title: Editing many files
text:
# Editing many files

## Replace an identifier in all Go files

Replace a function name in every Go file under a directory.

```nurt example
replace /oldName\(/ "newName(" in: ["/home/user/app/src"] glob: "**/*.go"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/src/a.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"x := oldName(1)\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.go
```

```bash
grep -rl 'oldName(' --include='*.go' /home/user/app/src | xargs sed -i 's/oldName(/newName(/g'
```

## Replace only when the expected number of files matches

Stop before any change when the pattern occurs in a different number of files than expected.

```nurt example
search /oldName\(/ "/home/user/app/src" glob: "**/*.go" |> assert paths: 1 |> replace "newName("
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/src/a.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"x := oldName(1)\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.go
```

## Replace a literal text

Replace a literal text that contains characters special to regular expressions.

```nurt example
replace "a.b(c)" "x" in: ["/home/user/app/notes.txt"] mode: literal
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/notes.txt","type":"file","content_utf8":"call a.b(c) now\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/notes.txt
```

## Replace only the first occurrence in each file

Replace the first occurrence of a text in each file and leave the others.

```nurt example
replace "http://" "https://" in: ["/home/user/app/site"] glob: "**/*.html" occurrence: 1
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/site/index.html","type":"file","content_utf8":"http://a http://b\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/site/index.html
```

## Replace a word without touching longer identifiers

Replace a whole word only, so that longer identifiers that contain it stay unchanged.

```nurt example
replace "id" "uid" in: ["/home/user/app/src"] glob: "**/*.py" whole_word: true
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/src/a.py","type":"file","content_utf8":"id = 1\nvalid = 2\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.py
```

## Replace and verify with a build

Replace a name and run the build in the same program; the changes are rolled back when the build fails.

```nurt example
search /oldName\(/ "/home/user/app/src" glob: "**/*.go"
|> replace "newName("
|> verify (run ["go", "build", "./..."] cwd: "/home/user/app" |> assert exit_code: 0)
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/src/a.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"x := oldName(1)\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.go
```

## Preview a replacement

Compute the targets of a replacement without changing anything.

```nurt example
replace /oldName\(/ "newName(" in: ["/home/user/app/src"] glob: "**/*.go"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/src/a.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"x := oldName(1)\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.go
```

The call parameter `preview: true` of the request turns the program into a preview.

## Remove the matching lines of many files

Remove the lines that contain a debug statement from a file.

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/app/app.js" |> filter text ~ /console\.log/ |> remove
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/app.js","type":"file","content_utf8":"a();\nconsole.log(1);\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/app.js
```

```bash
sed -i '/console\.log/d' /home/user/app/app.js
```

## Insert a line after a matching line

Insert an import after the package clause of a Go file.

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/app/main.go" |> filter text == "package main" |> insert r#"import "fmt""# position: after
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"package main\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/main.go
```

```bash
sed -i '/^package main$/a import "fmt"' /home/user/app/main.go
```

## Append a line to a file

Append one line to a file that exists.

```nurt example
write "/home/user/app/.gitignore" "node_modules/\n" mode: append
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/.gitignore","type":"file","content_utf8":"dist/\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/.gitignore
```

```bash
echo "node_modules/" >> /home/user/app/.gitignore
```

## Sort a file in place

Sort the lines of a file and write the result to the same file.

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/app/names.txt" |> sort text |> write "/home/user/app/names.txt" mode: overwrite
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/names.txt","type":"file","content_utf8":"b\na\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/names.txt
```

## Change the line endings of many files

Convert text files to LF line endings.

```nurt example
convert "/home/user/app/a.txt" line_ending: lf
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/a.txt","type":"file","content_utf8":"a\r\nb\r\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/a.txt
```

```bash
dos2unix /home/user/app/a.txt
```

## Convert the encoding of a file

Convert a file from Windows-1250 to UTF-8.

```nurt example
convert "/home/user/legacy/plik.txt" encoding: "utf-8"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/legacy/plik.txt","type":"file","content_utf8":"text\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/legacy/plik.txt
```

```bash
iconv -f windows-1250 -t utf-8 /home/user/legacy/plik.txt
```

## Apply a patch

Apply a unified diff to a project directory.

```nurt example
patch "--- a/a.txt\n+++ b/a.txt\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-one\n+two\n" root: "/home/user/app"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/a.txt","type":"file","content_utf8":"one\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/a.txt
```

```bash
patch -p1 -d /home/user/app < change.diff
```

## Replace regardless of letter case

Replace a product name in every Markdown file whatever its letter case.

```nurt example
replace "acme" "Acme" in: ["/home/user/app/docs"] glob: "**/*.md" case_sensitive: false
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/docs/a.md","type":"file","content_utf8":"ACME and acme\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/docs/a.md
```

```bash
grep -rli 'acme' --include='*.md' /home/user/app/docs | xargs sed -i 's/acme/Acme/gI'
```

## Replace only inside comments

Change a spelling in comments and leave the code unchanged.

```nurt example
replace "colour" "color" in: ["/home/user/app/src"] glob: "**/*.go" scope: comments
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/src/a.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"// colour of the text\nvar colour = 1\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.go
```

## Replace across lines

Join a call that is split over two lines.

```nurt example
replace /open\(\n\s+path\)/ "open(path)" in: ["/home/user/app/src"] glob: "**/*.js" multiline: true
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/src/a.js","type":"file","content_utf8":"open(\n  path)\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.js
```

## Replace with a bound on the number of changes

Stop before any change when the pattern occurs fewer than two or more than five times.

```nurt example
replace "timeout = 30" "timeout = 60" in: ["/home/user/app/conf"] glob: "*.conf" expect: 2..5
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/conf/a.conf","type":"file","content_utf8":"timeout = 30\n"},{"path":"/home/user/app/conf/b.conf","type":"file","content_utf8":"timeout = 30\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/conf/a.conf
```

## Replace in files of one language

Replace a name in the files of one language, wherever they are.

```nurt example
replace "getUser" "fetchUser" in: ["/home/user/app"] file_type: ["ts"]
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/src/a.ts","type":"file","content_utf8":"getUser(1)\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.ts
```

## Replace and respect the ignore rules

Replace a name in the files that the repository does not ignore.

```nurt example
replace "v1/api" "v2/api" in: ["/home/user/app"] gitignore: true
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/client.py","type":"file","content_utf8":"url = 'v1/api'\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/client.py
```

## Remove lines by number

Remove the first two lines of a file, for example a banner.

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/app/export.csv" 1..2 |> remove
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/export.csv","type":"file","content_utf8":"banner\ngenerated\nid,name\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/export.csv
```

```bash
sed -i '1,2d' /home/user/app/export.csv
```

## Insert a header at the start of a file

Insert a shebang line at the start of a script.

```nurt example
insert "#!/bin/sh" in: "/home/user/app/run.sh" position: start
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/run.sh","type":"file","content_utf8":"echo run\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/run.sh
```

```bash
sed -i '1i #!/bin/sh' /home/user/app/run.sh
```

## Insert a line at the end of a file

Insert a closing line at the end of a file.

```nurt example
insert "# end of file" in: "/home/user/app/app.conf" position: end ensure_newline: true
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/app.conf","type":"file","content_utf8":"a = 1"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/app.conf
```

## Copy the non-empty lines to another file

Write the non-empty lines of a file to a new file.

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/app/in.txt" |> filter text != "" |> write "/home/user/app/out.txt" mode: create
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/in.txt","type":"file","content_utf8":"a\n\nb\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/out.txt
```

```bash
grep -v '^$' /home/user/app/in.txt > /home/user/app/out.txt
```

## Write several files in one transaction

Create two files together; when one of them cannot be created, neither is.

```nurt example
write files: [{path: "/home/user/app/a.txt", text: "one\n"}, {path: "/home/user/app/b.txt", text: "two\n"}] mode: create
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/a.txt
```

## Convert all text files to LF

Convert the line endings of every text file of a directory.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app/docs" glob: "**/*.txt" |> convert line_ending: lf
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/docs/a.txt","type":"file","content_utf8":"a\r\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/docs/a.txt
```

## Add a byte order mark

Add a byte order mark to a file that a legacy program reads.

```nurt example
convert "/home/user/legacy/list.csv" bom: true
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/legacy/list.csv","type":"file","content_utf8":"a;b\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/legacy/list.csv
```

## Revert a patch

Apply a unified diff in reverse to undo the change that it describes.

```nurt example
patch "--- a/a.txt\n+++ b/a.txt\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-one\n+two\n" root: "/home/user/app" reverse: true
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/a.txt","type":"file","content_utf8":"two\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/a.txt
```

```bash
patch -R -p1 -d /home/user/app < change.diff
```

## Apply a patch from a file

Apply a diff stored in a file and strip one leading path component.

```nurt example
patch from: "/home/user/dl/change.diff" root: "/home/user/app" strip: 1
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/dl/change.diff","type":"file","content_utf8":"--- a/a.txt\n+++ b/a.txt\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-one\n+two\n"},{"path":"/home/user/app/a.txt","type":"file","content_utf8":"one\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/a.txt
```

title: Editing a single file
text:
# Editing a single file

## Create a file

Create a new file with a given content; the program fails when the file exists.

```nurt example
write "/home/user/app/notes.txt" "first\n" mode: create
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/notes.txt
```

## Overwrite a file

Replace the whole content of an existing file.

```nurt example
write "/home/user/app/notes.txt" "second\n" mode: overwrite
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/notes.txt","type":"file","content_utf8":"first\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/notes.txt
```

## Create a file with several lines

Create a multi-line file without escaping quotation marks.

```nurt example
write "/home/user/app/Dockerfile" r#"FROM alpine:3.20
RUN apk add --no-cache curl
CMD ["sh"]
"# mode: create
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/Dockerfile
```

```bash
cat > /home/user/app/Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM alpine:3.20
RUN apk add --no-cache curl
CMD ["sh"]
EOF
```

## Prepend a line to a file

Add a header line at the start of a file.

```nurt example
write "/home/user/app/notes.txt" "# Notes\n" mode: prepend
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/notes.txt","type":"file","content_utf8":"a\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/notes.txt
```

## Insert a line at a line number

Insert a comment before line 3 of a file.

```nurt example
insert "// updated" in: "/home/user/app/main.go" line: 3 position: before
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"a\nb\nc\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/main.go
```

## Apply several changes as one transaction

Apply three changes to one file; when one of them does not apply, none is applied.

```nurt example
edit "/home/user/app/main.go" changes: [
  {replace: "oldName(", with: "newName(", occurrence: 1},
  {insert: "// updated", line: 3, position: before},
  {delete_lines: 10..12}
] expect: 3
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"oldName(1)\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/main.go
```

## Set a key in a JSON file

Set one key of a JSON file and keep the layout of the rest.

```nurt example
set "/home/user/app/package.json" key: "scripts.test" value: "vitest"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/package.json","type":"file","content_utf8":"{\n  \"scripts\": {\n    \"test\": \"jest\"\n  }\n}\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/package.json
```

```bash
jq '.scripts.test = "vitest"' package.json > p.tmp && mv p.tmp package.json
```

## Set a key in a TOML file

Change a version in a TOML manifest and keep its comments.

```nurt example
set "/home/user/app/Cargo.toml" key: "package.version" value: "0.4.0"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/Cargo.toml","type":"file","content_utf8":"[package]\nversion = \"0.3.9\" # bump on release\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/Cargo.toml
```

## Set several keys at once

Set several keys of a YAML file in one operation.

```nurt example
set "/home/user/app/config.yaml" values: {"server.port": 8080, "server.debug": false}
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/config.yaml","type":"file","content_utf8":"server:\n  port: 80\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/config.yaml
```

## Read a key of a structured document

Read one value from a JSON document.

```nurt example
read "/home/user/app/package.json" key: "scripts.test"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/package.json","type":"file","content_utf8":"{\"scripts\":{\"test\":\"jest\"}}"}]}
```

```text expected
jest
```

## Query a document

Select the names of all dependencies of a JSON manifest.

```nurt example
read "/home/user/app/package.json" |> query "dependencies"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/package.json","type":"file","content_utf8":"{\"dependencies\":{\"left-pad\":\"1.0.0\"}}"}]}
```

```text expected
left-pad
```

## Run a query on a SQLite database

Read the active users of a SQLite database.

```nurt example
sql "/home/user/app/app.db" "select id, name from users where active = ? limit 5" params: [1]
```

```text expected
id
```

```bash
sqlite3 /home/user/app/app.db "select id, name from users where active = 1 limit 5"
```

## Write a file only when it did not change meanwhile

Replace a text only when the file still has the content that was read earlier.

```nurt example
replace "debug" "info" in: ["/home/user/app/app.conf"] if_match: "1a2b3c4d"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/app.conf","type":"file","content_utf8":"level = debug\n"}]}
```

```text expected
E_STALE
```

## Write a Windows registry value

Write a DWORD value to the registry of the current user.

```nurt example
write "registry:/HKCU/Software/Example/Mode" "3" value_type: dword mode: overwrite
```

```text expected
registry:/HKCU/Software/Example/Mode
```

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty HKCU:\Software\Example -Name Mode -Value 3 -Type DWord
```

## Append a line to a log file

Append a line to the end of a file and keep its content.

```nurt example
write "/home/user/app/notes.txt" "done\n" mode: append ensure_newline: true
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/notes.txt","type":"file","content_utf8":"start"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/notes.txt
```

```bash
printf '\ndone\n' >> /home/user/app/notes.txt
```

## Create a file with Windows line endings

Create a batch file with CRLF line endings.

```nurt example
write "/home/user/app/run.cmd" "@echo off\necho run\n" mode: create line_ending: crlf
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/run.cmd
```

## Create a file in a missing directory

Create a file together with the directories of its path.

```nurt example
write "/home/user/app/out/logs/today.txt" "start\n" mode: create parents: true
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/out/logs/today.txt
```

```bash
mkdir -p /home/user/app/out/logs && printf 'start\n' > /home/user/app/out/logs/today.txt
```

## Write a JSON file

Write a JSON file; a document that is not valid JSON is rejected.

```nurt example
write "/home/user/app/settings.json" r#"{"debug": false}"# mode: create format: json
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/settings.json
```

## Replace a text in one file

Replace one text in one file.

```nurt example
replace "localhost" "db.internal" in: ["/home/user/app/app.conf"]
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/app.conf","type":"file","content_utf8":"host = localhost\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/app.conf
```

```bash
sed -i 's/localhost/db.internal/g' /home/user/app/app.conf
```

## Insert a line after the last line

Insert a line at the end of a file.

```nurt example
insert "exit 0" in: "/home/user/app/run.sh" position: end
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/run.sh","type":"file","content_utf8":"echo run\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/run.sh
```

## Delete a range of lines

Delete lines 10 to 12 of a file.

```nurt example
edit "/home/user/app/main.go" changes: [{delete_lines: 10..12}]
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"a\nb\nc\nd\ne\nf\ng\nh\ni\nj\nk\nl\nm\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/main.go
```

```bash
sed -i '10,12d' /home/user/app/main.go
```

## Edit a file only when the content matches

Apply a change only when the file still has the content that was read earlier.

```nurt example
edit "/home/user/app/main.go" changes: [{replace: "oldName(", with: "newName("}] if_match: "1a2b3c4d"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"oldName(1)\n"}]}
```

```text expected
E_STALE
```

## Remove a key of a configuration file

Remove one key of a JSON file.

```nurt example
set "/home/user/app/package.json" key: "scripts.lint" value: null
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/package.json","type":"file","content_utf8":"{\"scripts\":{\"lint\":\"eslint .\",\"test\":\"jest\"}}"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/package.json
```

## Set a value in an INI file

Set a value in an INI file and keep the other lines.

```nurt example
set "/home/user/app/app.ini" key: "database.host" value: "db.internal" format: ini
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/app.ini","type":"file","content_utf8":"[database]\nhost = localhost\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/app.ini
```

## Set a variable of an environment file

Change a variable of a dotenv file.

```nurt example
set "/home/user/app/.env" key: "LOG_LEVEL" value: "debug" format: env
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/.env","type":"file","content_utf8":"LOG_LEVEL=info\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/.env
```

## Read a key of a YAML file

Read one nested value of a YAML file.

```nurt example
read "/home/user/app/config.yaml" key: "server.port"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/config.yaml","type":"file","content_utf8":"server:\n  port: 8080\n"}]}
```

```text expected
8080
```

## Read lines of a file

Read lines 5 to 15 of a file with their numbers.

```nurt example
read "/home/user/app/main.go" lines: 5..15 line_numbers: true
```

```text expected
main.go
```

```bash
sed -n '5,15p' /home/user/app/main.go | cat -n
```

## Read the last lines of a file

Read the last twenty lines of a log.

```nurt example
read "/home/user/app/app.log" last: 20
```

```text expected
app.log
```

```bash
tail -n 20 /home/user/app/app.log
```

## Write to a SQLite database

Insert a row into a SQLite database.

```nurt example
sql "/home/user/app/app.db" "insert into users (name, active) values (?, ?)" params: ["ann", 1]
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/app.db
```

title: Files and directories
text:
# Files and directories

## Remove a directory

Remove a directory with its content.

```nurt example
remove "/home/user/app/build"
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/build
```

```bash
rm -rf /home/user/app/build
```

## Remove the files of a pattern

Remove the temporary files of a build directory.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app/build" glob: "**/*.tmp" |> remove
```

```text expected
nothing_matched
```

## Remove the content of a directory

Remove everything inside a directory and keep the directory.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app/build" glob: "*" depth: 1 |> remove
```

```text expected
nothing_matched
```

## Remove a file with a space in its name

Remove a file whose name contains a space; the path is one value.

```nurt example
remove "/home/user/data/my file.txt"
```

```text expected
my file.txt
```

## Copy a directory

Copy a directory and keep the attributes.

```nurt example
copy "/home/user/app" to: "/home/user/backup" preserve: true
```

```text expected
/home/user/backup
```

```bash
cp -a /home/user/app /home/user/backup
```

## Copy several files into a directory

Copy two files into a directory.

```nurt example
copy ["/home/user/a.txt", "/home/user/b.txt"] into: "/home/user/out"
```

```text expected
/home/user/out
```

## Move the old logs

Move the log files older than seven days to an archive directory.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/logs" glob: "*.log" depth: 1 |> filter modified < ago(7d) |> move into: "/home/user/logs/old"
```

```text expected
nothing_matched
```

```bash
find /home/user/logs -maxdepth 1 -name '*.log' -mtime +7 -exec mv {} /home/user/logs/old/ \;
```

## Rename a file

Rename a file inside its directory.

```nurt example
rename path: "/home/user/a.txt" to: "b.txt"
```

```text expected
b.txt
```

## Rename files by a pattern

Replace the extension of the files of a directory.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/photos" glob: "*.jpeg" depth: 1 |> rename /\.jpeg$/ ".jpg"
```

```text expected
nothing_matched
```

## Create a directory with its parents

Create a nested directory.

```nurt example
create "/home/user/app/out/reports" type: directory
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/out/reports
```

## Create a symbolic link

Create a link to a directory.

```nurt example
create "/home/user/current" type: link target: "/home/user/app/releases/42"
```

```text expected
/home/user/current
```

## Change permissions

Make a script executable.

```nurt example
attributes "/home/user/app/run.sh" mode: "755"
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/run.sh
```

## Show the size of the subdirectories

List the directory tree with the size of every directory.

```nurt example
list "/home/user/app" view: sizes depth: 2
```

```text expected
/home/user/app
```

```bash
du -h --max-depth=2 /home/user/app
```

## Find duplicates by hash

Compute the hash of every file of a directory and keep the groups that share a hash.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/photos" |> hash |> group by: sha256
```

```text expected
sha256
```

## Compare two files

Show the differences between two files.

```nurt example
diff "/home/user/a.txt" "/home/user/b.txt"
```

```text expected
hunk
```

## List the largest entries

List the entries of a directory, the largest first.

```nurt example
list "/home/user/app" sort: size order: desc
```

```text expected
/home/user/app
```

```bash
ls -lS /home/user/app
```

## Show a directory tree

Show the tree of a directory down to the third level.

```nurt example
list "/home/user/app" view: tree depth: 3
```

```text expected
/home/user/app
```

```bash
tree -L 3 /home/user/app
```

## List only the subdirectories

List the subdirectories of a directory without hidden entries.

```nurt example
list "/home/user/app" type: directory hidden: false
```

```text expected
/home/user/app
```

## Find the largest files

Find the ten largest files of a directory.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/data" |> filter size > 100mb |> sort size order: desc |> first 10
```

```text expected
nothing_matched
```

```bash
find /home/user/data -type f -size +100M -exec ls -lS {} + | head -10
```

## Find the files changed today

Find the files that changed during the last 24 hours.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app/src" |> filter modified > ago(1d)
```

```text expected
nothing_matched
```

```bash
find /home/user/app/src -type f -mtime -1
```

## Find a file by an approximate name

Find the files whose path resembles a name.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" fuzzy: "readme" exclude_preset: ["vcs", "deps"]
```

```text expected
README
```

## Show the hash of a file

Show the BLAKE3 hash of a file together with its size.

```nurt example
hash "/home/user/dl/image.iso" algorithm: blake3
```

```text expected
blake3
```

```bash
b3sum /home/user/dl/image.iso
```

## Copy without overwriting

Copy a directory and keep the files that already exist in the target.

```nurt example
copy "/home/user/photos" to: "/home/user/backup/photos" on_conflict: skip
```

```text expected
/home/user/backup/photos
```

```bash
rsync -a --ignore-existing /home/user/photos/ /home/user/backup/photos/
```

## Move a file

Move a file to another path.

```nurt example
move "/home/user/dl/report.pdf" to: "/home/user/docs/report.pdf"
```

```text expected
/home/user/docs/report.pdf
```

```bash
mv /home/user/dl/report.pdf /home/user/docs/report.pdf
```

## Update the modification time

Create a file when it is missing and update its modification time otherwise.

```nurt example
create "/home/user/app/.stamp" type: file on_exists: touch
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/.stamp
```

```bash
touch /home/user/app/.stamp
```

## Create several directories

Create the directories of a project layout in one call.

```nurt example
create ["/home/user/app/src", "/home/user/app/docs", "/home/user/app/tests"] type: directory
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src
```

```bash
mkdir -p /home/user/app/src /home/user/app/docs /home/user/app/tests
```

## Create a temporary directory

Create a directory that Nurt removes at the end of the session.

```nurt example
create "/home/user/tmp/work" type: directory temporary: true
```

```text expected
/home/user/tmp/work
```

## Change the account and group of a tree

Set the account and group of a directory tree.

```nurt example
attributes "/home/user/www" owner: "deploy" group: "deploy" recursive: true
```

```text expected
/home/user/www
```

```bash
chown -R deploy:deploy /home/user/www
```

## Make a file read-only

Set the read-only attribute of a file.

```nurt example
attributes "/home/user/app/config.lock" readonly: true
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/config.lock
```

```bash
chmod a-w /home/user/app/config.lock
```

## Fail when a file is missing

Remove a file and report an error when it does not exist.

```nurt example
remove "/home/user/app/app.pid" on_missing: error
```

```text expected
E_NOT_FOUND
```

## Compare files ignoring whitespace

Show the differences between two files and ignore changes of whitespace.

```nurt example
diff "/home/user/a.txt" "/home/user/b.txt" ignore_whitespace: true context: 1
```

```text expected
hunk
```

```bash
diff -w -U 1 /home/user/a.txt /home/user/b.txt
```

title: Git
text:
# Git

## Show the status of a repository

Show the changed and untracked files of a repository.

```nurt example
git.status "/home/user/app"
```

```text expected
/home/user/app
```

```bash
git status --short
```

## Show the staged changes

Show the differences of the staged changes with their statistics.

```nurt example
git.diff "/home/user/app" staged: true stat: true
```

```text expected
files
```

## Show the history of a file

Show the last ten commits that changed a file.

```nurt example
git.log "/home/user/app" count: 10 path: ["src/main.go"]
```

```text expected
commit
```

## Show one commit

Show the changes of one revision.

```nurt example
git.show "/home/user/app" "HEAD"
```

```text expected
HEAD
```

## Find who changed a line

Show the author of each line of a range of a file.

```nurt example
git.blame "/home/user/app/src/main.go" lines: 10..20
```

```text expected
main.go
```

## Stage files and commit

Commit selected files with a message.

```nurt example
git.commit "/home/user/app" message: "fix: parser" paths: ["/home/user/app/a.go"]
```

```text expected
fix: parser
```

```bash
git add a.go && git commit -m "fix: parser"
```

## Commit with a trailer

Add a trailer line to the message of a commit.

```nurt example
git.commit "/home/user/app" message: "fix: parser" trailers: ["Co-Authored-By: Name <name@example.com>"] staged: true
```

```text expected
fix: parser
```

## Create and switch to a branch

Create a branch and switch to it.

```nurt example
git.switch "/home/user/app" branch: "feature/x" create: true
```

```text expected
feature/x
```

## Save a checkpoint before a risky change

Record the state of the working tree so that it can be restored.

```nurt example
git.checkpoint "/home/user/app" action: create label: "before refactoring"
```

```text expected
before refactoring
```

## Restore a checkpoint

Restore the working tree from a checkpoint.

```nurt example
git.checkpoint "/home/user/app" action: restore checkpoint_id: "before refactoring"
```

```text expected
before refactoring
```

## Stash the changes

Stash the changes, including untracked files.

```nurt example
git.stash "/home/user/app" action: push include_untracked: true
```

```text expected
stash
```

## Review the changes before a commit

Check the working tree for conflict markers, large files and secrets.

```nurt example
git.review "/home/user/app" scope: working checks: ["conflict_markers", "secrets"]
```

```text expected
finding
```

## Fetch from the remote

Fetch the branches and prune the deleted ones.

```nurt example
git.fetch "/home/user/app" prune: true
```

```text expected
origin
```

## Push a branch

Push a branch and set its upstream.

```nurt example
git.push "/home/user/app" branch: "feature/x" set_upstream: true
```

```text expected
feature/x
```

## Clone a repository

Clone a repository into a directory.

```nurt example
git.clone "https://example.com/team/app.git" "/home/user/src/app" depth: 1
```

```text expected
/home/user/src/app
```

## Show the untracked files

Show every untracked file, not only the collapsed directories, with the numbers of changed lines.

```nurt example
git.status "/home/user/app" untracked: all stat: true
```

```text expected
/home/user/app
```

```bash
git status --short --untracked-files=all
```

## Compare two revisions

Show the changes between two revisions of a path.

```nurt example
git.diff "/home/user/app" from: "v1.0.0" to: "HEAD" path: ["src"] stat: true
```

```text expected
files
```

```bash
git diff --stat v1.0.0 HEAD -- src
```

## Show a word-level diff

Show the changes of the working tree by words and ignore changes of whitespace.

```nurt example
git.diff "/home/user/app" word_diff: true ignore_whitespace: true
```

```text expected
hunk
```

## Show the commits of an author

Show the commits of one author since a date.

```nurt example
git.log "/home/user/app" author: "ann" since: "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z" count: 50
```

```text expected
commit
```

```bash
git log --author=ann --since=2026-10-01 -n 50
```

## Find the commit that introduced a text

Find the commits that added or removed a given text.

```nurt example
git.log "/home/user/app" pickaxe: "retryLimit" path: ["src"]
```

```text expected
commit
```

```bash
git log -S retryLimit -- src
```

## Group the commits by type

Group the last 100 commits by their conventional type.

```nurt example
git.log "/home/user/app" count: 100 group_by: type
```

```text expected
group
```

## Show a file in a revision

Show the changes of one file in a revision with its statistics.

```nurt example
git.show "/home/user/app" "HEAD~2" file: "/home/user/app/src/main.go" stat: true
```

```text expected
main.go
```

```bash
git show --stat HEAD~2 -- src/main.go
```

## List the branches

List the local branches of a repository.

```nurt example
git.branch "/home/user/app"
```

```text expected
main
```

```bash
git branch
```

## Create a branch from a revision

Create a branch that starts at a tag and keep the current branch.

```nurt example
git.branch "/home/user/app" create: "hotfix/1.0.1" from: "v1.0.0"
```

```text expected
hotfix/1.0.1
```

```bash
git branch hotfix/1.0.1 v1.0.0
```

## Delete a merged branch

Delete a branch; the repository keeps it in the trash so that it can be restored.

```nurt example
git.branch "/home/user/app" delete: "feature/x" trash: true
```

```text expected
feature/x
```

## Stage the changes of a path

Stage the changes of a directory.

```nurt example
git.stage "/home/user/app" action: add paths: ["/home/user/app/src"]
```

```text expected
src
```

```bash
git add src
```

## Unstage a file

Remove a file from the index and keep its changes.

```nurt example
git.stage "/home/user/app" action: unstage paths: ["/home/user/app/a.go"]
```

```text expected
a.go
```

```bash
git restore --staged a.go
```

## Restore a file from a revision

Restore a file to its state in the last commit and save a checkpoint first.

```nurt example
git.restore "/home/user/app" paths: ["/home/user/app/a.go"] source: "HEAD" checkpoint: true
```

```text expected
a.go
```

```bash
git restore --source=HEAD a.go
```

## Amend the last commit

Replace the message of the last commit.

```nurt example
git.commit "/home/user/app" message: "fix: parser error" amend: true
```

```text expected
fix: parser error
```

```bash
git commit --amend -m "fix: parser error"
```

## Create an annotated tag

Create an annotated tag for a release.

```nurt example
git.tag "/home/user/app" name: "v1.2.0" message: "release 1.2.0"
```

```text expected
v1.2.0
```

```bash
git tag -a v1.2.0 -m "release 1.2.0"
```

## Merge a branch

Merge a branch and refuse a merge that is not a fast-forward.

```nurt example
git.merge "/home/user/app" branch: "feature/x" fast_forward: only
```

```text expected
feature/x
```

## Abort a merge

Abort a merge that stopped on a conflict.

```nurt example
git.merge "/home/user/app" action: abort
```

```text expected
effect
```

```bash
git merge --abort
```

## Rebase onto a branch

Rebase the current branch onto the main branch.

```nurt example
git.rebase "/home/user/app" onto: "main"
```

```text expected
main
```

## Pull with a rebase

Fetch the upstream branch and rebase the local commits onto it.

```nurt example
git.pull "/home/user/app" mode: rebase
```

```text expected
origin
```

```bash
git pull --rebase
```

## Apply and drop a stash

Apply the newest stash and remove it from the stash list.

```nurt example
git.stash "/home/user/app" action: pop
```

```text expected
stash
```

## Add a worktree for a branch

Check out a branch in a second directory.

```nurt example
git.worktree "/home/user/app" action: add path: "/home/user/app-hotfix" branch: "hotfix/1.0.1"
```

```text expected
/home/user/app-hotfix
```

```bash
git worktree add /home/user/app-hotfix hotfix/1.0.1
```

## Push the tags

Push a branch together with the tags.

```nurt example
git.push "/home/user/app" branch: "main" tags: true
```

```text expected
main
```

## Push with a lease

Replace a remote branch only when it has not changed since it was fetched.

```nurt example
git.push "/home/user/app" branch: "feature/x" force: lease
```

```text expected
feature/x
```

```bash
git push --force-with-lease origin feature/x
```

title: Journal, undo and safety
text:
# Journal, undo and safety

## Show the history of operations

Show the five latest operations of the journal.

```nurt example
history limit: 5
```

```text expected
id
```

## Undo an operation

Undo one operation by its number.

```nurt example
undo 18
```

```text expected
18
```

## Undo with later changes included

Undo an operation together with the later operations that touched the same files.

```nurt example
undo 18 on_conflict: include_later
```

```text expected
18
```

## Undo the changes of one file

Undo the changes of one file made since an operation.

```nurt example
undo since: 18 paths: ["/home/user/app/src/a.go"]
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.go
```

## Redo an undone operation

Apply an undone operation again.

```nurt example
redo 18
```

```text expected
18
```

## Show the details of an operation

Show the files of one operation.

```nurt example
history 18 details: true
```

```text expected
18
```

## Find the operations that touched a path

Show the operations that changed a path.

```nurt example
history path: "/home/user/app/src/a.go"
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.go
```

## Pin an operation

Keep an operation in the journal for 24 hours.

```nurt example
journal.pin 18 until: 24h
```

```text expected
18
```

## Show the space of the journal

Show the free space and the space held by the journal of a volume.

```nurt example
journal.space
```

```text expected
free
```

## Show the state of the journal

Show whether the journal is on and how many operations it holds.

```nurt example
journal.status
```

```text expected
journal
```

## Set the retention limits

Keep the last 100 operations of the session.

```nurt example
journal.limits steps: 100
```

```text expected
100
```

## Purge expired entries

Remove the entries up to an operation from the journal.

```nurt example
journal.purge up_to: 17
```

```text expected
17
```

## Guard a change with a count

Stop before any change when a command targets more files than expected.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app/build" glob: "**/*.o" |> assert count: 12 |> remove
```

```text expected
E_ASSERT
```

## Check a change with a build

Run a build after a change and roll back when it fails.

```nurt example
search /oldName\(/ "/home/user/app/src" glob: "**/*.go" |> replace "newName(" |> verify (run ["go", "build", "./..."] cwd: "/home/user/app" |> assert exit_code: 0)
```

```text expected
newName
```

## List the operations that were only partly undoable

List the operations whose changes are only partly kept in the journal.

```nurt example
history state: partial limit: 10
```

```text expected
partial
```

## List the operations that were undone

List the operations that were undone and can be redone.

```nurt example
history state: undone
```

```text expected
undone
```

## List the operations that removed files

List the operations that deleted at least one file.

```nurt example
history deleted: true limit: 20
```

```text expected
id
```

## Undo every operation back to a point

Undo all operations newer than operation 12, latest first, in one transaction.

```nurt example
undo to: 12
```

```text expected
12
```

## Undo operations of all sessions

Undo the operations of every session that are newer than operation 12.

```nurt example
undo to: 12 all_sessions: true
```

```text expected
12
```

## Undo what is possible and report the rest

Undo the files of an operation that are not touched by later changes and report the others.

```nurt example
undo 18 on_conflict: partial
```

```text expected
18
```

## Cancel an undo on conflict

Leave all files unchanged when a later change touches a file of the operation.

```nurt example
undo 18 on_conflict: abort
```

```text expected
18
```

## Undo the changes of a file made in the last hour

Restore one file to its state of one hour ago.

```nurt example
undo file: "/home/user/app/src/a.go" since: ago(1h)
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.go
```

## Release a pinned operation

Allow the journal to release an operation that was pinned.

```nurt example
journal.pin 18 release: true
```

```text expected
18
```

## Limit the age of the journal for the account

Keep the operations of the last seven days for the current account.

```nurt example
journal.limits age: 7d scope: user
```

```text expected
7d
```

## Guard a replacement with a file count

Stop before the replacement when the search finds more than five files.

```nurt example
search /legacyApi/ "/home/user/app/src" |> assert paths: 1..5 |> replace "currentApi"
```

```text expected
E_ASSERT
```

title: Records and text processing
text:
# Records and text processing

## Sort records by a field

Sort the entries of a directory by size, largest first.

```nurt example
list "/home/user/app" |> sort size order: desc
```

```text expected
/home/user/app
```

## Take the first records

Take the ten most recently modified files.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" |> sort modified order: desc |> first 10
```

```text expected
/home/user/app
```

## Select fields

Show only the path and the size of the files.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" |> select path size
```

```text expected
path
```

## Compute a field

Show the size of the files in kilobytes.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" |> select path kb: size / 1000
```

```text expected
kb
```

## Group and summarize

Count the files by extension.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" |> group by: extension |> summarize
```

```text expected
extension
```

## Remove duplicates

List the distinct file extensions of a project.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" |> select extension |> distinct
```

```text expected
extension
```

## Skip a header

Skip the first line of a file.

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/data.csv" |> skip 1 |> first 5
```

```text expected
data.csv
```

## Split lines into fields

Split lines of a colon separated file into named fields.

```nurt example
lines "/etc/example/passwd" |> split ":" names: ["user", "uid", "home"]
```

```text expected
user
```

```bash
awk -F: '{print $1, $3}' /etc/example/passwd
```

## Parse lines with a pattern

Extract named parts of each log line.

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/app/app.log" |> parse /(?P<level>\w+) (?P<message>.*)/
```

```text expected
level
```

## Describe the fields of records

Show the fields and the types of the records of a command.

```nurt example
processes |> describe
```

```text expected
field
```

## Evaluate an expression

Evaluate an expression without reading any file.

```nurt example
evaluate 40 + 2
```

```text expected
42
```

## Name a result and use it twice

Store the result of a search and count it.

```nurt example
let recent = find "/home/user/app/src" glob: "**/*.ts" |> filter modified > ago(1h)
@recent |> count
```

```text expected
0
```

## Hash a file

Compute the SHA-256 hash of a file.

```nurt example
hash "/home/user/dl/a.tar.gz" algorithm: sha256
```

```text expected
sha256
```

```bash
sha256sum /home/user/dl/a.tar.gz
```

## Filter by a pattern in a field

Keep the entries whose name matches a regular expression.

```nurt example
list "/home/user/app" |> filter name ~ /^test_/
```

```text expected
test_
```

## Sort by two fields

Sort the files by extension and, within an extension, by size.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" |> sort by: [extension, size] order: desc
```

```text expected
extension
```

## Take the last records

Take the five oldest files of a directory.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" |> sort modified |> first 5
```

```text expected
/home/user/app
```

## Keep the last lines of a file

Keep the last three lines of a file.

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/app/app.log" |> last 3
```

```text expected
app.log
```

## Filter the lines of a file

Keep the lines of a file that contain a warning.

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/app/app.log" |> filter text ~ /WARN/
```

```text expected
WARN
```

## Select the number and the text of lines

Show the number and the text of every line.

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/app/main.go" |> select no text
```

```text expected
text
```

## Count the records by a field

Count the files of each type.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" |> group by: type |> summarize
```

```text expected
type
```

## Sum a field

Add up the sizes of the files by extension.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" |> summarize size by: extension
```

```text expected
size
```

## Split a table into fields

Split lines of a semicolon separated file and keep two columns.

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/data.csv" |> skip 1 |> split ";" names: ["id", "name", "city"] |> select id name
```

```text expected
id
```

## Query a SQLite database

Read the rows of a table of a database file.

```nurt example
sql "/home/user/app/data.db" "select id, name from users where active = 1"
```

```text expected
name
```

## Query with named parameters

Bind the values of a query by name.

```nurt example
sql "/home/user/app/data.db" "select id from orders where total > :min and city = :city" params: {min: 100, city: "Gdansk"}
```

```text expected
id
```

## Change rows and review the result

Update rows of a database file and show the number of rows that changed.

```nurt example
sql "/home/user/app/data.db" "update users set active = 0 where last_seen < ?" params: ["2025-01-01"]
```

```text expected
rows_changed
```

title: Running programs and background jobs
text:
# Running programs and background jobs

## Run a program in a directory

Run a build in a project directory.

```nurt example
run ["make", "build"] cwd: "/home/user/app"
```

```text expected
exit_code
```

```bash
cd /home/user/app && make build
```

## Fail when the exit code is not zero

Run a program and make the program fail unless it exits with code 0.

```nurt example
run ["go", "test", "./..."] cwd: "/home/user/app" |> assert exit_code: 0
```

```text expected
exit_code
```

## Pass environment variables

Run a program with an additional environment variable.

```nurt example
run ["npm", "test"] cwd: "/home/user/app" env: {"CI": "1"}
```

```text expected
exit_code
```

```bash
CI=1 npm test
```

## Limit the run time

Stop a program that runs longer than one minute.

```nurt example
run ["make", "test"] cwd: "/home/user/app" timeout: 60s
```

```text expected
timed_out
```

## Show only the errors of a long output

Show the lines that look like errors, the first 5 lines and the last 10 lines.

```nurt example
run ["npm", "test"] cwd: "/home/user/app" show: errors head: 5 tail: 10
```

```text expected
exit_code
```

```bash
npm test 2>&1 | tail -n 50
```

## Start a program in the background

Start a long build and return at once.

```nurt example
run ["npm", "run", "build"] cwd: "/home/user/app" background: true
```

```text expected
job
```

```bash
npm run build > out.log 2>&1 &
```

## Read the output of a background job

Read the last 20 lines of the output of a job.

```nurt example
jobs "j1" tail: 20
```

```text expected
j1
```

## Wait for a job

Wait up to 30 seconds for a job to finish.

```nurt example
jobs "j1" wait: 30s
```

```text expected
j1
```

## List the running jobs

List the jobs that are still running.

```nurt example
jobs state: running
```

```text expected
running
```

## Stop a job

Stop a running job.

```nurt example
jobs "j1" |> stop
```

```text expected
j1
```

## Retry a failed job

Run a failed job again with the same arguments.

```nurt example
jobs "j1" |> retry
```

```text expected
j1
```

## List the files a program changed

Run a formatter and list the files it changed.

```nurt example
run ["gofmt", "-w", "."] cwd: "/home/user/app" watch: ["/home/user/app"]
```

```text expected
exit_code
```

## Pause for a number of seconds

Wait five seconds before the next call.

```nurt example
sleep 5s
```

```text expected
5s
```

## Run the tests and read the failures

Run the tests of a project and show at most 10 failures with 5 lines of message each.

```nurt example
test.run "/home/user/app" failures: 10 message_lines: 5
```

```text expected
test_run
```

## Feed a file to a program

Run a program with the content of a file as its standard input.

```nurt example
run ["sort", "-u"] stdin: "/home/user/app/names.txt"
```

```text expected
exit_code
```

```bash
sort -u < /home/user/app/names.txt
```

## Stop a program that produces no output

Stop an installation that prints nothing for two minutes.

```nurt example
run ["npm", "install"] cwd: "/home/user/app" idle_timeout: 2m
```

```text expected
exit_code
```

## Show only warnings and errors with context

Merge the error stream into the output and keep the lines that match a pattern with two lines of context.

```nurt example
run ["make"] cwd: "/home/user/app" merge_stderr: true filter: /warning|error/ context: 2
```

```text expected
exit_code
```

```bash
make 2>&1 | grep -E -C 2 'warning|error'
```

## Run with a clean environment

Run a program without the environment of the session and with one variable.

```nurt example
run ["env"] inherit_env: none env: {"LANG": "C"}
```

```text expected
LANG
```

```bash
env -i LANG=C env
```

## Limit the resources of a program

Run a build with a low priority and a limit of memory.

```nurt example
run ["make", "-j4"] cwd: "/home/user/app" max_memory: 2gb priority: low
```

```text expected
exit_code
```

```bash
nice -n 19 make -j4
```

## Run a program for each file

Run an image optimizer on every PNG file, four at a time, 8 files per call.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app/img" glob: "**/*.png" |> run ["optipng", "-o2"] parallel: 4 batch: 8
```

```text expected
exit_code
```

```bash
find /home/user/app/img -name '*.png' -print0 | xargs -0 -n 8 -P 4 optipng -o2
```

## Name a background job

Start a release build as a labelled job.

```nurt example
run ["make", "release"] cwd: "/home/user/app" background: true label: "release-build" description: "Release build of the application"
```

```text expected
release-build
```

## Report progress and a summary of a run

Report the percentage lines of a run and keep the line that sums up the result.

```nurt example
run ["cargo", "test"] cwd: "/home/user/app" progress: /\d+%/ summary: [/test result/]
```

```text expected
summary_lines
```

## Read the errors of a job

Read the lines of the output of a job that match a pattern, with two lines of context.

```nurt example
jobs "j1" view: output filter: /error/ context: 2
```

```text expected
j1
```

## Read the result of a finished job

Read the exit code and the duration of a finished job.

```nurt example
jobs "j1" view: result
```

```text expected
exit_code
```

## Stop a job gently

Interrupt a job and give it ten seconds to finish before it is killed.

```nurt example
jobs "j1" |> stop signal: interrupt grace: 10s
```

```text expected
j1
```

title: Searching and reading
text:
# Searching and reading

## List the entries of a directory

List the files and directories directly under a project directory.

```nurt example
list "/home/user/app"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"package main\n"},{"path":"/home/user/app/docs","type":"dir"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/main.go
```

```bash
ls -la /home/user/app
```

```powershell
Get-ChildItem C:\Users\user\app
```

## Find the largest Go files changed in the last day

Find Go files larger than 1 MB that changed in the last 24 hours, largest first.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" glob: "**/*.go"
|> filter size > 1mb and modified > ago(24h)
|> sort size order: desc
|> first 20
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/gen/schema.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"package gen\n"}]}
```

```text expected
matched 0
```

```bash
find /home/user/app -name '*.go' -size +1M -mtime -1 -printf '%s %p\n' | sort -rn | head -20
```

```powershell
Get-ChildItem C:\Users\user\app -Recurse -Filter *.go | Where-Object { $_.Length -gt 1MB -and $_.LastWriteTime -gt (Get-Date).AddDays(-1) } | Sort-Object Length -Descending | Select-Object -First 20
```

## Count the files of one type

Count the TypeScript files of a project.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" glob: "**/*.ts" |> count
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/a.ts","type":"file","content_utf8":""},{"path":"/home/user/app/b.ts","type":"file","content_utf8":""}]}
```

```text expected
2
```

```bash
find /home/user/app -name '*.ts' | wc -l
```

## Find files by a name fragment

Find files whose name contains the word `config`, in any directory.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" glob: "**/*config*"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/config.toml","type":"file","content_utf8":""},{"path":"/home/user/app/src/main.rs","type":"file","content_utf8":""}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/config.toml
```

```bash
find /home/user/app -name '*config*'
```

## Find a text pattern in source files

Find every call of a function in the Go files of a directory.

```nurt example
search /oldName\(/ "/home/user/app/src" glob: "**/*.go"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/src/a.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"x := oldName(1)\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.go
```

```bash
grep -rn 'oldName(' --include='*.go' /home/user/app/src
```

```powershell
Get-ChildItem C:\Users\user\app\src -Recurse -Filter *.go | Select-String 'oldName\('
```

## List the files that contain a pattern

List only the paths of the files that contain a pattern, without the matching lines.

```nurt example
search /pending/ "/home/user/app/src" output: files
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/src/a.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"// pending\n"},{"path":"/home/user/app/src/b.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"x\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.go
```

```bash
grep -rl 'pending' /home/user/app/src
```

## Search without regard to letter case

Search for a word in a log file and accept any letter case.

```nurt example
search "error" "/home/user/app/app.log" case_sensitive: false
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/app.log","type":"file","content_utf8":"ok\nERROR disk full\n"}]}
```

```text expected
disk full
```

```bash
grep -in 'error' /home/user/app/app.log
```

## Show context around a match

Show three lines before and after each match of a pattern.

```nurt example
search /panic/ "/home/user/app/app.log" context: 3
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/app.log","type":"file","content_utf8":"a\nb\npanic: boom\nc\n"}]}
```

```text expected
panic: boom
```

```bash
grep -C 3 'panic' /home/user/app/app.log
```

## Read a file
