Read the whole content of a text file.

```nurt example
read "/home/user/app/README.md"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/README.md","type":"file","content_utf8":"# App\n"}]}
```

```text expected
# App
```

```bash
cat /home/user/app/README.md
```

```powershell
Get-Content C:\Users\user\app\README.md
```

## Read a range of lines

Read lines 10 to 20 of a source file with line numbers.

```nurt example
read "/home/user/app/main.go" lines: 10..20 line_numbers: true
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"package main\n"}]}
```

```text expected
main.go
```

```bash
sed -n '10,20p' /home/user/app/main.go
```

## Read the last lines of a log

Read the last 50 lines of a log file.

```nurt example
read "/home/user/app/app.log" last: 50
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/app.log","type":"file","content_utf8":"started\n"}]}
```

```text expected
started
```

```bash
tail -n 50 /home/user/app/app.log
```

```powershell
Get-Content C:\Users\user\app\app.log -Tail 50
```

## Read the lines around a pattern

Read the lines around the first line that matches a pattern.

```nurt example
read "/home/user/app/main.go" around: /func main/ context: 3
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"package main\n\nfunc main() {}\n"}]}
```

```text expected
func main
```

## Show the metadata of a file

Show the size, times and permissions of a file together with its SHA-256 hash.

```nurt example
info "/home/user/app/main.go" hash: sha256
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"package main\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/main.go
```

```bash
stat /home/user/app/main.go && sha256sum /home/user/app/main.go
```

## Count the lines of a file

Count the lines of a file.

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/app/main.go" |> count
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"a\nb\nc\n"}]}
```

```text expected
3
```

```bash
wc -l /home/user/app/main.go
```

## List a directory by modification time

List the entries of a directory, the most recently modified first.

```nurt example
list "/home/user/app" sort: modified order: desc
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"package main\n"},{"path":"/home/user/app/go.mod","type":"file","content_utf8":"module app\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/main.go
```

```bash
ls -lt /home/user/app
```

## Find only directories

Find the directories of a project whose name contains `test`.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" type: directory glob: "**/*test*"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/tests","type":"dir"},{"path":"/home/user/app/src","type":"dir"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/tests
```

```bash
find /home/user/app -type d -name '*test*'
```

## Find files without dependency and build directories

Find JavaScript files and skip dependency and build directories.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" glob: "**/*.js" exclude_preset: [deps, build]
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/index.js","type":"file","content_utf8":""},{"path":"/home/user/app/node_modules/x/index.js","type":"file","content_utf8":""}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/index.js
```

## Search for a whole word

Find the word `id` and skip longer words that contain it.

```nurt example
search "id" "/home/user/app/src" whole_word: true
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/src/a.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"x := id\ny := width\n"}]}
```

```text expected
x := id
```

```bash
grep -rnw 'id' /home/user/app/src
```

## Count the matches per file

Count the lines that contain a pattern in every file.

```nurt example
search /deprecated/ "/home/user/app/src" output: counts
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/src/a.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"// deprecated a\n// deprecated b\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.go
```

```bash
grep -rc 'deprecated' /home/user/app/src
```

## List the files without a pattern

List the files that do not contain a license notice.

```nurt example
search /Copyright/ "/home/user/app/src" glob: "**/*.go" output: unmatched
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/src/a.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"// Copyright 2026\n"},{"path":"/home/user/app/src/b.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"package b\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/b.go
```

```bash
grep -rL 'Copyright' --include='*.go' /home/user/app/src
```

## Extract only the matching text

Extract the version numbers from a file without the rest of the line.

```nurt example
search /v\d+\.\d+\.\d+/ "/home/user/app/CHANGELOG.md" only_matching: true
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/CHANGELOG.md","type":"file","content_utf8":"## v1.2.3\n"}]}
```

```text expected
v1.2.3
```

```bash
grep -oE 'v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' /home/user/app/CHANGELOG.md
```

## Search a pattern that spans lines

Find a function that starts with an empty body.

```nurt example
search /func main\(\) \{\n\}/ "/home/user/app/main.go" multiline: true
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"func main() {\n}\n"}]}
```

```text expected
func main
```

## Read one function

Read the definition of a function by its name.

```nurt example
read "/home/user/app/main.go" symbol: "main"
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"package main\n\nfunc main() {}\n"}]}
```

```text expected
func main
```

## Read the outline of a file

Read the declarations of a file without their bodies.

```nurt example
read "/home/user/app/main.go" view: outline
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"package main\n\nfunc main() {}\n"}]}
```

```text expected
main
```

## Show the metadata of several files

Show the metadata of two files in one call.

```nurt example
info ["/home/user/app/main.go", "/home/user/app/go.mod"]
```

```json fs-before
{"format":"nurt-fs-snapshot/1","entries":[{"path":"/home/user/app/main.go","type":"file","content_utf8":"package main\n"},{"path":"/home/user/app/go.mod","type":"file","content_utf8":"module app\n"}]}
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/go.mod
```

```bash
stat /home/user/app/main.go /home/user/app/go.mod
```

title: Source code
text:
# Source code

## Find the definition of a function

Find the symbols named `parseConfig` that are functions.

```nurt example
code.symbols "parseConfig" path: ["/home/user/app/src"] kind: function
```

```text expected
parseConfig
```

## Rename a function by syntax

Rename a function and its references; strings and comments are not changed.

```nurt example
code.symbols "oldName" path: ["/home/user/app/src"] kind: function |> code.rename "newName"
```

```text expected
newName
```

```bash
gopls rename -w /home/user/app/src/a.go:12:6 newName
```

## List the references of a symbol

List the references of the symbol at a position of a file.

```nurt example
code.references "/home/user/app/src/a.go" line: 12 column: 6
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.go
```

## Show the outline of a file

Show the symbols of a source file as an outline.

```nurt example
code.outline "/home/user/app/src/a.go"
```

```text expected
a.go
```

## Go to the definition at a position

Find the definition of the symbol at a position.

```nurt example
code.definition "/home/user/app/src/a.go" line: 40 column: 9
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src
```

## Show the diagnostics of a project

Show the errors and warnings of the source files of a directory.

```nurt example
code.diagnostics ["/home/user/app/src"] severity: warning
```

```text expected
severity
```

## Find the implementations of an interface

Find the types that implement an interface method.

```nurt example
code.implementations "/home/user/app/src/shape.go" line: 5 column: 6
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src
```

## Show the call hierarchy of a function

Show the functions that call a function.

```nurt example
code.call_hierarchy "/home/user/app/src/a.go" line: 12 column: 6 direction: incoming
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src
```

## List the languages with a language server

List the languages for which code commands have an analyzer.

```nurt example
code.languages
```

```text expected
go
```

## Summarize a repository

Show the manifests, entry points and languages of a repository.

```nurt example
code.profile "/home/user/app" sections: ["manifests", "languages"]
```

```text expected
manifests
```

## Search code inside comments only

Search a pattern only in comments of source files.

```nurt example
search /deprecated/ "/home/user/app/src" scope: comments
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src
```

## Replace only in code

Replace an identifier in code and leave strings and comments unchanged.

```nurt example
replace "oldName" "newName" in: ["/home/user/app/src"] glob: "**/*.go" scope: code whole_word: true
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src
```

## Run the tests of a Go project

Run the tests of a project and require a zero exit code.

```nurt example
run ["go", "test", "./..."] cwd: "/home/user/app" |> assert exit_code: 0
```

```text expected
exit_code
```

## Check types and style of a project

Run the checks of the project analyzers on the changed files only.

```nurt example
analyze.check changed_only: true
```

```text expected
finding
```

## List the exported functions with their signatures

List the exported functions whose name starts with `New`.

```nurt example
code.symbols "New" match: prefix kind: function exported_only: true with_signature: true path: ["/home/user/app/src"]
```

```text expected
signature
```

## List the structures outside the tests

List the structures of a project and skip the test files.

```nurt example
code.symbols kind: struct path: ["/home/user/app/src"] exclude_preset: [tests]
```

```text expected
struct
```

## List the references within one file

List the references of a symbol in the file of its definition only.

```nurt example
code.references "/home/user/app/src/a.go" line: 12 column: 6 scope: file include_definition: true
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src/a.go
```

## List the actions available for a range of lines

List the fixes and refactorings that the analyzer offers for lines 20 to 25.

```nurt example
code.actions "/home/user/app/src/a.go" line: 20 end_line: 25
```

```text expected
code_action
```

## Show the errors of the changed files

Show only the errors of the files that changed since the last commit.

```nurt example
code.diagnostics changed: true severity: error
```

```text expected
severity
```

## Show the entry points and the commands of a project

Show how a project is built, tested and started.

```nurt example
code.profile "/home/user/app" sections: ["commands", "entry_points"]
```

```text expected
commands
```

## Rename a symbol and its mentions in comments

Rename a function and change its name in comments of the code.

```nurt example
code.symbols "oldName" path: ["/home/user/app/src"] kind: function |> code.rename "newName" include_comments: true
```

```text expected
newName
```

## Search the strings of the source files

Find the web addresses written in the string literals of the code.

```nurt example
search /https?:\/\// "/home/user/app/src" scope: strings
```

```text expected
/home/user/app/src
```

## Check types and lint for the whole project

Run the type check and the linter and fail on errors only.

```nurt example
analyze.check ["/home/user/app/src"] checks: [types, lint] fail_on: error
```

```text expected
analysis
```

## Read the findings of an analysis

Read at most 20 errors of an earlier analysis.

```nurt example
analyze.show "a1" min_severity: error max_findings: 20
```

```text expected
finding
```

## Repeat the failed tests

Run again only the tests that failed in an earlier run.

```nurt example
test.failed "r1" failures: 10 message_lines: 5
```

```text expected
test_run
```

title: System and processes
text:
# System and processes

## List the processes by memory

List the five processes that use the most memory.

```nurt example
processes |> sort memory order: desc |> first 5
```

```text expected
pid
```

```bash
ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -6
```

## Find a process by name

Find the processes whose name matches a pattern.

```nurt example
processes /node/
```

```text expected
node
```

## Show who listens on a port

Show the process that listens on port 8080.

```nurt example
ports state: listen |> filter port == 8080
```

```text expected
8080
```

```bash
ss -ltnp | grep :8080
```

## Stop a process

Stop the process with a given identifier.

```nurt example
processes pid: 4132 |> stop
```

```text expected
4132
```

## Kill a process that ignores termination

Kill a process that does not react to the termination signal.

```nurt example
processes pid: 4132 |> stop signal: kill
```

```text expected
4132
```

## Show the disks

Show the mounted volumes and their free space.

```nurt example
disks
```

```text expected
free
```

```bash
df -h
```

## Show the host

Show the operating system, the user and the programs that are installed.

```nurt example
host programs: ["git", "python3", "node"] versions: true
```

```text expected
git
```

## Show the environment variables

Show the environment variables of the process whose name contains `PATH`.

```nurt example
environment /PATH/
```

```text expected
PATH
```

## Find the program in the search path

Find where a program is installed.

```nurt example
program.find "git"
```

```text expected
git
```

## Find the processes that hold a file open

Find the processes that keep a file open.

```nurt example
open_files "/home/user/app/app.log"
```

```text expected
pid
```

## Read the system log

Read the 50 latest error events of the system log.

```nurt example
logs level: error limit: 50
```

```text expected
error
```

## Read the log of one unit

Read the log of one service unit since one hour ago.

```nurt example
logs unit: "nginx" since: ago(1h)
```

```text expected
nginx
```

## Show the accounts

List the user accounts of the host.

```nurt example
accounts kind: user
```

```text expected
user
```

## Suspend a process

Suspend a process until it is resumed.

```nurt example
processes pid: 4132 |> suspend
```

```text expected
4132
```

## Resume a process

Resume a suspended process.

```nurt example
processes pid: 4132 |> resume
```

```text expected
4132
```

## List the processes of an account

List the processes that run for one account.

```nurt example
processes user: "deploy"
```

```text expected
deploy
```

```bash
ps -u deploy
```

## Show the working directory of processes

Show the working directories of the processes whose name matches a pattern.

```nurt example
processes /node/ cwd: true
```

```text expected
node
```

## Show the UDP ports

Show all ports that use the UDP protocol, not only the listening ones.

```nurt example
ports state: all protocol: udp
```

```text expected
udp
```

```bash
ss -uanp
```

## Find the disk with the least free space

Show the volume with the least free space.

```nurt example
disks |> sort free order: asc |> first 1
```

```text expected
free
```

```bash
df -h --output=source,avail | sort -h -k2 | head -2
```

## Show the variables of the account

Show the environment variable `PATH` as it is set for the account, not for the session.

```nurt example
environment "PATH" scope: user
```

```text expected
PATH
```

## Search the warnings of the system log

Show the warnings of the last day that mention a timeout.

```nurt example
logs level: warning message: /timeout/ since: ago(24h)
```

```text expected
timeout
```

```bash
journalctl -p warning --since '-1 day' | grep -i timeout
```

## Read a window of the log of a unit

Read the log of a unit between two points in time.

```nurt example
logs unit: "sshd" since: ago(2h) until: ago(1h)
```

```text expected
sshd
```

## Find an installed program by a keyword

Search the path, the packages and the applications for programs that handle JSON.

```nurt example
program.search "json" source: [path, package] limit: 10
```

```text expected
json
```

## Read the description of a program

Read the card of a program with its usage guide.

```nurt example
program.describe "jq" include_guide: true
```

```text expected
jq
```

## Show the versions of installed programs

Show the locations and versions of several programs.

```nurt example
program.find ["git", "make"] versions: true
```

```text expected
git
```

## Stop a process after a grace period

Terminate a process and kill it when it does not exit within five seconds.

```nurt example
processes /^runaway$/ |> stop grace: 5s
```

```text expected
runaway
```

title: Command documentation
text:
# Command documentation

Every command of the catalog has one page: the reference description for
people and the source of the examples and notes that the built-in help and the
model description show. Signatures are not written by
hand: names, types, positions, defaults and enumeration values come from the
catalog (`catalog/*.toml`, format `nurt-catalog/1`, see `spec/catalog.md`), and
the build checks that every page agrees with it.

## 1. Files

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `docs/commands/<command>.md` | page of one command; the file name is the full command name (`replace.md`, `git.status.md`) |
| `docs/commands/_template.md` | template of a new page |
| `docs/commands/README.md` | these conventions |

Every command of the catalog has exactly one page, and every page belongs to a
command of the catalog.

## 2. Front matter

A page starts with a YAML front matter block:

```yaml
---
command: replace
group: core
summary: Replace text in files or in the found text.
since: 0.1.0
---
```

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `command` | full command name; equal to the file name without `.md` |
| `group` | group of the command in the catalog |
| `summary` | equal to the `summary` of the command in the catalog |
| `since` | version of Danaco Nurt that introduced the command |

## 3. Sections

The sections appear in this order, with these headings. Sections marked
"generated" are written by the generator from the catalog and are checked, not
edited.

| Heading | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `# <command>` | title: the command name | front matter |
| `## Synopsis` | the forms of the command in variant A, one per line | generated |
| `## Description` | what the command does, in a few paragraphs; behaviour on empty input; how targets are computed | written |
| `## Parameters` | table: name, type, default, description; required parameters first | generated, descriptions may be extended |
| `## Input and output` | accepted and produced record kinds, per form | generated |
| `## Effect` | category, effect, reversibility and its conditions, external programs, journal behaviour | generated, notes written |
| `## Examples` | at least three examples executed by the build (section 4) | written |
| `## Errors` | error codes the command reports with their typical fix | written |
| `## Related` | related commands and guides | written |

A parameter description in the page may be longer than the catalog
`summary`, but must not contradict it. A page may add a `## Notes` section
before `## Examples` for platform differences.

## 4. Examples

Every page has at least three examples. Each example is a fenced block with
the info string `nurt example`, written in variant A of the syntax, optionally
followed by a block with the info string `fs-before` and a block with the
info string `text expected`:

````markdown
Replace a call in one file:

```nurt example
replace "oldName(" "newName(" in: ["/home/user/app/a.go"] occurrence: 1
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/a.go", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "x := oldName(1)\n" }
] }
```

```text expected
1 file changed, 1 replacement
```
````

| Block | Rule |
|---|---|
| `nurt example` | one program; it must parse, bind against the catalog and run |
| `fs-before` | optional snapshot of the virtual file system before the example, in the format `nurt-fs-snapshot/1`; without it the example runs on an empty file system |
| `text expected` | optional fragment that must appear in the text result of the example |

The sentence before an example says what it does. Examples use the paths
`/home/user/…` and `C:/Users/user/…` and the host `example.com`; they never
depend on the machine that builds them. The first three examples of a page are
the examples shown by `help <command>`; `help <command> examples: N` shows
more.

## 5. Documentation layers generated from the pages

| Layer | Content taken from the catalog | Content taken from the page |
|---|---|---|
| 1, core description for the model | name, positional parameters, defaults, enumeration values, summary | the first example of selected core commands |
| 2, group description | the same for the commands of the group | the first example of selected commands |
| 3, guides | command names only | none; guides are separate documents |
| 4, built-in help (`help <command>`) | synopsis, parameters with defaults, input and output, effect | the first three examples, `## Errors`, `## Related` |
| 5, reference (`nurt help --format man\|html\|markdown`) | everything | the whole page |

Reading any layer is optional; no command requires its documentation to be
read before it runs.

## 6. Checks

The build fails when:

1. a command of the catalog has no page, or a page has no command;
2. the front matter differs from the catalog (`command`, `group`, `summary`);
3. a generated section differs from the text generated from the catalog;
4. a page has fewer than three `nurt example` blocks;
5. an example does not parse, does not bind, fails to run on the virtual file
   system, or its result does not contain the `text expected` fragment;
6. a parameter or command name mentioned in backticks does not exist in the
   catalog.

## 7. Style

Pages are written in English, in the present tense and the impersonal style
of reference documentation ("`insert` adds text before or after …"), without tutorial
narrative. Commands, parameters, values and record fields are
written in backticks. Lines are wrapped at about 80 characters, except tables
and code.

title: accounts.create
text:
# accounts.create

## Synopsis

```text
accounts.create <name> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`accounts.create` creates a user account with `useradd` on Linux, `sysadminctl` on macOS and `net user` on Windows. The account is read first: an existing name is `E_EXISTS`. `groups` lists the groups other than the primary one, `create_home: false` or `system: true` leaves the home directory out. The report records the state after the change (`uid`, `shell`, `home`, `groups`, `comment`, `locked`) as the `after` of the target `account:<name>`.

Rights: the command accepts `privilege`; write `privilege: elevated` when the account that runs Nurt is not the administrator. A program that fails for lack of rights ends the command with `E_PERMISSION`, and `privilege: auto` repeats it once elevated. An elevated entry is undone by the same elevated process.

`undo` runs `accounts.remove name: "<name>" keep_home: true`; the home directory is kept.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `text` | required | Account name. |
| `uid` | `int` | none | Numeric identifier; the system chooses one when omitted. |
| `shell` | `text` | none | Login shell. |
| `home` | `text` | none | Home directory. |
| `groups` | `list<text>` | none | Groups other than the primary one. |
| `comment` | `text` | none | Comment or full name. |
| `system` | `bool` | `false` | Create a system account without a home directory. |
| `create_home` | `bool` | `true` | Create the home directory. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `system_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | Undo removes the account and keeps its home directory. |
| External use | `system_program`: `useradd`, `sysadminctl`, `net`; Accounts are created with useradd on Linux, sysadminctl on macOS and net user on Windows. |

## Examples

Create an account with a shell and a group.

```nurt example
accounts.create "deploy" shell: "/bin/bash" groups: ["docker"] privilege: elevated
```

Create a system account without a home directory.

```nurt example
accounts.create "svc-backup" system: true privilege: elevated
```

Create an account with a fixed identifier and a comment.

```nurt example
accounts.create "ann" uid: 2001 comment: "Ann Smith" privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_EXISTS` | The account exists. | Use `accounts.modify`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | The name or a text starts with `-`, is empty or holds a control character, `:` or `/`. | Give a valid name. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The account lacks the rights of the administrator. | Add `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The system program of the command is not installed. | Install the program named in the message. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The system program ended with an error. | Read the end of the error output in the message. |

## Related

`accounts.modify`, `accounts.remove`, `groups.create`, `accounts`.

title: accounts
text:
# accounts

## Synopsis

```text
accounts [name: value]...
```

## Description

`accounts` lists the local user accounts and groups as `account` records.
Users come first, in the order of the account database, followed by groups.

| Field | Users | Groups |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UID; on Windows the security identifier | GID; on Windows the security identifier |
| `groups` | primary group, then the groups that list the user as a member | members |
| `home`, `shell` | home directory and login shell | not set |
| `full_name` | first part of the comment field; on Windows the full name | not set |
| `disabled` | locked password on Linux; `UF_ACCOUNTDISABLE` on Windows | not set |
| `last_login` | last logon on Windows | not set |
| `system` | account of the operating system | group of the operating system |

| System | Source | `system` |
|---|---|---|
| Linux | user and group databases of the system library, including every configured source | identifier below `UID_MIN` of `/etc/login.defs`, 1000 when unset |
| macOS | user and group databases of the system library; the directory service supplies the local accounts | identifier below 500, or a name starting with `_` |
| Windows | local accounts and local groups | relative identifier below 1000; built-in groups |

`nobody`, `nogroup` and `nfsnobody` are system accounts on every system. On
Linux `disabled` comes from `/etc/shadow`: an account whose password field
starts with `!` or is `*` is disabled. When the file cannot be read,
`disabled` is not set and the report carries one `permission_denied_skipped`
note. macOS does not report `disabled`. Domain accounts on Windows are not
listed.

`name` selects the account or group with that name, compared
case-sensitively on Linux and macOS and regardless of case on Windows.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `enum(user\|group\|all)` | `all` | Users, groups or both. |
| `name` | `text` | none | Only the account or group with this name. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `account` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

List the accounts of people:

```nurt example
accounts kind: user |> filter not system
```

```text expected
kind: user
system: false
```

Show the members of one group:

```nurt example
accounts kind: group name: "docker" |> select groups
```

List the disabled accounts:

```nurt example
accounts kind: user |> filter disabled
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_TYPE` | `kind` is not a listed value, or `name` is not text. | Use `user`, `group` or `all`, and a text name. |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | The account database refuses access. | Run the console as an administrator. |
| `E_IO` | The account database cannot be read. | Check that `/etc/passwd` and `/etc/group` exist. |

## Related

`host`, `processes`, `open_files`.

title: accounts.modify
text:
# accounts.modify

## Synopsis

```text
accounts.modify <name> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`accounts.modify` changes the login shell, the home directory, the groups, the comment or the lock state of an account. `groups` is the complete list of groups other than the primary one. A call that gives the values the account already has changes nothing and reports `unchanged`. The report records the whole state before and after, so that `undo` restores the fields that changed.

Rights: the command accepts `privilege`; write `privilege: elevated` when the account that runs Nurt is not the administrator. A program that fails for lack of rights ends the command with `E_PERMISSION`, and `privilege: auto` repeats it once elevated. An elevated entry is undone by the same elevated process.

`undo` runs `accounts.modify` with the recorded values of the fields that changed.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `text` | required | Account name. |
| `shell` | `text` | none | New login shell. |
| `home` | `text` | none | New home directory. |
| `groups` | `list<text>` | none | Complete list of groups other than the primary one. |
| `comment` | `text` | none | New comment or full name. |
| `lock` | `bool` | none | Lock the account when true and unlock it when false. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `system_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | Undo restores the recorded values of the fields that changed. |
| External use | `system_program`: `usermod`, `dscl`, `net`; Accounts are changed with usermod on Linux, dscl on macOS and net user on Windows. |

## Examples

Change the shell of an account.

```nurt example
accounts.modify "deploy" shell: "/bin/zsh" privilege: elevated
```

Lock an account.

```nurt example
accounts.modify "ann" lock: true privilege: elevated
```

Replace the groups of an account.

```nurt example
accounts.modify "deploy" groups: ["docker", "wheel"] comment: "Deploy user" privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The account does not exist. | Create it with `accounts.create`. |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | No field to change was given. | Give at least one of `shell`, `home`, `groups`, `comment`, `lock`. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The account lacks the rights of the administrator. | Add `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The system program of the command is not installed. | Install the program named in the message. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The system program ended with an error. | Read the end of the error output in the message. |

## Related

`accounts.create`, `accounts.remove`, `accounts`.

title: accounts.password
text:
# accounts.password

## Synopsis

```text
accounts.password <name> <value>
```

## Description

`accounts.password` sets the password of an account. `value` is a secret parameter: it is masked in the journal, the report and the printed tree, it is written to the standard input of `chpasswd` on Linux and to an environment variable of `Set-LocalUser` on Windows, and it never appears in an argument list of Linux programs. On macOS `dscl -passwd` takes the value as an argument. The previous password is not recorded, so the change is irreversible and the report says so.

Rights: the command accepts `privilege`; write `privilege: elevated` when the account that runs Nurt is not the administrator. A program that fails for lack of rights ends the command with `E_PERMISSION`, and `privilege: auto` repeats it once elevated. An elevated entry is undone by the same elevated process.

A password is irreversible: `undo` reports that no inverse exists.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `text` | required | Account name. |
| `value` | `text` | required | New password; masked in the journal and the report. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `system_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | The previous password is not recorded. |
| External use | `system_program`: `chpasswd`, `dscl`, `powershell`; The password is passed to chpasswd on its standard input on Linux, and in an environment variable of Set-LocalUser on Windows. |

## Examples

Set a password.

```nurt example
accounts.password "deploy" "correct horse battery" privilege: elevated
```

Set a password with the named parameter.

```nurt example
accounts.password name: "ann" value: "s3cret" privilege: elevated
```

Set a password and check the account afterwards.

```nurt example
accounts.password "ann" "s3cret" privilege: elevated |> select target
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The account does not exist. | Create it with `accounts.create`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | The password holds a control character. | Use another password. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The account lacks the rights of the administrator. | Add `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The system program of the command is not installed. | Install the program named in the message. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The system program ended with an error. | Read the end of the error output in the message. |

## Related

`accounts.create`, `accounts.modify`.

title: accounts.remove
text:
# accounts.remove

## Synopsis

```text
accounts.remove <name> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`accounts.remove` removes an account with `userdel` on Linux, `sysadminctl` on macOS and `net user` on Windows. The home directory is not deleted by the system program: unless `keep_home` is true it is removed through the journal, so `undo` brings it back with its content. The account with identifier 0 is never removed. The report records the whole state of the account before the change.

Rights: the command accepts `privilege`; write `privilege: elevated` when the account that runs Nurt is not the administrator. A program that fails for lack of rights ends the command with `E_PERMISSION`, and `privilege: auto` repeats it once elevated. An elevated entry is undone by the same elevated process.

`undo` runs `accounts.create` with the recorded identifier, shell, home, groups and comment (`create_home: false`), then `accounts.modify` for a locked account; the journal restores the home directory.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `text` | required | Account name. |
| `keep_home` | `bool` | `false` | Keep the home directory; otherwise it is removed through the journal. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `system_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | Undo creates the account again with its identifier, shell, groups and comment; the home directory returns with the journal. |
| External use | `system_program`: `userdel`, `sysadminctl`, `net`; Accounts are removed with userdel on Linux, sysadminctl on macOS and net user on Windows. |

## Examples

Remove an account and its home directory.

```nurt example
accounts.remove "olduser" privilege: elevated
```

Remove an account and keep the home directory.

```nurt example
accounts.remove "olduser" keep_home: true privilege: elevated
```

Run the removal with elevated rights; adding the call parameter `preview: true` shows the effect first.

```nurt example
accounts.remove "olduser" privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The account does not exist. | Check the name with `accounts`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | The account is the superuser. | The superuser cannot be removed. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The account lacks the rights of the administrator. | Add `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The system program of the command is not installed. | Install the program named in the message. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The system program ended with an error. | Read the end of the error output in the message. |

## Related

`accounts.create`, `accounts.modify`, `accounts`.

title: analyze.check
text:
# analyze.check

## Synopsis

```text
analyze.check <path>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

Runs the analyzers configured in the project and the built-in analyses, merges
their findings and returns the verdict as an `analysis` header followed by
`finding` records. The analysis is stored and can be read again with
`analyze.show`.

Analyzers are detected from configuration files (`tsconfig.json`, ESLint,
Biome, Prettier, `pyproject.toml`, `ruff.toml`, `mypy.ini`, `go.mod`,
`Cargo.toml`) and run with machine-readable output. A program installed in
`node_modules/.bin` is used before the program on the search path. A check
whose tool is not installed has the status `missing` and produces the note
`tool_missing`; the command does not fail.

Complexity and duplication are computed from the data of the code service.
Without the service both checks have the status `missing`.

The verdict is `passed: false` when a finding has the severity of `fail_on` or
a higher one. `min_severity` and `max_findings` limit the returned findings
only; the counts and the verdict cover all findings.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `list<path>` | none | Files or directories to check. |
| `changed_only` | `bool` | `false` | Only files changed in the repository. |
| `checks` | `list<enum(types\|lint\|format\|complexity\|duplication)>` | none | Checks to run; all available checks when omitted. |
| `include_tests` | `bool` | `true` | Include test files. |
| `complexity_max` | `int` | `15` | Highest cyclomatic complexity accepted. |
| `fail_on` | `enum(error\|warning)` | `error` | Lowest severity that fails the verdict. |
| `min_severity` | `enum(error\|warning\|info)` | `info` | Lowest severity of findings returned. |
| `max_findings` | `int` | `100` | Maximum number of findings returned. |
| `sample_lines` | `int` | `5` | Maximum number of source lines shown with each finding. |
| `wait` | `duration` | `3s` | Time to wait before the analysis continues in the background as a job. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `analysis`, `finding`, `job` |

No input. Output: one `analysis` record, then `finding` records ordered by
severity, check, file and line. A job record is returned when the analysis
continues in the background.

The field `duplication_percent` of the `analysis` record holds the share of
lines of code in the analysed files that belong to a duplicated block, in
both copies, in percent with one decimal. A line counts once however many
blocks cover it. The field is empty when the duplication check did not run.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `run` |
| Effect | `process` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `user_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | Files changed by the analysis programs are reversible when their previous content was preserved; effects outside the file system are irreversible. |

## Examples

Check the whole project.

```nurt example
analyze.check
```

Check changed files for errors and warnings.

```nurt example
analyze.check changed_only: true fail_on: warning
```

Run only the complexity check with a lower threshold.

```nurt example
analyze.check checks: ["complexity"] complexity_max: 10
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_ARG` | Unknown check or `fail_on` value. | Use a value from the parameter table. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | `changed_only` without a repository query service. | Run with `changed_only: false`. |
| `E_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND` | An analyzer program could not be started. | Install the tool or fix its path. |

## Related

`analyze.show`, `analyze.format`, `analyze.tools`.

title: analyze.format
text:
# analyze.format

## Synopsis

```text
analyze.format <path>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

Finds the files that the configured formatters would change, then runs the
formatters on exactly those files. The formatters are Prettier, Biome, Ruff,
`gofmt` and `rustfmt`. The set of files is determined before any formatter
starts: each formatter is first run in its check mode on the requested files.

The result lists the files and shows up to `sample_lines` changed lines per
file as `-old` and `+new` lines.

Files changed outside the determined set are detected as for `run`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `list<path>` | none | Files or directories to format. |
| `changed_only` | `bool` | `false` | Only files changed in the repository. |
| `sample_lines` | `int` | `12` | Maximum number of changed lines shown per file, from 1 to 200. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

No input. Output: an effect report with one change per formatted file.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `process` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `user_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | The previous content of every file passed to the formatter is kept in the journal. |

## Examples

Format files changed in the repository.

```nurt example
analyze.format changed_only: true
```

Format one directory and show more changed lines.

```nurt example
analyze.format "src" sample_lines: 40
```

Format two directories.

```nurt example
analyze.format "src" "tests"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_SPAWN` | A formatter ended with a failure. | Run `analyze.check checks: ["format"]` and fix the reported syntax errors. |
| `E_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND` | A formatter program could not be started. | Install the formatter or fix its path. |

## Related

`analyze.check`, `analyze.tools`.

title: analyze.show
text:
# analyze.show

## Synopsis

```text
analyze.show [<analysis_id>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

Returns the stored `analysis` header and the findings of an analysis made by
`analyze.check`. Without `analysis_id` the latest analysis is used. Findings
are filtered by check, by file (a path that contains the given text) and by
severity, then paged with `offset` and `max_findings`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `analysis_id` | `text` | the latest analysis | Earlier analysis. |
| `check` | `text` | none | Only findings of this check. |
| `file` | `path` | none | Only findings in this file. |
| `offset` | `int` | none | Number of findings to skip. |
| `min_severity` | `enum(error\|warning\|info)` | `info` | Lowest severity of findings returned. |
| `max_findings` | `int` | `100` | Maximum number of findings returned. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `finding` |

No input. Output: the `analysis` header and `finding` records.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Show the findings of the latest analysis.

```nurt example
analyze.show
```

Show lint errors of one analysis in one file.

```nurt example
analyze.show "an-3" check: "lint" file: "src/app.py" min_severity: error
```

Show the second page of findings.

```nurt example
analyze.show offset: 100
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_UNKNOWN_ANALYSIS` | No stored analysis has the identifier; the error lists candidates. | Use an identifier from the candidates or run `analyze.check`. |

## Related

`analyze.check`.

# analyze.tools

## Synopsis

```text
analyze.tools <path>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

Lists one `analyze_tool` record for every analyzer and formatter that the
project configuration selects: TypeScript (`tsc`, ESLint, Biome, Prettier),
Python (Ruff, mypy), Go (`go vet`, `gofmt`) and Rust (Clippy, `rustfmt`).
Detection uses configuration files and the extensions of the files in scope.
A program installed in `node_modules/.bin` is preferred to the program on the

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |

| `path` | `list<path>` | none | Files or directories to inspect. |
| `changed_only` | `bool` | `false` | Only languages of files changed in the repository. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `analyze_tool` |

No input. Output: `analyze_tool` records with `tool`, `language`, `check`,
`found`, `version`, `config` and `command`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

List the tools of the project.

```nurt example
analyze.tools
```

List the tools for changed files.

```nurt example
analyze.tools changed_only: true
```

```nurt example
analyze.tools "services/api"
```

|---|---|---|

## Related

`analyze.check`, `analyze.format`.

title: archive.create
text:
# archive.create

## Synopsis

```text
entry |> archive.create <to> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`archive.create` writes a new archive `to` with the files, directories and
links named by the input `entry` records, for example the records of `find`
or `list`. A directory adds its whole tree. An entry given more than once,
such as a directory and the files `find` lists inside it, is stored once.

The name of a member is the path of the entry relative to `base`. Without
`base` it is the `relative` field of the record, which `find` and `list`
set, otherwise the name of the entry. An entry outside `base` is an error;
the entry `base` itself adds its content without a member of its own.

Members are stored in byte order of their names, with the permissions and
modification times of the files and without account names, so the same tree
always produces the same archive. Symbolic links are stored as links; with
`follow_links: true` the files and directories they lead to are stored
instead, and a link that leads back into a directory being stored is skipped
and reported with `link_loop_skipped`. Devices, FIFOs and other special
files are skipped and reported with `special_file`.

`format: auto` selects the format from the extension of `to`: `.zip`,
`.jar`, `.whl`, `.apk`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz` or `.tgz`, `.tar.zst` or `.tzst`,
`.tar.xz` or `.txz`, `.tar.bz2` or `.tbz2`, `.7z`. `level` is the compression
level of the format: 0 to 9 for zip (0 stores members uncompressed) and 7z,
and the range of the stream algorithm for compressed tar (gzip, xz and bzip2
0 to 9, zstd 1 to 22). A 7z archive is assembled in memory and is limited to
1 GiB.

An empty input creates an empty archive.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | `path` | required | Archive file to create. |
| `format` | `enum(auto\|zip\|tar\|tar_gz\|tar_zst\|tar_xz\|tar_bz2\|seven_zip)` | `auto` | Archive format; auto selects it from the file extension. |
| `base` | `path` | none | Directory that entry names in the archive are relative to. |
| `level` | `int` | none | Compression level of the format. |
| `follow_links` | `bool` | `false` | Store the targets of symbolic links instead of the links. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `entry` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Archive the build output of an application with names starting at `dist`:

```nurt example
find "/srv/app/dist" |> archive.create "/srv/out/dist.zip" base: "/srv/app"
```

```text expected
effect archive.create  /srv/out/dist.zip  files: 2  directories: 1
```

Archive the entries of a directory as a gzip-compressed tar archive:

```nurt example
list "/srv/app" |> archive.create "/srv/out/app.tar.gz"
```

Archive the sources as a zstd-compressed tar archive at a high level:

```nurt example
find "/srv/app/src" depth: 0 |> archive.create "/srv/out/app.bin" format: tar_zst level: 19
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_EXISTS` | `to` exists | Remove it first or choose another name. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | the directory of `to` or an input entry does not exist, or a followed link is dangling | Check the paths. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | the format cannot be told from the extension of `to`, `level` is outside the range of the format, an entry lies outside `base`, or a name is not valid Unicode | Set `format`, correct `level` or `base`, or rename the entry. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` | the value of `format` is unknown | Use one of the listed values. |
| `E_STALE` | an input file changed while it was stored, or `to` was created after the plan | Run the command again. |
| `E_LIMIT` | a 7z archive exceeds the in-memory limit | Create a zip or tar archive instead. |
| `E_TYPE` | an input record has no `path` field | Pass records of files. |

## Related

`archive.list` lists the members of the new archive; `archive.extract`
extracts it; `compress` compresses single files.

title: archive.extract
text:
# archive.extract

## Synopsis

```text
archive.extract <path> into: <path> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`archive.extract` extracts the members of the archive `path` into the
directory `into`, which is created with its missing parents when it does not
exist. The format is recognised from the content of the file, as by
`archive.list`.

Before anything is written, every member path and link target is checked. A
member is not extracted, and is reported with the notable entry
`archive_path_escape`, when its path:

- contains a `..` component, or a component of only dots and spaces;
- is absolute, starts with a drive letter or contains `\`;
- passes through a symbolic link created by the same archive, or through an
  existing symbolic link inside `into`;
- is a symbolic link whose target is absolute or leads outside `into`;
- is a hard link to a file that is not extracted from the same archive.

With `allow_outside: true` these members are extracted at the path stored in
the archive, relative to `into`, and still reported. A member whose name is
empty, contains NUL or is not valid UTF-8 is never extracted. Devices, FIFOs
and other special files are never extracted and are reported with
`special_file`.

`only` selects members by their path in the archive, with the pattern rules
of `archive.list`. `strip_components` removes leading components from member
paths and hard link targets; a member left without components is skipped.
When several members have the same destination, the last one is extracted.

An existing regular file is replaced, kept or reported as an error according
to `on_conflict`. An existing directory receives the content of the archive.
An existing entry of another type than the member is kept with
`on_conflict: skip` and is an error otherwise; a symbolic link with the same
target as the member is left unchanged.

Regular files receive the permissions stored in the archive; the set-user-id
and set-group-id bits are kept only when `preserve_permissions: true` is given
explicitly and the process runs as `root`, and are dropped otherwise, so that
an archive extracted by an unprivileged process or without that option never
creates a privileged program. With `preserve_permissions: false` the sticky bit
and the write permission of the group and others are dropped as well. A replaced file keeps
its own permissions. Directories always grant the account full access, so
that their content can be written. Files receive the time they are written as
their modification time.

The extracted size and the ratio of the extracted size to the size of the
archive are limited (1 TiB, and a ratio of 1000 above 64 MiB, so that an archive
of 300 KiB that declares 300 MiB is refused with `E_LIMIT`); an archive that
declares more fails before anything is written.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | Archive file. |
| `into` | `path` | required | Directory to extract into; created when missing. |
| `only` | `glob` | none | Only entries whose path matches this pattern. |
| `strip_components` | `int` | `0` | Number of leading path components removed from entry paths. |
| `on_conflict` | `enum(overwrite\|skip\|error)` | `overwrite` | Behaviour when a target file already exists. |
| `preserve_permissions` | `bool` | `true` | Apply the permissions stored in the archive. |
| `allow_outside` | `bool` | `false` | Extract entries whose resolved path lies outside the target directory. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

Notable entries: `archive_path_escape` for every rejected or, with
`allow_outside`, extracted escaping member, with the member as
`archive:<archive>!/<member>` and the reason (`parent_component`,
`absolute`, `drive_letter`, `backslash`, `invalid_name`, `link_outside`,
`through_link`, `hard_link_outside`); `special_file` for special files;
`overwrote_existing` with the number of replaced files.

## Examples

Extract a compressed tar archive into a new directory:

```nurt example
archive.extract "/srv/dl/data.tar.gz" into: "/srv/data"
```

```text expected
effect archive.extract  files: 2  directories: 2  bytes: 18
```

Extract the Markdown files of a release without its top directory:

```nurt example
archive.extract "/home/user/dl/project-1.2.zip" into: "/home/user/docs" only: "*.md" strip_components: 1
```

Extract a release over an installation and keep the files that exist there:

```nurt example
archive.extract "/srv/dl/release.tar" into: "/srv/app" on_conflict: skip
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | `path` does not exist | Check the path. |
| `E_FORMAT` | the file is not an archive of a supported format, or the archive is damaged | Check the file. |
| `E_ENCRYPTED` | a selected member is encrypted | Decrypt the archive with its own tool, or exclude the member with `only`. |
| `E_LIMIT` | the declared extracted size or compression ratio exceeds the limit | Check the archive; it may be a decompression bomb. |
| `E_EXISTS` | a target exists and `on_conflict` is `error`, an existing entry has another type than the member, or `into` is not a directory | Set `on_conflict`, remove the entry, or choose another `into`. |
| `E_STALE` | the archive or a target changed after the plan | Run the command again. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `strip_components` is negative or `only` is not a valid pattern | Correct the value. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` | the value of `on_conflict` is unknown | Use one of the listed values. |
| `E_PATH_RELATIVE` | a path is relative and no base directory is set | Give an absolute path or set the `base` option. |

## Related

`archive.list` shows the members before extraction; `archive.create`
creates an archive; `undo` reverts an extraction.

title: archive.list
text:
# archive.list

## Synopsis

```text
archive.list <path> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`archive.list` produces one `archive_entry` record for every member of the
archive `path`, in the order of the archive. The format is recognised from
the content of the file, not from its name: zip (including jar, whl and apk),
tar, tar compressed with gzip, zstd, xz, bzip2 or lz4, and 7z.

Every record carries the archive, the member path with `/` separators, the
name, the type (`file`, `directory`, `link` or `other`), the size after
extraction, the size in the archive when the format records it per member,
the modification time, the permissions in octal, the target of a link, the
compression method, whether the content is encrypted, the CRC-32 checksum
when the format records it, and the format of the archive. Paths and names
are in NFC; a name stored with bytes that are not valid UTF-8 is shown with
U+FFFD in their place.

`glob` selects members by path. A pattern without `/` is matched against the
last component of the member path, a pattern with `/` against the whole
path; `*` and `?` do not match `/`, `**` matches any number of components.

A compressed tar archive and a solid 7z archive are decoded from the start,
so their members are collected before the first record is produced. An empty
archive produces no records.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | Archive file. |
| `glob` | `glob` | none | Only entries whose path matches this pattern. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `archive_entry` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

List the members of a zip archive:

```nurt example
archive.list "/home/user/dl/site.zip"
```

```text expected
css           directory
css/site.css  file  4 B
index.html    file  13 B
```

List only the Rust sources of a compressed tar archive:

```nurt example
archive.list "/home/user/dl/src.tar.gz" glob: "*.rs"
```

List a zstd-compressed tar archive whose name has no archive extension; the
`format` field of the records is `tar_zst`:

```nurt example
archive.list "/home/user/dl/backup.bin"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | `path` does not exist | Check the path. |
| `E_FORMAT` | the file is not an archive of a supported format, or the archive is damaged | Check the file; use `decompress` for a compressed file that holds no tar archive. |
| `E_ENCRYPTED` | the header of a 7z archive is encrypted | Decrypt the archive with its own tool first. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `glob` is not a valid pattern | Correct the pattern. |
| `E_LIMIT` | the archive has more members than the record limit | Select fewer members with `glob`. |
| `E_PATH_RELATIVE` | `path` is relative and no base directory is set | Give an absolute path or set the `base` option. |

## Related

`archive.extract` extracts an archive; `archive.create` creates one;
`decompress` decompresses a single compressed file.

title: assert
text:
# assert

## Synopsis

```text
any |> assert (count: <range> | paths: <range> | exit_code: <range> | all: <expression> | any: <expression> | empty: <bool> | contains: <text> | if_match: <text>)
```

## Description

`assert` reads the whole input, checks exactly one condition and passes the
records on unchanged, with their header and order, when the condition holds.
When it does not hold, the program stops with `E_ASSERT`; the error carries
`expected`, `actual` and a `sample` of up to five records or paths.

| Condition | Holds when |
|---|---|
| `count` | the number of records is in the range |
| `paths` | the number of distinct `path` values is in the range |
| `exit_code` | every record has an `exit_code` in the range; fails when no program ran |
| `all` | the expression is `true` for every record |
| `any` | the expression is `true` for at least one record |
| `empty` | the input has no records (`true`) or has records (`false`) |
| `contains` | a text field of a record contains the text |
| `if_match` | every input record has the given `etag`; fails without input |

Before an effect (stage `3`) a failed assertion changes nothing. After an
effect (stage `5a`), for example after `run`, the effect stays, the report is
complete and the error has the stage `5a`; only `verify` rolls an effect
back.

A range is written as `5`, `1..5`, `40..` or `..9`; both bounds are included.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | `range` | one of `condition` | Expected number of records. |
| `paths` | `range` | one of `condition` | Expected number of distinct paths. |
| `exit_code` | `range` | one of `condition` | Expected exit code of the programs run. |
| `all` | `expression` | one of `condition` | Condition that every record meets. |
| `any` | `expression` | one of `condition` | Condition that at least one record meets. |
| `empty` | `bool` | one of `condition` | Whether there are no records. |
| `contains` | `text` | one of `condition` | Text that the records contain. |
| `if_match` | `text` | one of `condition` | Expected etag of the input file. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `any` | `same` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `check` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Check that a search found exactly two files before they are changed:

```nurt example
search /oldName\(/ "/home/user/project/src" |> assert paths: 2
```

Stop when the number of files differs from the expected one:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" glob: "*.md" |> assert count: 2
```

Check the exit code of a program after it ran:

```nurt example
run ["go", "test", "./..."] cwd: "/home/user/project" |> assert exit_code: 0
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_ASSERT` | the condition does not hold; `expected`, `actual` and `sample` describe it | correct the input or the expected value |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | no condition is given | give one of the parameters |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | more than one condition is given; `fix` lists each alone | keep one condition per `assert`, chain several stages |
| `E_TYPE` | a condition has a value of another type, or `all`/`any` gives a value other than `bool` | use the type of the parameter |

## Related

`verify`, `count`, `filter`.

title: attributes
text:
# attributes

## Synopsis

```text
attributes <path>... [name: value]...
entry |> attributes [name: value]...
```

## Description

`attributes` changes the metadata of the given entries, or of the input
entries in the stage form. At least one change is required. Every target must
exist; a missing target fails the call before anything is changed.

The plan step reads every target and computes its change from the current
state. A target whose metadata already has the requested values is left out
and reported as `unchanged`. In the stage form an input entry carrying an
`etag` is checked against the current state; a changed entry fails with
`E_STALE`.

A link given as a target is resolved: the change applies to the entry the
link points to, and a link to a missing entry fails with `E_NOT_FOUND`. With
`recursive: true` the entries below a directory are changed as well; links
below it are neither followed nor changed.

With an empty input the call changes nothing and reports `nothing_matched`.

| Parameter | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | permission bits | permission bits | only the read-only attribute, from the write permission of the account; the change has the flag `acl_unchanged` |
| `owner`, `group` | account and group ids | account and group ids | `E_UNSUPPORTED` |
| `acl` | POSIX access ACL | `E_UNSUPPORTED` | `E_UNSUPPORTED` |
| `readonly` | `true` removes every write permission, `false` adds the write permission of the account | as Linux | read-only attribute |
| `hidden` | follows the name; a different value gives the flag `hidden_unsupported` | as Linux | hidden attribute |
| `created` | not settable; the flag `created_unsupported` | birth time | creation time |
| `xattrs` | extended attributes | extended attributes | `E_UNSUPPORTED` |

A flag names a requested element that the system could not apply. It appears
in the `flags` field of the change, or in the detail of the `unchanged`
entry when nothing else changed.

Changing the account of a file needs administrator rights; a call by another
account fails with `E_PRIVILEGE` before anything is changed.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `list<path>` | required | Entries to change in the source form. |
| `mode` | `text` | none | Permissions, such as "0644" or "u+x". |
| `owner` | `text` | none | Account of the file. |
| `group` | `text` | none | Group of the file. |
| `acl` | `list<map<any>>` | none | Access control entries. |
| `readonly` | `bool` | none | Read-only attribute. |
| `hidden` | `bool` | none | Hidden attribute. |
| `modified` | `instant` | none | Modification time. |
| `accessed` | `instant` | none | Access time. |
| `created` | `instant` | none | Creation time. |
| `xattrs` | `map<text>` | none | Extended attributes to set. |
| `recursive` | `bool` | `false` | Apply to the content of directories. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `none` | `effect` |
| `stage` | `entry` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Make a script executable for the account of the file:

```nurt example
attributes "/home/user/run.sh" mode: "u+x"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/run.sh", "type": "file", "mode": "0644", "content_utf8": "content\n" }
] }
```

Restrict a file to its account and set its modification time:

```nurt example
attributes "/home/user/notes.txt" mode: "0600" modified: "2026-01-31T12:00:00Z"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/notes.txt", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "content\n" }
] }
```

Remove the write permission of the group and others in a whole tree:

```nurt example
attributes "/home/user/site" mode: "go-w" recursive: true
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/site", "type": "dir", "mode": "0777" },
  { "path": "/home/user/site/index.html", "type": "file", "mode": "0777", "content_utf8": "content\n" },
  { "path": "/home/user/site/css/main.css", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "content\n" }
] }
```

Make the files found by `find` read-only:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/site" type: file |> attributes readonly: true
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/site/index.html", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "content\n" },
  { "path": "/home/user/site/css/main.css", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "content\n" }
] }
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | no change was requested | give at least one of `mode`, `owner`, `group`, `acl`, `readonly`, `hidden`, `modified`, `accessed`, `created`, `xattrs` |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | a mode, time, account, group or ACL entry is not valid | use the forms in the parameter table |
| `E_TYPE` | a parameter has a value of another type | pass texts to `xattrs` and maps to `acl` |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | a target or the entry a link points to does not exist | check the path |
| `E_STALE` | an input entry changed since it was read | read the entries again |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | changing the account of a file needs administrator rights | run as an administrator or leave `owner` out |
| `E_PERMISSION` | the system refused the change | check the account of the file and the permissions of its directory |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | the system or volume has no form for a requested element | see the table in Notes |

## Related

`info`, `create`, `copy`, `undo`.

title: clock.ntp
text:
# clock.ntp

## Synopsis

```text
clock.ntp <state>
```

## Description

`clock.ntp` switches synchronisation with network time on or off: `timedatectl set-ntp` on Linux, `systemsetup -setusingnetworktime` on macOS and the service `w32time` on Windows. A state that the system already has changes nothing. `undo` restores the previous state.

The previous value is read before the change and recorded as the target `clock:ntp`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | `enum(on\|off)` | required | Synchronise the clock with network time or not. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | `undo` restores the previous state. |
| External use | `system_program`: `timedatectl`, `systemsetup`, `tzutil`, `date`, `powershell`; The clock is read and set through timedatectl, systemsetup, tzutil, date and, on Windows, PowerShell for the time service. |

## Examples

Switch network time on.

```nurt example
clock.ntp on privilege: elevated
```

Switch network time off.

```nurt example
clock.ntp off privilege: elevated
```

Switch network time off before setting the clock by hand.

```nurt example
clock.ntp state: off privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `state` is neither `on` nor `off`. | Write `on` or `off`. |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | The program of the system refused the change for want of rights. | Repeat the call with `privilege: elevated`. |

## Related

`clock.timezone_set`, `clock.set`.

title: clock.set
text:
# clock.set

## Synopsis

```text
clock.set <time>
```

## Description

`clock.set` sets the date and time of the clock to an instant in UTC: `date -u -s` on Linux, `date -u` on macOS and `Set-Date` on Windows. Setting the time is irreversible: the previous reading is lost, so `undo` cannot restore it and the report lists the change as irreversible. A system with network time switched on corrects the clock again; switch it off first with `clock.ntp`.

The previous value is read before the change and recorded as the target `clock:time`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `time` | `instant` | required | New time; an instant in UTC. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | The previous reading of the clock cannot be restored. |
| External use | `system_program`: `timedatectl`, `systemsetup`, `tzutil`, `date`, `powershell`; The clock is read and set through timedatectl, systemsetup, tzutil, date and, on Windows, PowerShell for the time service. |

## Examples

Set the clock.

```nurt example
clock.set "2026-11-21T09:12:00Z" privilege: elevated
```

Set the clock to midnight UTC.

```nurt example
clock.set "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z" privilege: elevated
```

Set the clock to the last minute of the year.

```nurt example
clock.set "2026-12-31T23:59:00Z" privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_TYPE` | `time` is not an instant. | Write an instant such as `2026-11-21T09:12:00Z`. |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | The program of the system refused the change for want of rights. | Repeat the call with `privilege: elevated`. |

## Related

`clock.ntp`, `clock.timezone_set`.

title: clock.timezone_set
text:
# clock.timezone_set

## Synopsis

```text
clock.timezone_set <zone>
```

## Description

`clock.timezone_set` sets the time zone of the system: `timedatectl set-timezone` on Linux, `systemsetup -settimezone` on macOS and `tzutil /s` on Windows, where `zone` is a Windows identifier such as `W. Europe Standard Time`. A zone that the system already has changes nothing. `undo` sets the previous zone.

The previous value is read before the change and recorded as the target `clock:timezone`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zone` | `text` | required | Name of the time zone, for example Europe/Warsaw; on Windows the identifier such as W. Europe Standard Time. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | `undo` sets the previous time zone. |
| External use | `system_program`: `timedatectl`, `systemsetup`, `tzutil`, `date`, `powershell`; The clock is read and set through timedatectl, systemsetup, tzutil, date and, on Windows, PowerShell for the time service. |

## Examples

Set the time zone of the system.

```nurt example
clock.timezone_set "Europe/Warsaw" privilege: elevated
```

Use UTC.

```nurt example
clock.timezone_set "UTC" privilege: elevated
```

Set a Windows time zone.

```nurt example
clock.timezone_set "W. Europe Standard Time" privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `zone` is not a time zone name. | Write a name of the time zone database. |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | The program of the system refused the change for want of rights. | Repeat the call with `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The system does not know the zone. | List the zones with `timedatectl list-timezones`. |

## Related

`clock.ntp`, `clock.set`.

title: code.actions
text:
# code.actions

## Synopsis

```text
code.actions <path> line: <int> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Lists the code actions (quick fixes, refactorings, source actions) that the
language server offers for the lines `line` to `end_line` of `path`. The
range starts at `column` of the first line, or at its start, and ends at
the end of the last line. The diagnostics the server published for the
range are sent as the context of the request.

The command lists actions and applies none. Code actions are offered only
by a language server: without a server for the language the command fails
with `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING`, and a failure of the server is the error of the
command.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | Source file. |
| `line` | `int` | required | First line of the range, counted from 1. |
| `end_line` | `int` | none | Last line of the range. |
| `column` | `int` | none | Column within the first line, counted from 1. |
| `language` | `text` | `"auto"` | Programming language; auto detects it from the file extension. |
| `root` | `path` | detected from the location of the file | Project root for the language server. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `code_action` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `language_server` |
| Fallback | `builtin` |

## Examples

List the actions for one line.

```nurt example
code.actions "/srv/app/src/main.py" line: 14
```

List the refactorings offered for a block of lines.

```nurt example
code.actions "/srv/app/src/main.ts" line: 20 end_line: 34 |> filter kind == "refactor.extract"
```

List the quick fixes at an error.

```nurt example
code.actions "/srv/app/src/lib.rs" line: 52 column: 17 |> filter kind == "quickfix" |> select title
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `line` was not given. | Give `line`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `end_line` is before `line`, or the file has fewer lines than the range. | Give a range inside the file. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | No server is available for the language. | Install the server named by `fix`, or allow it in `code.servers_allow`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_FAILED` | The server failed. | See the message of the server. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The server gave no answer within `code.timeout`. | Raise `code.timeout`. |

## Related

`code.diagnostics`, `code.rename`, `replace`.

title: code.call_hierarchy
text:
# code.call_hierarchy

## Synopsis

```text
code.call_hierarchy <path> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Lists the functions that call the function at a position of `path` (or
named by `symbol`), the functions it calls, or both.

The language server answers first. Under `source: auto` without a usable
server, syntax analysis approximates the hierarchy: callers are the
functions and methods that contain a reference to the name in code, callees
are the functions of the project called in the body of the definition.
Calls of members (`object.name(...)`) are not callees of the syntax
analysis. The result then carries a `semantic_fallback` note with the
cause.

Each `reference` record is one caller or callee. Its `text` holds the
direction (`<-` for a caller, `->` for a callee), the kind, the qualified
name and, for more than one call, the number of calls (`x3`).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | Source file. |
| `line` | `int` | none | Line of the function, counted from 1. |
| `column` | `int` | none | Column of the function, counted from 1. |
| `symbol` | `text` | none | Function name, optionally qualified as Container.name, instead of a position. |
| `direction` | `enum(incoming\|outgoing\|both)` | `both` | Callers, callees or both. |
| `language` | `text` | `"auto"` | Programming language; auto detects it from the file extension. |
| `root` | `path` | detected from the location of the file | Project root for the language server. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `reference` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `language_server` |
| Fallback | `builtin` |

## Examples

List the callers of a function.

```nurt example
code.call_hierarchy "/srv/app/src/shapes.py" symbol: "scale" direction: incoming
```

```text expected
<- function total x2
```

List the functions called by a method.

```nurt example
code.call_hierarchy "/srv/app/src/cart.ts" symbol: "Cart.checkout" direction: outgoing
```

List callers and callees of the function at another line.

```nurt example
code.call_hierarchy "/srv/app/src/main.go" line: 42
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
