| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | Neither `line` nor `symbol` was given. | Give `line` or `symbol`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `direction` or `source` is not valid, or the file has fewer lines than `line`. | Check the parameters. |
| `E_SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND` | `symbol` has no definition in the file. | Check the name with `code.symbols`. |
| `E_SYMBOL_AMBIGUOUS` | `symbol` has several definitions in the file. | Qualify the name as `Container.name`. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE` | Syntax analysis is needed and no grammar is available for the file. | Give `language`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | `source: lsp` and no server is available for the language. | Install the server named by `fix`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_FAILED` | `source: lsp` and the server failed. | See the message of the server. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | `source: lsp` and the server gave no answer within `code.timeout`. | Raise `code.timeout`, or use `source: auto`. |

## Related

`code.references`, `code.definition`, `code.profile`.

title: code.definition
text:
# code.definition

## Synopsis

```text
code.definition <path> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Finds the definition of the identifier at `line` and `column` of `path`, or
of the definition named by `symbol` in `path`. A `symbol` may be qualified by
its container (`Circle.area`); a name with several definitions in the file
fails with `E_SYMBOL_AMBIGUOUS` and lists the candidates. Without `column`
the first identifier of the line is used.

The language server of the file answers first. Under `source: auto` a
missing, failing or slow server, or an empty answer, gives way to syntax
analysis: the definitions of the identifier in the file and then in the
files of the project in the same language. The result then carries a
`semantic_fallback` note with the cause. A cancelled request is never
replaced. Under `source: lsp` the answer of the server is final, also when
it is empty.

The project root is the nearest directory above the file that holds a
project marker (`pyproject.toml`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `go.mod`,
`Cargo.toml`, `compile_commands.json`, `.git`), or the directory of the
file.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | Source file. |
| `line` | `int` | none | Line of the symbol, counted from 1. |
| `column` | `int` | none | Column of the symbol, counted from 1. |
| `symbol` | `text` | none | Symbol name, optionally qualified as Container.name, instead of a position. |
| `language` | `text` | `"auto"` | Programming language; auto detects it from the file extension. |
| `root` | `path` | detected from the location of the file | Project root for the language server. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `symbol` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `language_server` |
| Fallback | `builtin` |

## Examples

Find the definition of the identifier at line 12, column 8.

```nurt example
code.definition "/srv/app/src/main.py" line: 12 column: 8
```

Find a method by its qualified name.

```nurt example
code.definition "/srv/app/src/shapes.py" symbol: "Circle.area"
```

Find the definition of the symbol at a column of a line.

```nurt example
code.definition "/srv/app/src/index.ts" line: 40 column: 15
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | Neither `line` nor `symbol` was given. | Give `line` or `symbol`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | The file has fewer lines than `line`, or `source` or `root` is not valid. | Check the position and the parameters. |
| `E_SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND` | `symbol` has no definition in the file. | Check the name with `code.symbols`, or give `line` and `column`. |
| `E_SYMBOL_AMBIGUOUS` | `symbol` has several definitions in the file; the samples list them. | Qualify the name as `Container.name`, or give `line` and `column`. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE` | Syntax analysis is needed and no grammar is available for the file. | Give `language`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | `source: lsp` and no server is available for the language. | Install the server named by `fix`, or allow it in `code.servers_allow`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_FAILED` | `source: lsp` and the server failed. | See the message, which ends with the last line the server wrote to standard error. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | `source: lsp` and the server gave no answer within `code.timeout`. | Raise `code.timeout`, or use `source: auto`. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The request was cancelled. | Run the command again. |

## Related

`code.references`, `code.type_definition`, `code.symbols`, `code.languages`.

title: code.diagnostics
text:
# code.diagnostics

## Synopsis

```text
code.diagnostics <path>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

Reports the errors and warnings of the given files. A directory stands for
the source files and structured documents below it, without `.git`,
`node_modules`, `__pycache__`, `venv` and `.venv`, up to
`code.index_max_files` files. With `changed: true` only the files changed in
the repository are checked: changes in the working tree and the index and
untracked files, limited to the given paths when there are any.

Each file is checked by its language server. A server that supports pull
diagnostics is asked; for the others the client opens the file and waits
until the server has published nothing for `code.diagnostics_quiet`
(1500 ms). Under `source: auto` a file without a usable server is checked
by syntax analysis: the grammar of its language or, for structured
documents (JSON, YAML, TOML and the other document formats), the parser of
the format. Each distinct cause of a fallback is reported once as a
`semantic_fallback` note.

Records are free of repetitions and ordered by severity, path, line and
column. For more than five files the command reports its progress.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `list<path>` | none | Files or directories to check. |
| `changed` | `bool` | `false` | Only files changed in the repository. |
| `severity` | `enum(error\|warning\|info\|hint)` | `hint` | Lowest severity reported. |
| `source` | `enum(auto\|lsp\|syntax)` | `auto` | Language server, syntax analysis, or the server when available. |
| `language` | `text` | `"auto"` | Programming language; auto detects it from file extensions. |
| `root` | `path` | detected from the location of the file | Project root for the language server. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `diagnostic` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `language_server` |
| Fallback | `builtin` |

## Examples

Check one file.

```nurt example
code.diagnostics "/srv/app/src/main.py"
```

Report the errors of a directory only.

```nurt example
code.diagnostics "/srv/app/src" severity: error
```

Check the files changed in the repository and list the files with errors.

```nurt example
code.diagnostics changed: true |> filter severity == "error" |> select path line message
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | No path was given and `changed` is `false`. | Give a path or `changed: true`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `severity` or `source` is not valid, or the start path of `changed: true` is not in a repository. | Check the parameters. |
| `E_ARG` | `changed: true` without a path and without a base directory. | Give a path inside the repository. |
| `E_LIMIT` | A file is larger than `code.file_bytes_max`. | Raise the limit or leave out the file. |
| `E_ENCODING` | A file is not UTF-8 text. | Convert the file to UTF-8. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | `source: lsp` and no server is available, or `changed: true` and repository queries are not available. | Install the server named by `fix`, or give the paths. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_FAILED` | `source: lsp` and the server failed. | See the message of the server. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | `source: lsp` and the server gave no answer within `code.timeout`. | Raise `code.timeout`, or use `source: auto`. |

## Related

`code.languages`, `validate`, configuration keys `code.diagnostics_quiet`,
`code.timeout`.

title: code.hover
text:
# code.hover

## Synopsis

```text
code.hover <path> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Shows the signature and the documentation of the identifier at a position
of `path`, or of the definition named by `symbol`.

The answer of the language server is shortened: the signature is the first
code block of the answer, with a signature written over several lines
joined into one line, and the documentation is the first sentence of the
remaining text. With `verbosity: detailed` in the request options the
documentation is the whole answer of the server.

Under `source: auto` without a usable server, or when the server has no
information, the definition is found by syntax analysis; the signature is
its declaration line and the documentation is the first sentence of the
docstring below the name or of the comment lines above the definition. The
result then carries a `semantic_fallback` note with the cause. Under
`source: lsp` a server without information gives no record.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | Source file. |
| `line` | `int` | none | Line of the symbol, counted from 1; required unless symbol is given. |
| `column` | `int` | none | Column of the symbol, counted from 1; required unless symbol is given. |
| `symbol` | `text` | none | Symbol name, optionally qualified as Container.name, instead of a position. |
| `language` | `text` | `"auto"` | Programming language; auto detects it from the file extension. |
| `root` | `path` | detected from the location of the file | Project root for the language server. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `hover` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `language_server` |
| Fallback | `builtin` |

## Examples

Show the signature of the function called at line 5.

```nurt example
code.hover "/srv/app/src/main.py" line: 5 column: 12
```

```text expected
signature: def scale(value) -> int
```

Show the signature and the documentation of a class.

```nurt example
code.hover "/srv/app/src/shapes.py" symbol: "Circle" |> select signature documentation
```

Read the documentation of a symbol by name.

```nurt example
code.hover "/srv/app/src/shapes.py" symbol: "scale"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | Neither `line` nor `symbol` was given. | Give `line` or `symbol`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | The file has fewer lines than `line`, or `source` is not valid. | Check the parameters. |
| `E_SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND` | `symbol` has no definition in the file. | Check the name with `code.symbols`. |
| `E_SYMBOL_AMBIGUOUS` | `symbol` has several definitions in the file. | Qualify the name as `Container.name`. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE` | Syntax analysis is needed and no grammar is available for the file. | Give `language`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | `source: lsp` and no server is available for the language. | Install the server named by `fix`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_FAILED` | `source: lsp` and the server failed. | See the message of the server. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | `source: lsp` and the server gave no answer within `code.timeout`. | Raise `code.timeout`, or use `source: auto`. |

## Related

`code.definition`, `code.symbols`, `code.outline`.

title: code.implementations
text:
# code.implementations

## Synopsis

```text
code.implementations <path> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Finds the implementations of the interface, trait or abstract method at a
position of `path`, or of the definition named by `symbol`, and the types
derived from a class.

The language server answers first. Under `source: auto` without a usable
server, or with an empty answer, syntax analysis lists the classes,
structures, interfaces and enumerations of the project whose declaration
names the identifier after `extends`, `implements` or `for`, after `impl`,
or in a list of base types. The result then carries a `semantic_fallback`
note with the cause. Syntax analysis does not follow aliases or imports
under another name.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | Source file. |
| `line` | `int` | none | Line of the symbol, counted from 1. |
| `column` | `int` | none | Column of the symbol, counted from 1. |
| `symbol` | `text` | none | Symbol name, optionally qualified as Container.name, instead of a position. |
| `language` | `text` | `"auto"` | Programming language; auto detects it from the file extension. |
| `root` | `path` | detected from the location of the file | Project root for the language server. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `symbol` |

The fields of the `symbol` record are described in `code.definition`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `language_server` |
| Fallback | `builtin` |

## Examples

List the classes that implement an interface.

```nurt example
code.implementations "/srv/app/src/repo.ts" symbol: "Repository"
```

List the implementations of a trait method at a position.

```nurt example
code.implementations "/srv/app/src/store.rs" line: 18 column: 8
```

List the derived classes with their files.

```nurt example
code.implementations "/srv/app/src/shapes.py" symbol: "Shape" |> select name path line
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | Neither `line` nor `symbol` was given. | Give `line` or `symbol`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | The file has fewer lines than `line`, or `source` is not valid. | Check the parameters. |
| `E_SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND` | `symbol` has no definition in the file. | Check the name with `code.symbols`. |
| `E_SYMBOL_AMBIGUOUS` | `symbol` has several definitions in the file. | Qualify the name as `Container.name`. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE` | Syntax analysis is needed and no grammar is available for the file. | Give `language`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | `source: lsp` and no server is available for the language. | Install the server named by `fix`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_FAILED` | `source: lsp` and the server failed. | See the message of the server. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | `source: lsp` and the server gave no answer within `code.timeout`. | Raise `code.timeout`, or use `source: auto`. |

## Related

`code.definition`, `code.type_definition`, `code.symbols`.

title: code.languages
text:
# code.languages

## Synopsis

```text
code.languages
```

## Description

Lists one `language` record for every language with a built-in grammar, in
the order of the grammar registry, followed by the languages that have only
a configured language server, in alphabetical order.

The server fields come from the pool of language servers. The command does
not start servers and does not wait for requests in progress, so it answers
while other commands use the servers. A server is reported as found when its
program is on `PATH` and `code.servers_allow` allows it. Without a server
pool, `server` gives the configured program and `server_found` is `false`.

## Parameters

The command has no parameters.

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `language` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

List every language.

```nurt example
code.languages
```

List the languages whose server is installed.

```nurt example
code.languages |> filter server_found
```

Show the running servers with their roots.

```nurt example
code.languages |> filter server_running |> select language server server_pid server_root
```

## Errors

The command reports no errors of its own.

## Related

`code.diagnostics`, `code.rename`, configuration keys `code.servers`,
`code.servers_allow`, `code.max_servers`.

title: code.outline
text:
# code.outline

## Synopsis

```text
code.outline <path> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Lists the symbols of one source file in source order, one `symbol` record
per definition; a container comes before the symbols it contains. The
`container` field gives the qualified name of the enclosing symbol, so
`depth` 0 selects the top-level symbols, 1 adds their members, and so on.

A file of a language with a built-in grammar is outlined by syntax analysis.
The language is detected from a modeline, the file name, the extension and
the shebang line, in this order. A file of another language is outlined by
its language server when one is available.

Local variables declared inside functions are not part of an outline.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | Source file. |
| `depth` | `int` | no limit | Maximum nesting depth of symbols. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `symbol` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Outline a file.

```nurt example
code.outline "src/server.py"
```

List the top-level symbols only.

```nurt example
code.outline "src/lib.rs" depth: 0
```

List the methods of one class.

```nurt example
code.outline "src/Cart.java" |> filter container == "Cart" and kind == "method"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `path` was not given. | Give `path`. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE` | The file has no built-in grammar and no language server is available. | Install the server for the language. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `depth` is negative. | Give a depth of 0 or more. |
| `E_LIMIT` | The file is larger than `code.file_bytes_max`. | Raise the limit. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The file does not exist. | Check the path. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_FAILED` | The language server of a language without a grammar failed. | See the message of the server. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The language server of a language without a grammar did not answer. | Raise `code.timeout`. |

## Related

`code.symbols`, `read view: outline`, `code.languages`.

title: code.profile
text:
# code.profile

## Synopsis

```text
code.profile <root> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Describes the project under `root` without running or changing anything in
it. The result is one `profile_entry` record per entry, grouped by section in
the order `languages`, `modules`, `entry_points`, `commands`,
`instructions`, `hotspots`, `manifests`, preceded by a header record.

| Section | Entries |
|---|---|
| `languages` | Languages of the files, by number of files. |
| `modules` | Directories holding a project manifest. |
| `entry_points` | Programs and libraries the project starts from: `main`, `module`, `bin` and `exports` of `package.json`, `[[bin]]` and `src/main.rs` of `Cargo.toml`, `[project.scripts]` of `pyproject.toml`, `cmd/<name>/main.go`, and files with conventional names such as `__main__.py`, `main.py`, `main.go` and `index.js`. |
| `commands` | Build, test and check commands of `package.json` scripts, `Cargo.toml`, `Makefile`, `justfile`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, `tox.ini`, `go.mod`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `build.gradle`, `build.gradle.kts`, `pom.xml`, `*.csproj`, `composer.json`, `Gemfile` and `deno.json`. |
| `instructions` | Files with instructions for contributors and tools (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and similar). |
| `hotspots` | Files with the most commits in the last `days` days, then files with uncommitted changes. Outside a repository, the most recently modified files. Dependency lock files and build output are left out. |
| `manifests` | Every manifest found. |

Every command and entry point names its origin: the manifest, followed by
the key or the line it was read from (`package.json:scripts.test`,
`Makefile:12`). Paths are absolute.

JSON and TOML manifests are read through the document service; without it,
JSON manifests are read directly and TOML manifests contribute only the
commands their presence implies, with a note in the report. History and
status come from the repository query service.

The profile is cached in the state directory. A cached profile is used while
it is younger than ten minutes, the repository is on the same commit, the
history period is the same and no manifest it was read from has changed.
Uncommitted changes are read on every call. `refresh: true` reads the tree
again.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `root` | `path` | required | Repository root. |
| `sections` | `list<enum(commands\|entry_points\|hotspots\|manifests\|languages\|modules\|instructions)>` | none | Sections to return; all when omitted. |
| `limit` | `int` | none | Maximum number of entries per section. |
| `days` | `int` | `90` | Days of history used for change hotspots. |
| `refresh` | `bool` | `false` | Rebuild the profile instead of using the cached one. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `profile_entry` |

The header record has the fields `root`, `revision` (commit, or null outside
a repository), `repository`, `files` (number of files listed), `truncated`
(the listing stopped at 50 000 files), `cached` and, for a cached profile,
`cache_age_ms`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Profile the project in `/srv/app`.

```nurt example
code.profile "/srv/app"
```

```text expected
section       name    command         origin
commands      build   npm run build   package.json:scripts.build
commands      test    npm run test    package.json:scripts.test
```

List the build and test commands only.

```nurt example
code.profile "/srv/app" sections: [commands]
```

Show the five files changed most often in the last 30 days.

```nurt example
code.profile "/srv/app" sections: [hotspots] days: 30 limit: 5 |> select name changes last_change
```

Read the profile again after a change of the build setup.

```nurt example
code.profile "/srv/app" refresh: true
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | `root` is not a directory. | Pass the root directory of a project. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `sections`, `limit` or `days` is out of range. | Use the values listed under Parameters. |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `root` is missing. | Pass the root directory. |

## Related

`code.languages`, `code.symbols`, `code.outline`, `git.log`.

title: code.references
text:
# code.references

## Synopsis

```text
code.references <path> [name: value]...
symbol |> code.references [name: value]...
```

## Description

Finds the references to the identifier at a position of `path`, or to the
definition named by `symbol`. In the stage form every input `symbol` record
is a target, at the position of its name.

The language server answers first. Under `source: auto` without a usable
server, syntax analysis finds the occurrences of the name in code in the
files of the project in the same language; occurrences in comments and
strings are not references. The result then carries a `semantic_fallback`
note with the cause.

Every reference has a role:

| Role | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `definition` | The definition of the symbol. |
| `import` | An import or include line. |
| `test` | A use in a test file (`tests/`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.go`, `*.spec.ts` and similar). |
| `reference` | Any other use. |

Records are free of repetitions and ordered by path, line and column; the
number of records of each role is the count of that role.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | Source file in the source form. |
| `line` | `int` | none | Line of the symbol, counted from 1. |
| `column` | `int` | none | Column of the symbol, counted from 1. |
| `symbol` | `text` | none | Symbol name, optionally qualified as Container.name, instead of a position. |
| `include_definition` | `bool` | `true` | Include the definition among the references. |
| `scope` | `enum(project\|file)` | `project` | Search the whole project or only the file. |
| `language` | `text` | `"auto"` | Programming language; auto detects it from the file extension. |
| `root` | `path` | detected from the location of the file | Project root for the language server. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `none` | `reference` |
| `stage` | `symbol` | `reference` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `language_server` |
| Fallback | `builtin` |

## Examples

Find every reference to a function.

```nurt example
code.references "/srv/app/src/shapes.py" symbol: "scale"
```

List the uses of a symbol in test files.

```nurt example
code.references "/srv/app/src/shapes.py" symbol: "scale" include_definition: false |> filter role == "test"
```

Find the references to every exported class of a directory.

```nurt example
code.symbols path: ["/srv/app/src"] kind: class exported_only: true |> code.references scope: project
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | Neither `line` nor `symbol` was given in the source form. | Give `line` or `symbol`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `scope`, `source` or the position is not valid. | Check the parameters. |
| `E_TYPE` | An input record is not a `symbol` record. | Pipe the output of `code.symbols` or `code.definition`. |
| `E_SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND` | `symbol` has no definition in the file. | Check the name with `code.symbols`. |
| `E_SYMBOL_AMBIGUOUS` | `symbol` has several definitions in the file. | Qualify the name as `Container.name`, or give `line` and `column`. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE` | Syntax analysis is needed and no grammar is available for the file. | Give `language`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | `source: lsp` and no server is available for the language. | Install the server named by `fix`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_FAILED` | `source: lsp` and the server failed. | See the message of the server. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | `source: lsp` and the server gave no answer within `code.timeout`. | Raise `code.timeout`, or use `source: auto`. |

## Related

`code.definition`, `code.call_hierarchy`, `code.rename`, `code.symbols`.

title: code.rename
text:
# code.rename

## Synopsis

```text
symbol |> code.rename <to> [name: value]...
code.rename <to> path: <path> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Renames one symbol and every reference to it. The source form addresses the
symbol by `path` with `line` and `column`, or by `symbol`, a name or a
qualified name such as `Parser.parse`. Without `column`, the first identifier
of `line` is used. The stage form renames each input `symbol` record.

The edits come from the language server of the language (`source: lsp`) or
from syntax analysis (`source: syntax`), which replaces the whole identifier
in code of the files of the same language family (TypeScript and JavaScript
form one family, C and C++ another). `source: auto` uses the server when one
is available and syntax analysis otherwise; a server that fails, times out
or returns no edits is reported as `semantic_fallback`. Occurrences in
comments and string literals are renamed only with `include_comments` and
`include_strings`.

The plan is checked before anything is written:

- an edit outside the scope is not applied and is reported as
  `outside_project` (outside `root` and `paths`) or `rename_incomplete`
  (another file under `scope: file`);
- a changed file that already uses the new name in code fails with
  `E_RENAME_CONFLICT`;
- syntax analysis that finds more than one definition of the name fails
  with `E_SYMBOL_AMBIGUOUS`, because every definition would be renamed;
- server edits that do more than replace the old name are listed in the
  `alarms` field of the plan summary.

The result holds one `rename_edit` record per edit and a `map` record with the
plan summary: `plan` (identifier), `from`, `to`, `source`, `server`,
`confidence` (`semantic` for server edits, `identifier` for syntax
analysis), `root`, `files`, `total`, `alarms` and `leftovers`.

Execution writes every file in one journal operation, together with the file
creations, renames and deletions requested by the server. A file changed
after it was read fails with `E_STALE` before anything is written. After the
change, syntax errors and language server errors of every written file are
compared with the errors before the change; a new error restores every file
and fails with `E_ROLLED_BACK`. With `check_references`, occurrences of the
old name left in code, comments, strings, documentation, configuration and
file names are reported as `references_left`; occurrences left in code of the
same language family are also reported as `rename_incomplete`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | `text` | required | New name of the symbol. |
| `path` | `path` | none | Source file of the symbol in the source form. |
| `line` | `int` | none | Line of the symbol in the source form, counted from 1. |
| `column` | `int` | none | Column of the symbol in the source form, counted from 1. |
| `symbol` | `text` | none | Symbol name, optionally qualified as Container.name, instead of a position. |
| `scope` | `enum(project\|file)` | `project` | Rename in the whole project or only in the file. |
| `paths` | `list<path>` | the project | Files and directories to rename in. |
| `include_comments` | `bool` | `false` | Also rename occurrences in comments. |
| `include_strings` | `bool` | `false` | Also rename occurrences in string literals. |
| `source` | `enum(auto\|lsp\|syntax)` | `auto` | Language server, syntax analysis with confidence, or the server when available. |
| `check_references` | `bool` | `true` | Report references to the old name left after the change. |
| `language` | `text` | `"auto"` | Programming language; auto detects it from the file extension. |
| `root` | `path` | detected from the location of the file | Project root for the language server. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `stage` | `symbol` | `effect` |
| `source` | `none` | `effect` |

The `effect` record has `kind: "code.rename"`, the changed files in
`changes`, the counters `files_modified`, `files_created`, `files_deleted`,
`files_renamed` and `replacements` in `summary`, and the codes of the
notable effects in `notable`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `language_server` |
| Reversibility conditions | All changed files are restored together by one undo. |
| Fallback | `builtin` |

## Examples

Rename the function `total` defined in `math.py`.

```nurt example
code.rename "sum_all" path: "/srv/app/src/math.py" symbol: "total"
```

Rename the symbol at line 12, column 5, also in comments.

```nurt example
code.rename "parse_header" path: "/srv/app/src/reader.py" line: 12 column: 5 include_comments: true
```

Rename a method found by name, with syntax analysis limited to one
directory.

```nurt example
code.symbols "loadConfig" path: ["/srv/app/src"] kind: method match: exact |> code.rename "readConfig" source: syntax paths: ["/srv/app/src"]
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `to` is not an identifier or equals the current name. | Give another name. |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | Neither `symbol` nor `line` was given. | Give `symbol`, or `line` and `column`. |
| `E_SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND` | No identifier at the position, no definition of `symbol`, or the server found nothing to rename. | Check the position or the name. |
| `E_SYMBOL_AMBIGUOUS` | `symbol` has several definitions in the file, or syntax analysis found several definitions of the name; `candidates` lists one call for each definition. | Give `line` and `column`, narrow `paths`, or use `source: lsp`. |
| `E_RENAME_CONFLICT` | The new name is already used in a changed file. | Choose another name. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE` | No grammar for the file and no server. | Give `language` or install the server. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | `source: lsp` and no server for the language. | Install the server or use `source: syntax`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_FAILED` | `source: lsp` and the server failed. | See the message of the server. |
| `E_STALE` | A file changed after the plan. | Run the rename again. |
| `E_ROLLED_BACK` | The rename introduced a new error; every file was restored. | Review the reported error. |
| `E_LIMIT` | More than 500 files would change, or a file exceeds `code.file_bytes_max`. | Narrow `paths` or raise the limit. |

## Related

`code.references`, `code.symbols`, `code.diagnostics`, `undo`,
`help skill: "refactoring"`.

title: code.symbols
text:
# code.symbols

## Synopsis

```text
code.symbols [<name>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

Lists the definitions whose names match `name` in the given files and
directories, one `symbol` record per definition.

With `source: auto` and a name, the language server of the project answers
first. When no server answers, without a name, and with `exported_only`, the
symbols come from syntax analysis with the built-in grammars, and a server
failure is reported as `semantic_fallback`.

Syntax analysis of a directory uses a symbol index kept in the state
directory. A later search reads only the files whose size or modification
time changed. The listing applies ignore files and skips version control,
dependency and cache directories. `.git`, `node_modules`, `__pycache__`,
`venv` and `.venv` are always skipped, as are files larger than
`code.file_bytes_max`. The index holds no more than `code.index_max_files`
files. When the limit is reached, the result is incomplete and the report
carries `source_unavailable`.

A directory search covers programming languages. Data and markup formats
(JSON, YAML, TOML, Markdown, HTML, CSS, XML) are searched when `language`
names them or when `path` names a file. Files without an extension are
searched when their shebang line or modeline names a language.

Names are ranked from 6 (same text) to 1 (the letters of the query appear in
order). Records are ordered by rank, then by path and position. Without a
name every symbol is listed in path and source order.

| Rank | Condition | Modes |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | same text | all |
| 5 | same text regardless of case; for `regex`, equal to the pattern | all |
| 4 | starts with the query, regardless of case | `prefix`, `substring`, `fuzzy` |
| 3 | contains the query, regardless of case | `substring`, `fuzzy` |
| 2 | the words of the query start words of the name in order; any `regex` match | `fuzzy`, `regex` |
| 1 | the letters and digits of the query appear in order | `fuzzy` |

Words are split at camelCase boundaries and at characters other than
letters and digits, so `getUserById`, `get_user_by_id` and `GetUserByID`
share the words `get`, `user`, `by`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `text \| regex \| list<text>` | none | Symbol name, pattern or names; all symbols when omitted. |
| `path` | `list<path>` | none | Files or directories to search. |
| `glob` | `glob` | `"**"` | Only files whose path matches this pattern. |
| `kind` | `enum(function\|method\|class\|struct\|interface\|enum\|variable\|constant\|field\|module\|type\|macro\|any)` | `any` | Kind of symbol. |
| `match` | `enum(exact\|prefix\|substring\|fuzzy\|regex)` | `fuzzy` | How the name is matched. |
| `language` | `text` | `"auto"` | Programming language; auto detects it from file extensions. |
| `source` | `enum(auto\|lsp\|syntax)` | `auto` | Language server, syntax analysis, or the server when available. |
| `with_signature` | `bool` | `false` | Include the signature of each symbol. |
| `with_references` | `bool` | `false` | Include the number of references to each symbol. |
| `exported_only` | `bool` | `false` | Only symbols visible outside their module. |
| `exclude` | `list<glob>` | `[]` | Paths to skip, in gitignore syntax. |
| `exclude_preset` | `list<enum(vcs\|deps\|build\|cache\|tests)>` | `[]` | Predefined groups of paths to skip, such as dependencies or test files. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `symbol` |

Visibility rules: Python, a name not starting with `_`; Go, a capitalized
name; Rust, a visibility modifier; JavaScript and TypeScript, an `export` at
top level; C and C++, not `static`; Java and C#, `public`; Kotlin, not
`private`, `protected` or `internal`; Swift, `public` or `open`; PHP, not
`private` or `protected`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| External use | `language_server`; Uses a language server when one is installed and syntax analysis otherwise; source selects the analysis explicitly. |

## Examples

Find a function by an abbreviation of its words.

```nurt example
code.symbols "getUser" kind: function
```

List the exported classes of a directory without test files.

```nurt example
code.symbols path: ["src"] kind: class exported_only: true exclude_preset: [tests]
```

Find the handlers with their signatures and reference counts from syntax analysis.

```nurt example
code.symbols /Handler$/ match: regex source: syntax with_signature: true with_references: true
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | Unknown `match`, `kind` or `exclude_preset` value, or an invalid glob. | Use a value listed under Parameters. |
| `E_REGEX` | The regular expression of `name` is not valid. | Correct the pattern. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE` | `language` names no known language, or the language of a file given in `path` is not known. | Check the names with `code.languages`. |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | `exported_only` with `source: lsp`: servers do not report visibility. | Use `source: syntax` or `auto`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | `source: lsp` without an available language server. | Install the server named by `fix`. |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | No `path` and no base directory. | Give `path`. |
| `E_LIMIT` | A file given in `path` is larger than `code.file_bytes_max`. | Raise the limit or give a directory. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | A path does not exist. | Check the path. |

## Related

`code.outline`, `code.definition`, `code.references`, `code.languages`,
configuration keys `code.index_max_files`, `code.file_bytes_max`.

title: code.type_definition
text:
# code.type_definition

## Synopsis

```text
code.type_definition <path> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Finds the definition of the type of the variable, parameter, field or
expression at a position of `path`, or of the definition named by `symbol`.

The type of a symbol is known only to a language server, so the command has
no syntax analysis: without a server for the language it fails with
`E_EXTERNAL_MISSING`, and a failure of the server is the error of the
command. `source: syntax` fails with `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` as well.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | Source file. |
| `line` | `int` | none | Line of the symbol, counted from 1. |
| `column` | `int` | none | Column of the symbol, counted from 1. |
| `symbol` | `text` | none | Symbol name, optionally qualified as Container.name, instead of a position. |
| `language` | `text` | `"auto"` | Programming language; auto detects it from the file extension. |
| `root` | `path` | detected from the location of the file | Project root for the language server. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `symbol` |

The fields of the `symbol` record are described in `code.definition`;
`source` is always `lsp`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `language_server` |
| Fallback | `builtin` |

## Examples

Find the type of the variable at a position.

```nurt example
code.type_definition "/srv/app/src/main.ts" line: 22 column: 9
```

Find the type of a field named by its container.

```nurt example
code.type_definition "/srv/app/src/model.py" symbol: "Order.customer"
```

Show the file and line of the type.

```nurt example
code.type_definition "/srv/app/src/main.ts" line: 22 column: 9 |> select name path line
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | Neither `line` nor `symbol` was given. | Give `line` or `symbol`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | The file has fewer lines than `line`, or `source` is not valid. | Check the parameters. |
| `E_SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND` | `symbol` has no definition in the file. | Check the name with `code.symbols`. |
| `E_SYMBOL_AMBIGUOUS` | `symbol` has several definitions in the file. | Qualify the name as `Container.name`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | No server is available for the language. | Install the server named by `fix`, or allow it in `code.servers_allow`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_FAILED` | The server failed. | See the message of the server. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The server gave no answer within `code.timeout`. | Raise `code.timeout`. |

## Related

`code.definition`, `code.hover`, `code.languages`.

title: compress
text:
# compress

## Synopsis

```text
compress <path>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

`compress` writes the compressed form of each file next to it. The name of the
output is the name of the file with the extension of the algorithm appended:
`.gz`, `.zst`, `.xz`, `.bz2` or `.lz4`. A name that already has the extension
is extended again, so `data.tar` becomes `data.tar.gz`.

Each file is a separate stream; to pack several files into one archive use
`archive.create`. Content is streamed into a staged file of the transaction,
so memory use does not depend on the size of the file. zstd and lz4 streams carry a checksum of the content.

With `keep: false` the sources are removed in the same transaction, after
every output has been written. A failure leaves the sources in place.

An output that exists fails with `E_EXISTS` before anything is changed; the
command never overwrites a file. In the stage form, records of directories
and other entries that are not regular files are skipped. A path given twice
is compressed once.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `list<path>` | none | Files to compress in the source form. |
| `algorithm` | `enum(gzip\|zstd\|xz\|bzip2\|lz4)` | `gzip` | Compression algorithm. |
| `keep` | `bool` | `true` | Keep the original files. |
| `level` | `int` | none | Compression level of the algorithm. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none`, `entry` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

Notable entries: `nothing_matched` for an empty input.

## Examples

Compress a log file with gzip and keep it.

```nurt example
compress "/srv/app/app.log"
```

```text expected
op 41  compress  ok
targets 1 file
  + /srv/app/app.log.gz
```

Compress two files with zstd at level 19 and remove the originals.

```nurt example
compress "/srv/app/a.csv" "/srv/app/b.csv" algorithm: zstd level: 19 keep: false
```

```text expected
op 42  compress  ok
targets 2 files
  + /srv/app/a.csv.zst
  + /srv/app/b.csv.zst
  - /srv/app/a.csv
  - /srv/app/b.csv
```

Compress the old logs of a directory with xz.

```nurt example
find "/srv/app/logs" glob: "*.log" type: file |> compress algorithm: xz
```

```text expected
op 43  compress  ok
targets 1 file
  + /srv/app/logs/2026-01.log.xz
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | The source form has no `path`. | Give the files to compress or pass `entry` records. |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | `path` is given in the stage form. | Remove `path`, or start the pipeline with `compress`. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` | `algorithm` names no supported algorithm. | Use one of `gzip`, `zstd`, `xz`, `bzip2`, `lz4`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `level` is outside the range of the algorithm (`problem: level_out_of_range`), or a path of the source form is not a regular file (`problem: not_a_file`). | Use a level of the range in the table; compress the files of a directory with `find ... type: file \|> compress`. |
| `E_EXISTS` | The output file exists (`problem: output_exists`). | Remove or rename the existing file. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | A file does not exist. | Check the path. |
| `E_STALE` | A source changed after the plan. | Repeat the call. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | A file cannot be read or the output cannot be written. | Check the permissions and the free space. |
| `E_IO` | A file cannot be read or the output cannot be written. | Check the permissions and the free space. |
| `E_NO_SPACE` | A file cannot be read or the output cannot be written. | Check the permissions and the free space. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The call was cancelled or reached its time limit. | Repeat the call with a longer `timeout`. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The call was cancelled or reached its time limit. | Repeat the call with a longer `timeout`. |

## Related

`decompress` reverses the command. `archive.create` packs several files into
one archive. `read ... decompress: auto` reads a compressed file without
writing the decompressed form.

title: convert
text:
# convert

## Synopsis

```text
convert <path>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

`convert` rewrites text files in another encoding, with other line endings
or with the byte order mark added or removed. At least one of `encoding`,
`line_ending` and `bom` must be given.

The encoding and the line endings of each file are detected as by `read`;
encodings other than UTF-8 and UTF-16 are recognised from the list of the
configuration key `text.legacy_encodings`. The whole conversion is checked
before any file changes: a character the target encoding cannot represent
fails with `E_ENCODING`, with the path, line and column of the character,
and no file is written. A file that already has the requested form is not
written and is reported as `unchanged`.

`line_ending` converts every line ending, also in files with mixed line
endings; a missing line ending at the end of the file stays missing. Without
`bom`, a file that keeps its encoding keeps its byte order mark, a file
converted to UTF-16 receives one, and a file converted to any other encoding
is written without one. A byte order mark exists only in UTF-8 and UTF-16.

In the source form every path must be a text file. In the stage form the
input `entry` records name the files; records of directories and of other
entries that are not regular files are skipped, and files with binary
content are skipped and counted in `binary_skipped`. A path given twice is
converted once.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `list<path>` | none | Files to convert in the source form. |
| `encoding` | `text` | none | Target encoding, such as utf-8 or windows-1250. |
| `line_ending` | `enum(lf\|crlf\|cr\|keep)` | `keep` | Target line ending, or keep to leave line endings unchanged. |
| `bom` | `bool` | none | Add or remove the byte order mark. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none`, `entry` | `effect` |

The `effect` record has one `change` per converted file with
`encoding_before`, `encoding_after`, `line_ending_before`,
`line_ending_after`, `bom_before`, `bom_after`, `size_before` and
`size_after`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

Notable entries: `encoding_changed` and `line_ending_changed` with the values
before and after in `detail`, `bom_changed` with `added` or `removed`,
`unchanged` for files already in the requested form, `binary_skipped` and
`nothing_matched` for an empty input.

## Examples

Convert a Windows-1250 file with CRLF line endings to UTF-8 with LF.

```nurt example
convert "/srv/legacy/notes.txt" encoding: "utf-8" line_ending: lf
```

```text expected
op 31  convert  ok
targets 1 file
  ~ /srv/legacy/notes.txt  windows-1250 -> utf-8, crlf -> lf
notable
  i encoding_changed  /srv/legacy/notes.txt  windows-1250 -> utf-8
  i line_ending_changed  /srv/legacy/notes.txt  crlf -> lf
```

Convert the line endings of the listed scripts to CRLF.

```nurt example
find "/srv/app/scripts" glob: "*.cmd" type: file |> convert line_ending: crlf
```

```text expected
op 32  convert  ok
targets 1 file
  ~ /srv/app/scripts/build.cmd  lf -> crlf
notable
  i line_ending_changed  /srv/app/scripts/build.cmd  lf -> crlf
  i unchanged  /srv/app/scripts/test.cmd
```

Remove the byte order mark of a CSV file.

```nurt example
convert "/srv/app/data.csv" bom: false
```

```text expected
op 33  convert  ok
targets 1 file
  ~ /srv/app/data.csv  bom removed
notable
  i bom_changed  /srv/app/data.csv  removed
```

Convert a file of the DOS code page 852, with `ibm852` in
`text.legacy_encodings`, to UTF-8.

```nurt example
convert "/srv/dos/menu.txt" encoding: "utf-8"
```

A character that Latin-2 cannot represent stops the conversion.

```nurt example
convert "/srv/app/notes.txt" encoding: "iso-8859-2"
```

```text expected
error E_ENCODING  stage 4  /srv/app/notes.txt:2:8
  character `→` (U+2192) at line 2, column 8 cannot be represented in `iso-8859-2`
  fix: convert "/srv/app/notes.txt" encoding: "utf-8"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | No `path` in the source form, or none of `encoding`, `line_ending` and `bom`. | Give the files and the form to convert to. |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | `path` is given in the stage form. | Remove `path`, or start the pipeline with `convert`. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` | `encoding` or `line_ending` has an unknown value. | Use a listed encoding or line ending. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `bom: true` for an encoding without a byte order mark (`problem: bom_not_supported`), or a path that is not a regular file (`problem: not_a_file`). | Remove `bom`, or convert the files of a directory with `find ... type: file \|> convert`. |
| `E_ENCODING` | A file is not valid in its detected encoding, or a character cannot be represented in the target encoding; `details` give `character`, `line`, `column` and `byte`. | Convert to `utf-8`, or remove the character. |
| `E_BINARY` | A path of the source form has binary content. | Give text files only. |
| `E_LIMIT` | A file is larger than the limit of text files. | Convert smaller files. |
| `E_STALE` | A file changed after the plan. | Repeat the call. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | A file cannot be read or written. | Check the path and its permissions. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | A file cannot be read or written. | Check the path and its permissions. |
| `E_IO` | A file cannot be read or written. | Check the path and its permissions. |

## Related

`read ... encoding:` reads a file in a given encoding. `write`, `replace`,
`insert` and `edit` keep the encoding and line endings of a file; `convert`
is the explicit way to change them. `undo` restores the previous content.

title: copy
text:
# copy

## Synopsis

```text
copy <from>... [<to>] (to: <path> | into: <path>) [name: value]...
entry |> copy [<to>] (to: <path> | into: <path>) [name: value]...
```

## Description

`copy` copies files, symbolic links, junctions and directory trees. The
source form takes the paths of `from`; the stage form takes `entry` records,
for example from `list` or `find`. `to` and `into` exclude each other, and
one of them is required.

`to` is the new path of the copy. When `to` names an existing directory, the
copy is placed inside it under the name of the source and the result reports
`to_is_dir`. `into` always names a directory that receives the copies; it is
created with its missing parents. Several sources need a directory: `into`,
or `to` naming an existing directory. `to` is evaluated per input record in
the stage form.

A directory is walked once, links not followed, and copied with its whole
content in one operation. An existing destination directory receives the
content of the source directory; conflicts are then decided per file. An
existing directory is never replaced by a file or a link, and a directory is
never copied over a file.

`on_conflict` decides what happens to an existing file or link at the
destination: `overwrite` replaces it, `skip` keeps it and leaves the source
out, `error` fails before anything changes. A symbolic link is copied as a
link with the same target; its target is not copied.

`preserve: true` keeps the permission bits of directories, except that a
directory whose user permissions lack read, write or search is created with
`rwx` for the user, because its content is copied into it afterwards; the
notable entry `attributes_changed` names the path and both modes. It also lets the
journal keep the times, permissions and extended attributes of files where
the file system supports them. `clone: auto` uses block clones when source
and destination share a volume that supports them, and a byte copy
otherwise; `clone: always` fails when block clones are not available, and
`clone: never` always copies the bytes.

An entry record with `etag` must still have that entity tag; a changed entry
fails with `E_STALE` before anything changes. Empty input copies nothing and
reports `nothing_matched`.

| Notable code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `to_is_dir` | `to` named an existing directory, which received the copy |
| `case_collision` | the destination differs from an existing name only in letter case on a volume that does not distinguish case |
| `nothing_matched` | the input had no entries |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | `list<path>` | required | Files and directories to copy in the source form. |
| `to` | `path` | one of `destination` | Target path; an existing directory receives the copy. |
| `into` | `path` | one of `destination` | Target directory, created when missing. |
| `on_conflict` | `enum(overwrite\|skip\|error)` | `overwrite` | Behaviour when the target file exists. |
| `preserve` | `bool` | `true` | Keep times, permissions and attributes. |
| `clone` | `enum(auto\|always\|never)` | `auto` | Use file system clones when available, always or never. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `none` | `effect` |
| `stage` | `entry` | `effect` |

The `effect` record has one `change` per created directory, copied file and
created link, with `from` set to the source. Its `summary` counts `files`,
`directories`, `links`, `overwritten` and `skipped`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Copy a file next to itself:

```nurt example
copy "/srv/app/config.toml" "/srv/app/config.toml.bak"
```

```text expected
copy: 1 target, files 1
```

Copy a directory tree into a new directory:

```nurt example
copy "/srv/app/src" into: "/backup/2026-11-22"
```

Copy found log files and keep copies that already exist:

```nurt example
find "/srv/app/logs" glob: "*.log" |> copy into: "/archive/logs" on_conflict: skip
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | no source, or neither `to` nor `into` | give `from` and a destination |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | both `to` and `into`, or several sources and `to` is not an existing directory | give one destination; use `into` for several sources |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | a source or the directory of `to` does not exist | check the path or use `into` |
| `E_EXISTS` | the target exists with `on_conflict: error`, is an existing directory, has another kind than the source, or two sources share one target | choose another destination or `on_conflict` value |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | a directory copied into itself, a source that is its own target, or `into` that is not a directory | choose a destination outside the source |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | `clone: always` without block clones, or a device, pipe or socket as a source | use `clone: auto`; exclude the special file |
| `E_STALE` | an input entry changed since it was read | read the entries again |
| `E_IN_USE` | Windows: a file is open in another process; the error lists the processes | close the file there |
| `E_PATH_RELATIVE` | a relative path without a base directory | give an absolute path or set `base` |

## Related

`move`, `rename`, `remove`, `create`, `find`, `list`.

title: count
text:
# count

## Synopsis

```text
any |> count
```

## Description

`count` reads the whole input and gives the number of records as an `int`.
The records are not held in memory. An empty input gives 0.

`count` counts file records before an effect and the records of an effect
after it (stage `5a`), for example the `exec` records of a program run.

## Parameters

The command has no parameters.

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `any` | `int` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `transform` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Count the files of a project:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> count
```

Counting the lines of an empty file gives 0:

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/empty.txt" |> count
```

Count the results of a program run:

```nurt example
run ["git", "status", "--short"] cwd: "/home/user/project" |> count
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_TYPE` | the input is a single value, not records | apply `count` to a stage that produces records |

## Related

`assert`, `summarize`, `group`.

title: create
text:
# create

## Synopsis

```text
create <path>... type: <enum(file|directory|link|junction|fifo|device)> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`create` creates one entry per path: an empty file, a directory, a symbolic
or hard link, a junction, a named pipe or a device node. `type` has no default. Missing parent
directories are created unless `parents` is `false`; each one is a target of
its own, and a directory named twice, as a path and as a parent, is created
once.

An existing entry of the requested kind is left as it is with `on_exists:
skip` and reported as `unchanged`, fails with `E_EXISTS` with `on_exists:
error`, and gets the current time as its access and modification time with
`on_exists: touch`. An existing entry of another kind always fails with
`E_EXISTS`.

A symbolic link stores `target` as written; a relative target is relative to
the directory of the link, and the target need not exist. `hard: true`
creates a hard link to the existing file `target`. A junction needs an
existing directory as its target and exists only on Windows.

With `temporary: true`, every `path` is a directory, and `create` makes one
file or directory with a unique name that starts with `nurt-` in each; without
`path`, in the temporary directory of the host. The `change` records of the
result hold the new paths.

`type: fifo` creates a named pipe (FIFO) with the permission bits of `mode`,
written in octal, for example `mode: "0660"` (without `mode` the default `0666` is reduced by the
umask; with `mode` the bits are set exactly, without following a link). `type: device` creates a device node and needs `kind: char` or
`kind: block`, `major` and `minor`; `mode` applies as for a pipe. Both exist
on Linux and macOS only; on Windows they fail with `E_OS_ONLY`, and for a
pipe the message points to the named pipes of the system, which are objects
of the `\\.\pipe\` namespace created by the program that serves them. A
device node needs `privilege: elevated`; without it the system refuses with
`E_PRIVILEGE`. An exact `mode` is set through `/proc/self/fd` on Linux; without `/proc` the command fails and removes the new node. Both are journaled as created files, and `undo` removes them.
`info` and `list` report such an entry with the type `fifo` or `device`;
a device node also reports `major` and `minor`. `kind`, `major`, `minor`
and `mode` cannot be combined with other types, and `temporary` cannot be
combined with `fifo` or `device`.

On Windows a symbolic link needs the privilege to create symbolic links or
developer mode; without it the command fails with `E_PRIVILEGE`, and a
junction is the alternative for directories.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `enum(file\|directory\|link\|junction\|fifo\|device)` | required | Kind of entry; there is no default. fifo (named pipe) and device (device node) exist on Linux and macOS; a device needs privilege elevated. |
| `path` | `list<path>` | none | Paths to create; with temporary, the directory of the new entry. |
| `target` | `text` | none | Target of a link or junction. |
| `hard` | `bool` | `false` | Create a hard link instead of a symbolic link. |
| `temporary` | `bool` | `false` | Create an entry with a unique name in the temporary directory. |
| `parents` | `bool` | `true` | Create missing parent directories. |
| `on_exists` | `enum(skip\|error\|touch)` | `skip` | Behaviour when the entry exists; touch updates its modification time. |
| `kind` | `enum(char\|block)` | none | Kind of device node for type device. |
| `major` | `int` | none | Major device number for type device. |
| `minor` | `int` | none | Minor device number for type device. |
| `mode` | `text` | none | Permission bits of a fifo or device node in octal, for example "0660"; the default is 0666 reduced by the umask. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Create a directory and its missing parent:

```nurt example
create "/home/user/app/build/cache" type: directory
```

Update the modification time of an existing file:

```nurt example
create "/home/user/notes.txt" type: file on_exists: touch
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/notes.txt", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "keep\n" }
] }
```

Point a link at a release directory:

```nurt example
create "/home/user/app/current" type: link target: "releases/v2"
```

Create an empty file with a unique name:

```nurt example
create "/home/user/tmp" type: file temporary: true
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `type` is missing, `path` is missing without `temporary`, a link has no `target`, or a device lacks `kind`, `major` or `minor` | give the missing parameter |
| `E_EXISTS` | the entry exists with `on_exists: error`, or exists as another kind | choose another path or `on_exists: skip` |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | `target` or `hard` with a type other than `link`, `kind`, `major` or `minor` with a type other than `device`, `mode` with a type other than `fifo` or `device`, `temporary` with a link, a fifo or a device, or a path given twice | remove the parameter |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `major` or `minor` exceeds the device number of the system (Linux: major up to 4095, minor up to 1048575; macOS: 255 and 16777215), or `mode` is not octal permission bits | give a valid value |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | a parent directory is missing and `parents` is `false`, or the target of a hard link or junction is missing | set `parents: true` or create the target |
| `E_OS_ONLY` | `type: junction` outside Windows, `type: fifo` or `type: device` on Windows | use `type: link`; on Windows create the named pipe in the program that serves it |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | Windows refuses to create a symbolic link, or a device node is created without `privilege: elevated` | enable developer mode, use a junction, or add `privilege: elevated` |

## Related

`write`, `copy`, `move`, `remove`, `attributes`, `list`.

title: decompress
text:
# decompress

## Synopsis

```text
decompress <path>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

`decompress` writes the decompressed form of each file next to it. The
algorithm (gzip, zstd, xz, bzip2 or lz4) is taken from the content of the
file; the name of the output is the name without the compression extension.
The extensions `.gz`, `.zst`, `.xz`, `.bz2`, `.lz4` are removed, and `.tgz`,
`.tzst`, `.txz`, `.tbz2` become `.tar`. Extensions are compared without regard
to case. A file whose name has none of these extensions fails with
`E_INVALID_VALUE`, because the output name cannot be derived; rename the
file first.

Streams made of several members or frames are decompressed to the
concatenation of the members. Content is streamed into a staged file of the
transaction, so memory use does not depend on the size of the file. The
output of one file is limited to 1 TiB; a stream that would produce more
fails with `E_LIMIT` and nothing is written.

With `keep: false` the compressed files are removed in the same transaction,
after every output has been written. A failure leaves them in place.

An output that exists fails with `E_EXISTS` before anything is changed; the
command never overwrites a file. In the stage form, records of directories
and other entries that are not regular files are skipped.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `list<path>` | none | Files to decompress in the source form. |
| `keep` | `bool` | `true` | Keep the compressed files. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none`, `entry` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

Notable entries: `nothing_matched` for an empty input.

## Examples

Decompress a gzip file and keep it.

```nurt example
decompress "/srv/app/app.log.gz"
```

```text expected
op 51  decompress  ok
targets 1 file
  + /srv/app/app.log
```

Decompress a zstd file and remove the compressed file.

```nurt example
decompress "/srv/app/data.csv.zst" keep: false
```

```text expected
op 52  decompress  ok
targets 1 file
  + /srv/app/data.csv
  - /srv/app/data.csv.zst
```

Decompress a compressed tar file to a tar file, then list its entries.

```nurt example
decompress "/srv/app/backup.tgz"
```

```text expected
op 53  decompress  ok
targets 1 file
  + /srv/app/backup.tar
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | The source form has no `path`. | Give the files to decompress or pass `entry` records. |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | `path` is given in the stage form. | Remove `path`, or start the pipeline with `decompress`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | The name has no compression extension (`problem: unknown_extension`), or a path of the source form is not a regular file (`problem: not_a_file`). | Rename the file to end in a compression extension. |
| `E_FORMAT` | The content is not gzip, zstd, xz, bzip2 or lz4 data (`problem: not_compressed`), or the stream is damaged or ends early. | Check the file or restore it from its source. |
| `E_LIMIT` | The decompressed output exceeds the limit (`problem: decompressed_size`). | Check that the file is not a compression bomb; read part of it with `read ... decompress: auto`. |
| `E_EXISTS` | The output file exists, or two sources have the same output name (`problem: output_exists`). | Remove or rename the existing file. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | A file does not exist. | Check the path. |
| `E_STALE` | A source changed after the plan. | Repeat the call. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | A file cannot be read or the output cannot be written. | Check the permissions and the free space. |
| `E_IO` | A file cannot be read or the output cannot be written. | Check the permissions and the free space. |
| `E_NO_SPACE` | A file cannot be read or the output cannot be written. | Check the permissions and the free space. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The call was cancelled or reached its time limit. | Repeat the call with a longer `timeout`. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The call was cancelled or reached its time limit. | Repeat the call with a longer `timeout`. |

## Related

`compress` reverses the command. `archive.extract` unpacks archives.
`read ... decompress: auto` reads a compressed file without writing the
decompressed form.

title: describe
text:
# describe

## Synopsis

```text
any |> describe
```

## Description

`describe` lists the fields of the records that reach it. It replaces the
inspection of an object with `Get-Member` and answers the question which
fields a following `filter`, `select` or `sort` can use.

The result has one `field_info` record per field:

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `field` | name of the field |
| `type` | language type of the values; `mixed` when the records hold values of different types in the field |
| `example` | the first value that is not `null` |
| `required` | `true` when every input record has the field |
| `records` | number of input records that have the field |

Fields appear in the order of their first occurrence, so the order of the
definition of the record kind is kept. Fields that are computed on request
(`hash`, `encoding`, `line_ending`, `mime`, `language`, `binary`, `lines`)
are listed only when the producing command computed them, and then show
`required: false` when some records lack them.

Empty input yields no records. Input that is a single value instead of
records fails with `E_TYPE`. The result is deterministic: the same input gives
the same records in the same order.

## Parameters

The command has no parameters.

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `any` | `field_info` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `transform` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

List the fields of the entries of a directory.

```nurt example
list "/home/user/app" |> describe
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app", "type": "dir" },
  { "path": "/home/user/app/a.go", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "package main\n" }
] }
```

```text expected
path
```

Show only the fields that not every record has.

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" glob: "**/*" |> describe |> filter required == false
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app", "type": "dir" },
  { "path": "/home/user/app/a.go", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "package main\n" }
] }
```

Show the fields of the matches of a search with their types.

```nurt example
search "main" "/home/user/app" |> describe |> select field type
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app", "type": "dir" },
  { "path": "/home/user/app/a.go", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "package main\n" }
] }
```

```text expected
column
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_TYPE` | the input is a single value, or `describe` is the first stage and has no records to describe | put a source before it, for example `list` |

## Related

`help`, `select`, `filter`, `summarize`.

title: diff
text:
# diff

## Synopsis

```text
diff <from> <to> [name: value]...
entry|content |> diff <against> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`diff` compares texts line by line and returns one `hunk` record per region
of change. For the same texts and number of context lines the hunks equal
those of GNU `diff -u`.

In the source form `from` is the old side and `to` the new side. Two files
give the hunks of their difference. Two directories are compared
recursively by relative path, in byte order of the paths: a file present
only in `to` is `added`, a file present only in `from` is `deleted`, and a
deleted file and an added file with the same non-empty content are reported
once as `renamed`. Links to regular files are compared as files; links to
directories are not followed. A file compared with a directory is compared
with the file of the same name in that directory.

In the stage form each input record is the new side and `against` is the old
side. An `entry` record names a file; a `content` record carries the text
itself, so a text read or changed earlier in the pipeline can be compared
without writing it. `against` is a file, a directory (each input file is
compared with the file of the same name in it, and an input directory with
the whole tree), or a named result whose records are matched to the input by
`path`; a named result of one record is compared with every input. An input
without a counterpart is `added`. Entries that are neither files nor
directories are skipped.

Files are decoded before the comparison, so files in different encodings are
compared by their characters, and the difference of encodings is reported as
`encoding_changed`. A carriage return belongs to the line, so lines with
`crlf` and `lf` endings differ unless `ignore_whitespace` is set. Files with
binary content are compared by content hash; a difference gives one record
with `binary: true` and no lines.

Equal inputs give no records.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | `path` | required | Old file in the source form. |
| `to` | `path` | required | New file in the source form. |
| `against` | `path \| stream<any>` | none | File or named result that the input is compared with in the stage form. |
| `context` | `int` | `3` | Lines of context around each change. |
| `ignore_whitespace` | `bool` | `false` | Ignore changes in whitespace. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `none` | `hunk` |
| `stage` | `entry`, `content` | `hunk` |

Fields of the `hunk` record:

An added or deleted empty file and a renamed file give one record without
lines.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Compare two versions of a configuration file.

```nurt example
diff "/srv/app/config.old.toml" "/srv/app/config.toml"
```

```text expected
--- /srv/app/config.old.toml
+++ /srv/app/config.toml
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 [server]
-timeout = 30
+timeout = 60
 port = 8080
```

Compare two release trees; the moved file is reported once as renamed.

```nurt example
diff "/srv/release/1.0" "/srv/release/1.1"
```

```text expected
added     /srv/release/1.1/CHANGELOG.md
deleted   /srv/release/1.0/NOTES.txt
modified  /srv/release/1.1/src/main.rs
renamed   /srv/release/1.0/src/util.rs -> /srv/release/1.1/src/run.rs
```

Compare the listed sources with the files of the same name in a copy, with
one line of context.

```nurt example
find "/srv/app/src" glob: "*.rs" type: file |> diff against: "/srv/app.orig/src" context: 1
```

Compare two scripts without regard to indentation and line endings.

```nurt example
diff "/srv/app/build.cmd" "/srv/app/build.new.cmd" ignore_whitespace: true
```

A response that leaves records out ends with the hint "more: next" and carries the field
`continuation`; the command `next` returns the next part without running the
command again.

```text
matched 140  shown 50  more: next
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `from` or `to` is missing in the source form, or `against` in the stage form. | Give both sides. |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | `against` is given in the source form, or `from` or `to` in the stage form. | Use the parameters of the form. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `context` is negative, or a path is neither a regular file nor a directory (`problem: not_a_file`). | Give zero or more lines, and files or directories. |
| `E_TYPE` | `against` is neither a path nor a named result of `entry` or `content` records, or a `content` record has no `text`. | Pass a path or the result of `read`. |
| `E_LIMIT` | A file is larger than the limit of text files. | Compare smaller files. |
| `E_ENCODING` | A file is not valid in its detected encoding. | Convert the file with `convert`. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | A file cannot be read. | Check the path and its permissions. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | A file cannot be read. | Check the path and its permissions. |
| `E_IO` | A file cannot be read. | Check the path and its permissions. |

## Related

`patch` applies a unified or git diff. `read ... since:` returns the
difference of a file against the version read earlier. `hash` compares files
by content without reading their lines.

title: disable
text:
# disable

## Synopsis

```text
service |> disable
```

## Description

`disable` stops each input service from starting automatically. On Linux the
unit file is disabled and the manager reloads its configuration; a masked unit
already counts as `disabled`. `before` and `after` hold the start type. A
running service keeps running; `stop` stops it.

Each input service is read before the action. A service whose start type is
already `disabled` is not passed to the manager; its effect record has
`before` equal to `after` and the notable code `unchanged`. For every other
service the operation is marked irreversible with `service_changed` before
the manager is asked to act. Services are processed in input order; an error
stops the processing of the remaining services.

**Privilege.** System units need the administrator: write `privilege: elevated` on the stage. `undo` of the entry enables the services again, when their start type before was `automatic`.

```nurt
services name: "cron" |> disable privilege: elevated
```

## Parameters

The command has no parameters.

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `service` | `effect` |

Each `effect` record holds `kind: "disable"`, `target` (`service:<name>`),
`action`, `before` and `after`. A preview shows the same records with
`status: planned` and the expected `after`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| External use | `system_program`: `launchctl`; On macOS services are disabled through the launchctl component of the operating system. |

## Examples

Disable one service:

```nurt example
services name: "cups" |> disable
```

Disable a service of the current account:

```nurt example
services name: "syncthing" scope: user |> disable
```

Disable the stopped services whose name starts with `legacy`:

```nurt example
services name: /^legacy/ state: "stopped" |> disable
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The service no longer exists. | Read the services again with `services`. |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | The manager refused the action; `required` names the privilege, `root` on Linux and `administrator` on Windows. Interactive authorization is never requested. | Run as an account with that privilege. |
| `E_SERVICE` | The manager reported an error; `os_code` and `os_message` hold the error of the manager. | Correct the cause named in `os_message`. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | The record comes from the manager of another system. | Read the services on this system with `services`. |
