| `E_CANCELLED` | The execution was cancelled. | None; the cancellation was requested by the caller. |

## Related

`services` produces the input records. `enable` makes a service start
automatically and `stop` stops it now. The `administration` group page lists the other
commands of the group.

title: disks.format
text:
# disks.format

## Synopsis

```text
disks.format <device> fs: <enum(ext4|xfs|btrfs|vfat|ntfs|exfat)> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`disks.format` creates a file system with `mkfs.<type>` on Linux, `diskutil eraseVolume` on macOS and `Format-Volume` on Windows. The change is irreversible. The preview and the report list the device, its partitions, file systems, mount points and the size of the data that is lost; a device with a mounted partition is refused with `E_IN_USE`. `fs` is `ext4`, `xfs`, `btrfs`, `vfat`, `ntfs` or `exfat` (macOS accepts `vfat` and `exfat`).

Rights: the command accepts `privilege`; write `privilege: elevated` when the account that runs Nurt is not the administrator. A program that fails for lack of rights ends the command with `E_PERMISSION`, and `privilege: auto` repeats it once elevated. An elevated entry is undone by the same elevated process.

A format is irreversible: the preview is the only safeguard.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | `text` | required | Partition or disk such as /dev/sdb1, or a drive letter such as D: on Windows. |
| `fs` | `enum(ext4\|xfs\|btrfs\|vfat\|ntfs\|exfat)` | required | File system. |
| `label` | `text` | none | Label of the file system. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `system_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | Irreversible; the preview lists the device, its partitions, file systems, mount points and the size of the data that is lost. |
| External use | `system_program`: `mkfs`, `lsblk`, `diskutil`, `powershell`; File systems are created with mkfs on Linux, diskutil on macOS and Format-Volume on Windows. |

## Examples

Run a format with elevated rights; adding the call parameter `preview: true` shows the effect first.

```nurt example
disks.format "/dev/sdb1" fs: ext4 label: "data" privilege: elevated
```

Format a partition.

```nurt example
disks.format "/dev/sdb1" fs: xfs label: "backup" privilege: elevated
```

Format a drive of Windows.

```nurt example
disks.format "D:" fs: ntfs label: "Data" privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_IN_USE` | A partition of the device is mounted. | Unmount it first. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | The device is not a block device or the file system is unknown. | Check the device with `disks`. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The account lacks the rights of the administrator. | Add `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The system program of the command is not installed. | Install the program named in the message. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The system program ended with an error. | Read the end of the error output in the message. |

## Related

`disks`, `disks.partition`, `unmount`.

title: disks
text:
# disks

## Synopsis

```text
disks [name: value]...
```

## Description

`disks` lists the mounted volumes of the host as `disk` records, ordered by
`mount`. Pseudo file systems of the kernel, such as `proc`, `sysfs`,
`cgroup2`, `devpts` and `autofs`, are not volumes and are left out. When
several file systems are mounted on the same point, only the visible one is
listed.

`type` selects volumes by kind. The kind of a volume follows the rules of the
journal space:

| `type` | Volumes |
|---|---|
| `network` | `nfs`, `nfs4`, `cifs`, `smb3`, `smbfs`, `sshfs`, `fuse.sshfs`, `9p`, `afs`, `afpfs`, `webdav`; on macOS every volume without `MNT_LOCAL`; on Windows `DRIVE_REMOTE` |
| `ram` | `tmpfs`, `ramfs`, `devtmpfs`; on Windows `DRIVE_RAMDISK` |
| `removable` | removable media and, on macOS, external devices |
| `fixed` | every other local volume, including the `overlay` file system of containers |
| `other` | file systems in user space other than the listed network file systems |

`ram` and `other` volumes appear only with `type: all`.

`total` is the capacity, `free` the space available to the account, and
`used` the capacity minus all free blocks, so `used` and `free` do not add up
to `total` on file systems that reserve blocks. `inodes_total` and
`inodes_free` are set on Linux and macOS for file systems that report them.
`options` holds the mount options on Linux.

| System | Volumes | Space | Removable media | Label |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Linux | `/proc/self/mountinfo` | `statvfs` | `removable` attribute of the block device | `/dev/disk/by-label` |
| macOS | `getmntinfo` | `statfs` | volume resource keys | volume name |
| Windows | drive letters | `GetDiskFreeSpaceExW` | `GetDriveTypeW` | `GetVolumeInformationW` |

On Windows `mount` is the drive root in canonical form, for example `C:/`. A
volume whose space cannot be read, for example an unreachable network share,
is left out; the report carries one `source_unavailable` note with the number
of such volumes.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `enum(all\|fixed\|removable\|network)` | `all` | Kind of volume. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `disk` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

List the network volumes:

```nurt example
disks type: network
```

List the removable media:

```nurt example
disks type: removable
```

List all mounted volumes:

```nurt example
disks
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `type` has a value outside the enumeration. | Use one of the listed values. |
| `E_IO` | The mount table cannot be read. | Check that `/proc` is mounted. |

## Related

`journal.space`, `host`, `list`.

title: disks.partition
text:
# disks.partition

## Synopsis

```text
disks.partition <device> action: <enum(create|delete|resize)> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`disks.partition` creates, deletes or resizes a partition with `parted` on Linux, `diskutil` on macOS and the storage cmdlets on Windows. The change is irreversible. The preview and the report list the device, its partitions with file systems, labels and mount points, and the size of the data that the change destroys; a partition that is mounted is refused with `E_IN_USE`. `device` is the disk (`/dev/sdb`, or the number of the disk on Windows); `number` selects the partition to delete or resize; a new partition starts at `start` (1 MiB by default) and takes `size` or the rest of the disk.

Rights: the command accepts `privilege`; write `privilege: elevated` when the account that runs Nurt is not the administrator. A program that fails for lack of rights ends the command with `E_PERMISSION`, and `privilege: auto` repeats it once elevated. An elevated entry is undone by the same elevated process.

A partition change is irreversible: the preview is the only safeguard.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | `text` | required | Disk device such as /dev/sdb, or the number of the disk on Windows. |
| `action` | `enum(create\|delete\|resize)` | required | Change to make. |
| `number` | `int` | none | Number of the partition to delete or resize. |
| `start` | `size` | none | Start of a new partition; 1 MiB when omitted. |
| `size` | `size` | none | Size of a new or resized partition; the rest of the disk when omitted for create. |
| `fs_type` | `text` | none | File system type hint of a new partition. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `system_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | Irreversible; the preview lists the device, its partitions, file systems, mount points and the size of the data that is lost. |
| External use | `system_program`: `parted`, `lsblk`, `diskutil`, `powershell`; Partitions are changed with parted on Linux, diskutil on macOS and the storage cmdlets on Windows. |

## Examples

Run the deletion of a partition with elevated rights; adding the call parameter `preview: true` shows the effect first.

```nurt example
disks.partition "/dev/sdb" action: delete number: 2 privilege: elevated
```

Create a partition of 10 GiB.

```nurt example
disks.partition "/dev/sdb" action: create size: 10gib privilege: elevated
```

Resize a partition.

```nurt example
disks.partition "/dev/sdb" action: resize number: 1 size: 20gib privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_IN_USE` | The partition is mounted. | Unmount it first. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The partition does not exist. | Check the number with `disks`. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The account lacks the rights of the administrator. | Add `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The system program of the command is not installed. | Install the program named in the message. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The system program ended with an error. | Read the end of the error output in the message. |

## Related

`disks`, `disks.format`, `unmount`.

title: distinct
text:
# distinct

## Synopsis

```text
any |> distinct <by>...
```

## Description

`distinct` keeps the first record of each distinct value of the fields in
`by` and adds the field `count` with the number of records that had this
value. Without `by`, records are distinct by their kind and all their fields.
Values compare by the total order of values.

The first occurrences keep their input order, so an order declared by the
source stays valid. `distinct` reads the whole input; the number of distinct
records is bounded by the record limit of the request. An empty input gives
an empty output.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `by` | `list<field>` | none | Fields that make records distinct; all fields when omitted. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `any` | `same` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `transform` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Keep one file per extension:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> distinct extension
```

Count repeated lines of a file:

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/words.txt" |> distinct text
```

List the files with matches once each:

```nurt example
search /error/ "/home/user/logs" |> select path |> distinct
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_UNKNOWN_FIELD` | a field is not in the records; `expected` lists their fields | use one of the listed fields |
| `E_LIMIT` | more distinct records than the limit | narrow the input first |

## Related

`group`, `select`, `sort`.

title: edit
text:
# edit

## Synopsis

```text
edit <path> changes: <list<map<any>>> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`edit` applies a list of changes to one text file as one operation: either
every change is applied or the file is not changed. A change is a map of one
of three kinds:

| Change | Keys | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| replacement | `replace` (text or regular expression), `with`, and optionally `occurrence`, `whole_word`, `whitespace`, `on_missing`, `expect` | replaces the matches of the pattern, as `replace` does |
| insertion | `insert` (text), and optionally `line` and `position` | inserts lines before or after `line`, or at the `start` or `end` of the file, as `insert` does |
| deletion | `delete_lines` (range or line number) | deletes the lines of the range |

Every change is located in the file as it was before the edit: line numbers
and matches of a change refer to the original text, never to the text left
by the changes listed before it. Insertions at the same place keep the order
of the list, and an insertion at the line where a deletion starts comes
before it, so `{delete_lines: a..b}` together with
`{insert: …, line: a, position: before}` replaces lines `a` to `b`. Changes
whose ranges overlap are rejected before anything is written.

`whitespace` and `on_missing` of the command apply to the replacements
without their own value. `expect` of the command applies to every
replacement without its own `expect`. A replacement that matches nothing
with `on_missing: skip` is reported as `nothing_matched` with its number. A
list of changes that leaves the text as it was writes nothing and is
reported as `unchanged`.

The file keeps its encoding, byte order mark and line endings; inserted and
replaced lines take the line endings of the file.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | File to change. |
| `changes` | `list<map<any>>` | required | Changes: replace and with, insert with line and position, or delete_lines. |
| `expect` | `range` | none | Expected number of replacements of each change. |
| `if_match` | `text` | none | Expected etag of the file. |
| `whitespace` | `enum(exact\|trailing\|indent\|normalize)` | `normalize` | Tolerance of whitespace differences. |
| `on_missing` | `enum(skip\|error)` | `skip` | Behaviour when a change matches nothing. |
| `validate` | `enum(off\|warn\|reject)` | `reject` | Roll back changes that add a new syntax error to a known format. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Change a value and add a line after it:

```nurt example
edit "/home/user/app/config.toml" changes: [{replace: "debug = true", with: "debug = false"}, {insert: "log = \"info\"", line: 2, position: after}]
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/config.toml", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "[server]\ndebug = true\nport = 8080\n" }
] }
```

Replace lines 2 to 4 with one line:

```nurt example
edit "/home/user/app/util.py" changes: [{delete_lines: 2..4}, {insert: "    return a + b", line: 2, position: before}]
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/util.py", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "def add(a, b):\n    total = a + b\n    print(total)\n    return total\n" }
] }
```

Raise the patch version when exactly one version line exists:

```nurt example
edit "/home/user/app/Cargo.toml" changes: [{replace: /version = "(\d+)\.(\d+)\.\d+"/, with: "version = \"$1.${2}.3\"", occurrence: 1}] expect: 1
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/Cargo.toml", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "version = \"1.4.2\"\nedition = \"2024\"\n" }
] }
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | a change has no or several kinds, an unknown key, or overlaps another change | correct the change or merge the overlapping changes |
| `E_OUT_OF_RANGE` | a line lies outside the file, or a replacement with `on_missing: error` names an occurrence above the number of its matches | give a line from 1 to the number of lines, or a smaller `occurrence` |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | a replacement has no `with`, or an insertion before or after a line has no `line` | add the key, or use `position: start` or `end` |
| `E_ASSERT` | the number of matches of a replacement is outside `expect` | extend the pattern, set `occurrence` or change `expect` |
| `E_NO_MATCH` | a replacement matches nothing and `on_missing` is `error` | read the current text and give an existing fragment |
| `E_REGEX` | a regular expression or a template is not valid | correct the pattern or the template |
| `E_STALE` | the file changed since it was read, or does not have the `if_match` tag | read the file again and repeat the edit |
| `E_ENCODING` | the encoding of the file cannot represent the new text | convert the file with `convert` first |
| `E_BINARY` | the file is binary | edit text files only |
| `E_ROLLED_BACK` | the edit added a syntax error and `validate` is `reject` | correct the changes or pass `validate: warn` |

## Related

`replace`, `insert`, `write`, `patch`, `read`.

title: enable
text:
# enable

## Synopsis

```text
service |> enable
```

## Description

`enable` makes each input service start automatically: at boot for system
services and at login for services of the current account. On Linux the unit
file is enabled and the manager reloads its configuration. `before` and
`after` hold the start type; a unit without an installation section keeps
`static`. The service is not started; `start` starts it.

Each input service is read before the action. A service whose start type is
already `automatic` is not passed to the manager; its effect record has
`before` equal to `after` and the notable code `unchanged`. For every other
service the operation is marked irreversible with `service_changed` before
the manager is asked to act. Services are processed in input order; an error
stops the processing of the remaining services.

**Privilege.** System units need the administrator: write `privilege: elevated` on the stage. `undo` of the entry disables the services again, when their start type before was `disabled`.

```nurt
services name: "cron" |> enable privilege: elevated
```

## Parameters

The command has no parameters.

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `service` | `effect` |

Each `effect` record holds `kind: "enable"`, `target` (`service:<name>`),
`action`, `before` and `after`. A preview shows the same records with
`status: planned` and the expected `after`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| External use | `system_program`: `launchctl`; On macOS services are enabled through the launchctl component of the operating system. |

## Examples

Enable one service:

```nurt example
services name: "cron" |> enable
```

Enable a service of the current account:

```nurt example
services name: "syncthing" scope: user |> enable
```

Enable the services whose name starts with `backup`:

```nurt example
services name: /^backup/ |> enable
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The service no longer exists. | Read the services again with `services`. |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | The manager refused the action; `required` names the privilege, `root` on Linux and `administrator` on Windows. Interactive authorization is never requested. | Run as an account with that privilege. |
| `E_SERVICE` | The manager reported an error, for example a masked unit; `os_code` and `os_message` hold the error of the manager. | Correct the cause named in `os_message`. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | The record comes from the manager of another system. | Read the services on this system with `services`. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The execution was cancelled. | None; the cancellation was requested by the caller. |

## Related

`services` produces the input records. `disable` stops a service from starting
automatically and `start` starts it now. The `administration` group page lists the
other commands of the group.

title: environment
text:
# environment

## Synopsis

```text
environment [<name>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

`environment` lists environment variables as `environment_variable` records
with `name`, `value` and `scope`. Values are listed as they are and are never
masked.

`name` selects variables. Text selects one variable by its name, compared
case-sensitively on Linux and macOS and regardless of case on Windows. A
pattern selects every variable whose name matches it.

| `scope` | Variables | Systems |
|---|---|---|
| `process` | environment of the console process | all |
| `user` | persistent variables of the account, `registry:/HKCU/Environment` | Windows |
| `machine` | persistent variables of the computer, `registry:/HKLM/SYSTEM/CurrentControlSet/Control/Session Manager/Environment` | Windows |

Persistent variables of type `REG_EXPAND_SZ` are listed without expanding
references such as `%USERPROFILE%`. A value that is not valid UTF-8 is listed
with the invalid bytes replaced by U+FFFD; the report carries one
`encoding_changed` note for each such variable.

Linux and macOS have no persistent variables outside profile files, so
`scope: user` and `scope: machine` fail there with `E_OS_ONLY`. Persistent
variables are changed with `write` and `replace`: on Windows by writing the
registry value, which also notifies running programs with
`WM_SETTINGCHANGE`; on Linux and macOS by editing a profile file such as
`~/.profile` or `~/.zshenv`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `text \| regex` | none | Variable name or pattern. |
| `scope` | `enum(process\|user\|machine)` | `process` | Variables of this process, or persistent user or machine variables on Windows. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `environment_variable` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Show the search path of the console process:

```nurt example
environment "PATH"
```

```text expected
name: PATH
scope: process
```

List the variables whose names start with `CARGO_`:

```nurt example
environment /^CARGO_/
```

List the persistent variables of the account on Windows:

```nurt example
environment scope: user
```

Set a persistent variable of the account on Windows:

```nurt example
write "registry:/HKCU/Environment/EDITOR" "code" mode: overwrite value_type: string
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_OS_ONLY` | `scope: user` or `scope: machine` outside Windows. | Use `scope: process`, or edit a profile file with `write` or `replace`. |
| `E_REGEX` | `name` is an invalid pattern. | Correct the pattern. |
| `E_TYPE` | `name` is neither text nor a pattern, or `scope` is not a listed value. | Pass a name, a pattern or one of the listed scopes. |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | The registry key of the scope cannot be read. | Run the console with an account that can read the key. |
| `E_IO` | The registry key of the scope cannot be read for another reason. | Check the key with `list "registry:/HKCU/Environment"`. |

## Related

`host`, `write`, `replace`, `list`.

title: evaluate
text:
# evaluate

## Synopsis

```text
evaluate <expression>
```

## Description

`evaluate` computes the value of one expression and returns it with its type.
It starts a pipeline, so the value can be passed to later stages, and it is
the Nurt form of the shell commands that print a computed value (`date`,
`echo`, `Get-Date`, `Write-Output`).

The expression uses the operators and the built-in functions of the language:
arithmetic on integers, numbers, sizes and durations; `instant - instant` is a
duration and `instant +- duration` is an instant; `+` joins texts. Time is
read from the clock of the execution, so `now()` and `ago(7d)` give the time of
the call. The expression is evaluated by the evaluator of the execution; no
other evaluation exists, so `filter`, `select` and `evaluate` give the same
value for the same expression.

The result is one `value` record with the fields `value` and `type`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expression` | `expression` | required | Expression to evaluate. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `value` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Compute an integer.

```nurt example
evaluate 6 * 7
```

```text expected
42
```

Join two texts.

```nurt example
evaluate "Release " + "1.0"
```

```text expected
Release 1.0
```

Compute the time three days ago.

```nurt example
evaluate now() - 3d
```

Compute a size.

```nurt example
evaluate 1.5gib / 3
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_TYPE` | an operand has a type the operator does not accept, for example `"a" - 1` | convert the operand or change the operator |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | the expression is missing | give the expression as the first argument |

## Related

`describe`, `filter`, `select`, `help`.

title: filter
text:
# filter

## Synopsis

```text
any |> filter <condition>
```

## Description

`filter` evaluates `condition` on each input record and passes on the records
for which it is `true`. A condition that evaluates to `null`, for example a
comparison with a field that has no value, counts as `false`. Any other value
than a `bool` stops the program with `E_TYPE`.

When the kinds of the input records are known, an expression that no record
can satisfy is checked before the program runs, by `check` and by the binding
of every run, with the error the evaluation would raise for every record that
has a value in the field (same code, message and `expected`). The check
covers a field of a known type and a literal, in either order, in these
places:

| Expression | Error |
|---|---|
| `size > "abc"`, `modified < "never"`, `size == "abc"`: a text that does not form a value of the type of a `size`, `duration`, `instant`, `path`, `glob` or `key` field | `E_INVALID_VALUE`, with the type in `expected` |
| `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` with a literal of another type family (`size > 5`, `name > 5`, `flags > 5`, `raw_name > "abc"`) | `E_TYPE` |
| `in` with a range and a field that is not an `int` (`size in 1..5`), and `in` with a right operand that is not a list, a range or a map (`5 in size`, `name in "abc"`) | `E_TYPE` |
| `+ - * /` on types without a result (`size + "abc"`, `size - 5`, `modified - 5`, `name - 1`) | `E_TYPE` |
| `~` and `!~` with a field that is not text (`flags ~ /a/`) | `E_TYPE` |
| A call of a built-in function whose argument is a field of a type the function does not take (`lower(size)`, `len(exists)`) | `E_TYPE` |
| A call with literal arguments only that the function refuses (`ago("abc")`, `len()`) | the error of the function |

The error is placed at the literal, at the call, or at the whole operation
when both operands are fields. Lists, maps, bytes and ranges take part with
their type family: a literal is never converted to them, so `flags > 5` is
rejected, while `==`, `!=` and `in` with a list or a map never raise an error
on their elements and are not checked. `==` and `!=` with a literal of another
type are not an error and are `false` or `true`.

Only what does not depend on the value of the field is checked. Overflow and
division by zero, an operand that is itself a computed expression, a field of
type `any` (for example `value` of a configuration record) and a field of a
kind that is not known at binding are checked when the program runs, record
by record, and stop it with the same errors. A `null` field value gives
`false` or `null` as before. The condition is checked as written: `and` and
`or` do not hide an error in their right operand from `check`.

The stage is lazy: it reads the next input record only when the following
stage asks for one, so `filter … |> first 10` stops reading the source after
the tenth match. The order of the records, the header of the stream and the
presentation hint of the source are kept. An empty input gives an empty
output.

`filter` works before an effect, where it selects the targets of a change,
and after an effect (stage `5a`), where it reads the records of the effect
such as `exec`, `job`, `test_result`, `finding` and `effect`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `condition` | `expression` | required | Condition evaluated on each record. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `any` | `same` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `transform` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Keep the files larger than 2 kB:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> filter size > 2kb
```

Keep the lines that set `debug` in a configuration file:

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/app/config.ini" |> filter text ~ /^\s*debug\s*=/
```

Keep the result of a program run only when it failed:

```nurt example
run ["go", "vet", "./..."] cwd: "/home/user/project" |> filter exit_code != 0
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `condition` is missing | write a condition after `filter` |
| `E_TYPE` | the condition gives a value other than `bool`, or `<`, `<=`, `>` or `>=` compares a field with a literal of another type family | compare the field, for example `size > 1mb` instead of `size`, and write a literal of the type of the field |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | a text compared with a `size`, `duration` or `instant` field does not form a value of that type; `expected` names the type | write a valid value, for example `"1mb"`, `"5m"` or `"2026-11-01"` |
| `E_UNKNOWN_FIELD` | the condition names a field the records do not have; `expected` lists their fields | use one of the listed fields |

## Related

`select`, `sort`, `first`, `assert`, `count`.

title: find
text:
# find

## Synopsis

```text
find <path> [<glob>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

`find` walks the directory `path` and produces one `entry` record for every
entry that matches `glob`, `type`, `file_type` and `fuzzy`, down to `depth`
levels. Unlike `list`, the root itself is a candidate at depth 0: `find
"/a" depth: 0 type: any` yields exactly one record when `/a` exists and fails
with `E_NOT_FOUND` otherwise. A root that is a file is a candidate in the
same way.

`glob` patterns are matched against the path relative to `path`, with `/`
separators on every system. `*`, `?` and `[...]` do not match `/`; `**`
matches any number of directories, so `*.rs` matches the top level only and
`**/*.rs` matches at any depth. The root is matched by its own name. An
entry matching any pattern of the list is selected. Patterns are case
sensitive unless `case_sensitive: false`.

`glob` and `exclude` compare patterns and paths in Unicode normalization
form C (NFC). A name stored decomposed, as on macOS volumes, matches a
pattern written composed, and a decomposed pattern matches a composed name.

Entries are excluded before they are matched, and an excluded directory is
not entered, so `!pattern` cannot restore an entry below an excluded
directory. The rules apply in this order: `hidden: false`, `exclude_preset`,
`exclude` and, with `gitignore: true`, the ignore files.

| `exclude_preset` | Excluded directories |
|---|---|
| `vcs` | `.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`; also a `.git` file |
| `deps` | `node_modules`, `vendor`, `.venv`, `venv` |
| `build` | `target`, `dist`, `build`, `out` |
| `cache` | `.cache`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache` |

`exclude` uses the gitignore syntax: a pattern without `/` matches a name at
any depth, a leading `/` anchors it at `path`, a trailing `/` matches
directories only, and the last matching pattern decides, where `!pattern`
restores. With `gitignore: true`, `.ignore` files apply in every directory,
and `.gitignore`, `.git/info/exclude` and the global exclude file apply in a
git repository; the files of the ancestors of `path` apply as well, and a
deeper file takes precedence.

`file_type` selects the files whose name matches a pattern of one of the
types. The types are those of `search` and carry the names of
`rg --type-list`. A pattern matches the whole name, `*` stands for any
sequence of characters, and letter case is significant: `*.c` does not match
`main.C`. Directories and links that are not followed are never selected by
`file_type`.

| Type | Name patterns |
|---|---|
| `asm` | `*.asm`, `*.s`, `*.S` |
| `c` | `*.c`, `*.h`, `*.H`, `*.c.in`, `*.h.in`, `*.cats` |
| `clojure` | `*.clj`, `*.cljc`, `*.cljs`, `*.cljx`, `*.edn` |
| `cmake` | `*.cmake`, `CMakeLists.txt` |
| `config` | `*.cfg`, `*.conf`, `*.config`, `*.ini` |
| `cpp` | `*.C`, `*.H`, `*.cc`, `*.cpp`, `*.cxx`, `*.c++`, `*.h`, `*.hh`, `*.hpp`, `*.hxx`, `*.h++`, `*.inl` |
| `cs` | `*.cs`, `*.csx` |
| `css` | `*.css`, `*.scss` |
| `csv` | `*.csv` |
| `dart` | `*.dart` |
| `docker` | `*Dockerfile*`, `*dockerfile*` |
| `elixir` | `*.ex`, `*.eex`, `*.exs`, `*.heex`, `*.leex`, `*.livemd` |
| `erlang` | `*.erl`, `*.hrl` |
| `go` | `*.go` |
| `gradle` | `*.gradle`, `*.gradle.kts` |
| `groovy` | `*.groovy`, `*.gradle` |
| `haskell` | `*.hs`, `*.lhs`, `*.cpphs`, `*.c2hs`, `*.hsc` |
| `html` | `*.htm`, `*.html`, `*.ejs` |
| `java` | `*.java`, `*.jsp`, `*.jspx`, `*.properties` |
| `js` | `*.js`, `*.jsx`, `*.vue`, `*.cjs`, `*.mjs` |
| `json` | `*.json`, `*.jsonc`, `composer.lock`, `*.sarif` |
| `jsonl` | `*.jsonl`, `*.ndjson` |
| `julia` | `*.jl` |
| `kotlin` | `*.kt`, `*.kts` |
| `less` | `*.less` |
| `lua` | `*.lua` |
| `make` | `GNUmakefile`, `Gnumakefile`, `gnumakefile`, `Makefile`, `makefile`, `Makefile.am`, `makefile.am`, `Makefile.in`, `makefile.in`, `*.mk`, `*.mak` |
| `markdown`, `md` | `*.markdown`, `*.md`, `*.mdown`, `*.mdwn`, `*.mkd`, `*.mkdn`, `*.mdx` |
| `nix` | `*.nix` |
| `ocaml` | `*.ml`, `*.mli`, `*.mll`, `*.mly` |
| `perl` | `*.perl`, `*.pl`, `*.PL`, `*.plh`, `*.plx`, `*.pm`, `*.t` |
| `php` | `*.php`, `*.php3`, `*.php4`, `*.php5`, `*.php7`, `*.php8`, `*.pht`, `*.phtml` |
| `protobuf` | `*.proto` |
| `ps` | `*.cdxml`, `*.ps1`, `*.ps1xml`, `*.psd1`, `*.psm1` |
| `py` | `*.py`, `*.pyi`, `*.pyw` |
| `r` | `*.R`, `*.r`, `*.Rmd`, `*.Rnw` |
| `rst` | `*.rst` |
| `ruby` | `Gemfile`, `*.gemspec`, `.irbrc`, `Rakefile`, `*.rake`, `*.rb`, `config.ru` |
| `rust` | `*.rs` |
| `sass` | `*.sass`, `*.scss` |
| `scala` | `*.scala`, `*.sbt` |
| `sh` | `*.bash`, `.bashrc`, `.bash_profile`, `.bash_login`, `.bash_logout`, `*.sh`, `.profile`, `*.zsh`, `.zshrc`, `.zshenv`, `.zprofile`, `*.ksh`, `*.csh`, `*.tcsh` |
| `sql` | `*.sql`, `*.psql` |
| `svelte` | `*.svelte` |
| `svg` | `*.svg` |
| `swift` | `*.swift` |
| `tex` | `*.tex`, `*.ltx`, `*.cls`, `*.sty`, `*.bib`, `*.dtx`, `*.ins` |
| `tf` | `*.tf`, `*.tfvars`, `*.tf.json` |
| `toml` | `*.toml`, `Cargo.lock` |
| `ts` | `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `*.cts`, `*.mts` |
| `tsv` | `*.tsv` |
| `txt` | `*.txt` |
| `vue` | `*.vue` |
| `xml` | `*.xml`, `*.xml.dist`, `*.dtd`, `*.xsl`, `*.xslt`, `*.xsd`, `*.xjb`, `*.rng`, `*.sch`, `*.xhtml` |
| `yaml` | `*.yaml`, `*.yml` |
| `zig` | `*.zig` |

`fuzzy` keeps the entries whose name contains the characters of the text in
the same order and sets `rank`; a higher rank denotes a closer match.
Matches at the start of the name, after `_`, `-`, `.`, `/` or a space, at a
change from lower to upper case and in consecutive characters rank higher.
The text matches without regard to letter case unless it contains an upper
case letter. `sort: rank` puts the closest matches first and needs `fuzzy`.

With `follow_links: true`, links to directories are entered and `type`
classifies a link by its target. A link that leads back to a directory
being walked is a record but is not entered; the notable entry
`link_loop_skipped` gives the number of such links.

Records carry `depth` (0 for the root) and `relative` (`.` for the root).
A path that is not valid Unicode is shown with U+FFFD in `path`, `parent` and
`relative` and carries the native bytes in `raw_path`, `raw_parent` and
`raw_relative`, as in `list`; the next stage reads the entry from `raw_path`.
The text view of a listing that holds only some of the entries of a tree draws
the directories above them, derived from their paths.
The orders of `view` are those of `list`: `flat` sorts all records by `sort`
with ties by path, `tree` and `sizes` are depth first with the entries of one
directory sorted by `sort`. `sort: path` compares paths component by
component, so a directory comes right before its contents. With
`view: sizes`, every directory record carries `total_size` and `file_count`
for all files below it that pass the exclusions, whether or not they match
`glob`, `type` or `depth`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | Directory to search. |
| `glob` | `glob \| list<glob>` | `"**"` | Name patterns relative to the directory. |
| `type` | `enum(file\|directory\|link\|any)` | `file` | Kind of entries to find. |
| `depth` | `int` | no limit | Maximum number of directory levels to descend. |
| `hidden` | `bool` | `true` | Include hidden entries. |
| `follow_links` | `bool` | `false` | Descend into linked directories. |
| `gitignore` | `bool` | `false` | Apply the rules of .gitignore files. |
| `exclude` | `list<glob>` | `[]` | Patterns to exclude, in gitignore syntax; a leading ! restores a match. |
| `exclude_preset` | `list<enum(vcs\|deps\|build\|cache)>` | `[]` | Predefined exclusions: version control, dependencies, build output, caches. |
| `file_type` | `list<text>` | `[]` | File types by extension, such as go or ts. |
| `fuzzy` | `text` | none | Rank entries by similarity of their name to this text. |
| `case_sensitive` | `bool` | `true` | Match name patterns with case sensitivity. |
| `sort` | `enum(path\|modified\|size\|rank)` | `path` | Sort key; rank orders by fuzzy similarity. |
| `order` | `enum(asc\|desc)` | `asc` | Sort order. |
| `view` | `enum(flat\|tree\|sizes)` | `flat` | Flat list, tree, or tree with directory size totals. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `entry`, `registry_value` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

Notable entries: `permission_denied_skipped`, `source_unavailable`,
`nfd_name`, `portability` and `case_alias` as in `list`, and
`link_loop_skipped` for link loops. Each entry gives the number of entries
concerned and a sample of up to five paths.

## Examples

Find the Rust sources of a project at any depth:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" glob: "**/*.rs"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/Cargo.toml", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "\n" },
  { "path": "/home/user/app/src/main.rs", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "\n" },
  { "path": "/home/user/app/src/parser/lexer.rs", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "\n" },
  { "path": "/home/user/app/web/fooBar.ts", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "\n" },
  { "path": "/home/user/app/web/fabric.ts", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "\n" },
  { "path": "/home/user/app/web/node_modules/left-pad/index.ts", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "\n" }
] }
```

Find the TypeScript files outside version control and dependency
directories:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" exclude_preset: [vcs, deps] file_type: ["ts"]
```

Rank the files by the similarity of their names to `fb`:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" fuzzy: "fb" sort: rank
```

Produce the record of one path, as the source of a changing command:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app/Cargo.toml" depth: 0 type: any
```

Find a file by its composed name on a volume that stores the name
decomposed; the record carries the NFC `name` and the stored bytes in
`raw_name`:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/notes" glob: "**/café.md"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/notes/2026/cafe\u0301.md", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "\n" },
  { "path": "/home/user/notes/2026/cafe.md", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "\n" }
] }
```

A response that leaves records out ends with the hint "more: next" and carries the field
`continuation`; the command `next` returns the next part without running the
command again.

```text
matched 1480  shown 50  more: next
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | `path` does not exist | Check the path. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | `path` cannot be read | Search a directory the account may read. |
| `E_PATH_RELATIVE` | `path` is relative and no base directory is set | Give an absolute path or set the `base` option. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | a pattern of `glob` or `exclude` is not valid, or `depth` is negative | Correct the pattern shown in `found`. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` | an unknown file type, preset or enumeration value | Use one of the values listed in `expected`. |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `sort: rank` without `fuzzy` | Give `fuzzy`, or sort by another key. |
| `E_LIMIT` | the result exceeds the record limit | Narrow it with `glob`, `depth` or `exclude`. |

## Related

`list` shows the entries of one directory; `search` finds text in files;
`info` describes one entry.

title: firewall.allow
text:
# firewall.allow

## Synopsis

```text
firewall.allow <port> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`firewall.allow` adds a rule that lets traffic through on a port. A rule that is already in the firewall is not added again: the report states `unchanged` and nothing is marked. The call is a change of the target `firewall:<rule>` from `absent` to `present`; `undo` removes the rule again with `firewall.remove`, in the same backend and table. Rules are described by `port`, `protocol`, `source`, `direction` and `zone`. `source` is the remote address of the traffic: the sender of incoming and the receiver of outgoing traffic. A port is a number from 1 to 65535 or a range `first-last`.

The firewall is chosen by `backend`. With `auto` the command takes the first that is installed and running: firewalld, then ufw, then nftables on Linux; pf on macOS; the Windows Defender Firewall on Windows.

| Backend | System | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `nftables` | Linux | Rules live in the chains `input` and `output` of the table `table` (default `nurt`, family `inet`); the table and the chain are created when absent. The comment of a rule holds its key. `zone` is not available. |
| `firewalld` | Linux | A rule is added to the runtime configuration and to the permanent one. Plain allow rules are ports; rules with `source` and every deny rule are rich rules. `zone` defaults to the default zone of firewalld; only incoming traffic is supported. |
| `ufw` | Linux | Rules are added and deleted with `ufw`; `zone` is not available. |
| `pf` | macOS | Rules live in the anchor `nurt`, which holds only rules of Nurt and is loaded as a whole with `pfctl -a nurt -f -`. The anchor takes effect when `pf.conf` refers to it with `anchor "nurt"`. `zone` is not available. |
| `windows` | Windows | Rules are created with `New-NetFirewallRule` under the display name `nurt:<key>`; `zone` names the profile `domain`, `private` or `public`. |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `port` | `int \| text` | required | Port or range of ports such as 8000-8100. |
| `protocol` | `enum(tcp\|udp)` | `tcp` | Transport protocol. |
| `source` | `text` | none | Remote address or network in CIDR form: the sender of incoming and the receiver of outgoing traffic; any when omitted. |
| `direction` | `enum(inbound\|outbound)` | `inbound` | Direction of the traffic. |
| `zone` | `text` | none | Zone of firewalld or profile of Windows (domain, private, public); the default one when omitted. |
| `backend` | `enum(auto\|nftables\|firewalld\|ufw\|pf\|windows)` | `auto` | Firewall to use; auto selects the first one that is installed and running. |
| `table` | `text` | `"nurt"` | Table of the family inet that holds the rules of nftables. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | `undo` removes the rule that was added; a rule that already exists is left alone. |
| External use | `system_program`: `nft`, `firewall-cmd`, `ufw`, `pfctl`, `powershell`; The rules are read and changed through nft, firewall-cmd, ufw or pfctl; on Windows through the NetSecurity cmdlets of PowerShell. |

## Examples

Allow port 22 for TCP.

```nurt example
firewall.allow 22 privilege: elevated
```

Allow a range of UDP ports from one network.

```nurt example
firewall.allow "8000-8100" protocol: udp source: "10.0.0.0/8" privilege: elevated
```

Use nftables and a named table, outgoing traffic.

```nurt example
firewall.allow 443 direction: outbound backend: nftables table: "nurt" privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `port`, `source` or `zone` is not valid. | Write a port from 1 to 65535, an address in CIDR form or a plain name. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | The backend cannot express the field, for example `zone` on ufw or `direction: outbound` on firewalld. | Leave the field out or choose another `backend`. |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | The program of the system refused the change for want of rights. | Repeat the call with `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | No program of the system that can do this was found. | Install the program or name the `backend`. |

## Related

`firewall.rules` lists the rules, `firewall.remove` removes them, and `firewall.allow` is the opposite of `firewall.deny`.

# firewall.remove

## Synopsis

```text
firewall.remove <port> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`firewall.remove` removes the rules that match `port`, `protocol`, `source`, `direction` and `zone`. `action` limits the removal to allow or deny rules; with `any` both are removed. A call that matches no rule fails with `E_NOT_FOUND` and changes nothing. Every removed rule is one change of the target `firewall:<rule>` from `present` to `absent`; `undo` adds the rules again with `firewall.allow` or `firewall.deny`. Rules are described by `port`, `protocol`, `source`, `direction` and `zone`. `source` is the remote address of the traffic: the sender of incoming and the receiver of outgoing traffic. A port is a number from 1 to 65535 or a range `first-last`.

The firewall is chosen by `backend`. With `auto` the command takes the first that is installed and running: firewalld, then ufw, then nftables on Linux; pf on macOS; the Windows Defender Firewall on Windows.

| Backend | System | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `nftables` | Linux | Rules live in the chains `input` and `output` of the table `table` (default `nurt`, family `inet`); the table and the chain are created when absent. The comment of a rule holds its key. `zone` is not available. |
| `firewalld` | Linux | A rule is added to the runtime configuration and to the permanent one. Plain allow rules are ports; rules with `source` and every deny rule are rich rules. `zone` defaults to the default zone of firewalld; only incoming traffic is supported. |
| `ufw` | Linux | Rules are added and deleted with `ufw`; `zone` is not available. |

| `windows` | Windows | Rules are created with `New-NetFirewallRule` under the display name `nurt:<key>`; `zone` names the profile `domain`, `private` or `public`. |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `port` | `int \| text` | required | Port or range of ports such as 8000-8100. |
| `protocol` | `enum(tcp\|udp)` | `tcp` | Transport protocol. |
| `source` | `text` | none | Remote address or network in CIDR form: the sender of incoming and the receiver of outgoing traffic; any when omitted. |
| `direction` | `enum(inbound\|outbound)` | `inbound` | Direction of the traffic. |
| `zone` | `text` | none | Zone of firewalld or profile of Windows (domain, private, public); the default one when omitted. |
| `backend` | `enum(auto\|nftables\|firewalld\|ufw\|pf\|windows)` | `auto` | Firewall to use; auto selects the first one that is installed and running. |
| `table` | `text` | `"nurt"` | Table of the family inet that holds the rules of nftables. |
| `action` | `enum(any\|allow\|deny)` | `any` | Remove only rules with this action; both when any. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |


# firewall.rules

## Synopsis

```text
firewall.rules [<port>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

`firewall.rules` lists the rules of the firewall as records with the fields `backend`, `place` (table and chain, or zone), `managed` (the rule was created by Nurt), `action` (`allow` or `deny`), `protocol`, `port`, `direction`, `source`, `zone` and `rule` (the rule as the firewall prints it). A rule of a shape that Nurt does not model, for example a rule without a port, has only `backend`, `place`, `managed` and `rule`. `port` and `protocol` keep only the rules that match.

Reading the rules of most firewalls needs the administrator: write `privilege: elevated`.

The firewall is chosen by `backend`. With `auto` the command takes the first that is installed and running: firewalld, then ufw, then nftables on Linux; pf on macOS; the Windows Defender Firewall on Windows.

| Backend | System | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `nftables` | Linux | Rules live in the chains `input` and `output` of the table `table` (default `nurt`, family `inet`); the table and the chain are created when absent. The comment of a rule holds its key. `zone` is not available. |

| `ufw` | Linux | Rules are added and deleted with `ufw`; `zone` is not available. |
| `pf` | macOS | Rules live in the anchor `nurt`, which holds only rules of Nurt and is loaded as a whole with `pfctl -a nurt -f -`. The anchor takes effect when `pf.conf` refers to it with `anchor "nurt"`. `zone` is not available. |
| `windows` | Windows | Rules are created with `New-NetFirewallRule` under the display name `nurt:<key>`; `zone` names the profile `domain`, `private` or `public`. |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `port` | `int \| text` | none | Only rules for this port or range. |
| `protocol` | `enum(tcp\|udp)` | none | Only rules of this protocol. |
| `backend` | `enum(auto\|nftables\|firewalld\|ufw\|pf\|windows)` | `auto` | Firewall to use; auto selects the first one that is installed and running. |
| `table` | `text` | `"nurt"` | Table of the family inet that holds the rules of nftables. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `any` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| External use | `system_program`: `nft`, `firewall-cmd`, `ufw`, `pfctl`, `powershell`; The rules are read and changed through nft, firewall-cmd, ufw or pfctl; on Windows through the NetSecurity cmdlets of PowerShell. |

## Examples

List every rule of the firewall.

```nurt example
firewall.rules
```

List the rules of port 22 of nftables.

```nurt example

```

| `E_PRIVILEGE` | The program of the system refused the change for want of rights. | Repeat the call with `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | No program of the system that can do this was found. | Install the program or name the `backend`. |
| `E_OS_ONLY` | The backend does not exist on this system. | Use `backend: auto`. |

## Related

`firewall.allow`, `firewall.deny` and `firewall.remove` change the rules.

title: first
text:
# first

## Synopsis

```text
any |> first <count>
```

## Description

`first` passes on the first `count` input records and drops the rest. The
stage reads no more than `count` records from its input, so the source stops
once they are read; `first 0` reads nothing. The planner passes the count to
the sources of the pipeline, which may stop early.

The order, the header and the presentation hint of the stream are kept. An
input with fewer records than `count` passes on whole.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | `int` | required | Number of records to keep. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `any` | `same` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `transform` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Keep the first two files:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> first 2
```

Keep the largest file:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> sort size order: desc |> first 1
```

Show the first two lines of a log:

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/app.log" |> first 2
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `count` is missing | write a number after `first` |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `count` is negative | use 0 or a larger number |
| `E_TYPE` | `count` is not an integer | write an integer, for example `first 20` |

## Related

`last`, `skip`, `sort`.

title: git.blame
text:
# git.blame

## Synopsis

```text
git.blame <path> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Annotates each line of a file with the commit that last changed it, in line
order. The history is followed as `git blame` follows it by default: through
renames of the whole file, comparing lines with the Myers algorithm. Lines
moved within the file or copied from another file are attributed to the
commit that moved or copied them unless `find_moves` or `find_copies` is
set. Identities are mapped through `.mailmap`. Root commits are reported as
boundaries.

Without `revision`, the file of the working tree is annotated after the
built-in conversions (`core.autocrlf`, `eol`, `text`); filter programs are
not run. Lines that differ from `HEAD` belong to no commit: their commit is
the null identifier and their author `Not Committed Yet`. A file that is
staged but not in `HEAD` has only such lines. With `revision`, the file of
that commit is annotated.

`find_moves` (`git blame -M`) attributes a block of lines that a commit moved
within the file to the commit that wrote it, when the block holds at least
20 alphanumeric characters. `find_copies` (`git blame -C`) implies
`find_moves` and also looks for blocks of at least 40 alphanumeric characters
in the other files that the same commit changed. Lines of a commit with
several parents are searched in each parent in turn.

Line breaks, including a carriage return before the line feed, are not part
of `text`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | File in a repository. |
| `lines` | `range` | none | Only these lines. |
| `revision` | `text` | `"HEAD"` | Revision to annotate. |
| `find_moves` | `bool` | `false` | Follow lines moved within the file. |
| `find_copies` | `bool` | `false` | Follow lines copied from other files. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `blame_line` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Annotate a file of the working tree.

```nurt example
git.blame "/home/user/repo/src/main.rs"
```

```text expected
blame_line no: 1 short_id: 9b07d3e author: "Ann Lee" text: "use std::io;"
blame_line no: 2 short_id: 0000000 author: "Not Committed Yet" text: "use std::fs;"
```

Annotate lines 40 to 60 as they were in a release.

```nurt example
git.blame "/home/user/repo/src/parser.rs" lines: 40..60 revision: "v1.4.0"
```

Count the annotated lines per author.

```nurt example
git.blame "/home/user/repo/src/parser.rs" revision: "HEAD" |> group author |> sort count order: desc
```

A response that leaves records out ends with the hint "more: next" and carries the field
`continuation`; the command `next` returns the next part without running the
command again.

```text
matched 640  shown 50  more: next
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_NOT_REPOSITORY` | `path` is not inside a repository. | Give a file inside a working tree |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | `revision` is unknown, ambiguous or names no commit. | List branches with `git.branch` |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The file does not exist at `revision`, or is neither in `HEAD` nor staged. | Find the file with `git.log` or stage it |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `path` names a directory, a submodule or the repository root, or `lines` starts before line 1 or after the last line. | Give a file and a range inside it |
| `E_IO` | An object of the repository cannot be read. | Check the repository with `git.status` |

## Related

`git.log`, `git.show`, `git.diff`.

title: git.branch
text:
# git.branch

## Synopsis

```text
git.branch <repo> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Without `create`, `rename`, `delete` or `purge` the command reads the
repository and lists the local branches in the order of `git branch --list`,
or the remote-tracking branches with `remote: true`. Symbolic remote
references such as `origin/HEAD` are not listed. Each local branch carries its
upstream, the numbers of commits ahead of and behind it, `upstream_gone` when
the configured upstream no longer exists, and the working tree in which it is
checked out.

`create` writes `refs/heads/<name>` at the commit of `from` and the reflog
entry `branch: Created from <from>`. When `from` names a remote-tracking branch
of a configured remote and `branch.autoSetupMerge` is not `false`, the
configuration receives `branch.<name>.remote` and `branch.<name>.merge`, as
`git branch` writes them. With `switch: true` the working tree, the index and
`HEAD` move to the new branch by the rules of `git switch -c`: local changes
that do not conflict are carried over, and the reflog of `HEAD` receives
`checkout: moving from <old> to <name>`. `checkpoint: true` records the working
tree and the index as a checkpoint (`git.checkpoint`) in the same operation,
before the switch.

`rename` moves the reference, its reflog and the `branch.<name>` section of
the configuration, and moves `HEAD` of every working tree that points to the
branch, writing `Branch: renamed <old> to <new>` to the reflogs as
`git branch -m` does.

`delete` removes branches and their reflogs, also from `packed-refs`. A branch
is merged when its commit is reachable from its upstream, or from `HEAD` when
it has no upstream; a branch that is not merged is deleted only with
`force: true` and is reported as `branch_deleted_unmerged`. A branch checked
out in this or another working tree is never deleted. When the configuration
key `git.trash_refs` is `true`, the value of each deleted branch is kept as
`refs/nurt/trash/<name>-<seconds>`; `trash: true` lists the kept copies and
`purge` removes them, or all of them with `purge: all`. A `purge` name selects
a copy by its reference, by the last component of the reference
(`<name>-<seconds>`), or every copy of a deleted branch by the branch name. A
name that is both the last component of one copy and the branch name of other
copies, such as `a-1` for the copy `a-1` and the copies `a-1-<seconds>`, is
refused with the problem `ambiguous`; name the references instead.

With `check_references` the command reports references that still name a
renamed or deleted branch: symbolic references to it and `branch.<name>.merge`
entries of branches that track it with `remote = .`.

`expect_state` takes the `state_token` of an earlier `git.branch` effect.
The token covers `HEAD`, `packed-refs` and the local branches; when it differs
nothing changes and the command fails with `E_STALE`.

Every reference file is written under a Git-compatible `<file>.lock`
protocol through the journal; an existing lock fails with `E_GIT_LOCKED`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `remote` | `bool` | `false` | List remote-tracking branches. |
| `create` | `text` | none | Name of a branch to create. |
| `from` | `text` | `"HEAD"` | Start point of the new branch. |
| `rename` | `text` | none | Branch to rename. |
| `new_name` | `text` | none | New name of the renamed branch. |
| `switch` | `bool` | `false` | Switch to the branch after creating it. |
| `checkpoint` | `bool` | `false` | Create a checkpoint of the working tree before switching. |
| `delete` | `text \| list<text>` | none | Branches to delete. |
| `force` | `bool` | `false` | Delete branches that are not merged. |
| `trash` | `bool` | `false` | List the preserved copies of deleted branches instead of the branches. |
| `purge` | `list<text> \| enum(all)` | none | Preserved copies of deleted branches to remove. |
| `check_references` | `bool` | `true` | After delete or rename, report other references that still name the old branch. |
| `expect_state` | `text` | none | State token from an earlier read; nothing changes when the repository state differs. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `branch`, `effect`, `git_trash_entry` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | Branch changes are reversible from the journal, which keeps the previous value of each reference. |

| Action | Effect | Reversibility | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `create` | `local` | `reversible` | Applies when create is given, with or without switch. |
| `rename` | `local` | `reversible` | Applies when rename is given. |
| `delete` | `local` | `reversible` | Applies when delete is given. |
| `purge` | `local` | `reversible` | Applies when purge is given. |

## Examples

List the local branches with their upstreams.

```nurt example
git.branch "/home/user/repo"
```

```text expected
branch name: main current: true upstream: origin/main ahead: 1 behind: 0
```

Create a branch at a tag and check it out, keeping a checkpoint first.

```nurt example
git.branch "/home/user/repo" create: "fix/1.2" from: "v1.2.0" switch: true checkpoint: true
```

Rename the current branch.

```nurt example
git.branch "/home/user/repo" rename: "master" new_name: "main"
```

Delete a branch that was never merged.

```nurt example
git.branch "/home/user/repo" delete: "spike" force: true
```

List the kept copies of deleted branches.

```nurt example
git.branch "/home/user/repo" trash: true
```

```text expected
git_trash_entry name: spike kind: branch ref: refs/nurt/trash/spike-1767225600
```

Remove all kept copies of deleted branches.

```nurt example
git.branch "/home/user/repo" purge: all
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_REF` | The name is invalid (`invalid_name`), the branch exists (`exists`), does not exist (`missing`), is checked out (`current_branch`, `checked_out`) or is not merged (`not_merged`). | `git.branch "/home/user/repo" delete: "spike" force: true` |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | `from` does not resolve to a commit. | `git.log "/home/user/repo"` |
| `E_GIT_DIRTY` | With `switch`, local changes would be overwritten. | `git.stash "/home/user/repo" action: push` |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | A reference lock exists. | Wait for the other process or remove the stale lock |
| `E_STALE` | A reference changed between planning and writing, or `expect_state` differs. | Read the branches again and repeat the call |
| `E_ARG` | Parameters exclude each other (`param_conflict`). | Pass one changing parameter per call |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `rename` without `new_name`. | Add `new_name` |

## Related

`git.switch`, `git.tag`, `git.checkpoint`, `git.status`, `undo`.

title: git.checkpoint
text:
# git.checkpoint

## Synopsis

```text
git.checkpoint <repo> action: <enum(create|list|compare|restore|delete)> [name: value]...
```

## Description

A checkpoint is a commit that records the working tree as `git add -A` would
stage it in a temporary index: tracked files with their working tree content
and untracked files that are not ignored. Ignored files are not recorded. With
`index: true` a second commit records the index and becomes the last parent of
the checkpoint commit, as in a stash entry. The first parent is `HEAD`; a
repository without commits gives a checkpoint without parents.

Checkpoints are stored as `refs/nurt/checkpoints/cp-<N>`, numbered from 1 in
increasing order. Creating a checkpoint does not change `HEAD`, the index,
branches or the working tree. The commit message has the form

```text
nurt checkpoint cp-3: before refactoring

branch: main
head: 5b6f0e3c0a2d7c1b0d1e9f6a4c3b2a1908f7e6d5
index: none
```

Checkpoints under `refs/danaco/checkpoints/` are listed, compared and
restored, but not deleted; new numbers continue after the highest number of
both prefixes.

`list` returns the checkpoints newest first. `compare` computes the difference
between the checkpoint and the `against` side: another checkpoint (`cp-<N>`),
any revision, or the working tree when `against` is absent. Hunks use the
Myers algorithm with the indent heuristic of `git diff`. `restore` writes the
files of the checkpoint that differ from the working tree, removes tracked and
untracked files that are not ignored and are absent from the checkpoint, and
removes directories left empty by the removals. `HEAD` and branches do not
change. With `index: true` the index entries within `paths` are replaced by
the recorded index. `delete` removes the named checkpoints, or all but the
`keep` newest ones.

Content filter drivers configured by the repository are not run; line ending
conversion, `ident` and `working-tree-encoding` are applied.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `action` | `enum(create\|list\|compare\|restore\|delete)` | required | Operation on checkpoints. |
| `label` | `text` | none | Label of a new checkpoint. |
| `checkpoint_id` | `text \| list<text>` | none | Checkpoint to compare or restore, or checkpoints to delete. |
| `against` | `text` | the working tree | With compare: revision or checkpoint to compare with. |
| `stat` | `bool` | `false` | With compare: only changed files with added and removed lines. |
| `context` | `int` | `3` | With compare: lines of context around each change. |
| `function_context` | `bool` | `false` | With compare: extend each change to the whole enclosing function. |
| `symbol` | `text` | none | With compare: only changes within this code element. |
| `word_diff` | `bool` | `false` | With compare: show changes word by word. |
| `ignore_whitespace` | `bool` | `false` | With compare: ignore changes in whitespace. |
| `ignore_moved` | `bool` | `false` | With compare: hide blocks of lines that were only moved. |
| `paths` | `list<path>` | none | Only these files or directories. |
| `index` | `bool` | `false` | With restore: also restore the index. |
| `keep` | `int` | none | With delete: keep only this many newest checkpoints. |
| `save_current` | `bool` | `true` | Create a checkpoint of the current changes before restore. |
| `exclude` | `list<glob>` | `[]` | Paths to leave out of create; the report counts the excluded files. |
| `expect_state` | `text` | none | State token from an earlier read; nothing changes when the repository state differs. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `git_checkpoint`, `hunk`, `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | Restore keeps the exact previous content of every file it changes or removes. |

| Action | Effect | Reversibility | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | `read` |  |
| `compare` | `read` | `read` |  |

## Examples

Record the working tree and the index before a change.

```nurt example
git.checkpoint "/home/user/repo" action: create label: "before refactoring" index: true
```

```text expected
git_checkpoint id: cp-3 ref: refs/nurt/checkpoints/cp-3 label: before refactoring index_included: true
```

Show which files changed since a checkpoint.

```nurt example
git.checkpoint "/home/user/repo" action: compare checkpoint_id: "cp-3" stat: true
```

```text expected
change path: src/main.rs action: modify added: 4 removed: 1
```

Restore one directory from a checkpoint.

```nurt example
git.checkpoint "/home/user/repo" action: restore checkpoint_id: "cp-3" paths: ["src"]
```

Keep the ten newest checkpoints and delete the others.

```nurt example
git.checkpoint "/home/user/repo" action: delete keep: 10
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `action`, `checkpoint_id` or, with `delete`, both `checkpoint_id` and `keep` are missing. | `git.checkpoint "/home/user/repo" action: delete keep: 10` |
| `E_ARG` | `checkpoint_id` and `keep` are both given (`param_conflict`), an identifier is malformed (`invalid_id`), or a path names the `.git` directory. | Pass one selection; use the form `cp-1` |
| `E_ARITY` | More than one checkpoint is given to `compare` or `restore`. | Pass a single identifier |
| `E_GIT_REF` | The checkpoint does not exist (`not_found`) or was written by another tool (`read_only`). | `git.checkpoint "/home/user/repo" action: list` |
| `E_GIT_CHECKPOINT` | `index: true` is requested from a checkpoint without a recorded index (`no_index`). | Restore without `index` |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | `against` names neither a checkpoint nor a revision. | Pass an existing revision |
| `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED` | A comparison option is not available (`diff_option`) or the repository is bare. | `git.diff` with the checkpoint reference |
| `E_GIT_NOT_REPOSITORY` | `repo` is not inside a repository, or a path lies outside the working tree (`path_outside_repo`). | Pass a path inside the working tree |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | A reference, `packed-refs` or the index is locked by another process. | Wait for the other process or remove the stale lock file |
| `E_STALE` | A file, a reference or the index changed between planning and writing. | Run the command again |

## Related

`git.stash`, `git.diff`, `git.restore`, `undo`.

title: git.clone
text:
# git.clone

## Synopsis

```text
git.clone <url> <to> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Clones a repository into a directory that does not exist, as `git clone`
does.

`url` is an address reached through smart HTTP (`http://`, `https://`), SSH
(`ssh://`, `user@host:path`), a `file://` address or an absolute local path.
A relative local path is refused. `to` must not exist and its parent
directory must.

The result has the layout that `git clone` creates:

- the remote `origin` with the address and, in a repository with a working
  tree, the refspec `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`;
- the branches of the remote as `refs/remotes/origin/*`, and the tags, in
  `packed-refs`;
- `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` naming the default branch of the remote;
- the local branch `branch`, or the default branch of the remote, with
  `branch.<name>.remote` and `branch.<name>.merge`, checked out into the
  working tree and the index;
- the reflog message `clone: from <address>` for `HEAD`, the branch and
  `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`.

A remote whose `HEAD` is detached gives a detached `HEAD`. A remote without
commits gives an unborn branch named after its default branch.

With `depth` only the chosen branch is fetched, its history is limited to
that many commits, `shallow` records the boundary, the refspec names the
single branch, and only the tags that point into the fetched history are
stored. With `bare: true` the repository has no working tree, the branches
of the remote become local branches, no refspec and no reflog are written.

The address stored in `remote.origin.url` has no password. The credentials
for HTTP are taken from the address, from the variables `NURT_GIT_TOKEN_<HOST>`
and `NURT_GIT_TOKEN`, from the variables of hosting providers or from the
credential stores; credential helpers that are programs are not run.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | `text` | required | Address of the repository. |
| `to` | `path` | required | Directory to create. |
| `depth` | `int` | none | Limit the cloned history to this many commits. |
| `branch` | `text` | none | Branch to check out instead of the default branch. |
| `bare` | `bool` | `false` | Create a repository without a working tree. |
| `accept_host_key` | `text` | none | SHA-256 fingerprint (SHA256:<base64>) of the SSH host key to accept when the host is not known. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect`, `git_ref_update` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | The new directory is removed by undo; the network transfer cannot be reversed. |

## Examples

Clones the default branch of a repository.

```nurt example
git.clone "https://example.com/org/app.git" "/home/user/app"
```

```text expected
effect  git.clone  ok  /home/user/app  state: completed
```

Clones only the last commit of branch `release`.

```nurt example
git.clone "https://example.com/org/app.git" "/home/user/app" branch: "release" depth: 1
```

Creates a bare repository from a local path.

```nurt example
git.clone "/srv/git/app.git" "/home/user/app.git" bare: true
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_EXISTS` | `to` exists (`destination_exists`). | Pass a directory that does not exist. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The parent directory of `to` does not exist (`parent_missing`). | Create the parent directory first. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `depth` is 0, or `url` is empty or a relative local path. | Pass `depth` of 1 or more and an absolute path or a `file://` address. |
| `E_GIT_REF` | `branch` is not a branch of the remote (`remote_branch_not_found`). | Pass one of the branches listed in the error, or omit `branch`. |
| `E_GIT_AUTH` | The remote requires credentials that are missing or were refused. | Set `NURT_GIT_TOKEN_<HOST>` and use an `https://` address. |
| `E_GIT_HOST_KEY` | The SSH host key is unknown or changed. | Pass `accept_host_key` with the fingerprint of the host. |
| `E_GIT_PROTOCOL` | The remote answered outside the protocol. | Check that the address names a Git repository. |
| `E_NETWORK` | The connection failed; the problem is `dns`, `connect`, `tls`, `timeout`, `proxy`, `http_status` or `insecure_credentials` (an `Authorization` header or token would be sent over `http://` to a host other than this machine). | Check the address, the proxy settings and the network; use an `https://` address. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The transfer was interrupted; the new directory was removed. | Repeat the call. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The transfer was interrupted; the new directory was removed. | Repeat the call. |

## Related

`git.fetch`, `git.switch`, `git.worktree`, `git.status`, `undo`.

title: git.commit
text:
# git.commit

## Synopsis

```text
git.commit <repo> message: <text> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Records a commit on the branch `HEAD` points to, or on `HEAD` itself when it
is detached, and reports the new commit with its files.

Exactly one of `staged`, `all` and `paths` selects the content:

- `staged: true` commits the index as it is. While a merge is in progress
  (`MERGE_HEAD` exists), the commit concludes the merge: its parents are
  `HEAD` and the commits of `MERGE_HEAD`, the files `MERGE_HEAD`,
  `MERGE_MSG`, `MERGE_MODE` and `AUTO_MERGE` are removed and the reflog entry
  reads `commit (merge): <subject>`.
- `all: true` stages every change of the working tree first: modified and
  deleted tracked files and untracked files that are not ignored. The index
  is written with the staged content.
- `paths` commits `HEAD` with the working tree content of the given files
  and directories, as `git commit --only` does. The index entries of these
  paths are updated; other staged changes stay in the index and out of the
  commit. A path that matches no file of the working tree or the index is an
  error.

`amend: true` without a selection replaces only the message of the last
commit: the tree and the parents stay, and the author and author time are
kept. With a selection, `amend` replaces the last commit by a commit of the
selected content with the same parents. Amending is refused while a merge is
in progress.

The message is completed with a line feed, followed by
`Signed-off-by: <committer>` with `sign_off` and by `trailers`, which join an
existing trailer block or start one after a blank line; a trailer equal to
the last trailer of the block is not repeated. The hooks `prepare-commit-msg`
and `commit-msg` may change the message; the result is cleaned up according
to `commit.cleanup` (`strip` also removes lines starting with
`core.commentChar`). The author comes from `author`, `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`,
`GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`, `author.*`, `user.*` and `EMAIL`; the committer from
`GIT_COMMITTER_*`, `committer.*`, `user.*` and `EMAIL`, with the parts of
`author` as the last resort. Dates come from `GIT_AUTHOR_DATE` and
`GIT_COMMITTER_DATE`, otherwise from the clock with the host time offset.
`i18n.commitEncoding` other than UTF-8 is recorded in the `encoding` header.
With `sign: true`, or without `sign` when `commit.gpgSign` is set, the
commit is signed with the key of `user.signingKey` in the format of
`gpg.format` (`openpgp` or `ssh`). An OpenPGP signature is made by GnuPG: the
program named by `gpg.openpgp.program` or `gpg.program` (`gpg` by default) is
started through the program service, as `run` starts programs, with the
arguments of `git commit -S` and the commit on its standard input. The key of
`git.signing.key_file` is imported into a temporary GnuPG home directory that
is removed, with its agent, after signing; the passphrase comes from the file
named by `NURT_GPG_PASSPHRASE_FILE`. A missing or failing program refuses the
commit with `E_GIT_SIGN` and the problem `program_unavailable` or
`program_failed`, and nothing is written. An SSH signature is made in the
process, without running `ssh-keygen`; `gpg.ssh.program` is not run.
`sign: false` leaves the commit unsigned whatever `commit.gpgSign` says.

A commit whose tree equals the tree of its first parent (the empty tree for
the first commit of a branch) is refused unless `allow_empty` is true or the
commit concludes a merge. `exclude` leaves matching paths out: their changes
are not staged and the commit records their version from `HEAD`; the report
counts them.

The hooks `pre-commit`, `prepare-commit-msg`, `commit-msg` and `post-commit`
of `core.hooksPath`, or of `hooks/` in the repository directory, run as user
programs in the root of the working tree, with the limit `git.hooks.timeout`.
They receive a copy of the index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`) and of the message in a
scratch directory outside the repository; content a `pre-commit` hook stages
into the copy becomes part of the commit. A failing `post-commit` hook does
not change the result.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `message` | `text` | required | Commit message. |
| `paths` | `list<path>` | none | Files to stage before committing. |
| `all` | `bool` | `false` | Stage all changes to tracked files before committing. |
| `staged` | `bool` | `false` | Commit exactly the content of the index. |
| `amend` | `bool` | `false` | Replace the last commit. |
