| `trailers` | `list<text>` | `[]` | Trailers appended to the message, such as Co-Authored-By lines. |
| `sign_off` | `bool` | `false` | Append a Signed-off-by trailer. |
| `author` | `text` | the repository configuration | Author as Name <email>. |
| `allow_empty` | `bool` | `false` | Allow a commit without changes. |
| `hooks` | `bool` | `true` | Run the pre-commit, prepare-commit-msg, commit-msg and post-commit hooks of the repository as user programs. |
| `sign` | `bool` | the setting commit.gpgSign of the repository configuration | Sign the commit with the signing key of the repository configuration. |
| `exclude` | `list<glob>` | `[]` | Paths to leave out of the commit; the report counts the excluded files. |
| `expect_state` | `text` | none | State token from an earlier read; nothing changes when the repository state differs. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect`, `commit` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | Undo moves the branch reference back; the working tree is not changed and written objects remain in the repository. |
| External use | `user_program`: `gpg`; Runs gpg (gpg.openpgp.program or gpg.program) when the commit is signed with an OpenPGP key, whether sign is given or commit.gpgSign is set; runs the pre-commit, prepare-commit-msg, commit-msg and post-commit hooks of the repository as user programs when hooks is given. |

## Examples

Commit every change of the working tree with a sign-off.

```nurt example
git.commit "/home/user/repo" message: "feat: add the parser" all: true sign_off: true
```

```text expected
effect kind: git.commit status: ok
commit short_id: 3f2a9c1 subject: "feat: add the parser" refs: [main]
```

Commit two files only, leaving other staged changes in the index.

```nurt example
git.commit "/home/user/repo" message: "fix: handle empty input" paths: ["src/parse.rs", "tests/parse.rs"]
```

Add a co-author trailer to the staged changes and skip the hooks.

```nurt example
git.commit "/home/user/repo" message: "docs: describe options" staged: true trailers: ["Co-Authored-By: Ada Lovelace <ada@example.com>"] hooks: false
```

Reword the last commit.

```nurt example
git.commit "/home/user/repo" message: "fix: handle empty input files" amend: true
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | None or more than one of `staged`, `all`, `paths` (problems `missing_selection`, `selection_conflict`), `amend` or `paths` during a merge. | Give one selection; conclude the merge with `staged: true` |
| `E_GIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT` | The commit would record no change (problem `nothing_to_commit`, `amend_empty`). | Stage changes, use `all: true`, or `allow_empty: true` |
| `E_GIT_IN_PROGRESS` | The index has unresolved conflicts (problem `unmerged_paths`). | Resolve and stage the files with `git.stage` |
| `E_CONFIG` | No author or committer identity (problem `missing_identity`), or `commit.cleanup` has an invalid value. | Set `user.name` and `user.email`, or give `author` |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `author` is not `Name <email>`, a trailer is malformed, a date variable is invalid, or the message is empty after cleanup. | Correct the value |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | A path of `paths` matches no file (problem `path_not_found`). | Check the spelling with `git.status` |
| `E_GIT_HOOK` | `pre-commit`, `prepare-commit-msg` or `commit-msg` failed; the error carries the last lines of its output. | Correct the reported problem, or `hooks: false` |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | A hook exceeded `git.hooks.timeout`. | Raise the limit or skip the hooks |
| `E_GIT_SIGN` | The commit cannot be signed (`no_key`, `agent_unavailable`, `key_locked`, `unsupported_format`). | Configure `user.signingKey` or start the key agent |
| `E_STALE` | `expect_state` differs from the repository state (problem `state_changed`), or a file changed during the commit. | Read the state again and repeat the call |
| `E_GIT_REF` | The branch moved after the plan. | Repeat the call |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | A lock file of `git` exists. | Wait for the other `git` process or remove the stale lock |
| `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED` | `all` or `paths` in a bare repository (problem `bare_repository`). | Use `staged: true` |

## Related

`git.status`, `git.stage`, `git.review`, `git.log`, `undo`.

title: git.diff
text:
# git.diff

## Synopsis

```text
git.diff <repo> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Compares two sides of a repository and returns the differences as hunks in
the unified format of `git diff`. The sides are chosen as follows.

| Parameters | Old side | New side |
|---|---|---|
| none | index | working tree |
| `staged` | `HEAD` | index |
| `from` | revision `from` | working tree |
| `from`, `staged` | revision `from` | index |
| `from`, `to` | revision `from` | revision `to` |

`path` selects files and directories literally, relative to the repository
root. Files with conflict stages are left out. Renames and copies are
detected as configured by `diff.renames` (on by default) with a similarity
threshold of 50 percent.

Lines are compared with the algorithm set by `diff.algorithm` (`myers` by
default, `minimal`, `histogram`; `patience` is computed with `histogram` and
noted as `semantic_fallback`) and the indentation heuristic
(`diff.indentHeuristic`, on by default). Changes at most twice the context
apart, plus `diff.interHunkContext`, share a hunk; a request for the canonical
layout (no `from` and `to`, the default context of 3 lines, without
`function_context`, `ignore_whitespace` and `symbol`) ignores
`diff.interHunkContext`, so its hunks and their identifiers do not depend on
the configuration. The text after `@@` is the
nearest function line above the hunk, found by the pattern of the `diff`
driver of the path (`diff.<driver>.xfuncname`, the built-in patterns for
`rust`, `python`, `golang`, `java`, `cpp`, `markdown` and `bash`, or the
default rule of `git`).

A file is binary when the attribute `-diff` or `binary` is set, when its
driver sets `diff.<driver>.binary`, or when its first 8000 bytes contain a NUL
byte; a binary file yields one record without lines. A change of the mode
only, or a rename without a change of content, yields one record without
lines. A missing line feed at the end of a file is written as the line
`\ No newline at end of file`.

Text conversion programs (`diff.<driver>.textconv`) and filter drivers are not
run: the stored content is compared and the report notes
`filter_not_applied`.

### Hunk identifiers

Without `from`, `to`, `symbol`, `function_context` and `ignore_whitespace` and
with the default context of 3 lines, every record of a file that is not
renamed carries an identifier `path#number` and a `fingerprint`. The number
counts the hunks of the file from 1 in the difference of the working tree
against the index, or of the index against `HEAD` with `staged`. The
fingerprint is the first six hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the hunk
lines, with their prefixes, joined by line feeds. `git.stage hunks:` and
`git.restore hunks:` accept the identifier as `path#number`,
`path#number:fingerprint` or with rows `path#number@2-4,7`; a fingerprint that
no longer matches is rejected.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `from` | `text` | the index or HEAD | Old revision. |
| `to` | `text` | the working tree | New revision. |
| `staged` | `bool` | `false` | Compare the index with HEAD. |
| `path` | `list<path>` | none | Only these files or directories. |
| `context` | `int` | `3` | Lines of context around each change. |
| `stat` | `bool` | `false` | Only the numbers of added and removed lines per file. |
| `function_context` | `bool` | `false` | Extend each change to the whole enclosing function. |
| `symbol` | `text` | none | Only changes within this code element on the new side. |
| `word_diff` | `bool` | `false` | Show changes word by word. |
| `ignore_whitespace` | `bool` | `false` | Ignore changes in whitespace. |
| `ignore_moved` | `bool` | `false` | Hide blocks of lines that were only moved. |
| `exclude` | `list<glob>` | `[]` | Paths to leave out; the report counts the excluded files. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `hunk` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Show the unstaged changes of one file.

```nurt example
git.diff "/home/user/repo" path: ["src/main.rs"]
```

```text expected
hunk path: src/main.rs id: src/main.rs#1 old_start: 10 old_len: 7 new_start: 10 new_len: 8
```

Summarize what a branch changed since the main branch.

```nurt example
git.diff "/home/user/repo" from: "main" to: "feature" stat: true
```

Show the staged changes with whole functions, ignoring white space.

```nurt example
git.diff "/home/user/repo" staged: true function_context: true ignore_whitespace: true
```

Show the changes of one function since the previous commit.

```nurt example
git.diff "/home/user/repo" from: "HEAD~1" path: ["src/parser.rs"] symbol: "parse_expr"
```

A response that leaves records out ends with the hint "more: next" and carries the field
`continuation`; the command `next` returns the next part without running the
command again.

```text
matched 120  shown 50  more: next
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `to` without `from`, or `symbol` without a file. | Add the missing parameter |
| `E_ARITY` | `symbol` with more than one file. | Give one file in `path` |
| `E_ARG` | `staged` together with `to` (problem `param_conflict`). | Remove one of them |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `context` outside 0 to 200, or an invalid word pattern. | Use a value in range |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | A revision does not exist or does not name a commit or tree. | Check the name with `git.log "/home/user/repo"` |
| `E_GIT_NOT_REPOSITORY` | The path is not inside a repository, a path lies outside it, or the working tree is needed in a bare repository. | Give a path inside the working tree |
| `E_SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND` | `symbol` is not defined in the new version of the file. | Check the name of the element |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | An object, the index or a file cannot be read (problem `read_failed`). | Restore the missing objects of the repository |

## Related

`git.status`, `git.stage`, `git.show`, `git.review`, `git.checkpoint`.

title: git.fetch
text:
# git.fetch

## Synopsis

```text
git.fetch <repo> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Fetches objects and references from a remote into the repository, as
`git fetch` does.

`remote` is the name of a configured remote or an address. A name selects the
refspecs of `remote.<name>.fetch`; an address fetches the remote `HEAD` into
`FETCH_HEAD` only. The remote is reached through a local path or `file://`
address, smart HTTP (`http://`, `https://`) or SSH (`ssh://`,
`user@host:path`) after the `url.<base>.insteadOf` rewrites. Protocol version
2 is used unless `protocol.version` is `0` or `1`.

For every remote reference selected by a refspec, the local reference is
created, fast-forwarded, or, when the refspec starts with `+`, moved
without a fast-forward check. A reference that would move without force is
rejected and reported with the status `rejected`. The branch checked out in
the working tree is never updated through a refspec.

Tags that point into the fetched history are fetched unless
`remote.<name>.tagOpt` is `--no-tags`. With `tags: true` every tag of the
remote is fetched. With `prune: true`, or `fetch.prune` or
`remote.<name>.prune` set, the local references that match the right-hand
side of a refspec and no longer exist on the remote are deleted.

`depth` limits the fetched history to that many commits from each fetched
tip and records the boundary in `shallow`; a larger depth deepens a
shallow repository.

`FETCH_HEAD` is written in the format of `git`: one line per fetched
reference, the heads that a pull merges first, the others marked
`not-for-merge`. The reflog message of each updated reference is
`fetch <remote>: fast-forward`, `fetch <remote>: forced-update` or
`fetch <remote>: storing head`.

Credentials for HTTP are taken from the address, from the variables
`NURT_GIT_TOKEN_<HOST>` and `NURT_GIT_TOKEN`, from the variables of hosting
providers or from the credential stores. Credential helpers that are programs
are not run and are reported as `credential_helper_ignored`. A password in the
address is used for the transfer and never written to the results.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `remote` | `text` | `"origin"` | Remote to fetch from. |
| `prune` | `bool` | `false` | Remove remote-tracking references that no longer exist on the remote. |
| `tags` | `bool` | `false` | Fetch all tags of the remote. |
| `depth` | `int` | none | Limit the fetched history to this many commits. |
| `accept_host_key` | `text` | none | SHA-256 fingerprint (SHA256:<base64>) of the SSH host key to accept when the host is not known. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect`, `git_ref_update` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Fetches the configured refspecs of `origin`.

```nurt example
git.fetch "/home/user/app"
```

```text expected
effect  git.fetch  ok  remote:origin  state: completed
```

Fetches all tags and removes the remote-tracking references of deleted
branches.

```nurt example
git.fetch "/home/user/app" remote: "upstream" prune: true tags: true
```

Deepens a shallow repository to 50 commits.

```nurt example
git.fetch "/home/user/app" depth: 50
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_NOT_REPOSITORY` | `repo` is not inside a repository. | Give the path of a repository. |
| `E_GIT_REF` | The remote is not configured (`unknown_remote`), a refspec selects nothing (`no_match`), or a refspec would update the checked out branch (`checked_out`). | `git.branch "<repo>" action: list` |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `depth` is 0, or a refspec is invalid. | Pass `depth` of 1 or more. |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | A lock file of a reference exists. | Remove the stale `.lock` file after checking that no Git process runs. |
| `E_GIT_AUTH` | The remote requires credentials that are missing or were refused. | Set `NURT_GIT_TOKEN_<HOST>` and use an `https://` address. |
| `E_GIT_HOST_KEY` | The SSH host key is unknown or changed. | Pass `accept_host_key` with the fingerprint of the host. |
| `E_GIT_PROTOCOL` | The remote answered outside the protocol, or its object format differs. | Check that the address names a Git repository. |
| `E_NETWORK` | The connection failed; the problem is `dns`, `connect`, `tls`, `timeout`, `proxy`, `http_status` or `insecure_credentials` (an `Authorization` header or token would be sent over `http://` to a host other than this machine). | Check the address, the proxy settings and the network; use an `https://` address. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The transfer was interrupted; no reference was changed. | Repeat the call. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The transfer was interrupted; no reference was changed. | Repeat the call. |

## Related

`git.pull`, `git.push`, `git.branch`, `git.clone`, `undo`.

title: git.log
text:
# git.log

## Synopsis

```text
git.log <repo> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Lists commits in the default order of `git log`: newest first by committer
time, without topological sorting; commits with equal times appear in the
order in which they were reached. `revision` accepts a single revision, a
range `A..B` (commits reachable from `B` and not from `A`), a symmetric range
`A...B`, an exclusion `^A`, the forms `A^@` and `A^!`, and several of these
separated by spaces. A repository without commits has an empty history.

With `path`, history is simplified as `git log -- <path>` simplifies it: a
commit is listed when it changes one of the paths, and a merge that equals
one of its parents within the paths is followed through that parent only. A
path names a file or a directory with everything below it.

`follow` lists the history of one file across renames and copies: when the
file appears in a commit and has a similar source in the parent, the source
is followed from there on. `symbol` lists the commits that changed the lines
of one code element of the file, as `git log -L` does; the lines are found
with the code service at the first listed revision and carried to older
commits through the differences.

`pickaxe` with a text keeps commits that change the number of occurrences of
the text in a file (`git log -S`); with a regular expression it keeps commits
that change the number of matches (`-S --pickaxe-regex`). `diff_regex` keeps
commits with an added or removed line that matches (`git log -G`). The two
cannot be combined. Merges have no changes of their own, so `follow`,
`pickaxe` and `diff_regex` never select them; binary files and submodules are
not searched.

`author` is a regular expression matched against `Name <email>`, and
`message` against each line of the message. Identities are mapped through
`.mailmap`. The field `trailers` of a commit record maps each trailer token
to its value; a token that occurs several times keeps every value, one per
line in message order, as `git interpret-trailers` lists them, in `git.log` and
in every other command that returns commit records. `since` stops the traversal at the first commit older than the
instant; `until` hides commits newer than it. Both compare the committer time
in whole seconds and include the bound.

`group_by` replaces the commits by `map` records with the number of selected
commits per Conventional Commits type (`other` for other subjects), per author
or per author day, most frequent first.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `count` | `int` | `20` | Maximum number of commits. |
| `skip` | `int` | `0` | Number of commits to skip. |
| `path` | `list<path>` | none | Only commits that change these files or directories. |
| `revision` | `text` | `"HEAD"` | Revision or range to list. |
| `author` | `text` | none | Only commits whose author matches this text. |
| `since` | `instant` | none | Only commits at or after this time. |
| `until` | `instant` | none | Only commits before this time. |
| `message` | `regex` | none | Only commits whose message matches this pattern. |
| `pickaxe` | `text \| regex` | none | Only commits that add or remove this text or pattern. |
| `follow` | `bool` | `false` | Follow a single file across renames. |
| `symbol` | `text` | none | Only commits that change the lines of this code element. |
| `stat` | `bool` | `false` | Include changed files with added and removed lines. |
| `group_by` | `enum(type\|author\|day)` | none | Group commits by conventional commit type, author or day. |
| `diff_regex` | `regex` | none | Only commits whose changed lines match this pattern. |
| `exclude` | `list<glob>` | `[]` | Paths to leave out, also from the pickaxe and diff_regex filters. |
| `find_renames` | `bool` | `false` | Detect renamed files when limiting the log to paths. |
| `find_copies` | `bool` | `false` | Detect copied files when limiting the log to paths. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `commit`, `group` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| External use | `user_program`: `gpg`; Runs gpg (gpg.openpgp.program or gpg.program) to verify OpenPGP signatures when the signature field of the commits is selected. |

## Examples

List the last five commits.

```nurt example
git.log "/home/user/repo" count: 5
```

```text expected
commit short_id: 4f2a9c1 subject: "fix(parser): accept empty input" author: "Ann Lee"
commit short_id: 9b07d3e subject: "feat: add the export command" author: "Ann Lee"
```

List the commits of a branch that are not in `main`, with changed files.

```nurt example
git.log "/home/user/repo" revision: "main..topic" stat: true
```

Follow one file across renames and keep the commits that added or removed a
call.

```nurt example
git.log "/home/user/repo" path: "/home/user/repo/src/io.rs" follow: true pickaxe: "read_all("
```

Count the commits of the last 30 days per Conventional Commits type.

```nurt example
git.log "/home/user/repo" since: now - 30d count: 1000 group_by: type
```

List the history of one function.

```nurt example
git.log "/home/user/repo" path: "/home/user/repo/src/lib.rs" symbol: "parse_header"
```

A response that leaves records out ends with the hint "more: next" and carries the field
`continuation`; the command `next` returns the next part without running the
command again.

```text
matched 900  shown 50  more: next
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_NOT_REPOSITORY` | `repo` is not inside a repository, or a path is outside it (problem `path_outside_repo`). | Give a path inside the working tree |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | A revision is unknown (`not_found`), ambiguous (`ambiguous`), malformed (`invalid_syntax`) or names no commit (`not_a_commit`). | List branches with `git.branch` |
| `E_REGEX` | `author`, `message`, `pickaxe` or `diff_regex` is not a valid pattern. | Correct the pattern |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `follow` or `symbol` without a file in `path`. | Give one file in `path` |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | More than one file with `follow` or `symbol`, `symbol` with `follow` or `stat`, `pickaxe` with `diff_regex`, an empty `pickaxe`, a negative `count` or `skip`, or an unknown `group_by`. | Remove one of the arguments |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | `symbol` on a host without the code service. | Use `path` without `symbol` |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE` | `symbol` in a file without a grammar. | Use `path` without `symbol` |
| `E_SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND` | The element is not defined, or defined several times; the candidates are listed. | Use a qualified name from the candidates |
| `E_SYMBOL_AMBIGUOUS` | The element is not defined, or defined several times; the candidates are listed. | Use a qualified name from the candidates |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The file of `symbol` does not exist at the listed revision. | Give an existing file |
| `E_IO` | An object of the repository cannot be read. | Check the repository with `git.status` |

## Related

`git.show`, `git.blame`, `git.diff`, `git.branch`, `git.tag`.

title: git.merge
text:
# git.merge

## Synopsis

```text
git.merge <repo> [name: value]...
```

## Description

With `action: start` (the default) the commit named by `branch` is merged
into the current branch. When the current commit is an ancestor of the
merged commit, the branch is fast-forwarded: the working tree, the index and
the branch move to the merged commit and no commit is created. When the
merged commit is already contained in the current branch, nothing changes
and the state is `up_to_date`. Otherwise a three-way merge against the best
common ancestor is computed; several best ancestors are first merged into a
virtual ancestor. Text is merged line by line with the histogram algorithm,
renames are followed according to `merge.renames` and `merge.renameLimit`,
and the `merge` and `conflict-marker-size` attributes are honoured.

A clean three-way merge creates a merge commit whose parents are the
current commit and the merged commit. Its message is `Merge branch '<name>'`,
`Merge remote-tracking branch '<name>'`, `Merge tag '<name>'` or
`Merge commit '<revision>'`, followed by ` into <branch>` unless the current
branch matches `merge.suppressDest` (by default `main` and `master`).

When the merge has conflicts, or when `no_commit` is true, the merge stops:
the working tree holds the merged files with conflict markers, the index
holds stages 1, 2 and 3 of each conflicting path, and the state files
`MERGE_HEAD`, `MERGE_MSG`, `MERGE_MODE`, `AUTO_MERGE` and `ORIG_HEAD` are
written in the format of Git, so Git can conclude the merge as well. The
call then fails with `E_GIT_CONFLICT` and `effect_applied: true`; the
`effect.git` record lists the conflicts.

`action: continue` concludes a stopped merge with a commit of the index. It
requires every conflict to be resolved and staged. The message is the
prepared `MERGE_MSG` without comment lines, or `message` when given.

`action: abort` returns the index and the working tree to `HEAD` for every
path the merge changed and removes the merge state files. Local changes of
paths that the merge did not touch are kept.

Every check that can refuse a merge runs before the first change: an
operation in progress, unresolved paths, staged changes (for a three-way
merge), local changes and untracked files in the way of the result.
Configured merge drivers (`merge.<name>.driver`) are not run. The built-in
text driver merges the file and the path is reported as
`filter_not_applied`.

Directory renames are applied as with `merge.directoryRenames=true`: a path
added on one side in a directory that the other side renamed is moved to
the renamed directory and the merge stays clean. Git, with its default
`merge.directoryRenames=conflict`, performs the same move and additionally
reports a `file location` conflict, leaving the moved path at stage 3 or 2.
The `merge.directoryRenames` setting is not read.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `branch` | `text` | none | Branch to merge; required when action is start. |
| `action` | `enum(start\|continue\|abort)` | `start` | Start a merge, continue it after resolving conflicts, or abort it. |
| `fast_forward` | `enum(auto\|only\|never)` | `auto` | Fast-forward when possible, only fast-forward, or always create a merge commit. |
| `message` | `text` | none | Message of the merge commit. |
| `no_commit` | `bool` | `false` | Stop before creating the merge commit. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect`, `git_conflict` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | The previous references and the exact previous content of every changed file are kept in the journal. |

## Examples

Merge the branch `topic` into the current branch.

```nurt example
git.merge "/home/user/project" branch: "topic"
```

```text expected
effect.git state: completed branch: main
```

Create a merge commit even when the branch could be fast-forwarded, with an
own message.

```nurt example
git.merge "/home/user/project" branch: "release/1.4" fast_forward: never message: "Merge release 1.4"
```

Conclude a merge after the conflicts were resolved and staged.

```nurt example
git.stage "/home/user/project" action: add paths: ["src/main.rs"]
git.merge "/home/user/project" action: continue
```

Abort a merge that stopped with conflicts.

```nurt example
git.merge "/home/user/project" action: abort
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_CONFLICT` | The merge stopped with conflicts (`effect_applied: true`), or the index has unresolved paths (`unmerged_paths`). | Resolve the files, stage them and run `action: continue`, or run `action: abort`. |
| `E_GIT_DIRTY` | Staged changes (`staged_changes`), local changes (`local_changes`) or untracked files are in the way. | Commit or stash the changes: `git.stash "<repo>" action: push`. |
| `E_GIT_IN_PROGRESS` | Another operation is in progress, or no merge is stopped for `continue` and `abort` (`no_merge_in_progress`). | Conclude or abort the operation in progress. |
| `E_GIT_NON_FAST_FORWARD` | `fast_forward: only` and the histories diverged (`not_possible`), or the histories are unrelated (`unrelated_histories`). | Merge with `fast_forward: auto`, or rebase onto the branch. |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | `branch` names no commit. | Give an existing branch, tag or commit. |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | `index.lock` or a reference lock exists. | Wait for the other Git process or remove the lock file. |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `action: start` without `branch`. | Give `branch: "<name>"`. |

## Related

`git.status`, `git.stage`, `git.commit`, `git.rebase`, `git.pull`,
`git.stash`, `undo`.

title: git.pull
text:
# git.pull

## Synopsis

```text
git.pull <repo> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Fetches from a remote and integrates the fetched branch into the current
branch, as `git pull` does.

The remote is `remote`, otherwise `branch.<name>.remote` of the current
branch, otherwise `origin`. The branch to integrate is `branch`, otherwise
the upstream branch of the current branch (`branch.<name>.merge`). Without
`branch`, the remote must be the upstream remote of the current branch.

The integration follows `mode`. Without `mode` the repository configuration
decides: `branch.<name>.rebase`, then `pull.rebase` select a rebase
(`true`, `merges`, `interactive`) or a merge (`false`); `pull.ff` selects
the fast-forward policy (`true`, `false`, `only`). The steps are:

- When the current branch is contained in the fetched branch, the branch is
  fast-forwarded, also when a rebase is configured.
- When the fetched branch is contained in the current branch, nothing
  changes and the state is `up_to_date`.
- When the histories diverged, `mode: merge` creates a merge commit with the
  message `Merge branch '<branch>' of <url>`, followed by ` into <current>`
  unless the current branch matches `merge.suppressDest` (by default `main`
  and `master`); `mode: rebase` replays the local commits onto the fetched
  branch, starting after the fork point recorded in the reflog of the
  remote-tracking branch; `mode: fast_forward_only` and `pull.ff=only`
  refuse.
- When neither `mode` nor the configuration chooses, diverged histories are
  refused with `E_GIT_NON_FAST_FORWARD` (problem `diverged`), as in Git 2.53,
  and the error offers `mode: merge` and `mode: rebase`.
- On a branch without commits, the fetched commit is checked out and the
  branch is created with the reflog message `initial pull`.

Checks that do not need the remote run before the transfer and change
nothing: unmerged files, a merge or rebase in progress, and, for a rebase
without `rebase.autoStash`, unstaged or staged changes. Local changes and
untracked files in the way of a fast-forward or a merge are found after the
transfer; then, as in Git, the fetched references and `FETCH_HEAD` are
updated and the working tree and the current branch stay unchanged.

A merge with conflicts stops as `git.merge` does: the working tree holds the
conflict markers, the index holds the conflict stages, and `MERGE_HEAD`,
`MERGE_MSG`, `MERGE_MODE`, `AUTO_MERGE` and `ORIG_HEAD` are written. The
conflict markers name the merged commit by its full identifier, as Git does
for a pull.

Programs named by the configuration (credential helpers, `core.sshCommand`,
content filters) do not run unless the corresponding setting of the console
allows them; skipped programs are reported as notable entries.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `remote` | `text` | `"origin"` | Remote to pull from. |
| `branch` | `text` | the upstream of the current branch | Remote branch to integrate. |
| `mode` | `enum(merge\|rebase\|fast_forward_only)` | the setting of the repository configuration | How the changes are integrated. |
| `accept_host_key` | `text` | none | SHA-256 fingerprint (SHA256:<base64>) of the SSH host key to accept when the host is not known. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect`, `git_ref_update`, `git_conflict` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | Local changes to the working tree are kept in the journal; the network transfer cannot be reversed. |

## Examples

Pulls the upstream branch of the current branch with the configured mode.

```nurt example
git.pull "/home/user/app"
```

```text expected
effect  git.pull  ok  remote:origin  state: fast_forward
```

Pulls branch `release` of remote `upstream` and creates a merge commit when
the histories diverged.

```nurt example
git.pull "/home/user/app" remote: "upstream" branch: "release" mode: merge
```

Replays the local commits onto the upstream branch.

```nurt example
git.pull "/home/user/app" mode: rebase
```

Updates the current branch only when no merge is needed, and accepts the
host key of a new SSH host.

```nurt example
git.pull "/home/user/app" mode: fast_forward_only accept_host_key: "SHA256:uNiVztksCsDhcc0u9e8BujQXVUpKZIDTMczCvj3tD2s"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_NOT_REPOSITORY` | `repo` is not inside a repository. | Give the path of a repository. |
| `E_GIT_IN_PROGRESS` | Unmerged files, or a merge or rebase in progress. | `git.merge "<repo>" action: abort`, `git.rebase "<repo>" action: continue` |
| `E_GIT_DIRTY` | Uncommitted changes block a rebase (before the transfer), or local changes would be overwritten (after the transfer, `effect_applied`). | `git.stash "<repo>" action: push` |
| `E_GIT_NON_FAST_FORWARD` | The histories diverged without a chosen mode (`diverged`), or only a fast-forward is allowed (`not_fast_forward`). | `git.pull "<repo>" mode: merge` or `mode: rebase` |
| `E_GIT_REF` | No upstream branch (`no_upstream`), detached `HEAD`, a remote other than the upstream remote without `branch`, or the branch does not exist on the remote. | `git.pull "<repo>" remote: "origin" branch: "<name>"` |
| `E_GIT_CONFLICT` | The merge stopped with conflicts; `effect_applied` is true. | Resolve, then `git.merge "<repo>" action: continue` |
| `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED` | Invalid `pull.rebase` or `pull.ff` value, a bare repository, several branches to merge at once, or a rebase that the installation does not provide. | Correct the configuration or give `mode`. |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | A lock file of the index or of a reference exists. | Remove the stale `.lock` file after checking that no Git process runs. |
| `E_NETWORK` | The transfer failed; nothing local changed. | See `git.fetch`. |
| `E_GIT_AUTH` | The transfer failed; nothing local changed. | See `git.fetch`. |
| `E_GIT_HOST_KEY` | The transfer failed; nothing local changed. | See `git.fetch`. |
| `E_GIT_PROTOCOL` | The transfer failed; nothing local changed. | See `git.fetch`. |

Errors after the transfer carry `effect_applied: true` and list the updated
remote-tracking references in `details.ref_updates`.

## Related

`git.fetch`, `git.merge`, `git.rebase`, `git.push`, `git.status`.

title: git.push
text:
# git.push

## Synopsis

```text
git.push <repo> branch: <text> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Sends the commits needed by the remote and updates its references through
the send-pack protocol (protocol version 0 with `report-status-v2`,
`side-band-64k`, `atomic`, `push-options`, `ofs-delta`, `quiet`, `agent` and
`object-format` when the remote announces them).

`branch` is a refspec:

- `main` pushes the local branch or tag to the remote reference of the same
  name; `HEAD` pushes the current branch;
- `src:dst` pushes the revision `src` to the remote reference `dst`; an
  unqualified `dst` is completed with `refs/heads/` or `refs/tags/` as the
  remote or the source requires;
- `:dst` deletes the remote reference;
- a leading `+` forces the update of that refspec.

Before the request every update is classified as `git push` does:
`up_to_date` updates are not sent; a new reference is `new`; an update whose
old value is an ancestor of the new one is `updated`; any other update is
rejected as `non_fast_forward` (the old commit is present locally) or
`fetch_first` (it is not) unless forced. A remote tag is replaced only by a
forced update (`already_exists`). With a lease the remote reference must
still have the expected value, otherwise the update is rejected as
`stale_info`.

The objects sent are those reachable from the new values and not reachable
from the references of the remote. Entries stored as deltas in local packs
are copied; no new deltas are computed.

Updates accepted by the remote move the remote-tracking references named by
`remote.<name>.fetch`; their reflog entries read `update by push`. With
`set_upstream` the configuration receives `branch.<name>.remote` and
`branch.<name>.merge`. The `pre-push` hook of the repository runs before the
request; a non-zero exit stops the push.

A remote on the local file system (`file://` URL or path) is served in the
process: the pack is stored in `objects/pack` of the target, the new tips are
checked for completeness, `receive.denyCurrentBranch` (default `refuse` for a
repository with a working tree), `receive.denyDeleteCurrent`,
`receive.denyNonFastForwards`, `receive.denyDeletes` and `receive.hideRefs`
apply, and the hooks `pre-receive`, `update` and `post-receive` of the target
run as user programs. The reflog entries of the target read `push`.

Other remotes are reached over smart HTTP (`http://`, `https://`) or SSH
(`ssh://`, `user@host:path`) after the `url.<base>.pushInsteadOf` and
`url.<base>.insteadOf` rewrites. The `http.*` settings of the repository
apply. When the server answers `401`, the credentials for the address are
taken from the variables `NURT_GIT_TOKEN_<HOST>` and `NURT_GIT_TOKEN`, from
the variables of hosting providers or from the credential stores, and the
request is repeated once; credentials are never sent over `http://`.
Credential helpers that are programs are not run. The `git://` and `ext::`
transports start programs and are not supported.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `branch` | `text` | required | Branch to push. |
| `remote` | `text` | `"origin"` | Remote to push to. |
| `force` | `bool \| enum(no\|lease\|yes)` | `false` | Overwrite a remote branch that is not an ancestor: lease or true only while it is unchanged since the last fetch, yes always. |
| `force_with_lease` | `text` | none | Overwrite the remote branch only while it still points to this revision. |
| `tags` | `bool` | `false` | Also push tags. |
| `set_upstream` | `bool` | `false` | Set the pushed branch as the upstream of the local branch. |
| `delete` | `bool` | `false` | Delete the branch on the remote. |
| `accept_host_key` | `text` | none | SHA-256 fingerprint (SHA256:<base64>) of the SSH host key to accept when the host is not known. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect`, `git_ref_update` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| External use | `user_program`; Runs the pre-push hook of the repository, and the pre-receive, update and post-receive hooks of a remote on the local file system, as user programs. |

## Examples

Push the current branch and record it as upstream.

```nurt example
git.push "/home/user/repo" branch: "HEAD" set_upstream: true
```

```text expected
effect git.push state: completed upstream: origin/main
git_ref_update ref: refs/heads/main status: new remote: origin remote_ref: refs/heads/main
```

Replace a rewritten branch only while the remote still has the fetched
commit.

```nurt example
git.push "/home/user/repo" branch: "feature/login" force: lease
```

Push a commit to a differently named remote branch of a local mirror.

```nurt example
git.push "/home/user/repo" remote: "/srv/git/mirror.git" branch: "4f2a9c1:refs/heads/release"
```

Delete a remote branch.

```nurt example
git.push "/home/user/repo" branch: "old-topic" delete: true
```

Push a branch together with all tags.

```nurt example
git.push "/home/user/repo" branch: "main" tags: true
```

Push to a hosting service over HTTPS with a token from the environment.

```nurt example
git.push "/home/user/repo" remote: "https://git.example.com/team/app.git" branch: "main"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_PUSH_REJECTED` | No reference was updated; the details list every update with its reason (`non_fast_forward`, `fetch_first`, `stale_info`, `already_exists`, `checked_out`, `hook_declined`, `atomic_failed`, `deletion_prohibited`, `remote_ref_missing`). | `git.pull "/home/user/repo" remote: "origin"`, then push again |
| `E_GIT_HOOK` | The `pre-push` hook declined the push. | Correct the problem reported by the hook |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | The source of the refspec does not resolve, or a revision has no destination. | Use `src:refs/heads/<name>` |
| `E_GIT_REF` | The refspec or a reference name is invalid. | Correct the name |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The remote is not configured. | Pass a URL or path, or configure `remote.<name>.url` |
| `E_GIT_NOT_REPOSITORY` | The repository or the local remote is not a Git repository. | Check the path and the remote URL |
| `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED` | The address uses `git://` or `ext::`, or SSH in a build without SSH. | Use an `https://` or `ssh://` address |
| `E_GIT_AUTH` | The remote requires credentials that are missing, were refused, or would be sent over `http://`. | Set `NURT_GIT_TOKEN_<HOST>` and use an `https://` address |
| `E_NETWORK` | The remote cannot be reached or answered with an HTTP error. | Check the address, the proxy settings and the connection |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | The address or an `http.*` setting cannot be parsed. | Correct the remote URL or the setting named in the message |
| `E_GIT_PROTOCOL` | The remote broke the protocol or lacks a required capability. | Push without the option named in the message |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | A reference lock or `config.lock` exists. | Wait for the other process or remove the stale lock |
| `E_STALE` | A reference changed while the push ran. | Fetch and push again |

## Related

`git.pull`, `git.fetch`, `git.branch`, `undo`.

.

title: git.rebase
text:
# git.rebase

## Synopsis

```text
git.rebase <repo> [name: value]...
```

## Description

With `action: start` (the default) the commits of `merge-base(onto, HEAD)..HEAD`
are replayed onto the commit named by `onto`, as `git rebase <onto>` does with
the `merge` back end. Merge commits are left out, and so are commits whose
patch identifier equals that of a commit already in `onto`. The commits are
replayed oldest first: each one is merged onto the result of the previous
one with the three-way merge of `git.merge`, and the new commit keeps the
author, the author date and the message of the original commit; the
committer and the commit date come from the environment of the session. A
commit whose change is already present in the new base is dropped; a commit
that was empty from the start is kept. When `HEAD` already contains `onto` on
a line of history without merges, nothing changes and the state is
`up_to_date`; when the current branch has no commits of its own, it is moved
to `onto` and the state is `fast_forward`.

The replay runs in the object database. The working tree and the index are
written once, from their state before the call to the final state, and the
branch is moved to the last replayed commit.

When a commit cannot be replayed without conflicts, the rebase stops:
`HEAD` is detached at the last replayed commit, the working tree holds the
merged files with conflict markers labelled `HEAD` and `<short> (<subject>)`,
and the index holds stages 1, 2 and 3 of each conflicting path. The state
directory `rebase-merge/` and the files `REBASE_HEAD`, `MERGE_MSG`,
`AUTO_MERGE` and `ORIG_HEAD` are written in the format of Git 2.53, so that
Git can continue the rebase as well, and a rebase stopped by Git can be
continued here. The call fails with `E_GIT_CONFLICT` and
`effect_applied: true`; the details hold the conflicts and the step
(`done`, `total`). A commit whose result would overwrite an untracked file
stops the rebase in the same way with `E_GIT_DIRTY`
(`untracked_overwritten`); the commit stays first in the todo list.

`action: continue` commits the resolved index with the author and the
message of the stopped commit, without the `# Conflicts:` section, and
replays the remaining commits. Every conflict must be resolved and staged,
and the working tree must have no unstaged changes. When the index equals
`HEAD`, no commit is created.

`action: skip` drops the stopped commit, discards its changes from the
index and the working tree, and replays the remaining commits.

`action: abort` returns the working tree, the index and `HEAD` to the state
before the rebase and removes the state files.

Every check that can refuse a rebase runs before the first change: an
operation in progress, unresolved paths, staged and unstaged changes, and
untracked files in the way of `onto`. Hooks are not run (`hooks_skipped`),
and merge driver programs are not started during a rebase.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `onto` | `text` | none | Revision to rebase onto; required when action is start. |
| `action` | `enum(start\|continue\|skip\|abort)` | `start` | Start a rebase, continue it, skip the current commit, or abort it. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect`, `git_conflict` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | The previous references and the exact previous content of every changed file are kept in the journal. |

## Examples

Replay the commits of the current branch onto `main`.

```nurt example
git.rebase "/home/user/project" onto: "main"
```

```text expected
effect.git state: completed branch: topic
```

Rebase onto the remote-tracking branch after a fetch.

```nurt example
git.fetch "/home/user/project"
git.rebase "/home/user/project" onto: "origin/main"
```

Continue a rebase after the conflicts were resolved and staged.

```nurt example
git.stage "/home/user/project" action: add paths: ["src/main.rs"]
git.rebase "/home/user/project" action: continue
```

Drop the commit at which the rebase stopped.

```nurt example
git.rebase "/home/user/project" action: skip
```

Abort a rebase and return to the branch as it was.

```nurt example
git.rebase "/home/user/project" action: abort
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_CONFLICT` | The rebase stopped with conflicts (`effect_applied: true`), or the index has unresolved paths (`unmerged_paths`). | Resolve the files, stage them and run `action: continue`, or run `action: skip` or `action: abort`. |
| `E_GIT_DIRTY` | Staged changes (`staged_changes`), unstaged changes (`unstaged_changes`) or untracked files in the way (`untracked_overwritten`); with `effect_applied: true` the rebase stopped at a commit. | Commit or stash the changes: `git.stash "<repo>" action: push`; move the untracked files away. |
| `E_GIT_IN_PROGRESS` | Another operation is in progress, or no rebase is stopped for `continue`, `skip` and `abort` (`no_rebase_in_progress`). | Conclude or abort the operation in progress. |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | `onto` names no commit. | Give an existing branch, tag or commit. |
| `E_GIT_REF` | `HEAD` has no commit (`unborn_branch`). | Create a first commit. |
| `E_GIT_SIGN` | `commit.gpgSign` is set; replayed commits cannot be signed. | Set `commit.gpgSign` to `false` for the repository. |
| `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED` | `rebase.updateRefs` is set, `rebase.autoStash` is set with uncommitted changes, the todo list has interactive commands, or the stopped rebase uses the `apply` back end. | Conclude the rebase with Git, or change the setting. |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | `index.lock` or a reference lock exists. | Wait for the other Git process or remove the lock file. |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `action: start` without `onto`. | Give `onto: "<revision>"`. |

## Related

`git.merge`, `git.pull`, `git.status`, `git.stage`, `git.stash`,
`git.log`, `undo`.

title: git.reset
text:
# git.reset

## Synopsis

```text
git.reset <repo> revision: <text> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Moves the current branch, or a detached `HEAD`, to the commit named by
`revision`. The mode decides what else is reset:

- `soft` changes only the reference. It is refused while a merge is in
  progress or the index has conflicts.
- `mixed` also replaces the index with the tree of the revision. Index
  entries whose object and mode do not change keep their file status data;
  the working tree is not touched.
- `hard` also brings the working tree to the revision. Local changes of
  tracked files are discarded and an untracked file in the way of a tracked
  file of the revision is overwritten. Other untracked files stay.

The previous commit of `HEAD` is written to `ORIG_HEAD`. The reflog of the
branch receives `reset: moving to <revision>` when the branch moves; the
reflog of `HEAD` receives the same entry. The state files of a merge,
cherry-pick or revert in progress (`MERGE_HEAD`, `MERGE_MSG`, `MERGE_MODE`,
`MERGE_RR`, `AUTO_MERGE`, `SQUASH_MSG`, `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, `REVERT_HEAD`)
are removed. Configured filter drivers are not run; the built-in line
ending, `ident` and working tree encoding conversions are applied.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `revision` | `text` | required | Revision to move to. |
| `mode` | `enum(soft\|mixed\|hard)` | `mixed` | Keep the index and working tree, reset the index, or reset both. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | The previous reference and the exact previous content of every changed file are kept in the journal. |

## Examples

Undo the last commit and keep its changes staged.

```nurt example
git.reset "/home/user/repo" revision: "HEAD~1" mode: soft
```

```text expected
effect git.reset branch: main notable: history_rewritten
```

Unstage everything, keeping the working tree.

```nurt example
git.reset "/home/user/repo" revision: "HEAD"
```

Discard all local changes of tracked files and return to the remote branch.

```nurt example
git.reset "/home/user/repo" revision: "origin/main" mode: hard
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_NOT_REPOSITORY` | `repo` is not inside a repository. | Give the path of a working tree |
| `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED` | The repository is bare (`bare_repository`) or the index is sparse (`sparse_index`). | Use a working tree with a full index |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | The revision does not exist (`unknown`) or is not a commit (`not_a_commit`). | Check the name with `git.log "/home/user/repo"` |
| `E_GIT_IN_PROGRESS` | `soft` during a merge (`merge_in_progress`). | `git.reset "/home/user/repo" revision: "HEAD" mode: mixed` |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | `index.lock` or a reference lock file exists. | Wait for the other process or remove the stale lock |
| `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` | `mode` is not one of the modes. | Use `soft`, `mixed` or `hard` |
| `E_STALE` | A file changed between planning and writing. | Run the command again |

## Related

`git.restore`, `git.switch`, `git.stash`, `git.log`, `undo`.

title: git.restore
text:
# git.restore

## Synopsis

```text
git.restore <repo> paths: <list<path>> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Copies the paths selected by `paths` from a source into the working tree, the
index or both. Paths use `git` pathspec syntax relative to the repository
root: a directory selects everything below it, `*.txt` and `:(glob)**/x` are
patterns. A pathspec that matches no path of the source or the index is an
error and nothing changes.

The source is the revision `source` (a commit, tag or tree). Without it the
working tree is restored from the index, and the index (with `staged`) from
`HEAD`; with `staged` and `worktree` together both come from `HEAD`.

Restoration does not overlay: a selected path present in the index but absent
from the source is removed from the restored side. The working tree is written
only where its content differs from the source. A path with unresolved
conflicts cannot be restored from the index into the working tree; restore it
with `staged: true` from a revision instead.

With `hunks` only the named hunks are taken back, as `git restore --patch`
does. Identifiers have the form of `git.stage` (`path#number`, optionally
`:fingerprint` and `@rows`). With `worktree` the hunks are those between the
index and the working tree file; with `staged: true worktree: false` they are
those between `HEAD` and the index, and a new file whose only hunk is taken
back leaves the index. Unselected hunks stay as they are. Every hunk must lie
in a file at or below one of `paths`, compared literally. `source` and the
restoration of both sides cannot be combined with `hunks`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `paths` | `list<path>` | required | Files or directories to restore. |
| `source` | `text` | the index, or HEAD with staged | Revision to restore from. |
| `staged` | `bool` | `false` | Restore the index. |
| `worktree` | `bool` | true, or false with staged | Restore the working tree. |
| `hunks` | `list<text>` | none | Only these hunks, by identifier as in git.stage. |
| `checkpoint` | `bool` | `false` | Create a checkpoint of the changes before they are discarded. |
| `expect_state` | `text` | none | State token from an earlier read; nothing changes when the repository state differs. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | The exact previous content of every changed file is kept in the journal. |

## Examples

Discard the local changes of one file.

```nurt example
git.restore "/home/user/repo" paths: ["src/main.rs"]
```

```text expected
effect git.restore written: src/main.rs
```

Unstage every change below a directory, keeping the working tree.

```nurt example
git.restore "/home/user/repo" paths: ["docs"] staged: true worktree: false
```

Take the files of a directory from an older commit into the index and the
working tree.

```nurt example
git.restore "/home/user/repo" paths: ["config"] source: "HEAD~2" staged: true worktree: true
```

Take back the second hunk of a file, keeping its other local changes.

```nurt example
git.restore "/home/user/repo" paths: ["src/main.rs"] hunks: ["src/main.rs#2"]
```

Unstage one hunk and keep a checkpoint of the state before it.

```nurt example
git.restore "/home/user/repo" paths: ["src/lib.rs"] hunks: ["src/lib.rs#1"] staged: true worktree: false checkpoint: true
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NO_MATCH` | A pathspec matched no file of the source or the index. | Check the path with `git.status "/home/user/repo"` |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | The source does not exist or is not a tree. | Give an existing commit, tag or tree |
| `E_GIT_DIRTY` | A selected path has unresolved conflicts (`unmerged`). | Restore with `staged: true source: "HEAD"` |
| `E_ARG` | Neither `staged` nor `worktree` is set, a pathspec or a hunk identifier is malformed, or a hunk lies outside `paths` (`hunk_outside_paths`). | Set `worktree: true`, or add the file of the hunk to `paths` |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | An absolute path is outside the repository (`outside_repository`). | Give a path inside the working tree |
| `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED` | `hunks` together with `source` (`hunks_source`), with both sides (`hunks_both`), or for a submodule (`hunks_submodule`). | Remove `source`, or set `worktree: false` for staged hunks |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | A hunk number or the change of a hunk does not exist (`not_found`). | List the hunks again with `git.stage "/home/user/repo" action: list` |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | `index.lock` exists. | Wait for the other process or remove the stale lock |
| `E_STALE` | A file changed between planning and writing, the fingerprint of a hunk no longer matches (`changed`), or the state differs from `expect_state` (`state_changed`). | Read the state or the hunks again and repeat the command |

## Related

`git.switch`, `git.stage`, `git.reset`, `git.checkpoint`, `undo`.

title: git.review
text:
# git.review

## Synopsis

```text
git.review <repo> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Checks changes before a commit and reports one `finding` record for each
problem. The repository is not changed.

Without `base`, `scope` selects the changes:

- `staged`: the index against `HEAD` (against the empty tree before the
  first commit);
- `working`: the working tree against the index, files with conflicts
  against the `ours` stage, and the untracked files that are not ignored;
- `all`: the working tree against `HEAD`, with the untracked files that are
  not ignored.

With `base`, the files of `target` (default `HEAD`) are compared with the
files of `base` and `scope` has no effect. Deleted files, links and
submodules are not checked. At most 300 untracked files are read; an
untracked file larger than 512 KiB is treated as binary without reading its
content.

The checks look at the added lines of the difference with three lines of
context, the difference that `git.diff` shows and whose hunk identifiers
`git.stage` and `git.restore` accept:

| Check | Rule | Severity | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| `secrets` | identifier of the rule | of the rule | An added line matches a rule of the review rule service. The value is never reported. |
| `conflict_markers` | `conflict_markers` | error | An added line starts with `<<<<<<< ` or `>>>>>>> `; one finding per line. |
| `whitespace` | `whitespace` | warning | Added lines end with spaces or tabs; one finding per file with the count. Markdown files (`.md`, `.markdown`) are left out of this rule. |
| `whitespace` | `space_before_tab` | warning | The indentation of added lines has a space before a tab; one finding per file. |
| `whitespace` | `blank_at_eof` | warning | The change adds blank lines at the end of the file; the line is the first of them. |
| `debug_statements` | `debug_statements` | warning | An added line of a source file calls `console.log(`, `console.debug(`, `debugger`, `dbg!(`, `pdb.set_trace(` or `breakpoint()`. |
| `final_newline` | `final_newline` | warning | The change leaves the file without a final line feed. |
| `large_files` | `large_files` | warning | The new content is larger than 512 KiB; `value` and `threshold` give the sizes in bytes. |
| `binary` | `binary` | warning | The new content is binary (a NUL byte in the first 8000 bytes, or the `binary` attribute); line checks are not applied. |
| `tests` | `tests_missing`, `tests_unchanged` | warning | A source file changed and no changed test path contains its name; `tests_unchanged` names an existing test. |
| `subject` | see below | see below | The subject line of `message` breaks a rule. |

Source files are files with the extensions `c`, `cc`, `cjs`, `cpp`, `cs`,
`cxx`, `go`, `h`, `hpp`, `java`, `js`, `jsx`, `kt`, `kts`, `mjs`, `php`,
`py`, `rb`, `rs`, `scala`, `swift`, `ts`, `tsx` and `vue`. A test path lies
in a directory `test`, `tests`, `spec`, `specs`, `__tests__` or `testing`, or
its name has the form `test_*`, `*_test.*`, `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`,
`*_spec.*`, `*Test.*` or `*Tests.*`. The name of a source file is its stem;
for the stems `index`, `main`, `mod`, `lib`, `__init__`, `utils` and `common`
it is the name of the directory.

The rules of `subject` apply to the first non-blank line of `message`:

| Rule | Severity | Applies | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subject_empty` | error | always | The message has no subject line. |
| `conventional_header` | error | `conventional: true` | The subject is not `type(scope)!: description`. |
| `missing_scope` | warning | `conventional: true` | The header has no scope. |
| `subject_case` | warning | `conventional: true` | The description starts with an upper case letter. |
| `subject_length` | warning | always | The subject has more than `subject_max` characters. |
| `subject_period` | warning | always | The subject ends with a full stop. |
| `subject_mood` | warning | always | The first word of the description is a past or third person form such as `added` or `fixes`. |
| `blank_line` | warning | always | The second line of the message is not blank. |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `scope` | `enum(all\|staged\|working)` | `all` | Staged changes, working tree changes, or both. |
| `paths` | `list<path>` | none | Only changes in these files or directories. |
| `base` | `text` | none | Base revision of a range to review instead of uncommitted changes. |
| `target` | `text` | none | End revision of the range. |
| `message` | `text` | none | Planned commit message to check. |
| `checks` | `list<enum(conflict_markers\|whitespace\|large_files\|binary\|secrets\|subject\|tests\|debug_statements\|final_newline)>` | none | Checks to run; all when omitted. |
| `subject_max` | `int` | `72` | Longest allowed subject line of the commit message, at least 20. |
| `conventional` | `bool` | `false` | Require a Conventional Commits subject line. |
| `exclude` | `list<glob>` | `[]` | Paths to leave out; the report counts the excluded files. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `finding` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Review the staged changes and the planned message before a commit.

```nurt example
git.review "/home/user/repo" scope: staged message: "feat(parser): add numbers" conventional: true
```

```text expected
finding path: src/parse.rs kind: conflict_markers severity: error rule: conflict_markers line: 42 hunk: "src/parse.rs#2:9c41e0"
finding path: src/parse.rs kind: whitespace severity: warning rule: whitespace line: 17 count: 3
```

Check only the white space of the working tree changes below `src`.

```nurt example
git.review "/home/user/repo" scope: working paths: ["src"] checks: [whitespace, final_newline]
```

Review the commits of a branch against `main`, without generated files.

```nurt example
git.review "/home/user/repo" base: "main" target: "topic" exclude: ["*.lock", "dist/**"]
```

Check a commit message with a shorter subject limit.

```nurt example
git.review "/home/user/repo" checks: [subject] message: "Fixed the parser." subject_max: 50
```

```text expected
finding path: /home/user/repo target: message kind: subject severity: warning rule: subject_period line: 1
finding path: /home/user/repo target: message kind: subject severity: warning rule: subject_mood line: 1
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `target` without `base` (problem `missing_base`). | Give `base` |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | Unknown scope or check, or `subject_max` below 20 (problem `out_of_range`). | Correct the value |
| `E_GIT_NOT_REPOSITORY` | `repo` is not in a repository, or a path is outside it. | Give a path inside the repository |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | `base` or `target` names no commit. | Use a branch, a tag or a commit |
| `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED` | `scope` `all` or `working` in a bare repository (problem `bare_repository`). | Use `scope: staged` or a range with `base` |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The call was cancelled. | Repeat the call |

## Related

`git.commit`, `git.diff`, `git.stage`, `git.restore`, `git.status`.

title: git.show
text:
# git.show

## Synopsis

```text
git.show <repo> <revision> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Shows each object named by `revision` and `revs`, in that order. A commit is
shown as a `commit` record followed by one `hunk` record per change against
its first parent, with renamed files detected as `git show` detects them; a
root commit is compared with the empty tree.

A merge is shown with the condensed combined difference of `git show`
(`--cc`): only files that differ from every parent are considered, each line
carries one prefix column per parent, and a group of changes is left out when
the parents hold at most two versions of it and the merge takes one of them
unchanged. A merge that only takes changes from its parents therefore shows
no hunks. The `old_start` and `old_len` fields of a combined hunk give the
lines of the first parent.

An annotated tag is shown as a `git_tag` record followed by the object it
tags; tags of tags are followed to the end. A revision that names a tree or a
file is rejected; the content of a file is read with `file`.

With `file`, the content of the file at the commit of `revision` is returned
as one `content` record. `offset` and `limit` select lines; the content is
read as stored in the repository, without conversion filters. Binary content
is reported without text.

A change without line differences, such as a change of mode or an exact
rename, is one hunk without lines. A binary change is one hunk with
`binary: true` and no lines.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `revision` | `text` | required | Revision to show. |
| `revs` | `list<text>` | none | Further revisions to show. |
| `file` | `path` | none | Return the content of this file at the revision. |
| `paths` | `list<path>` | none | Only changes in these files or directories. |
| `offset` | `int` | none | First line of the file content returned, counted from 1. |
| `limit` | `int` | none | Maximum number of lines of the file content returned. |
| `stat` | `bool` | `false` | Only changed files with added and removed lines. |
| `context` | `int` | `3` | Lines of context around each change. |
| `exclude` | `list<glob>` | `[]` | Paths to leave out; the report counts the excluded files. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `commit`, `hunk`, `git_tag`, `content` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| External use | `user_program`: `gpg`; Runs gpg (gpg.openpgp.program or gpg.program) to verify OpenPGP signatures when the signature field of the commits or tags is selected. |

## Examples

Show the last commit with its changes.

```nurt example
git.show "/home/user/repo" "HEAD"
```

```text expected
commit short_id: 4f2a9c1 subject: "fix(parser): accept empty input"
hunk path: src/parser.rs old_start: 41 old_len: 6 new_start: 41 new_len: 8 header: "fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<Ast> {"
```

Show the files changed by a merge against its first parent.

```nurt example
git.show "/home/user/repo" "HEAD" stat: true
```

Show a release tag and the commit it tags, without lock files.

```nurt example
git.show "/home/user/repo" "v1.4.0" exclude: ["*.lock"]
```

Read lines 100 to 149 of a file as it was two commits ago.

```nurt example
git.show "/home/user/repo" "HEAD~2" file: "/home/user/repo/src/main.rs" offset: 100 limit: 50
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_NOT_REPOSITORY` | `repo` is not inside a repository, or a path is outside it (problem `path_outside_repo`). | Give a path inside the working tree |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | A revision is unknown, ambiguous, a range (`range`), or names a tree or a file (`not_a_commit`). | Give a commit or a tag; read files with `file` |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | `file` does not exist at the revision. | Find the commits of the file with `git.log` |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `file` names a directory or a submodule, `file` with `revs`, `paths` or `stat`, `offset` or `limit` without `file`, or `offset: 0`. | Remove the conflicting argument |
| `E_TYPE` | `exclude` is not a list of patterns. | Give glob patterns |
| `E_IO` | An object of the repository cannot be read. | Check the repository with `git.status` |

## Related

`git.log`, `git.diff`, `git.blame`, `git.tag`.

title: git.stage
text:
# git.stage

## Synopsis

```text
git.stage <repo> action: <enum(list|add|unstage)> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`action: list` reports the changes of the working tree against the index, or
of the index against `HEAD` with `staged: true`, as `hunk` records. Each hunk
has an identifier `<path>#<number>:<fingerprint>` that `add` and `unstage`
accept; the fingerprint makes a later call fail with `E_STALE` when the hunk
changed in between.

`action: add` copies the working tree state of the selection into the index,
as `git add` does: changed and new files are staged, files deleted from the
working tree are removed from the index, and a staged conflicted file is
resolved, with its stages kept as resolve-undo data. A directory, and `.` for
the whole working tree, stands for the files below it: the entries of the
index and the untracked files that are not ignored. Files matching a pattern
of `exclude` are left out and counted. An ignored file named explicitly in
`paths` is staged, which `git add` refuses without `-f`; the report carries an
`ignored` note that lists such files.

`action: unstage` copies the `HEAD` state of the selection into the index, as
`git restore --staged` does: an entry returns to its content and mode in
`HEAD`, an entry missing from `HEAD` is removed, and the working tree does not
change.

`hunks` selects parts of files. `<path>#<number>` selects a whole hunk and
`<path>#<number>@<rows>` selected rows of it, where rows are numbers and
ranges such as `3-5,8` counted over the lines of the hunk. For `add` an
unselected added line is dropped and an unselected removed line stays; for
`unstage` the selection is taken out of the index content. The result equals
`git apply --cached` with the patch reduced to the selection. A new file can
be staged partially; files without a final line feed and with CRLF line
endings keep their bytes.

The index is written under `index.lock` through the journal; new blobs are
added to the object database. Index entries written by the command carry no
file status, as entries written by `git apply --cached`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `action` | `enum(list\|add\|unstage)` | required | List changes as hunks, add them to the index, or remove them from it. |
| `paths` | `list<path>` | none | Files or directories to act on. |
| `hunks` | `list<text>` | none | Hunks by identifier, such as file#2 or file#2@3-5,8 for selected lines. |
| `staged` | `bool` | none | With list: show staged instead of unstaged changes. |
| `exclude` | `list<glob>` | `[]` | Paths to leave out of add; the report counts the excluded files. |
| `intent_to_add` | `bool` | `false` | With add: record the paths in the index without their content. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect`, `hunk` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

| Action | Effect | Reversibility | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | `read` |  |

## Examples

List the unstaged hunks of one file.

```nurt example
git.stage "/home/user/repo" action: list paths: ["src/main.rs"]
```

```text expected
hunk path: src/main.rs id: src/main.rs#1:9c0d2e old_start: 12 new_start: 12
```

Stage the second hunk and rows 3 to 5 of the first hunk.

```nurt example
git.stage "/home/user/repo" action: add hunks: ["src/main.rs#2", "src/main.rs#1@3-5"]
```

Stage a directory without log files.

```nurt example
git.stage "/home/user/repo" action: add paths: ["src"] exclude: ["*.log"]
```

Unstage one hunk of a staged file.

```nurt example
git.stage "/home/user/repo" action: unstage hunks: ["README.md#1"]
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `add` or `unstage` without `paths` and `hunks` (`nothing_selected`). | `git.stage "/home/user/repo" action: list` |
| `E_ARG` | A path is outside the working tree or inside `.git` (`invalid_path`), or an identifier or row selection is malformed (`invalid_id`, `invalid_rows`). | Use a path relative to the working tree root |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | A file is neither in the working tree, the index nor `HEAD` (`pathspec_no_match`), or a hunk does not exist (`not_found`). | List the hunks again |
| `E_STALE` | The fingerprint of a hunk no longer matches (`changed`), or the index changed between planning and writing. | List the hunks again |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | `index.lock` exists. | Wait for the other process or remove the stale lock |
| `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED` | The repository has no working tree (`bare`). | Run the command in a working tree |

## Related

`git.status`, `git.diff`, `git.commit`, `git.restore`, `undo`.

title: git.stash
text:
# git.stash

## Synopsis

```text
git.stash <repo> action: <enum(push|pop|apply|list|show|drop|clear)> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`push` saves the staged and unstaged changes of tracked files as a new stash
entry and resets them to `HEAD`. The entry has the structure `git` uses: a
commit of the index (parent `HEAD`), with `include_untracked` a
commit of the untracked files (no parent), and a commit of the working tree
with the parents `HEAD`, the index commit and the untracked commit. Its
message is `WIP on <branch>: <commit> <subject>`, or `On <branch>: <message>`
with `message`. `refs/stash` points to the new entry and its reflog holds
the list. With `paths` only changes below the given files or directories are
saved and reset; `exclude` leaves out paths matching a pattern (a pattern
without `/` matches the file name). Nothing is saved when there are no
changes.

`apply` merges an entry into the working tree with the parent of its working
tree commit as the base; `pop` does the same and removes the entry when the
merge is clean. Changes are applied unstaged, except that files new in the
entry stay added. Untracked files of the entry are written back. When
the merge leaves conflicts, the files contain conflict markers labelled
`Updated upstream` and `Stashed changes`, the index holds the conflict
stages, `pop` keeps the entry and the command fails with `E_GIT_CONFLICT`
after the change is applied.

`drop` removes one entry and `clear` removes all of them by rewriting the
reflog of `refs/stash`; the stashed objects stay in the repository. `list`
and `show` only read.

Entries are named `stash@{N}` or `N`, 0 being the newest; `apply` and `show`
also accept a commit. Configured filter drivers are not run.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `action` | `enum(push\|pop\|apply\|list\|show\|drop\|clear)` | required | Operation on the stash; apply keeps the entry, pop removes it. |
| `stash` | `text` | the newest entry | Stash entry, such as stash@{2}. |
| `message` | `text` | none | With push: message of the new entry. |
| `include_untracked` | `bool` | `false` | With push: also stash untracked files. |
| `paths` | `list<path>` | none | With push: only changes in these files or directories. |
| `exclude` | `list<glob>` | `[]` | Paths to leave out of push; the report counts the excluded files. |
| `expect_state` | `text` | none | State token from an earlier read; nothing changes when the repository state differs. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect`, `git_stash`, `hunk` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | The exact previous content of changed files and the dropped stash references are kept in the journal. |

| Action | Effect | Reversibility | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | `read` |  |
| `show` | `read` | `read` |  |

## Examples

Save all local changes, including new untracked files.

```nurt example
git.stash "/home/user/repo" action: push message: "parser rewrite" include_untracked: true
```

```text expected
effect git.stash branch: main
```

List the entries.

```nurt example
git.stash "/home/user/repo" action: list
```

```text expected
git_stash index: 0 message: "On main: parser rewrite" includes_untracked: true branch: main
```

Bring back the newest entry and remove it.

```nurt example
git.stash "/home/user/repo" action: pop
```

Save only the changes of one directory, leaving out environment files.

```nurt example
git.stash "/home/user/repo" action: push paths: ["src"] exclude: ["*.env"]
```

Remove the second newest entry.

```nurt example
git.stash "/home/user/repo" action: drop stash: "stash@{1}"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_NOT_REPOSITORY` | `repo` is not inside a repository. | Give the path of a working tree |
| `E_GIT_REF` | The branch has no commit yet (`unborn_branch`), the stash is empty (`no_stash`) or `pop`/`drop` names a commit outside the list (`not_a_stash_reference`). | `git.stash "/home/user/repo" action: list` |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | The entry does not exist (`out_of_range`) or is not a stash commit (`not_a_stash`). | `git.stash "/home/user/repo" action: list` |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | A path of `paths` is outside the repository (`outside_repository`). | Give a path inside the working tree |
| `E_NO_MATCH` | A path of `paths` names no file known to git. | Check the path with `git.status "/home/user/repo"` |
| `E_GIT_IN_PROGRESS` | The index has unresolved conflicts (`unmerged_paths`). | Resolve and stage the conflicting files |
| `E_GIT_DIRTY` | Local changes would be overwritten (`local_changes`) or untracked files of the entry exist (`untracked_overwritten`); the paths are in `details.paths`. | `git.stash "/home/user/repo" action: push`, or move the files away |
| `E_GIT_CONFLICT` | The merge left conflicts (`conflicts`, effect applied). | Resolve the files listed in `details.conflicts` |
| `E_STALE` | `expect_state` differs from the current state (`state_changed`), or a file changed between planning and writing. | Read the state again |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | `index.lock` or a reference lock file exists. | Wait for the other process or remove the stale lock |

## Related

`git.reset`, `git.restore`, `git.status`, `git.checkpoint`, `undo`.

title: git.status
text:
# git.status

## Synopsis

```text
git.status <repo>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

Lists the paths of each repository whose index differs from `HEAD`, whose
working tree file differs from the index, that have conflict stages, and that
are untracked or ignored. The entries and their states correspond to
`git status --porcelain=v2`.
