The order within one repository is fixed: tracked paths and paths with
conflicts in byte order of the path, then untracked paths, then ignored
paths. Repositories follow the order of `repo`.
A path of the repository that is not valid Unicode is shown with U+FFFD in
`path` and `renamed_from` and carries its bytes in `raw_path` and
`raw_renamed_from`.

The index is compared with `HEAD` with rename and copy detection as
configured by `status.renames`, which defaults to the value of `diff.renames`
(on); a rename needs a similarity of at least 50 percent. The working tree is
compared with the index without rename detection. Paths with conflict stages
carry the kind of conflict derived from the stages present in the index.

With `untracked: normal`, a directory that contains no tracked file is one
entry whose path ends in `/`; `all` lists every untracked file and `no` none.
`ignored` adds ignored paths, collapsed in the same way. Empty directories are
not listed.

A submodule is reported as modified when its checked-out commit differs from
the recorded one, when it has modified tracked files, or when it has
untracked files; the `submodule` field tells which. Index entries outside a
sparse checkout are not compared with the working tree.

Filter drivers (`filter.<name>.clean`) are not run; files are compared after
the built-in conversions (`core.autocrlf`, `eol`, `text`, `ident`,
`working-tree-encoding`), and the report notes `filter_not_applied`.
`core.fsmonitor` is not used and is noted as `fsmonitor_ignored`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `list<path>` | required | Repositories or paths inside them. |
| `untracked` | `enum(normal\|all\|no)` | `normal` | Untracked files: directories collapsed, every file, or none. |
| `ignored` | `bool` | `false` | Include ignored files. |
| `limit` | `int` | `200` | Maximum number of entries per repository. |
| `stat` | `bool` | `false` | Include the numbers of added and removed lines. |
| `exclude` | `list<glob>` | `[]` | Paths to leave out; the report counts the excluded files. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `git_status` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Show the changes of one repository.

```nurt example
git.status "/home/user/repo"
```

```text expected
git_status path: src/main.rs index: unmodified worktree: modified kind: tracked
git_status path: notes/ index: untracked worktree: untracked kind: untracked
```

List every untracked file together with ignored files.

```nurt example
git.status "/home/user/repo" untracked: all ignored: true
```

Count changed lines in two repositories, leaving out lock files.

```nurt example
git.status ["/home/user/app", "/home/user/lib"] stat: true exclude: ["*.lock"]
```

List only the paths with conflicts after a merge.

```nurt example
git.status "/home/user/repo" untracked: no |> filter kind == "conflict"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_NOT_REPOSITORY` | The path is not inside a repository, or the repository is bare (problem `bare_repository`). | Give the path of a working tree |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `untracked` is not `normal`, `all` or `no`, or `limit` is outside 1 to 5000. | Use a listed value |
| `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED` | The repository uses a format that is not implemented, such as `reftable`. | Use a repository with the files reference backend |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The index, an object or a file cannot be read (problem `read_failed`). | Restore the missing objects of the repository |

## Related

`git.diff`, `git.stage`, `git.commit`, `git.review`, `git.checkpoint`, `undo`.

title: git.switch
text:
# git.switch

## Synopsis

```text
git.switch <repo> branch: <text> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Updates the working tree and the index to the tree of the target and points
`HEAD` at it. The update follows the two-tree rules of `git switch`:

- a path that is equal in the current commit and in the target keeps its
  index entry and its working tree file, so local changes are carried over;
- a path that differs is written from the target when its index entry and its
  working tree file agree with the current commit, and removed when the target
  lacks it; directories left empty are removed;
- a path that differs and has local changes (in the index or in the working
  tree) refuses the switch, also when the local content equals the target;
- an untracked file where the target has a file refuses the switch unless the
  file is ignored; a directory with untracked files where the target has a file
  refuses the switch.

All refusals are found before anything changes and are reported together.
The log of `HEAD` receives `checkout: moving from <old> to <new>`, also when
the target is the current branch. With `detach` the old and new names are the
branch name or the full commit id, as `git` writes them.

The target `-` selects the branch checked out before the current one, read
from the log of `HEAD`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `branch` | `text` | required | Branch to switch to. |
| `create` | `bool` | `false` | Create the branch from HEAD first. |
| `checkpoint` | `bool` | `false` | Create a checkpoint of the working tree before switching. |
| `guess` | `bool` | `false` | Create a local branch from a remote branch of the same name when no local branch exists. |
| `start_point` | `text` | none | Revision the new branch starts from; applies with create. |
| `detach` | `bool` | `false` | Detach HEAD at the revision instead of switching to a branch. |
| `discard_changes` | `bool` | `false` | Discard local changes of the working tree while switching. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | The exact previous content of every changed file is kept in the journal. |

## Examples

Switch to an existing branch.

```nurt example
git.switch "/home/user/repo" branch: "feature/login"
```

```text expected
effect git.switch head_after: 4f2a9c1 branch: feature/login
```

Create a branch at a tag and switch to it.

```nurt example
git.switch "/home/user/repo" branch: "fix/1.2" create: true start_point: "v1.2.0"
```

Check out a commit without a branch.

```nurt example
git.switch "/home/user/repo" branch: "HEAD~3" detach: true
```

Return to the previous branch.

```nurt example
git.switch "/home/user/repo" branch: "-"
```

Keep the current working tree in a checkpoint, then switch.

```nurt example
git.switch "/home/user/repo" branch: "main" checkpoint: true
```

```text expected
effect git.switch head_after: 9c03e7a branch: main checkpoint_before: cp-4
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_DIRTY` | Local changes, untracked files or unresolved conflicts block the switch; the details list the paths by kind (`local_changes`, `untracked_overwritten`, `untracked_removed`, `dir_loses_untracked`, `unmerged`). | `git.stash "/home/user/repo" action: push`, or `discard_changes: true` |
| `E_GIT_REF` | The branch exists (`create`), the name is invalid, or the name is a commit without `detach` (`expected_branch`). | Drop `create`, or add `detach: true` |
| `E_ARG` | `start_point` without `create` (`start_point_without_create`). | Add `create: true` |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | The branch or start point does not exist. | `git.branch "/home/user/repo"` to list branches |
| `E_GIT_IN_PROGRESS` | A merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert is in progress. | Finish or abort the operation |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | `index.lock` or a reference lock exists. | Wait for the other process or remove the stale lock |
| `E_STALE` | A file changed between planning and writing. | Run the command again |

## Related

`git.restore`, `git.branch`, `git.stash`, `git.checkpoint`, `undo`.

title: git.tag
text:
# git.tag

## Synopsis

```text
git.tag <repo> [name: value]...
```

## Description

Without `name` and `delete` the command lists the tags in the order of
`git tag --list`. An annotated tag reports its tagger, time, message and the
object it points to; a lightweight tag reports only its target.

`name` creates `refs/tags/<name>` at `revision`. Without `message` the tag is
lightweight. With `message` an annotated tag object is written first; the
message is cleaned as `git tag -m` cleans it (trailing white space removed,
runs of blank lines collapsed, leading and trailing blank lines removed, one
final line feed) and the object is byte-identical to the one `git tag -a -m`
writes for the same tagger and time. The tagger is the committer identity of
the repository: `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME`, `GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL` and
`GIT_COMMITTER_DATE`, then `user.name` and `user.email`, and the clock of the
execution.

With `sign: true` an annotated tag is signed with the key named by
`user.signingKey` in the format of `gpg.format` (`openpgp` or `ssh`); without
`sign` the setting `tag.gpgSign` decides, and `sign: false` creates an
unsigned tag when `tag.gpgSign` is `true`. An OpenPGP signature is made by the
program named by `gpg.openpgp.program` or `gpg.program` (`gpg` by default),
started through the program service as in `git.commit`; an SSH signature is
made in the process, and `gpg.ssh.program` and similar keys are not run. A
signed tag needs a message; a tag without a message stays lightweight and
unsigned.

`delete` removes the tag reference, from its loose file and from
`packed-refs`; the tag object stays in the object database.

A reflog of a tag is written only when `core.logAllRefUpdates` is `always`,
with the message `tag: tagging <id> (<subject>, <date>)` of `git tag`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `name` | `text` | none | Name of a tag to create. |
| `revision` | `text` | `"HEAD"` | Revision the new tag points to. |
| `message` | `text` | none | Message of an annotated tag. |
| `sign` | `bool` | the setting tag.gpgSign of the repository configuration | Create a signed annotated tag with the signing key of the repository configuration. |
| `delete` | `text` | none | Tag to delete. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `git_tag`, `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | Tag changes are reversible from the journal, which keeps the previous value of each reference. |
| External use | `user_program`: `gpg`; Runs gpg (gpg.openpgp.program or gpg.program) when an annotated tag is signed with an OpenPGP key, whether sign is given or tag.gpgSign is set. |

| Action | Effect | Reversibility | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `local` | `reversible` | Applies when name is given; creates the tag. |
| `delete` | `local` | `reversible` | Applies when delete is given. |

## Examples

List the tags.

```nurt example
git.tag "/home/user/repo"
```

```text expected
git_tag name: v1.2.0 kind: annotated target: 4f2a9c1
```

Create a lightweight tag at the current commit.

```nurt example
git.tag "/home/user/repo" name: "build-417"
```

Create an annotated tag at another commit.

```nurt example
git.tag "/home/user/repo" name: "v1.3.0" revision: "release/1.3" message: "Release 1.3.0"
```

Create a signed annotated tag.

```nurt example
git.tag "/home/user/repo" name: "v1.3.1" message: "Release 1.3.1" sign: true
```

Delete a tag.

```nurt example
git.tag "/home/user/repo" delete: "build-417"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_REF` | The name is invalid (`invalid_name`), the tag exists (`exists`) or does not exist (`missing`). | `git.tag "/home/user/repo" delete: "v1.3.0"` |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | `revision` cannot be resolved. | `git.log "/home/user/repo"` |
| `E_GIT_SIGN` | The tag is signed and no key is available (`signer_unavailable`), or signing fails. | Configure `user.signingKey`, or pass `sign: false` |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `sign: true` without `message` (`missing_message`). | Add `message` |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | A reference lock exists. | Wait for the other process or remove the stale lock |
| `E_STALE` | A reference changed between planning and writing. | Run the command again |
| `E_ARG` | `name` and `delete` are both given (`param_conflict`). | Pass one of them |

## Related

`git.branch`, `git.log`, `git.show`, `undo`.

title: git.worktree
text:
# git.worktree

## Synopsis

```text
git.worktree <repo> action: <enum(add|list|remove)> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`add` creates a linked working tree in a directory that does not exist or is
empty.
The registration is written to `.git/worktrees/<name>/` with the files `HEAD`,
`ORIG_HEAD`, `commondir`, `gitdir`, `index` and `logs/HEAD`, as `git worktree
add` writes them, and the new directory receives a `.git` file that points at
the registration. The reflogs of `HEAD` and of a new branch are written as
`core.logAllRefUpdates` asks, and not written when it is `false`. `<name>` is
the last component of `path`; when the name is
taken, the smallest number that makes it unique is appended (`wt`, `wt1`,
`wt2`).

The branch is `branch`. Without `branch` and `start_point` it is the last
component of `path` exactly as written, as in `git worktree add`; a component
that is not a valid branch name (a space, `~`, `^`, `:`, `..`, a leading `.`
or a trailing `.lock`) fails with `E_GIT_REF` (`invalid_name`), so pass
`branch`. Without `branch`, a `start_point` that names a local
branch checks that branch out, and any other `start_point` is checked out
detached: `HEAD` holds the commit and the record has `detached: true`. An
existing branch is checked out and must not be checked out in
another working tree. A missing branch is created at `start_point`, or at
`HEAD`, with the log message `branch: Created from <start_point>`. The files
of the commit are written to the new directory and recorded in its index.
Content filter drivers are not run.

`list` returns the main working tree first and then the linked working trees
sorted by path, with the lock reason and whether the directory is missing
(`prunable`). It gives the same result from any working tree of the
repository.

`remove` deletes a linked working tree and its registration. A working tree
with modified, staged or untracked files that are not ignored is removed only
with `force: true`. Ignored files do not block the removal. The branch is not
deleted.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `path` | required | Repository or path inside it. |
| `action` | `enum(add\|list\|remove)` | required | Operation on working trees. |
| `path` | `path` | none | Directory of the working tree to add or remove. |
| `branch` | `text` | none | Branch checked out in the new working tree. |
| `start_point` | `text` | none | Revision the new branch starts from. |
| `force` | `bool` | `false` | Remove a working tree that has uncommitted changes. |
| `checkpoint` | `bool` | `false` | Create a checkpoint of the changes before remove. |
| `expect_state` | `text` | none | State token from an earlier read; nothing changes when the repository state differs. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `git_worktree`, `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | Remove moves the working tree directory into the journal before unregistering it. |

| Action | Effect | Reversibility | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | `read` |  |

## Examples

Add a working tree with a new branch.

```nurt example
git.worktree "/home/user/repo" action: add path: "/home/user/repo-hotfix" branch: "hotfix/1.2" start_point: "v1.2.0"
```

```text expected
git_worktree path: /home/user/repo-hotfix branch: hotfix/1.2 main: false
```

List the working trees of a repository.

```nurt example
git.worktree "/home/user/repo" action: list
```

```text expected
git_worktree path: /home/user/repo branch: main main: true
git_worktree path: /home/user/repo-hotfix branch: hotfix/1.2 main: false prunable: false
```

Remove a working tree that still has local changes.

```nurt example
git.worktree "/home/user/repo" action: remove path: "/home/user/repo-hotfix" force: true
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `action` or, with `add` and `remove`, `path` is missing. | Pass `path` |
| `E_GIT_WORKTREE` | The directory exists and is not empty (`path_exists`), a registration names it (`already_registered`), the path is the main working tree (`main_worktree`), no working tree is registered there (`not_found`), or the working tree is locked (`locked`). | `git.worktree "/home/user/repo" action: list`; remove the `locked` file of the registration |
| `E_GIT_REF` | The branch is checked out in another working tree (`checked_out_elsewhere`), `start_point` is given for an existing branch (`branch_exists`), or the branch name is invalid (`invalid_name`). | Pass another `branch` |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | `start_point`, or `HEAD` of a repository without commits, names no commit. | Pass an existing revision as `start_point` |
| `E_GIT_DIRTY` | The working tree to remove has modified, staged or untracked files (`local_changes`). | `git.worktree "/home/user/repo" action: remove path: "/home/user/repo-hotfix" force: true` |
| `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED` | The commit contains an unsafe path (`unsafe_path`). | Check out another revision |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | The lock file of the new branch exists. | Wait for the other process or remove the stale lock file |
| `E_STALE` | The branch, the directory or the registration appeared between planning and writing. | Run the command again |

## Related

`git.switch`, `git.branch`, `git.checkpoint`, `undo`.

title: group
text:
# group

## Synopsis

```text
any |> group <by> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`group` computes `by` for each record and gives one `group` record per
distinct value, with the fields `key` (the value) and `count` (the number of
records). With `keep_items: true` the field `items` holds the records of the
group in input order. Values compare by the total order of values.

Groups are ordered by their key, so the output does not depend on the order
of the input; the output declares this order. `group` reads the whole input;
the number of groups, and with `keep_items` the number of held records, is
bounded by the record limit of the request. An empty input gives no groups.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `by` | `field \| expression` | required | Field or expression whose value forms the groups. |
| `keep_items` | `bool` | `false` | Include the records of each group. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `any` | `group` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `transform` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Count the files of each extension:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> group extension
```

Group the files by extension and keep them in each group:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> group extension keep_items: true
```

Split files into small and large ones:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> group size > 2kb
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `by` is missing | name a field or write an expression |
| `E_UNKNOWN_FIELD` | `by` names a field the records do not have; `expected` lists their fields | use one of the listed fields |
| `E_LIMIT` | more groups or records than the limit | narrow the input or omit `keep_items` |

## Related

`summarize`, `distinct`, `sort`, `count`.

title: groups.add_member
text:
# groups.add_member

## Synopsis

```text
groups.add_member <name> <member>
```

## Description

`groups.add_member` adds an account to a group with `gpasswd -a` on Linux, `dseditgroup` on macOS and `net localgroup /add` on Windows. An account that already belongs to the group is reported as `unchanged`.

Rights: the command accepts `privilege`; write `privilege: elevated` when the account that runs Nurt is not the administrator. A program that fails for lack of rights ends the command with `E_PERMISSION`, and `privilege: auto` repeats it once elevated. An elevated entry is undone by the same elevated process.

`undo` runs `groups.remove_member`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `text` | required | Group name. |
| `member` | `text` | required | Account to add. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `system_program` |
| External use | `system_program`: `gpasswd`, `dseditgroup`, `net`; Members are added with gpasswd on Linux, dseditgroup on macOS and net localgroup on Windows. |

## Examples

Add an account to a group.

```nurt example
groups.add_member "docker" "deploy" privilege: elevated
```

Add an account named by parameter.

```nurt example
groups.add_member name: "ops" member: "ann" privilege: elevated
```

Run the change with elevated rights; adding the call parameter `preview: true` shows the effect first.

```nurt example
groups.add_member "ops" "ann" privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The group does not exist. | Create it with `groups.create`. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The account lacks the rights of the administrator. | Add `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The system program of the command is not installed. | Install the program named in the message. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The system program ended with an error. | Read the end of the error output in the message. |

## Related

`groups.remove_member`, `groups.create`.

title: groups.create
text:
# groups.create

## Synopsis

```text
groups.create <name> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`groups.create` creates a group with `groupadd` on Linux, `dseditgroup` on macOS and `net localgroup` on Windows. `gid` fixes the identifier and `system` creates a system group on Linux.

Rights: the command accepts `privilege`; write `privilege: elevated` when the account that runs Nurt is not the administrator. A program that fails for lack of rights ends the command with `E_PERMISSION`, and `privilege: auto` repeats it once elevated. An elevated entry is undone by the same elevated process.

`undo` runs `groups.remove`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `text` | required | Group name. |
| `gid` | `int` | none | Numeric identifier; the system chooses one when omitted. |
| `system` | `bool` | `false` | Create a system group. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `system_program` |
| External use | `system_program`: `groupadd`, `dseditgroup`, `net`; Groups are created with groupadd on Linux, dseditgroup on macOS and net localgroup on Windows. |

## Examples

Create a group.

```nurt example
groups.create "ops" privilege: elevated
```

Create a group with an identifier.

```nurt example
groups.create "ops" gid: 3000 privilege: elevated
```

Create a system group.

```nurt example
groups.create "svc" system: true privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_EXISTS` | The group exists. | Use `groups.add_member`. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The account lacks the rights of the administrator. | Add `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The system program of the command is not installed. | Install the program named in the message. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The system program ended with an error. | Read the end of the error output in the message. |

## Related

`groups.remove`, `groups.add_member`, `accounts`.

title: groups.remove
text:
# groups.remove

## Synopsis

```text
groups.remove <name>
```

## Description

`groups.remove` removes a group. The identifier and the members are read first and recorded. The group with identifier 0 is never removed.

Rights: the command accepts `privilege`; write `privilege: elevated` when the account that runs Nurt is not the administrator. A program that fails for lack of rights ends the command with `E_PERMISSION`, and `privilege: auto` repeats it once elevated. An elevated entry is undone by the same elevated process.

`undo` runs `groups.create` with the recorded identifier and `groups.add_member` for every recorded member.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `text` | required | Group name. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `system_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | Undo creates the group again with its identifier and members. |
| External use | `system_program`: `groupdel`, `dseditgroup`, `net`; Groups are removed with groupdel on Linux, dseditgroup on macOS and net localgroup on Windows. |

## Examples

Remove a group.

```nurt example
groups.remove "ops" privilege: elevated
```

Remove a group and show the effect.

```nurt example
groups.remove "ops" privilege: elevated |> select target before
```

Run the removal with elevated rights; adding the call parameter `preview: true` shows the effect first.

```nurt example
groups.remove "ops" privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The group does not exist. | Check the name with `accounts kind: group`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | The group has identifier 0. | The group cannot be removed. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The account lacks the rights of the administrator. | Add `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The system program of the command is not installed. | Install the program named in the message. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The system program ended with an error. | Read the end of the error output in the message. |

## Related

`groups.create`, `groups.remove_member`.

title: groups.remove_member
text:
# groups.remove_member

## Synopsis

```text
groups.remove_member <name> <member>
```

## Description

`groups.remove_member` removes an account from a group with `gpasswd -d` on Linux, `dseditgroup` on macOS and `net localgroup /delete` on Windows. An account that is not a member is reported as `unchanged`.

Rights: the command accepts `privilege`; write `privilege: elevated` when the account that runs Nurt is not the administrator. A program that fails for lack of rights ends the command with `E_PERMISSION`, and `privilege: auto` repeats it once elevated. An elevated entry is undone by the same elevated process.

`undo` runs `groups.add_member`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `text` | required | Group name. |
| `member` | `text` | required | Account to remove. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `system_program` |
| External use | `system_program`: `gpasswd`, `dseditgroup`, `net`; Members are removed with gpasswd on Linux, dseditgroup on macOS and net localgroup on Windows. |

## Examples

Remove an account from a group.

```nurt example
groups.remove_member "docker" "deploy" privilege: elevated
```

Remove an account named by parameter.

```nurt example
groups.remove_member name: "ops" member: "ann" privilege: elevated
```

Run the change with elevated rights; adding the call parameter `preview: true` shows the effect first.

```nurt example
groups.remove_member "ops" "ann" privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The group does not exist. | Check the name with `accounts kind: group`. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The account lacks the rights of the administrator. | Add `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The system program of the command is not installed. | Install the program named in the message. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The system program ended with an error. | Read the end of the error output in the message. |

## Related

`groups.add_member`, `groups.remove`.

title: hash
text:
# hash

## Synopsis

```text
hash <path>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

`hash` computes a digest of the content of each file and returns it in the
`hash` field of an `entry` record, in the form `<algorithm>:<hex>`, for
example `sha256:ba7816bf...`. The hexadecimal part is the same as the output
of `sha256sum`, `sha512sum`, `sha1sum`, `md5sum` and `b3sum`; a CRC-32 is
written as eight hexadecimal digits in big-endian byte order, as by
`cksum -a crc32b` and `7z h`.

In the source form, `hash` returns one `entry` record per path, in the order
of the paths. A link is hashed by the content of its target, and its record
describes the link itself. A directory or another entry that is not a
regular file fails with `E_INVALID_VALUE`.

In the stage form, `hash` sets the `hash` field of every input `entry`
record and keeps its other fields. Records of directories and other entries
that are not regular files are passed on unchanged, without a `hash` field.
An empty input gives an empty output.

Content is read in chunks, so a file of any size is hashed in fixed memory.
With more than one thread in the limits of the call, files are hashed in
parallel; the output keeps the order of the input.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `list<path>` | none | Files to hash in the source form. |
| `algorithm` | `enum(sha256\|sha512\|sha1\|md5\|blake3\|crc32)` | `sha256` | Digest algorithm. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none`, `entry` | `entry` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Hash one file with SHA-256.

```nurt example
hash "/srv/app/release.txt"
```

```text expected
path                    hash
/srv/app/release.txt    sha256:ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad
```

Hash two files with MD5.

```nurt example
hash "/srv/app/a.txt" "/srv/app/b.txt" algorithm: md5
```

```text expected
path              hash
/srv/app/a.txt    md5:900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72
/srv/app/b.txt    md5:f96b697d7cb7938d525a2f31aaf161d0
```

Hash the files of a listing with BLAKE3 and group files with equal content.

```nurt example
find "/srv/app" type: file |> hash algorithm: blake3 |> group by: hash
```

Compute the CRC-32 of a file.

```nurt example
hash "/srv/app/check.txt" algorithm: crc32
```

```text expected
path                  hash
/srv/app/check.txt    crc32:cbf43926
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | The source form has no `path`. | Give the files to hash or pass `entry` records. |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | `path` is given in the stage form. | Remove `path`, or start the pipeline with `hash`. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` | `algorithm` names no supported algorithm. | Use one of `sha256`, `sha512`, `sha1`, `md5`, `blake3`, `crc32`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | A path of the source form is a directory or not a regular file (`problem: not_a_file`). | Hash the files of a directory with `find ... type: file \|> hash`. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | A file does not exist. | Check the path. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | A file cannot be read. | Check the permissions of the file. |
| `E_IO` | Reading a file failed. | Check the device and repeat the call. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The call was cancelled or reached its time limit while hashing. | Repeat the call with a longer `timeout`. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The call was cancelled or reached its time limit while hashing. | Repeat the call with a longer `timeout`. |

## Related

`info ... hash: sha256` returns the hash of one file together with its other
details. `find`, `list` and `group` combine with `hash` to find duplicate
files.

title: help
text:
# help

## Synopsis

```text
help [<topic>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

`help` returns documentation as text. Without arguments it prints the
introduction: the product line, a short description of programs and the
journal, and the lists of core commands, groups, guides and topics. The first
line is `Danaco Nurt <version> - command shell and language where every change
can be undone`.

A topic is resolved in this order when `kind` is not given: command, error
code, `syntax`, `corrections`, `commands`, `pipelines`, `let`, `paths`, `records`, `lists`, group, guide. The same name can denote a
command and a group (`verify`): `help verify` answers for the command,
`help verify kind: group` and `help group: verify` answer for the group.

With `kind` given, the topic is looked up among that kind only. `kind: syntax`
accepts the topic `syntax` and the topics of its parts (`pipelines`, `let`,
`paths`, `records`, `lists`); `kind: corrections` accepts the topic
`corrections`. Any other name fails with `E_UNKNOWN_NAME` and the names that
the kind accepts.

| Topic | Answer |
|---|---|
| a command | signature, parameters with defaults, input and output kinds, effect, the first `examples` examples of the command page, typical errors, related commands |
| a group | the description of the group: its commands with parameters and examples |
| an error code | meaning, the stages in which it occurs, typical fix |
| a guide | the text of the guide |
| `syntax` | grammar, literals and expressions, and the rule on stages after the effect |
| `corrections` | classes and policy of corrections, the rule families and the result fields |
| `commands` | every command of the catalog under its group, with its summary |
| `pipelines`, `let`, `paths`, `records`, `lists` | the part of the syntax that the name says, the lines of `syntax` that apply; the hints of errors point at these topics |
| `search` | commands, error codes and guides that match the words, best first |

With `kind: syntax` the topic is empty, `syntax` or one of the topics
`pipelines`, `let`, `paths`, `records`, `lists`; with `kind: corrections` it is
empty or `corrections`. Any other name fails with `E_UNKNOWN_NAME` and is not
ignored.

The topics `group`, `skill` and `search` exclude each other and the positional
topic. An unknown topic fails with `E_UNKNOWN_NAME`; the error lists up to
eight nearest names in `expected`.

The answer is text. With the call parameter `format: json` the answer is a
JSON document with the same content. `help "commands"` lists the commands of
all groups; `help group: "<group>"` describes one group.

The call parameter `language: pl`, or `output.language = "pl"` when the call
gives none, selects Polish for the fixed texts of `help` and `describe`: the
introduction, the headings and the labels. The call parameter wins over the
configuration. Command names, parameters, record fields, error codes, the
summaries of commands and the guides stay in English.

`language: pl` also puts the messages of a result into Polish: the `message`
of an error is the Polish meaning of its code followed by `found`, `expected`
and `problem`; the English message is kept in the error detail `message_en`.
The `detail` of every note and of every irreversible effect starts with the
Polish text of its code, followed by the English detail when there is one. The
codes, the programs in `fix` and `next_steps` and the help topic are never
translated. A code without a Polish text keeps its English message.

`help` never changes state and no command requires it to be read before it
runs.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `topic` | `text` | the list of commands, groups, guides and topics | Command, group, error code, syntax or corrections. |
| `kind` | `enum(command\|group\|error\|skill\|syntax\|corrections)` | `command` | Kind of the topic. |
| `group` | `text` | none | Group to describe, the same as kind: group. |
| `skill` | `text` | none | Guide to show, the same as kind: skill. |
| `search` | `text` | none | Words to look up in commands, errors and guides. |
| `examples` | `int` | `3` | Number of examples shown. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `text` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `help` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Show the introduction.

```nurt example
help
```

```text expected
command shell and language where every change can be undone
```

Show the signature of a command with its first example.

```nurt example
help "replace" examples: 1
```

```text expected
replace
```

Show the description of a group.

```nurt example
help group: "documents"
```

```text expected
GROUP documents
```

Show the meaning and the fix of an error code.

```nurt example
help "E_ASSERT"
```

```text expected
E_ASSERT
```

Look up the topics that mention a word.

```nurt example
help search: "rename symbol"
```

```text expected
code.rename
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_UNKNOWN_NAME` | the topic is not a command, group, error code, guide or topic | choose a name from `expected`, or run `help` for the list |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | more than one of `topic`, `group`, `skill` and `search` was given | keep one of them |

## Related

`describe`, `evaluate`, `help skill: "bash-migration"`.

title: history
text:
# history

## Synopsis

```text
history [<id>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

`history` lists the operations recorded in the journal of the account, latest
first. Reads, previews and failed operations rolled back before they took
effect have no entry and are not listed.

Each operation has a state:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `available` | the operation can be undone |
| `partial` | only some items can be undone: the others were released to free disk space or were undone individually |
| `undone` | the operation was undone |
| `expired` | the operation can no longer be undone; its metrics remain listed |

Operations still being recorded or rolled back are not listed. An operation
that failed its integrity check is listed as `expired`.

The filters combine. `path` selects operations that changed the file,
comparing paths as the volume does (letter case and Unicode normalisation on
case-insensitive volumes); expired operations keep no item list and never
match `path` or `deleted`. Without `limit` at most 20 operations are listed.

With `details: true` and `id`, an operation that is not in the journal or is
still being recorded fails with `E_JOURNAL_NOOP` instead of an empty result.
With `details: true` every listed record also carries `items`, the targets of
the operation; the list is empty for an `expired` operation, and without
`details` the field is absent.

The result states whether an operation can be undone, never until when;
retention limits and the state of the journal are reported by
`journal.status`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `int` | none | Operation to describe. |
| `limit` | `int` | `20` | Number of operations listed. |
| `state` | `enum(any\|available\|partial\|expired\|undone)` | `any` | State of the operations to list. |
| `before` | `int` | none | List only operations older than this one. |
| `since` | `int` | none | List only operations newer than this one. |
| `path` | `path` | none | List only operations that touched this file. |
| `deleted` | `bool` | `false` | List only operations that removed files. |
| `details` | `bool` | `false` | Include the changes and differences of each operation. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `operation` |

Each item of `items` has the fields `path`, `action` (the action on the target,
for example `create`, `modify` or `rename`), `mode` (how the previous content
is kept, for example `clone` or `none`), `before_hash` and `after_hash` (absent
when there was no content), `undone` and `released`.

The text form of the result shows the columns `id`, `time`, `kind`, `state`,
`files`, `bytes` and `summary`, and `items` with `details: true`. The other
fields of the operation (`action`, `irreversible`, `bulk`, `session`,
`undo_of`, `redo_of`, `undo_scope`, `ast_hash`, `manifest_sha256`, `chain`
and `pinned`) stay in the JSON form and appear in the text with verbosity
`detailed` or when the request names them in `fields`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `journal` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

List the latest operations:

```nurt example
history
```

List the operations that changed one file:

```nurt example
history path: "/home/user/app/main.go"
```

Describe operation 18; the call fails when the operation is not in the journal:

```nurt example
history 18 details: true
```

List the operations that removed files and can still be undone:

```nurt example
history deleted: true state: available
```

A response that leaves records out ends with the hint "more: next" and carries the field
`continuation`; the command `next` returns the next part without running the
command again.

```text
matched 90  shown 20  more: next
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_JOURNAL_NOOP` | with `details: true`, operation `id` is not in the journal or is still being recorded | list operations without `id` |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `limit` or an operation number is below 1 | give a number of at least 1 |
| `E_IO` | the journal index cannot be read | check the state directory of the account |

## Related

`undo`, `redo`, `journal.status`, `journal.pin`.

title: host
text:
# host

## Synopsis

```text
host [name: value]...
```

## Description

`host` returns one `host` record that describes the device, the operating
system and the account running the console. Paths in `home`, `temp`,
`programs.path` and `programs.all_paths` always use `/` as the separator; on
Windows they start with the drive letter, for example `C:/Users/user`.

| Field | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `os_version` | `VERSION_ID` of `/etc/os-release` | product version | version of the system |
| `kernel` | kernel release | kernel release | kernel version |
| `memory_total`, `memory_free` | `MemTotal`, `MemAvailable` of `/proc/meminfo` | host memory statistics | memory status |
| `uptime`, `boot_time` | `/proc/uptime`, `btime` of `/proc/stat` | boot time | time since start |
| `virtualization` | container markers, `/proc/1/cgroup`, firmware vendor | hypervisor flag | not reported |
| `uid`, `groups` | user and group identifiers of the process | as Linux | security identifier, local groups |
| `locale` | `LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES`, `LANG` | as Linux | user locale |

`features` lists the capabilities available to the console: `journal`,
`service`, `reflink`, `hardlink`, `exchange`, `xattr`, `acl` and
`case_sensitive`.

`service` is the state of the background service of the instance. It is
`running` when the heartbeat file `service.hb` in the state directory is no
older than `space.heartbeat_max_age_ms`, the process named in it exists, and
the service answers `ping` on its control channel within 50 ms. It is
`stopped` when the service is installed (a systemd unit
`nurt-service.service`, a launchd property list `nurt.service.plist`, or the
Windows service `NurtService`) but not alive, and `not_installed` otherwise.

`programs` resolves each name in `PATH` of the console process, with the
extensions of `PATHEXT` on Windows, and returns one `program_location` per
name in the order given. `path` is the first match and `all_paths` every
match in order of resolution.

With `versions: true`, `version` is read from the metadata of the program
file: the version resource of a PE file, the `Info.plist` of an application
bundle or the one embedded in a Mach-O file, or the `.note.package` note of
an ELF file. A program without such metadata has an empty `version`. No
program is started.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `programs` | `list<text>` | `[]` | Program names to locate in PATH. |
| `versions` | `bool` | `false` | Run each located program with --version to read its version. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `host` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| External use | `user_program`; used when `versions` is given; Runs each located program once with --version. |

## Examples

Describe the device:

```nurt example
host
```

```text expected
os: linux
architecture: x86_64
```

Locate two programs in `PATH`:

```nurt example
host programs: ["git", "cargo"]
```

Locate a program and read its version from the file metadata:

```nurt example
host programs: ["git"] versions: true |> select programs
```

Check whether the background service runs:

```nurt example
host |> select service
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_TYPE` | `programs` is not a list of names, or `versions` is not a boolean. | Pass a list of text values, for example `["git"]`. |

## Related

`environment`, `accounts`, `processes`, `disks`, `program.find`, `service`.

title: http.download
text:
# http.download

## Synopsis

```text
http.download <url> <to> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`http.download` sends a `GET` request to `url` and writes the body of the
response to the file `to`. The body is stored as received: the request asks
for `Accept-Encoding: identity`, and redirects are followed.

The body is first written to the partial file `<to>.part` in the directory
of the target. The file `<to>.part.meta` records the address and the
validator of the response: a strong `ETag`, otherwise `Last-Modified`. When a
download ends early (connection closed, time limit, cancellation), both files
stay. The next run for the same address and target with `resume: true` sends
`Range: bytes=<size of the partial file>-` with `If-Range: <validator>`:

| Answer of the server | Result |
|---|---|
| `206` from the size of the partial file | The rest is appended; `resumed_from` is the size of the partial file. |
| `200` | The resource changed or the server ignores ranges; the download starts again and `resumed_from` is 0. |
| `416` with the size of the partial file as the complete length | The partial file already holds the whole content; no bytes are transferred. |

With `hash`, the digest of the whole content is computed while the bytes
arrive, including the bytes of a resumed partial file. A mismatch removes the
partial file and leaves the target unchanged.

After a complete transfer with a matching digest, the content replaces the
target in one step and the partial file is removed. The directory of `to`
must exist.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | `text` | required | Address of the file. |
| `to` | `path` | required | File to write. |
| `resume` | `bool` | `true` | Continue a partial download. |
| `hash` | `text` | none | Expected digest of the file, for example sha256:<hex>; a mismatch keeps the target unchanged. |
| `headers` | `map<text>` | none | Request headers. |
| `timeout` | `duration` | `300s` | Time limit of the download. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

The `effect` record has `kind` `http.download`, one entry in `changes` for
the target (`action` `create` or `modify`, `size_before`, `size_after`,
`hash_after` as `<algorithm>:<hex>`) and the download object in `after`:

Progress events of phase `receive` report the bytes received.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | The written file is reversible; the request itself only reads from the network. |

The request only reads from the network and is not recorded as an
irreversible effect. The partial file and its description are written outside
the journal and are not undone; they are removed after a successful download
and after a digest mismatch.

## Examples

Download an archive and check its SHA-256 digest:

```nurt example
http.download "https://example.org/dist/tool-1.4.2.tar.gz" "/home/user/tool-1.4.2.tar.gz" hash: "sha256:9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08"
```

```text expected
effect  http.download  ok  /home/user/tool-1.4.2.tar.gz  create
```

Download an image again from the first byte, with a longer time limit:

```nurt example
http.download "https://example.org/images/disk.img" "/srv/images/disk.img" resume: false timeout: 30m
```

Download a build artifact with an additional request header:

```nurt example
http.download "https://artifacts.example.org/builds/42/app.zip" "/home/user/app.zip" headers: {accept: "application/zip"}
```

Show the download object, which tells whether an earlier partial download
was continued:

```nurt example
http.download "https://example.org/data.csv" "/home/user/data.csv" |> select after
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_ARG` | `url` is not a valid HTTP or HTTPS address. | Give an address such as `https://example.org/file`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `hash` has no known algorithm or a wrong number of digits, `headers` sets `Range` or `If-Range`, `timeout` is zero, or `to` is not a regular file. | Correct the value as described in the message. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The directory of `to` does not exist. | Create the directory, then run the command again. |
| `E_NETWORK` | The server cannot be reached, the TLS handshake fails, the connection closes before the end of the body (`problem` `incomplete`), or the server answers with a status of 400 or above (`problem` `http_status`, the status in `status`). | Check the address and the network; run the command again to resume an incomplete download. |
| `E_HASH_MISMATCH` | The digest of the content differs from `hash`. | Check the expected digest and the address. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The download did not finish within `timeout`. | Increase `timeout`; the next run resumes the partial download. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The execution was cancelled. | Run the command again to resume. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The partial file or the target cannot be written. | Check the permissions and the free space of the volume. |
| `E_NO_SPACE` | The partial file or the target cannot be written. | Check the permissions and the free space of the volume. |
| `E_IO` | The partial file or the target cannot be written. | Check the permissions and the free space of the volume. |
| `E_STALE` | The target was created by another process during the download. | Run the command again. |

## Related

`http.request`, `hash`, `undo`.

title: http.request
text:
# http.request

## Synopsis

```text
http.request <url> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`http.request` sends one request for each address of `url` and returns one
`response` record per address, in the order of the addresses. A list of
addresses is fetched with up to four requests at the same time. With
`extract: tables` the command returns `row` records instead, one per row of
each selected table.

An address without a scheme is requested with `https://`, and the report
carries the note `scheme_assumed`. Host names are converted to Punycode, and
IPv4 addresses written in decimal, octal or hexadecimal form are converted to
dotted form before the request. Only the schemes `http` and `https` are
accepted.

A status of 400 or above is a result, not an error: the status is the field
`status` of the record. Redirects with the statuses 301, 302, 303, 307 and 308
are followed up to `max_redirects`; the addresses passed are listed in
`redirects` and the last one is `final_url`. A redirect to another host drops
the headers `Authorization`, `Cookie` and `Proxy-Authorization`. A redirect
from `https` to `http` is not followed: the request fails with `E_NETWORK` and
the problem `scheme_downgrade`, and `follow_redirects: false` returns the
redirect itself. A `303` turns a request into a `get` unless it is a `head`,
which is sent again as a `head`. With
`retries`, a request that fails to connect, is reset, or receives the status
429 or a status of 500 and above is sent again after a pause; `Retry-After`
sets the pause when the server gives one. Requests with the methods `post` and
`patch` are not sent again.

Bodies of the types `gzip` and `deflate` are decompressed. The character set
of a text body is taken from, in order: `charset`, a byte order mark, the
`charset` parameter of `Content-Type`, a `<meta>` declaration of an HTML page
and detection from the bytes. A body that is not text, such as an image, can
only be written to a file with `save`.

With `as: text` or `as: markdown` an HTML page is converted to plain text or
Markdown. `main_only` keeps the main content and drops navigation, headers,
footers and forms; `links` and `images` select how links and images are
written. Markdown and plain text documents are returned in the same forms.
Parts of a page are selected with `section` (the content under one heading),
`find` (the paragraphs that match a pattern, with `find_context` paragraphs
around each) and `query` (the `query_limit` paragraphs most relevant to the
query, in document order). With `outline: auto`, a page longer than the
`max_chars` option of the call is returned as an outline: the title, the
length, the sections with their sizes, the start of the content and the path
of a file that holds the full content. `offset` skips characters of the
result; `total_chars` gives the length of the whole result.

The response cache keeps successful `get` responses of requests without own
headers. `cache: use` answers from a fresh cached response, `revalidate`
asks the server whether a cached response is still current with
`If-None-Match` and `If-Modified-Since`, and `only` answers from the cache
without any network access. `unchanged_since` takes the `etag` of an earlier
result; when the body is the same, the record has `unchanged: true` and an
empty body.

The console applies no network rules of its own. Every address, including
loopback and private addresses, is contacted. The check of a program
(`nurt_check`) lists every request in the `network` entry of its details with
the normalized address, host, port, scheme, proxy, header names, body kind,
cache mode and, for IP addresses, the address class. An embedding application
that controls network access can refuse connections before they are opened.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | `text \| list<text>` | required | Address, or several addresses with one result each. |
| `method` | `enum(get\|head\|post\|put\|patch\|delete\|options)` | `get` | HTTP method. |
| `headers` | `map<text>` | none | Request headers. |
| `body` | `text \| path` | none | Request body as text or from a file. |
| `json` | `any` | none | Value sent as a JSON body with the matching Content-Type header. |
| `save` | `path` | none | Write the response body to this file; the body of an answer with a status outside 200 to 299 is not written and the record has no `saved` field. |
| `as` | `enum(raw\|text\|markdown)` | `raw` | Return an HTML page unchanged, as plain text or as Markdown with an outline. |
| `extract` | `enum(content\|headers\|links\|headings\|meta\|tables)` | `content` | Part of the page returned: content, headers, links, headings, metadata or tables. |
| `table` | `int` | `0` | Number of the table returned with extract set to tables, counted from 1; 0 returns all tables. |
| `main_only` | `bool` | `true` | Keep only the main content of the page when converting to text or Markdown. |
| `links` | `enum(inline\|list\|none)` | `inline` | Keep links inline, collect them in a list, or drop them when converting. |
| `images` | `enum(drop\|alt)` | `alt` | Drop images or keep their alternative text when converting. |
| `section` | `text` | none | Return only the section under the heading with this text. |
| `outline` | `enum(auto\|always\|never)` | `auto` | Return an outline of a long page before its content. |
| `query` | `text` | none | Return only the paragraphs of the page most relevant to this query. |
| `query_limit` | `int` | `5` | Maximum number of paragraphs returned for query, from 1 to 20. |
| `find` | `regex` | none | Return only the paragraphs that match this pattern. |
| `find_context` | `int` | `1` | Number of paragraphs of context around each paragraph matched by find, up to 10. |
| `links_filter` | `regex` | none | Only links whose address matches this pattern, with extract set to links. |
| `same_host` | `bool` | `false` | Only links to the same host, with extract set to links. |
| `charset` | `text` | `"auto"` | Character set used to decode the body. |
| `offset` | `int` | `0` | Number of characters of the body to skip. |
| `cache` | `enum(bypass\|use\|revalidate\|only)` | `bypass` | Ignore the response cache, use it, revalidate cached responses, or answer only from the cache without the network. |
| `unchanged_since` | `text` | none | Etag of a known version; an unchanged response returns no body. |
| `timeout` | `duration` | `30s` | Time limit of the request. |
| `follow_redirects` | `bool` | `true` | Follow redirects. |
| `max_redirects` | `int` | `10` | Maximum number of redirects followed. |
| `verify_tls` | `bool` | `true` | Verify the TLS certificate of the server. |
| `retries` | `int` | `0` | Number of retries after a connection failure. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `response` |

The `response` record has the fields `url`, `status`, `headers` (names in
lower case; repeated headers joined with `, `, `set-cookie` as a list),
`body`, `bytes`, `elapsed`, `final_url`, `saved`, `content_type`, `charset`,
`truncated`, `offset`, `total_chars`, `redirects`, `from_cache`, `unchanged`,
`etag`, `last_modified` and `remote_address`. `etag` is the first 12
hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the returned body. A `row` record holds
the cells of one table row by column name, the row number `no` and the table
number `table`.

The text form of the result shows the columns `url`, `status`, `bytes`,
`content_type` and `elapsed`, and never the body. The body and the other
fields stay in the JSON form and appear in the text with verbosity `detailed`
or when the request names them in `fields`, for example `fields: ["status",
"body"]`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | Methods get, head and options only read; other methods change the remote side and are irreversible; a file written by save is reversible. |

| Action | Effect | Reversibility | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `post` | `external` | `irreversible` | Applies when method is post. |
| `put` | `external` | `irreversible` | Applies when method is put. |
| `patch` | `external` | `irreversible` | Applies when method is patch. |
| `delete` | `external` | `irreversible` | Applies when method is delete. |
| `save` | `local` | `reversible` | Applies to the file written when save is given. |

## Examples

Fetch a documentation page as Markdown:

```nurt example
http.request "https://docs.example.com/install" as: markdown
```

```text expected
# Installation
```

Return the three paragraphs of a page most relevant to a question:

```nurt example
http.request "https://docs.example.com/guide" as: text query: "proxy configuration" query_limit: 3
```

Save a release archive to a file:

```nurt example
http.request "https://example.com/releases/app.tar.gz" save: "/srv/downloads/app.tar.gz"
```

Read one section of a page from the cache filled by an earlier request:

```nurt example
http.request "https://docs.example.com/guide" as: markdown section: "Upgrade" cache: use
```

Send a JSON body and require a successful status:

```nurt example
http.request "https://api.example.com/items" method: post json: {name: "demo"} |> assert all: status < 400
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_ARG` | An address is not valid, parameters conflict (`problem: param_conflict`), a count is out of range, `offset` is past the end of the result, or `save` or a changing method is used where only reading is allowed. | Correct the address or remove the conflicting parameter. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` | A parameter has a value outside its enumeration. | Use one of the listed values. |
| `E_TYPE` | A parameter has a value of another type. | Give a value of the type in the table. |
| `E_REGEX` | The pattern of `find` or `links_filter` is not valid. | Correct the pattern. |
| `E_NETWORK` | The request failed. `problem` tells why: `dns`, `connect`, `reset`, `tls`, `proxy`, `redirect_limit`, `scheme_downgrade`, `bad_location`, `protocol`, `decode` or `denied`. | Check the address, the proxy and the certificate, or raise `max_redirects`. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The request did not finish within `timeout`. | Raise `timeout`. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The program was cancelled during the request. | Run the program again. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | `cache: only` found no cached response, the page has no section `section`, or the page has fewer tables than `table`. | Fetch the page with `cache: use` first, or use a section or table from `expected`. |
| `E_BINARY` | The body is not text. | Write the body to a file with `save`. |
| `E_CONFIG` | The file of `http.ca_file` cannot be read. | Correct the setting. |

## Related

`http.download`, `network.resolve`, `undo`, `help group: "network"`.

title: info
text:
# info

## Synopsis

```text
info <path>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

`info` produces one `entry` record per path, in the order given. A path that
does not exist, or whose parent is not a directory, gives an entry with
`exists: false`, `size` zero and the Unix epoch as `modified`; it is not an
error.

An existing entry carries the path and name fields, `type`, `size`, the
times, `mode` in octal, `readonly`, `hidden`, `links`, `etag`, the account
(`owner`) and group of the file, `acl`, `xattrs`, `streams`, `volume` and
`file_id`. A link is described without being followed; `link_target` holds
the target as stored in the link and `real_path` the path after resolving
links, when the target exists.

A regular file, and a link that resolves to one, also carries `mime`,
`binary`, `encoding`, `line_ending` and `bom`, recognised from the first
8192 bytes of the content. The media type comes from the signature of the
content, then, for text, from the file name; otherwise it is `text/plain`
or `application/octet-stream`.

`lines`, `hash` and the `details` groups read more of the content and are
computed only when requested. Files larger than the text limit of the
execution get no line count and no `text`, `pdf` or `symbols` details.

An entry whose entity tag equals the one given for its path in `known` is
reported with the path, name, type, size, times, mode and `etag` only, and
an `unchanged` notable entry names the path.

With no path the result is empty.

`owner` and `group` hold the name and the numeric identifier, as in
`user (1000)`, on Linux and macOS; the names come from the account tables of
the system, and an account without an entry there is shown by its
identifier. On Windows `owner` holds the security identifier of the account
and `group` is absent.

`acl` lists the POSIX ACL in the short form of `getfacl` on Linux (for
example `user:alice:r--`) and the entries of the access control list on
macOS; on Windows it is absent. Values of extended attributes that are not
UTF-8 text are written as `"hex:"` followed by hexadecimal digits.

`created` is present where the system reports a creation time.

The groups `git` and `symbols` need the repository and code services of the
engine. Without the service the group is left out and a `source_unavailable`
notable entry names the missing service once per call; a file in a language
without a grammar has no `symbols` group.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `list<path>` | required | Paths to describe; a missing path gives exists: false. |
| `hash` | `enum(none\|sha256\|sha512\|sha1\|md5\|blake3\|crc32)` | `none` | Hash algorithm of the content. |
| `details` | `list<enum(text\|exif\|pdf\|media\|git\|symbols)>` | `[]` | Additional groups of metadata. |
| `known` | `map<text>` | none | Map from path to etag; unchanged paths are reported without details. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `entry`, `registry_value` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Describe one file:

```nurt example
info "/home/user/notes.txt"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/notes.txt", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "line one\nline two\n" }
] }
```

Describe an existing and a missing path; the second entry has
`exists: false`:

```nurt example
info "/home/user/notes.txt" "/home/user/draft.txt"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/notes.txt", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "line one\nline two\n" }
] }
```

Add the SHA-256 hash and the number of lines:

```nurt example
info "/home/user/notes.txt" hash: sha256 details: [text]
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/notes.txt", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "line one\nline two\n" }
] }
```

Describe a link; `link_target` and `real_path` name the file it points to:

```nurt example
info "/home/user/current"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/notes.txt", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "line one\nline two\n" },
  { "path": "/home/user/current", "type": "symlink", "target": "/home/user/notes.txt" }
] }
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_PATH_RELATIVE` | a relative path without a base directory | give an absolute path or set the `base` option |
| `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` | an unknown hash algorithm or `details` group | use a value listed in the parameter table |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | a value of `known` is not an etag | pass the `etag` field of an entry read earlier |
| `E_TYPE` | a parameter has a value of another type | pass a list of names to `details` and a map to `known` |
| `E_PERMISSION` | the metadata or content of an entry cannot be read | check the permissions of the entry and its parents |
| `E_IO` | reading the file system failed | repeat the call; check the volume |

## Related

`list`, `find`, `read`, `hash`, `attributes`.

title: insert
text:
# insert

## Synopsis

```text
insert <text> in: <path> [name: value]...
line|match|node|entry |> insert <text> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`insert` adds lines to text files. The source form inserts into the file
`in`: before or after `line` with `position: before` or `after`, and at the
start or the end of the file with `position: start` or `end`. Without
`line`, `before` inserts at the start and `after` at the end of the file.

The stage form inserts at every input record. A `line` or `match` record
names its line, and `before` or `after` places the text before or after that
line; `start` and `end` insert once at the start or end of every file named
by the records. An `entry` record names a whole file: `before` and `start`
insert at its start, `after` and `end` at its end. Several records of one
line insert the text once.

All insertions into one file are placed against the file as read: the line
numbers of the input do not move because of earlier insertions, and
insertions at the same place keep the order of the input. The inserted
lines take the line endings of the file. Text inserted at the end of a file
without a final line break leaves the file without one unless
`ensure_newline` is set. A file keeps its encoding and byte order mark.
Empty input changes nothing and is reported as `nothing_matched`. A line
outside the file fails with `E_OUT_OF_RANGE` and changes nothing.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | `text` | required | Text to insert. |
| `in` | `path` | required | File in the source form. |
| `line` | `int` | none | Line number in the source form. |
| `position` | `enum(before\|after\|start\|end)` | `after` | Place of the text relative to the line, match or file. |
| `ensure_newline` | `bool` | `false` | End the inserted text with a line ending. |
| `validate` | `enum(off\|warn\|reject)` | `reject` | Roll back a change that adds a new syntax error to a known format. |
| `if_match` | `text` | none | Expected etag of the file. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `none` | `effect` |
| `stage` | `line`, `match`, `node`, `entry` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Insert an import before the first line of a file:

```nurt example
insert "use std::fmt;" in: "/home/user/app/src/lib.rs" line: 1 position: before
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/src/lib.rs", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "pub mod parse;\n" }
] }
```

Insert a comment before the line of every match of a search:

```nurt example
search "fn main" "/home/user/app/src/main.rs" |> insert "// Entry point of the program." position: before
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/src/main.rs", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "fn helper() {}\n\nfn main() {\n    helper();\n}\n" }
] }
```

Append a line at the end of a file:

```nurt example
insert "export PATH=\"$HOME/bin:$PATH\"" in: "/home/user/.profile" position: end
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/.profile", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "umask 022\n" }
] }
```

Add a header comment to every listed file:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app/src" glob: "*.rs" |> insert "// Part of the parser." position: start
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/src/a.rs", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "fn a() {}\n" },
  { "path": "/home/user/app/src/b.rs", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "fn b() {}\n" }
] }
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_OUT_OF_RANGE` | the line lies outside the file | give a line from 1 to the number of lines |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | the source form has no `in` | name the file with `in` |
| `E_STALE` | the file changed since it was read, or does not have the `if_match` tag | read the file again and repeat the change |
| `E_BINARY` | the file is binary | insert into text files only |
| `E_ENCODING` | the encoding of the file cannot represent the text | convert the file with `convert` first |
| `E_ROLLED_BACK` | the insertion added a syntax error and `validate` is `reject` | correct the text or pass `validate: warn` |

## Related

`edit`, `replace`, `write`, `lines`, `search`.

title: jobs
text:
# jobs

## Synopsis

```text
jobs [<id>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

Every program started by `run`, `retry`, `test.*` and `analyze.*` is a job
from its start and has an identifier `j1`, `j2`, … that is never reused in
the state directory. A program that is still running after the `wait` of its
command continues in the background; `jobs` reads its state, its output and
its final result.

Without `id` the command lists all jobs: running and suspended jobs first,
then finished jobs, each group in the order of the identifiers. `state`
selects jobs in one state.

With `id` the command returns one job record, filled according to `view`:

* `status`: the state, the elapsed time and the last 5 lines of each output
  stream;
* `output`: the complete lines written after the cursor `since`, or the whole
  output without `since`; `output_cursor` of the result is the cursor for the
  next read. `stream`, `head`, `tail`, `filter`, `context` and `dedupe`
  select the lines; the cursor of a stream left out by `stream` stays where it
  was, so a later read of that stream misses no line;
* `result`: the final record of a finished job (`exit_code`, `signal`,
  `elapsed`, `changes`, `op`, output files) with the kept output selected by
  the same parameters. For a job of `test.*` or `analyze.*` the stream header
  holds the final record of the tool, a `test_run` or an `analysis`.

`wait` blocks the call until the job ends or the duration elapses, whichever
is first; the job record is then returned as it is.

A job whose supervising process ended without finishing it has the state
`lost`: its program may still run, but nothing records its output or
changes. The state is determined at every read: each supervised job holds a
lock that the operating system releases when the supervising process ends,
however it ends.

Finished jobs whose end is older than `output.spool_ttl` are removed with
their output when jobs are listed and when the supervisor starts. Running
jobs are never removed.

`remove` on `job` records deletes finished jobs: the entry of each job in
the job table and its kept output in the state directory. Job entries and
their output are internal state of the console, not user files, so the
removal adds no journal entry, cannot be undone and is not marked
irreversible. Jobs in the states `exited`, `failed`, `stopped`, `timed_out`,
`stalled`, `limit` and `lost` can be removed; for a `lost` job only the
entry and the output are deleted, and a program that still runs is not
signalled. A job in the state `running` or `suspended` is refused with
`E_JOB_STATE`; `stop` ends it first. The input is checked as a whole before
the first job is deleted. Each removed job yields one `effect` record with
`kind` and `action` `remove`, `target` `job:<id>` and the last `job` record.
A removed identifier is not reused, and a later reference to it fails with
`E_UNKNOWN_JOB`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `text` | none | Job identifier, such as j7. |
| `state` | `enum(any\|running\|suspended\|exited\|failed\|stopped\|timed_out\|stalled\|limit\|lost)` | `any` | State of the jobs to list. |
| `head` | `int` | none | Number of first output lines returned. |
| `tail` | `int` | none | Number of last output lines returned. |
| `stream` | `enum(both\|stdout\|stderr)` | `both` | Output stream to read. |
| `since` | `text` | none | Cursor of an earlier read; only newer output is returned. |
| `wait` | `duration` | `0s` | Time to wait for the job to finish. |
| `view` | `enum(status\|output\|result)` | `status` | State, output, or final result of the job. |
| `filter` | `regex` | none | Return only output lines that match. |
| `context` | `int` | `0` | Lines of context around lines matching filter. |
| `dedupe` | `bool` | `false` | Collapse repeated identical output lines. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `job` |

Source only. Produces `job` records.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

List the running jobs.

```nurt example
jobs state: running
```

```text expected
j7  running  cargo build
```

Read the output of job `j7` written after an earlier read.

```nurt example
jobs "j7" view: output since: "120.4"
```

Wait up to one minute for job `j7` and return its final record.

```nurt example
jobs "j7" view: result wait: 60s
```

Remove all jobs that exited with code 0, together with their output.

```nurt example
jobs state: exited |> remove
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_UNKNOWN_JOB` | No job has the identifier. | Use one of the identifiers in `candidates`. |
| `E_JOB_STATE` | `view: result` on a job that still runs. | Add `wait:` or read `view: status`. |
| `E_JOB_STATE` | `remove` on a job that is running or suspended. | End the job with `stop`, then remove it. |
| `E_CONFIG` | The engine has no state directory. | Configure the state directory of the engine. |

## Related

`run`, `retry`, `stop`, `suspend`, `resume`, `remove`.

title: journal.limits
text:
# journal.limits

## Synopsis

```text
journal.limits [name: value]...
```

## Description

`journal.limits` shows the limits that decide how long the journal keeps
entries, or changes them. Without `steps`, `age` and `size` the command only
reads: it reports the effective limits of every volume, or of the volume that
contains `volume`, together with the configuration level that set each of
them.

An entry expires when any of three limits is exceeded:

| Limit | Key | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `steps` | `journal.max_ops` | entry `n` expires when the number of later changing operations reaches the limit; a bulk operation, an undo and a redo count as one operation each |
| `age` | `journal.max_age` | entry expires when its age reaches the limit; the age is measured by `journal.age_clock` |
| `size` | `journal.max_size` | when the bytes held on a volume exceed the budget, the oldest entries expire until the bytes held fit |

`unlimited` switches a limit off. Free space for the user is protected in
every case: the journal never keeps data below the space reserve of a volume.

Each limit is resolved on its own from seven levels, in increasing
precedence: built-in defaults, the system file, the user file, the project
file `.nurt.toml` (only for a trusted project), the file named by
`NURT_CONFIG`, the `NURT_JOURNAL_*` environment variables and run-time
settings made by this command. `journal.volume."<mount>".*` takes precedence
over the general key of the same level.

A protection floor, `journal.floor.max_ops` and `journal.floor.max_age`, is
set by an administrator in the system file or by an embedding application.
A lower value from any level, including this command, is raised to the floor
and reported with `raised_to_floor`. Values from a project file are raised to
at least 10 steps and 5 minutes.

Lowering a limit takes effect at once: the entries over the new limit expire
during the call, oldest first. Raising a limit never brings back entries that
