## Description

`program.search` ranks the cards of the program index against a query and emits the best `program_card` records with their `score`, highest first. It starts a pipeline and accepts no input.

The index merges the programs in `PATH`, the package databases (dpkg, rpm, pacman, Homebrew, winget, Scoop, Chocolatey), registered applications (desktop entries, Windows uninstall entries and application paths, macOS application bundles), the `NAME` lines of manual pages and the external catalogs of `programs.catalogs`. It works without configuration on the programs of the computer. The first call of a process builds the index; later calls reuse it while the files of every provider are unchanged. With `programs.index_dir` set, each provider is also kept in a cache file and a new process starts from it.

Query words are compared after folding: lower case, compatibility decomposition and no diacritics, so a query typed without diacritics matches a text with them. Common conjunctions and prepositions are ignored when other words remain. Each word scores 100 when it equals the program name, 40 when the name starts with it, 20 when the name contains it, 8 in the situations of use, 5 in the summary, 5 in the category and 3 in the guide description; a query whose every word is found somewhere gains 15. A word without any match is retried at half weight through the built-in table of synonyms, the synonyms of catalogs and a prefix stem of words of six characters or more. A program whose `not_for` entry covers every word of the query loses 30 points and gets the field `instead` with the program to use. Equal scores are ordered by provider priority and then by name. Results with no points are dropped.

A list of queries gives one ranked list per query; each record then has the field `query`.

`kind` keeps only programs, applications or standalone guides of the catalogs; the default `all` keeps every kind. `installed: true` keeps the programs that exist on this computer and `installed: false` the entries that do not; without it both are listed.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | `text \| list<text>` | required | Task, topic or program name, or several queries with one result list each. |
| `category` | `text` | none | Only programs in this category. |
| `source` | `list<enum(path\|package\|app\|catalog)>` | `[path, package, app, catalog]` | Sources searched. |
| `limit` | `int` | `15` | Maximum number of programs, best match first. |
| `kind` | `enum(all\|programs\|apps\|guides)` | `all` | Kind of results. |
| `installed` | `bool` | none | Only installed programs (true) or only catalog entries (false). |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `program_card` |

Each record carries the fields of `program_card` and the additional fields `score`, `kind` (`program`, `app` or `guide`), `has_guide`, `category_source` and, when they apply, `query`, `instead`, `guide_name`, `guide_shared_with`, `overview`, `alternatives`, `catalog_path`, `manager`, `app_id` and `language`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

Providers that cannot be read, and providers cut by the time budget of the index, are reported as warnings (`source_unavailable`, `index_partial`); the command still returns the results of the other providers.

## Examples

Find programs for a task.

```nurt example
program.search "convert video" limit: 5
```

```text expected
name     category  summary
ffmpeg   video     Converts and streams audio and video.
handbrake video    Transcodes video files.
```

Search only the installed packages and the search path.

```nurt example
program.search "pdf merge" source: [path, package] |> select name path score
```

Run two queries at once and keep the best match of each.

```nurt example
program.search ["compress files", "edit images"] limit: 1 |> select query name
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | No query was given. | Pass a query. |
| `E_ARG` | A query is shorter than 2 or longer than 200 characters. | Shorten or extend the query. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `limit` is outside 1 to 60, more than 8 queries were given, or the category is unknown; `candidates` lists the nearest categories. | Correct the value, or list the categories with `program.catalog`. |
| `E_CATALOG` | `source` names a program catalog that is not configured or cannot be read. | Check `programs.catalogs`. |

## Related

`program.describe`, `program.catalog`, `program.find`.

title: query
text:
# query

## Synopsis

```text
content|entry|item|response |> query <expression>
query <expression> path: <path>
```

## Description

`query` applies a filter in `jq` syntax to documents and produces one `item`
record per result. Filters are compiled and run in-process; the `jq` program
is not needed.

In the source form the document is the file `path`. In the stage form every
input record supplies the value given to the filter:

| Input | Value given to the filter |
|---|---|
| `content` | the text read as a document of its format; JSON when no format is recognised |
| `entry` | the file of the entry read as a document, from `raw_path` when the entry has it (a name that is not valid Unicode); entries other than files are refused |
| `item` | the value of the item; result keys extend the key of the item |
| `response` | the body read as a document; JSON when the content type names JSON or no format is recognised |

Every supported document format is read into the same value model: maps,
lists, text, numbers, booleans and null. Dates and times are text in RFC 3339
form, binary data is Base64 text, and numbers keep their exact digits when
the binary form would change them. A multi-document YAML stream gives one
value per document.

A result that the filter selects by a path, such as `.spec.replicas` or
`.items[]`, gets the canonical key path of its position in the document as
`key`, so that `set` and `remove` can change it. Other results, such as
`length` or an object built by the filter, get the key `"."`. The identity
filter on a whole document gives the key `$`. `value_type` is the type of the
result value; `path`, `format` and `etag` are those of the input.

A filter given as a constant is compiled when the program is bound, before
any document is read. A filter that does not compile fails with `E_QUERY`
and the line and column of the problem in `details`. A runtime error of the
filter, including `error(…)`, fails with `E_QUERY` after the results produced
before it, with the file in `at`. `halt` ends the filter; `halt_error` fails
with `E_QUERY` and the text written by the filter.

`env` and `$ENV` read the environment of the session, `now` reads the clock
of the session, and `debug` and `stderr` write log events. `input`,
`inputs` and modules are not available.

The filter language follows `jq` 1.8.1. A string multiplied by a number, a
deletion of several paths, an update below `null` or past the end of a list, a
fractional list index, the index of an object by a number, the slice of `null`,
`@base64d`, `repeat` and `fromstream` give the results of `jq` 1.8.1. Two
results differ from it:

| Case | `query` | `jq` 1.8.1 |
|---|---|---|
| `captures` of `match` | groups that did not take part are omitted | groups that did not take part are `null` |
| `@base32`, `@base32d` | the filter does not compile | runtime error |

An update that extends a list, and a string made by multiplying a string, are
limited in size by `limits.max_file_bytes_text`; a larger result fails with
`E_LIMIT`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expression` | `text` | required | Filter in jq syntax. |
| `path` | `path` | none | Document to query in the source form. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `stage` | `content`, `entry`, `item`, `response` | `item` |
| `source` | `none` | `item` |

Results are produced while the filter runs. A pipeline that uses only the
first results stops the filter.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `transform` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

List the dependency names of a package manifest:

```nurt example
query ".dependencies | keys[]" path: "/home/user/app/package.json"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/package.json", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "{\n  \"name\": \"app\",\n  \"dependencies\": {\n    \"react\": \"^19.0.0\",\n    \"zod\": \"^3.24.0\"\n  }\n}\n" }
] }
```

Select the images of a YAML file read by `read`:

```nurt example
read "/home/user/app/compose.yaml" |> query ".services[].image"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/compose.yaml", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "services:\n  web:\n    image: nginx:1.27\n  db:\n    image: postgres:17\n" }
] }
```

```text expected
nginx:1.27
```

Raise every replica count by one through the keys of the results:

```nurt example
query ".deployments[] | select(.replicas < 3) | .replicas" path: "/home/user/app/scale.json" |> set (value + 1)
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/scale.json", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "{\"deployments\": [{\"name\": \"api\", \"replicas\": 2}, {\"name\": \"worker\", \"replicas\": 5}]}\n" }
] }
```

Count the sections of a TOML file:

```nurt example
query "[.[] | objects] | length" path: "/home/user/app/config.toml"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/config.toml", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "[server]\nport = 8080\n\n[database]\nurl = \"postgres://localhost/app\"\n" }
] }
```

A response that leaves records out ends with the hint "more: next" and carries the field
`continuation`; the command `next` returns the next part without running the
command again.

```text
matched 700  shown 50  more: next
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_QUERY` | the filter does not compile (`problem`: `syntax`, `undefined`, `module`), fails while it runs (`runtime`), or ends with `halt_error` (`halt`) | correct the filter; `details` holds the line and column of a compile error |
| `E_DOC_PARSE` | the document is not valid in its format, or a text without a recognised format is not JSON | correct the document or read it with the right format |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | the file does not exist | check the path |
| `E_IO` | the file cannot be read | see the message |
| `E_BINARY` | the content record holds binary data | query text documents only |
| `E_TYPE` | an input record is of another kind, or an entry is not a file | pass `content`, `entry`, `item` or `response` records |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | the source form has no `path` | add `path:` |
| `E_STALE` | the file changed while it was read | run the command again |
| `E_LIMIT` | the filter produces more results than one execution may hold, multiplies a string into a result longer than `limits.max_file_bytes_text` bytes (`"x" * n`), or the file is larger than the document size limit | narrow the filter, use `limit(n; f)`, or raise the limit |
| `E_CANCELLED` | the execution was cancelled or its time limit passed, including inside endless generators such as `repeat` | run the command again with a narrower filter |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | the execution was cancelled or its time limit passed, including inside endless generators such as `repeat` | run the command again with a narrower filter |

## Related

`read` with `key:` for values at key paths, `set` to change the values found
by `query`, `sql` for SQLite databases.

title: read
text:
# read

## Synopsis

```text
read <path>... (path: <list<path>> | targets: <list<map<any>>>) [name: value]...
entry |> read [name: value]...
```

## Description

The command reads files and produces one `content` record per file, or
`item` records when `key` is given. In the source form the files are the
paths given, in order, or the maps of `targets`; each map names a `path` and
at most one selector of its own. In the stage form the files are those of the
input `entry` records; directories and special entries among them are
skipped.

A file is decoded in the encoding detected for it, or in the encoding given
with `encoding`. Content that is not text in any supported encoding fails
with `E_BINARY` unless `view: hex` is given. The `etag` field of the record
carries the SHA-256 hash of the file bytes and can be passed to `if_match` of
the changing commands.

Lines count from 1 and end at a line feed; a carriage return before the line
feed belongs to the line ending. `search` counts lines the same way. The text
of the record keeps the original line endings.

A call takes at most one selector:

| Selector | Result |
|---|---|
| none | the whole text |
| `lines` | the lines of one or more ranges, in the order given; overlapping ranges are merged into the place of the first of them; the end of a range beyond the last line is reduced to the last line, and a range that starts after it fails with `E_OUT_OF_RANGE` |
| `last` | the last lines; the whole text when the file is shorter |
| `around` | the lines of every match of the text or regular expression with `context` lines before and after; spans that overlap or touch are merged |
| `section` | a Markdown section: its ATX or Setext heading and the lines up to the next heading of the same or a higher level; nested headings are joined with ` > `; headings in fenced code are ignored, and emphasis, code and link markers are ignored when headings are compared |
| `symbol` | the definition of a code symbol; a qualified name such as `Server.start` narrows the container |
| `key` | `item` records of the values at a key path of a structured document, expanded to `depth` levels |
| `cell` | one cell of a notebook, by index from 0 or by identifier |

The record has `range` for one span of lines and `ranges` for none or
several. `total_lines` is the number of lines of the file and `lines` the
number of lines in `text`.

Files with the extension `.ipynb` are read as notebooks: the record has the
cells in `cells` and their sources in `text`.

`view` selects what the record holds: `full` the text; `header` the metadata
without text; `outline` the symbols of the file in `symbols` and one indented
line per symbol in `text`; `symbols` the symbols without text;
`outline_first` the symbols and the text of the selection. `header`,
`outline` and `symbols` take no selector. Without code analysis, or when no
grammar recognises the file, the views, `symbol` and `key` return the whole
text and report the notable effect `semantic_fallback`.

Conditional reads avoid sending text that is already known. Each of
`unchanged_since`, `since` and the values of `known` is an etag, a content
hash `sha256:…` or at least 8 leading hexadecimal digits of one. With
`unchanged_since` a file that still has that version gives a record with
`unchanged: true` and no text. With `since` the record holds the hunks of the
difference against that version in `diff`, without text, when the version is
in the read cache; otherwise it holds the text and `since_missing: true`.
Every text read stores the text in the cache, which keeps 64 MiB for one
hour. Files named in `known` that still have the given version are left out
of the result.

`max_line` cuts longer lines after that many characters and appends
`[N characters omitted]`; the record then has `truncated: true` and the
notable effect `truncated_lines` gives the number of lines cut.

### PDF documents

A file that starts with `%PDF-` is a PDF document, also when it consists of
ASCII characters only; a named `encoding` reads its source as text. A PDF
document gives one `content` record per page, with the page number in
`page` and the number of pages of the document in `pages_total`. `pages`
selects pages as one or more ranges, read in the order given; the end of a
range beyond the last page is reduced to the last page, and a range that
starts beyond it fails with `E_OUT_OF_RANGE`. `mode: text` extracts words and
lines in reading order; `mode: layout` places every word at its horizontal
position on a character grid, which keeps columns and tables aligned.
`mode: images` requires the PDFium library and fails with
`E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` in builds without it. `view: header` gives one record
with `pages_total` and no text. A document that requires a password fails
with `E_ENCRYPTED`; a document encrypted only to restrict printing or copying
is read. Text comes from the fonts of the document, so pages that carry text
only as images give empty text. Selectors of lines do not apply to documents
and fail with `E_UNSUPPORTED`.

### Images

An image gives one record with `binary: true`, empty `text` and `image`: the
media type in `mime`, the width and height in pixels, read from the image
header without decoding the pixels, and the bytes of the file in `data`.
`view: header` reads only the header and leaves out `data`. Types recognised
without a decoder, such as HEIF, have no dimensions.

### Hexadecimal dump

`view: hex` dumps the bytes of any file in the layout of `xxd`: the offset of
the row as eight or more hexadecimal digits, a colon, 16 bytes in groups of
two and the same bytes as ASCII, with `.` for bytes outside the printable
range. Each row is one line of `text`; `lines`, `last` and `pages` select
rows, counted from 1, and `total_lines` is the number of rows. Rows of a file
are read by position, so a range of a large file reads only that range. The
text of one dump is limited to the text limit and fails with `E_LIMIT` above
it.

### Compressed files

With `decompress: auto` a file whose name ends with `.gz`, `.zst`, `.xz` or
`.bz2`, or with `.tgz`, `.tzst`, `.txz` or `.tbz2`, and whose content starts
with the signature of the same format is decompressed while it is read. The
decompressed content is read as text, as a PDF document or as an image, and
`view: hex` dumps the decompressed bytes. The records keep the `path` and
the `etag` of the compressed file and name it in `decompressed_from`; the
notable effect `decompressed` is reported. Decompressed content larger than
the text limit fails with `E_LIMIT`, so a small file that expands without
bound is stopped. `decompress: none` reads the compressed bytes. With
`since`, the earlier text of a compressed file is found only in the read
cache shared by the session.

Records of PDF documents, images and dumps have `encoding: binary`,
`bom: false` and `line_ending: none`. Their `etag` carries the content hash
when the whole file was read, which is not the case for dumps and image
headers. `unchanged_since` and `known` apply to them; `since` returns the
content with `since_missing: true`.

### Encoding detection

With `encoding: auto` the signatures of binary formats are checked first: a
file that starts with `%PDF-` is a PDF document, a file read with
`decompress: auto` whose name and signature agree on a compression format is
decompressed, and a file that starts with the signature of an image is an
image unless its leading bytes are plain ASCII text. The first 64 KiB of any
other file decide its encoding, in this order: a byte order mark selects UTF-8, UTF-16 LE or UTF-16 BE; valid UTF-8
without NUL characters is UTF-8; content in which one code unit in ten or
more has a zero high byte is UTF-16 without a byte order mark; a NUL byte
makes the content binary; otherwise a statistical detector proposes a legacy
encoding, and the encodings of the configuration key `text.legacy_encodings`
(`windows-1250`, `ibm852`, `iso-8859-2` and `windows-1252` by default)
replace the proposal when one of them reads the content as Polish text.
Content with more than one control character in twenty characters is binary.

- The legacy encodings detected are `windows-1250`, `ibm852`, `iso-8859-2`
  and `windows-1252`. Content in another code page, such as `windows-1251`,
  is read in the most plausible of them.
- Samples shorter than 200 bytes contain few letters outside ASCII, so the
  choice between legacy encodings is less certain for them; give `encoding`
  for such files.
- UTF-16 without a byte order mark is recognised only for text in which at
  least one character in ten lies in the range U+0000 to U+00FF, such as
  text in Latin script; other UTF-16 text without a byte order mark is
  binary.
- A PDF document that consists of ASCII characters only is read as a PDF
  document; a named `encoding` reads its source as text.
- Image signatures that consist of ASCII letters, such as `BM` and `GIF`,
  do not apply to plain ASCII text, so a text file that starts with them is
  read as text.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `list<path>` | one of `target` | Files to read. |
| `lines` | `range \| list<range>` | none | Line ranges to read. |
| `last` | `int` | none | Number of last lines to read. |
| `around` | `text \| regex` | none | Read the lines around matches of this pattern. |
| `context` | `int` | `3` | Lines of context around matches of around. |
| `symbol` | `text` | none | Read the definition of this code symbol. |
| `section` | `text` | none | Read the Markdown section with this heading. |
| `cell` | `int \| text` | none | Notebook cell by index or identifier. |
| `targets` | `list<map<any>>` | one of `target` | Selectors per target: path, lines, around, symbol, key, section, cell. |
| `key` | `key` | none | Key path in a structured document; the result is item records. |
| `depth` | `int` | none | Depth of nested values read at key. |
| `view` | `enum(full\|outline\|outline_first\|symbols\|header\|hex)` | `full` | Full content, outline, symbols, header or hexadecimal dump. |
| `pages` | `range \| list<range>` | none | PDF pages to read. |
| `mode` | `enum(text\|layout\|images)` | `text` | Extraction mode of PDF pages. |
| `encoding` | `text` | `"auto"` | Text encoding; auto detects it. |
| `decompress` | `enum(auto\|none)` | `auto` | Read compressed files after decompressing them on the fly. |
| `unchanged_since` | `text` | none | Etag; an unchanged file is returned without text. |
| `since` | `text` | none | Etag of an earlier read; the result holds the differences since then. |
| `known` | `map<text>` | none | Map from path to etag; unchanged files are skipped. |
| `line_numbers` | `bool` | `false` | Prefix lines with their numbers. |
| `max_line` | `int` | no limit | Maximum length of a returned line in characters; longer lines are cut and marked. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `none` | `content`, `item` |
| `stage` | `entry` | `content`, `item` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Read the lines around the start of `main` with three lines of context and
line numbers.

```nurt example
read "/srv/app/main.go" around: /func main/ context: 3 line_numbers: true
```

```text expected
41  func helper() {}
42  
43  // main starts the server.
44  func main() {
45  	helper()
46  }
47  
```

Read the file again only when it changed since the version with the content
hash starting with `1a2b3c4d`.

```nurt example
read "/srv/app/main.go" unchanged_since: "1a2b3c4d"
```

```text expected
unchanged: true
```

Read several line ranges; the overlapping ranges `5..8` and `7..10` are
merged in the place of the first.

```nurt example
read "/srv/app/CHANGELOG.md" lines: [5..8, 1..2, 7..10]
```

```text expected
ranges: [5..10, 1..2]
```

Read the subsection `Linux` of the section `Install` of a Markdown file.

```nurt example
read "/srv/app/README.md" section: "Install > Linux"
```

```text expected
### Linux

apt install app

```

Read the last two lines of a log.

```nurt example
read "/var/log/app.log" last: 2
```

```text expected
request 2
stop
```

Read pages 2 and 3 of a PDF document.

```nurt example
read "/srv/docs/report.pdf" pages: 2..3
```

```text expected
page: 2, pages_total: 3
Revenue grew in the third quarter.
page: 3, pages_total: 3
Costs fell by four percent.
```

Dump the first two rows of the bytes of an executable.

```nurt example
read "/srv/app/bin/app" view: hex lines: 1..2
```

```text expected
00000000: 7f45 4c46 0201 0100 0000 0000 0000 0000  .ELF............
00000010: 0300 3e00 0100 0000 4010 0000 0000 0000  ..>.....@.......
```

Read the last line of a compressed log.

```nurt example
read "/var/log/app.log.gz" last: 1
```

```text expected
stop
decompressed_from: /var/log/app.log.gz
```

Read the type and dimensions of an image without its data.

```nurt example
read "/srv/site/logo.png" view: header
```

```text expected
image: {mime: image/png, width: 64, height: 32}
```

A response that leaves lines out ends with the hint "more: next" and carries the field
`continuation`; the command `next` returns the next part without running the
command again.

```text
shown 50  more: next
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The file does not exist. | Check the path, for example with `find`. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The file cannot be read. | Read a file the account may read. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | A directory or special file was given, a line number is below 1, `last` or `max_line` is below 1, a value is not an etag, or `cell` was given for a file that is not a notebook. | Give a file, or a valid value. |
| `E_OUT_OF_RANGE` | A range of `lines` starts after the last line of the file, which includes every range of an empty file, or the index of `cell` is not below the number of cells. `found` holds the range and `actual` the number of lines or cells. | Use lines from 1 to `total_lines`, or a cell index below `actual`. |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | More than one selector, selectors both for the call and in `targets`, or a selector with `view: header`, `outline` or `symbols`. | Use one selector, or `view: outline_first`. |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | Neither `path` nor `targets`, or a target without `path`. | Give the files to read. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_FIELD` | A map of `targets` has an unknown key. | Use the keys listed in `expected`. |
| `E_BINARY` | The content is not text. | Read it with `view: hex`. |
| `E_ENCODING` | The content is not valid in the encoding given with `encoding`. | Use `encoding: auto` or the encoding of the file. |
| `E_LIMIT` | The text is larger than the text limit. | Search the file with `search`. |
| `E_REGEX` | The pattern of `around` is not a valid regular expression. | Correct the pattern. |
| `E_KEY_NOT_FOUND` | The section or key does not exist, or no cell has the identifier given with `cell`. | Use a heading listed in `expected`, or an existing key or cell identifier. |
| `E_SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND` | The file defines no such symbol. | List the symbols with `view: symbols`. |
| `E_SYMBOL_AMBIGUOUS` | The name denotes several symbols. | Qualify the name with its container. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE` | No grammar recognises the file given with `symbol`. | Read lines or a section instead. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | The file given with `key` is not a structured document of a known format. | Read lines instead. |
| `E_FORMAT` | A notebook is not valid JSON of the notebook format. | Read its text with `lines`, which does not parse the notebook. |

`last` larger than the number of lines gives the whole text, and `around`
without a match gives empty text; neither is an error.

### Errors of PDF documents, images, dumps and compressed files

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_OUT_OF_RANGE` | A range of `pages` starts after the last page of the document. | Use pages from 1 to `pages_total`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | A page or row number of `pages` is below 1. | Count pages and rows from 1. |
| `E_ENCRYPTED` | The PDF document requires a password. | Read a copy without a password. |
| `E_FORMAT` | The PDF document, the image header or the compressed data is damaged. | Check that the file is complete, or read it with `decompress: none` or `view: hex`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | `mode: images` was given in a build without the PDFium library. | Use `mode: text` or `mode: layout`. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | A selector of lines or a view of text was given for a PDF document or an image, or a selector other than `lines` and `last` with `view: hex`. | Select pages with `pages`, or rows with `lines`, `last` or `pages`. |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | `view: hex` with more than one of `lines`, `last` and `pages`. | Select the rows once. |
| `E_LIMIT` | The document, the image, the decompressed content or the dump is larger than the text limit. | Dump selected rows with `view: hex` and `lines`, or read with `decompress: none`. |

## Related

`lines` produces one `line` record per line, `search` finds matches in many
files, `info` reports metadata, `notebook.cells` lists notebook cells and
`diff` compares two files.

title: redo
text:
# redo

## Synopsis

```text
redo [<id>]
```

## Description

`redo` applies again the changes reversed by an undo. `id` is the number of
the undo operation, as listed by `history` (written `op: N` or `operation: N`,
it is corrected to `id: N` as for `undo`); without it the latest available
undo of the session (of the account without a session) is selected.

The undo operation is reversed as a whole. For an undo of one file
(`undo file:`) or of selected items (`undo N paths:`) only the items that undo
restored are applied again.

Before anything is written, every item is compared with the state recorded by
the undo, with the same check as `undo`. A later operation on the same files
makes the comparison fail, so a redo never overwrites newer work: the call
fails with `E_JOURNAL_CONFLICT` and nothing changes. `redo` has no
`on_conflict` parameter; to apply the changes anyway, undo the undo operation
with `undo N on_conflict: force`.

The undo operation becomes `undone`. The operations it undid stay `undone`;
their changes are now held by the redo operation, which is undone with `undo`
like any other operation.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `int` | the latest undone operation | Undone operation to apply again. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `journal` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Apply the latest undo of the session again:

```nurt example
redo
```

Apply undo operation 42 again:

```nurt example
redo 42
```

Reverse a redo by undoing it:

```nurt example
undo 43
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_JOURNAL_NOOP` | there is no undo to redo, the operation is not an undo, or it is already redone | list operations with `history` |
| `E_JOURNAL_EXPIRED` | the undo operation expired; nothing changed | none; the changes can no longer be applied from the journal |
| `E_JOURNAL_CONFLICT` | the files changed after the undo; nothing changed | inspect the differences in `conflicts` |
| `E_JOURNAL_PARTIAL` | items of the undo operation were released for space; nothing changed | `undo N on_conflict: partial` with the undo operation |
| `E_JOURNAL_CORRUPT` | the undo operation failed its integrity check | `nurt journal salvage` |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | an item cannot be restored by the journal (a rename across volumes or over an existing entry); nothing changed | apply the change again with the original command |
| `E_STALE` | an item changed while the redo ran; the redo was rolled back | repeat the redo |

## Related

`undo`, `history`, `help skill: "journal"`.

title: remove
text:
# remove

## Synopsis

```text
remove <path>... [name: value]...
entry|registry_value|line|match|item|node|job |> remove [name: value]...
```

## Description

`remove` removes files, symbolic links, junctions and directories given by
path or by `entry` records. A directory is removed with its whole content as
one target, without a separate confirmation. A link is removed as a link;
its target stays. A path inside another removed path is removed once, with
the enclosing directory.

In a path written in the program, `..` that follows a symbolic link is refused
with `E_INVALID_VALUE` and the path without `..` as the fix: the system would
continue from the target of the link, the language from the directory that
holds it, and `remove` must not remove another entry than the one written. The
same rule holds for `move`, the destination of `copy`, `write`, `edit`,
`insert`, `create`, `replace`, `attributes`, `convert` and `compress`; commands
that only read keep the lexical meaning of `..`.

`on_missing` decides what happens to a path that does not exist: `skip`
counts it as `missing` and continues, `error` fails with `E_NOT_FOUND`
before anything changes. An `entry` record with `exists: false`, as `info`
produces it, is a missing path.

`line` records, as `lines` and `read` produce them, remove whole lines with
their line endings; `match` records, as `search` produces them, remove the
matched text at its line and column. All lines and matches of one file are
removed by one write that keeps the encoding, the byte order mark and the
line endings of the file. A file cannot be removed and edited in the same
call. `item`, `node` and `job` records are removed by the stages of the
document, syntax and job commands.

`check_references: true` searches the files below the base directory, or
below the directory of the first removed path, for whole-word occurrences of
the removed names and of the names without their last extension, and
reports them as `references_left` with up to 20 locations. Hidden entries,
version control, dependency, build and cache directories, binary files and
files larger than 1 MiB are not searched.

A record with `etag` must still have that entity tag; a changed entry or
file fails with `E_STALE` before anything changes. When nothing is removed,
the result reports `nothing_matched`.

| Notable code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `references_left` | other files still name a removed entry; `detail` lists the locations |
| `nothing_matched` | nothing was removed |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `list<path>` | required | Paths to remove in the source form; directories are removed recursively. |
| `on_missing` | `enum(skip\|error)` | `skip` | Behaviour when a path does not exist. |
| `check_references` | `bool` | `false` | Report references to the removed names left after the change. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `none` | `effect` |
| `stage` | `entry`, `registry_value`, `line`, `match`, `item`, `node`, `job` | `effect` |

The `effect` record has one `change` with action `delete` per removed entry;
a directory removed with its content has the flag `recursive`. A file edited
by `line` or `match` records has one `change` with action `modify` and the
number of removed lines or matches. The `summary` counts `removed`, `files`,
`directories`, `links`, `bytes`, `missing`, `lines` and `matches`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | Removed files, directories and content are kept in the journal. |

| Action | Effect | Reversibility | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `job` | `local` | `irreversible` | Removing a job deletes its record and output files without a journal copy. |

## Examples

Remove a file:

```nurt example
remove "/home/user/build.log"
```

```text expected
remove: 1 target, files 1
```

Remove a directory tree and ignore a path that does not exist:

```nurt example
remove "/home/user/app/cache" "/home/user/app/old.log"
```

Remove two lines from a file:

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/notes.txt" 2..3 |> remove
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | the source form has no path | give `path` |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | a path does not exist with `on_missing: error` | check the path or use `on_missing: skip` |
| `E_STALE` | an entry or file changed since it was read, or a line or match is no longer where the record says | read or search the file again |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | a file is removed and edited in the same call, or a path has `..` after a symbolic link | remove the file or its lines, not both, or write the path without `..` |
| `E_TYPE` | a record of a kind `remove` does not accept, or a `line` or `match` record without its number fields | pass records of `list`, `find`, `lines`, `read` or `search` |
| `E_IN_USE` | Windows: an entry is open in another process; the error lists the processes | close the entry there |
| `E_PATH_RELATIVE` | a relative path without a base directory | give an absolute path or set `base` |

## Related

`move`, `rename`, `copy`, `lines`, `search`, `find`, `undo`.

title: rename
text:
# rename

## Synopsis

```text
rename [<pattern>] [<with>] path: <path> (with: <text> | to: <text>) [name: value]...
entry |> rename [<pattern>] [<with>] (with: <text> | to: <text>) [name: value]...
```

## Description

`rename` changes the name of entries within their directory; `move` changes
the directory. The new name is given by `to`, evaluated per input record, or
derived from the old name: a text `pattern` replaces every occurrence of the
text with `with`, a regex `pattern` replaces every match with the template
`with`, in which `$1`, `${name}` and `$$` stand for a numbered group, a named
group and a dollar sign. `to` and `with` exclude each other.

The new name is a single name: a name with `/`, `\`, an empty name, `.` and
`..` are rejected. An entry whose new name equals its old name is counted as
`unchanged`.

`on_conflict` decides what happens when an entry with the new name exists:
`error` fails before anything changes, `skip` keeps both entries, `overwrite`
replaces an existing file or link. An existing directory is never replaced.
When the new name is the old name of another entry renamed in the same call,
that entry is renamed first; renames that form a cycle are rejected.

On a volume that does not distinguish letter case, a rename that changes only
the letter case renames the entry itself, and a new name that differs from
another existing name only in letter case is a conflict reported as
`case_collision`.

`check_references: true` reports whole-word occurrences of the old names in
other files as `references_left`, with the same rules as `remove`.

An entry record with `etag` must still have that entity tag; a changed entry
fails with `E_STALE` before anything changes. When nothing is renamed, the
result reports `nothing_matched`.

| Notable code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `case_collision` | the new name differs from an existing name only in letter case on a volume that does not distinguish case |
| `references_left` | other files still name a renamed entry by its old name |
| `nothing_matched` | nothing was renamed |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | Entry to rename in the source form. |
| `pattern` | `text \| regex` | none | Part of the name to replace; used with with. |
| `with` | `text` | one of `replacement` | Replacement of the pattern in the name. |
| `to` | `text` | one of `replacement` | New name. |
| `on_conflict` | `enum(overwrite\|skip\|error)` | `error` | Behaviour when an entry with the new name exists. |
| `check_references` | `bool` | `false` | Report references to the old names left after the change. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `none` | `effect` |
| `stage` | `entry` | `effect` |

The `effect` record has one `change` with action `rename` per renamed entry,
with `path` set to the old path and `to` to the new path, in the order the
renames run. Its `summary` counts `renamed`, `overwritten`, `skipped` and
`unchanged`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Rename a file:

```nurt example
rename path: "/home/user/draft.md" to: "final.md"
```

```text expected
rename: 1 target, renamed 1
```

Replace an extension in every listed name:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/photos" glob: "*.jpeg" |> rename ".jpeg" ".jpg"
```

Rewrite dates in names with a regex template:

```nurt example
list "/home/user/logs" |> rename /(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})/ "$3.$2.$1"
```

Change only the letter case of a name:

```nurt example
rename path: "/Volumes/data/readme.md" to: "README.md"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | no new name: neither `to` nor `pattern` with `with` | give `to`, or `pattern` and `with` |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | both `to` and `with`, or `pattern` with `to` | give one form of the new name |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | the new name contains a directory, is empty, `.` or `..`, or `pattern` is empty | use `move` to change the directory |
| `E_EXISTS` | an entry with the new name exists with `on_conflict: error`, is a directory, or the renames form a cycle | choose another name or `on_conflict` value |
| `E_REGEX` | the regex pattern is invalid, or the template names a group the pattern does not have | correct the pattern or the template |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | the entry does not exist | check the path |
| `E_STALE` | an input entry changed since it was read | read the entries again |
| `E_IN_USE` | Windows: an entry is open in another process; the error lists the processes | close the entry there |

## Related

`move`, `copy`, `remove`, `replace`, `list`, `find`.

title: replace
text:
# replace

## Synopsis

```text
replace <pattern> <with> in: <list<path>> [name: value]...
match|node|item |> replace <with> [name: value]...
line|content |> replace <pattern> <with> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`replace` changes text in files. The source form replaces the matches of
`pattern` in the files listed in `in`; a directory of `in` contributes its
files that match `glob` and `file_type`. The form on `line` and `content`
records replaces the matches of `pattern` inside the lines of the records:
a `line` record selects its line, a `content` record its `range` or the
whole file. The form on `match` records replaces the text of every input
match, for example the output of `search`.

A text pattern is literal. It is matched with the tolerance of `whitespace`:
with `normalize`, the default, differences of indentation, trailing white
space, line endings and runs of white space are tolerated, an exact
occurrence always takes precedence, and the replacement takes the
indentation, the indentation unit and the line endings of the place it
replaces. A regular expression `/…/` is matched exactly. `^` and `$` match at
line boundaries, and a match does not span lines unless `multiline` is set,
which also lets `.` match a line break. A regular expression with
look-around or back-references is evaluated by the backtracking engine.

For regular expressions and input matches `with` is a template: `$1` and
`${1}` insert a numbered group, `${name}` a named group, `$0` the whole match
and `$$` a `$`. Any other `$` is an error. With `template: false` the text is
inserted as written. For input matches `$n` is `groups[n]` of the record
(`groups[0]` is the whole match, as `search` writes it) and the named groups
are its `named` map. A literal pattern always
inserts `with` as written.

`expect` counts the matches of all files before `occurrence` applies;
`occurrence` keeps one match, counted from 1, in every file. When the count
is outside `expect` nothing is changed and the error lists the first
matches. When nothing matches, `on_missing: skip` reports the notable effect
`nothing_matched` and changes nothing, and `on_missing: error` fails with
the nearest fragments of the text. When the pattern matches but no file has
the occurrence, `on_missing: error` fails with `E_OUT_OF_RANGE` and lists
the first matches.

`scope` keeps the matches that start in code, comments or string literals,
as classified by the grammar of the file. `mode: syntax` matches a
structural pattern written in the syntax of the language of the file, and
`with` is a structural template. Both need a grammar for the file.

With `check_references`, the files are searched after the change for the
replaced text outside the replacements: symbolically when a grammar knows
the file and the text is an identifier, otherwise as a whole word. The
places found are reported as the notable effect `references_left` with
their number and the first places; they do not prevent the change.

Every file keeps its encoding, byte order mark and line endings. A file
whose encoding cannot represent the new text is not changed. Binary files
found in a directory are skipped and counted as `binary_skipped`; a binary
file listed in `in` is skipped as `binary_target`. With `binary: text` a
binary file is read as Windows-1252 text.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `text \| regex` | required | Text or regular expression to replace. |
| `with` | `text` | required | Replacement; $1, ${name} and $$ refer to groups unless template is false. |
| `in` | `list<path>` | required | Files or directories in the source form. |
| `glob` | `glob \| list<glob>` | `"**"` | Name patterns of the files in directories. |
| `mode` | `enum(auto\|literal\|regex\|syntax)` | `auto` | Pattern mode; auto treats text as literal and /…/ as a regular expression. |
| `occurrence` | `int` | every occurrence | Replace only this occurrence, counted from 1. |
| `case_sensitive` | `bool` | `true` | Match with case sensitivity. |
| `whole_word` | `bool` | `false` | Match whole words only. |
| `multiline` | `bool` | `false` | Allow matches across lines. |
| `whitespace` | `enum(exact\|trailing\|indent\|normalize)` | `normalize` | Tolerance of whitespace differences; normalize also adapts the replacement to the file style. |
| `scope` | `enum(any\|code\|comments\|strings)` | `any` | Part of source code in which matches are replaced. |
| `check_references` | `bool` | `false` | Report references to the replaced text left after the change. |
| `template` | `bool` | `true` | Treat the replacement as a template with group references. |
| `on_missing` | `enum(skip\|error)` | `skip` | Behaviour when nothing matches. |
| `expect` | `range` | none | Expected number of replacements; otherwise nothing is changed. |
| `if_match` | `text \| map<text>` | none | Expected etag of the file, or a map from path to etag for several files. |
| `validate` | `enum(off\|warn\|reject)` | `reject` | Roll back a change that adds a new syntax error to a known format. |
| `hidden` | `bool` | `true` | Include hidden files. |
| `gitignore` | `bool` | `false` | Apply the rules of .gitignore files. |
| `binary` | `enum(skip\|text)` | `skip` | Skip binary files or treat them as text. |
| `file_type` | `list<text>` | `[]` | File types by extension, such as go or ts. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `none` | `effect` |
| `matches` | `match`, `node`, `item` | `effect` |
| `lines` | `line`, `content` | `effect` |

The `effect` record lists one `change` per changed file with the number of
replacements, the lines added and removed and the difference.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Replace the first call in one file:

```nurt example
replace "oldName(" "newName(" in: ["/home/user/app/a.go"] occurrence: 1
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/a.go", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "x := oldName(1)\ny := oldName(2)\n" }
] }
```

Rewrite calls with a regular expression in the Rust files of a directory:

```nurt example
replace /(\w+\([^)]*\))\.unwrap\(\)/ "$1?" in: ["/home/user/app"] glob: "**/*.rs"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/src/main.rs", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "let a = load().unwrap();\n" },
  { "path": "/home/user/app/src/io/read.rs", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "let b = open(p).unwrap();\n" },
  { "path": "/home/user/app/README.md", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "call().unwrap()\n" }
] }
```

Replace a block written with other indentation; the new lines take the
indentation of the file:

```nurt example
replace "start()\nreport()" "prepare()\nstart()\nreport()" in: ["/home/user/app/run.py"]
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/run.py", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "def run():\n    if ready:\n        start()\n        report()\n" }
] }
```

Replace a word in lines 2 and 3 only:

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/notes.txt" 2..3 |> replace "draft" "final"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/notes.txt", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "draft one\ndraft two\ndraft three\n" }
] }
```

Reformat search matches with their groups:

```nurt example
search /(\w+)=(\S+)/ "/home/user/app/config.ini" |> replace "$1 = $2"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/config.ini", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "port=8080\nhost=example.com\n" }
] }
```

Replace a scheme only when it occurs exactly three times in a directory:

```nurt example
replace "http://" "https://" in: ["/home/user/site"] expect: 3
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/site/a.html", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "http://example.com http://example.com\n" },
  { "path": "/home/user/site/b.html", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "http://example.com\n" }
] }
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_ASSERT` | the number of matches is outside `expect` | extend the pattern, set `occurrence` or change `expect` |
| `E_NO_MATCH` | nothing matches and `on_missing` is `error` | read the current text and give an existing fragment |
| `E_OUT_OF_RANGE` | no file has the occurrence and `on_missing` is `error` | give an `occurrence` from 1 to the number of matches |
| `E_REGEX` | the regular expression or the template is not valid | correct the pattern or pass `template: false` |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | the pattern is empty, or `occurrence` is below 1 | give the text to replace and an occurrence from 1 |
| `E_STALE` | a file changed since it was read, or does not have the `if_match` tag | read the file again and repeat the change |
| `E_ENCODING` | the encoding of a file cannot represent the replacement | convert the file with `convert` first |
| `E_BINARY` | a file named by an input record is binary | pass text files only |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE` | `scope` or `mode: syntax` has no grammar for a file | use `scope: any` or a literal pattern |
| `E_LIMIT` | the regular expression exceeded the backtracking limit | simplify the pattern |
| `E_ROLLED_BACK` | the change added a syntax error and `validate` is `reject` | correct the new text or pass `validate: warn` |

## Related

`search`, `lines`, `edit`, `insert`, `write`, `diff`, `help skill: "text-editing"`.

title: restart
text:
# restart

## Synopsis

```text
service |> restart [name: value]...
```

## Description

`restart` asks the service manager to restart each input service and waits up
to `wait` until the service settles, as `start` does: the state is read every
100 ms at first, the interval grows by 100 ms up to 500 ms, and the wait ends
when the state is neither `starting` nor `stopping`. A stopped service is
started. A running service is always restarted, so `before` and `after` are
both `running` after a successful restart. With `wait: 0s` the command returns
at once with the state read right after the request.

The operation is marked irreversible with `service_changed` before the manager
is asked to act, so the effect is reported even when the wait fails. Services
are processed in input order; an error stops the processing of the remaining
services.

**Privilege.** System units need the administrator: write `privilege: elevated` on the stage. A restart has no inverse and is reported as irreversible.

```nurt
services name: "nginx" |> restart privilege: elevated
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wait` | `duration` | `10s` | Time to wait for each service to reach the running state. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `service` | `effect` |

Each `effect` record holds `kind: "restart"`, `target` (`service:<name>`),
`action`, `before` and `after`. A preview shows the same records with
`status: planned` and the expected `after`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `run` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| External use | `system_program`: `launchctl`; On macOS services are restarted through the launchctl component of the operating system. |

## Examples

Restart one service:

```nurt example
services name: "nginx" |> restart
```

Restart every running service whose name starts with `php`:

```nurt example
services name: /^php/ state: "running" |> restart
```

Restart a service and allow it thirty seconds to come up:

```nurt example
services name: "cron" |> restart wait: 30s
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The service did not settle within `wait` or the time limit of the program. `expected` holds `running`, `actual` the current state; the effect is already applied. | Give a longer `wait`. |
| `E_SERVICE` | The service entered the `failed` state; `os_code` and `result` hold the reason given by the manager and `next_steps` holds `logs unit: "<name>"`. The manager may also report another error in `os_code` and `os_message`. | Read the log of the service and correct its configuration. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The service no longer exists. | Read the services again with `services`. |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | The manager refused the action; `required` names the privilege, `root` on Linux and `administrator` on Windows. Interactive authorization is never requested. | Run as an account with that privilege. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | The record comes from the manager of another system. | Read the services on this system with `services`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `wait` is negative. | Give a non-negative duration such as `10s`. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The execution was cancelled. | None; the cancellation was requested by the caller. |

## Related

`services` produces the input records. `start` starts services and `stop`
stops them. `logs unit:` shows why a service failed. The `administration` group page
lists the other commands of the group.

title: resume
text:
# resume

## Synopsis

```text
job|process |> resume
```

## Description

Resumes the process tree of every input job suspended by `suspend`:
`SIGCONT` to the process group on Linux and macOS, resumption of the threads
of the job object on Windows. The job state becomes `running` again and its
time limit continues from where it stopped.

Only suspended jobs can be resumed. Job and process records are handled by
this implementation.

## Parameters

The command has no parameters.

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `job`, `process` | `effect` |

Input `job` or `process` records. Produces one `effect` record per input
record; its `job` field holds the job record after the change.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `run` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Resume job `j7`.

```nurt example
jobs "j7" |> resume
```

```text expected
resumed  job:j7
```

Resume all suspended jobs.

```nurt example
jobs |> filter state == "suspended" |> resume
```

Resume job `j3` and wait for its end.

```nurt example
jobs "j3" |> resume
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_JOB_STATE` | The job is not suspended. | Suspend it first: `jobs "j7" \|> suspend`. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_JOB` | No job has the identifier. | Use one of the identifiers in `candidates`. |

## Related

`suspend`, `stop`, `jobs`.

title: retry
text:
# retry

## Synopsis

```text
job |> retry [name: value]...
```

## Description

Runs the command of every input job again under the rules of `run`: the same
program and arguments, working directory, environment, standard input,
limits, change detection and output selection. The new job records the
repeated job in `retry_of`. A job of `test.*` or `analyze.*` is repeated as
such, so that its final record is produced again.

The environment of a job is kept outside the job record, in a file of the
state directory readable only by the account of the engine. Neither job
records nor events contain environment values.

Only finished jobs can be repeated. A program that the console ends because of
a limit or cancellation fails the call as in `run`; when several jobs are
repeated, the error has `effect_applied` set once any of them started. When the new program runs longer than
`wait`, it continues in the background; the result is then a `job` record and
the stages after `retry` are skipped (`post_stages_deferred`).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `timeout` | `duration` | the time limit of the original job | Time limit of the program. |
| `wait` | `duration \| enum(forever)` | the default wait of run | Time to wait for the program before it continues as a job. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `job` | `exec`, `job` |

Input `job` records. Produces an `exec` record for each program that ended
within `wait` and a `job` record for each program that continues in the
background.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `run` |
| Effect | `process` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `user_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | As for run: changes of watched files are reversible when kept; other effects are irreversible. |

## Examples

Repeat job `j7`.

```nurt example
jobs "j7" |> retry
```

```text expected
exit_code: 0
```

Repeat job `j7` with a longer time limit and wait until it ends.

```nurt example
jobs "j7" |> retry timeout: 30m wait: forever
```

Repeat every failed job in the background.

```nurt example
jobs state: failed |> retry wait: 0s
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_JOB_STATE` | The job still runs. | Stop it first: `jobs "j7" \|> stop`. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_JOB` | No job has the identifier. | Use one of the identifiers in `candidates`. |
| `E_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND` | The program cannot be started again. | Check the program and the working directory. |
| `E_SPAWN` | The program cannot be started again. | Check the program and the working directory. |
| `E_IO` | The stored environment and standard input of the job are missing or unreadable. | Start the command again with `run`. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The program reached `timeout` or `idle_timeout`; `details.exec` holds the record. | Raise the limit or repeat with `wait: 0s`. |
| `E_LIMIT` | The program exceeded `max_cpu` or `max_memory`; `details.exec` holds the record. | Start the command again with a higher limit. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The call was cancelled while the program ran; `details.exec` holds the record. | Repeat the call. |

## Related

`run`, `jobs`, `stop`.

title: run
text:
# run

## Synopsis

```text
run <command> cwd: <path> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`run` starts a program with the arguments of `command` as a list. No shell
takes part: the arguments reach the program exactly as written, and shell
syntax such as `|`, `>`, `*` or `$NAME` has no meaning. A shell script runs as
a program of its own, for example `run ["bash", "-c", "make && make install"]`.

The first element of `command` names the program. A name with a directory,
such as `./tool` or `/usr/bin/tool`, is taken relative to `cwd`. Any other name
is looked up in `PATH` of the environment the program receives, so a `PATH`
given in `env` takes effect; empty entries of `PATH` are skipped. On Windows
the extensions of `PATHEXT` are tried in order after the name as written, and
variable names are compared without case.

On Windows, batch files (`.bat`, `.cmd`) are started through
`%SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe /e:ON /v:OFF /d /c`, with every argument quoted
for the command interpreter: arguments with spaces or metacharacters
(`& | < > ^ ( ) ! "`) are enclosed in quotes, `"` is doubled and `%` is written
so that `%NAME%` is not expanded. The interpreter is never looked up in
`PATH`. The static check lists the arguments with metacharacters in
`metacharacter_arguments`.

The environment is built in three layers, each overriding the earlier ones:
the environment of the console (`inherit_env: all`), the table
`run.env_defaults`, and `env`. A variable of `env` with the value `null` is
removed; an empty text sets an empty value. With `inherit_env: none` the
program receives only `run.env_defaults` and `env`; on Windows `SystemRoot`,
`ComSpec` and `PATHEXT` are kept as well, because programs fail to start
without them. A program given by name is looked up in the `PATH` of that
environment, so on Unix it needs `PATH` in `env` (or in `run.env_defaults`)
with `inherit_env: none`, otherwise the result is `E_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND`. The
result lists the names given in `env` in `env_keys`; values
never appear in the result or in the journal. The static check reports the
variables of `run.env_defaults` in `env_defaults`.

There is no terminal: standard input is empty (`/dev/null`, `NUL`) unless
`stdin` gives a text, written to the program and then closed, or a path,
opened as the input of the program. When the program closes its input before
all of the text is written, the rest is discarded and the report notes
`stdin_closed_early`. The program runs in its own process group (Windows: job
object); `timeout`, `idle_timeout`, `max_cpu` and `max_memory` apply to the
whole process tree.

Output processing. The full output is kept in spool files; the parameters
below shape only the response, which is short by default. Each line is
decoded (`output_encoding`), cleaned (terminal control sequences, carriage
return redraws, which keep only the last state of the line, and trailing white
space are removed), checked against `summary` and `progress`, collapsed with
repeats when `dedupe` is set (the default: consecutive lines that are
identical, or that differ only in numbers, versions or the names after a step
word such as `Compiling`, become the first of them followed by ` (×N)`),
selected by `filter` with `context` lines around each match (or, for `show:
errors` and for `show: auto` after a failure of output longer than 20 lines,
by the built-in error line patterns with 2 lines of context), limited to the
first `head` and the last `tail` lines, and cut to 400 characters per line
(the rest becomes `… [+N characters]`). The text of all streams together then
fits in `max_bytes` bytes (4096 by default, key `output.max_bytes`, `0` is no
limit), filled in this order: the errors found in the output of a known tool,
the end of standard error, the end of standard output, the beginning of the
output; the end has precedence over the beginning. `quiet_on_success` and
`show: none` return no text but keep the counters, `summary_lines` and
`progress`. `shown` reports, per stream, the lines kept from the start and
from the end, the lines left out between them and the lines removed by the
filters.

With `show: auto` and without `head`, `tail` and `filter`, a run that exits
with 0 returns the last 5 lines of its output and the field `digest`, one line
with the exit code, the time, and the lines and bytes of output (for a known
tool also its counters, for example `cargo: 0 errors, 3 warnings`). A failed
run returns the full budget.

Known formats. After a failure of output longer than 20 lines, `show: auto`
recognises the output of `cargo` and `rustc` (`error[E0308]` with
`--> file:line:col`) and of `pytest` (`FAILED file::test - message` with the
traceback line). The field `diagnostics` then has `tool`, `errors` and
`warnings` (the numbers of all of them) and `first`, the first 10 distinct
errors, each with the one-line fields `file`, `line`, `col`, `code`, `message`
and `severity` (and `count` when the same error was reported in several
places); the text keeps only the last 10 lines of the output instead of
hundreds of warnings. A shorter output is returned whole and has no
`diagnostics`. A line `error: message` without a code and a location counts as
an error of `cargo` only when the output shows another mark of it.

When the response leaves lines out or cuts lines, the report carries the field
`continuation` (`id`, `unit: lines`, `shown`, `remaining`, `cut_lines`) and the
text ends with the hint "more: next". `next` returns the lines left out from the output
file in parts of the size of the first response, `next 200` returns 200 lines,
`next all` everything that is left and `next full` the lines that the response
cut, whole; the program does not run again. Line numbers are those of the
file, so lines collapsed by `dedupe` count as the lines they stand for. A
response that shows a selection of lines (`show: errors`) is continued from the
first line of the file. The output file stays in the record (`output_file`,
`stdout_file`, `stderr_file`) and can still be read with `read` and `search`.

`run` waits up to `wait` for the program. A program that ends within `wait`
yields an `exec` record. A program still running after `wait` continues as a
background job and the result is a `job` record with `state: running`; the
stages after the effect are then skipped and the report notes
`post_stages_deferred`. `background: true` is the same as `wait: 0s`;
`wait: forever` waits until `timeout`. Parameters the program does not give
take their values from the configuration keys `run.timeout`, `run.wait`,
`run.idle_timeout`, `run.track_changes`, `run.parallel`, `output.head`,
`output.tail` and `output.max_bytes`.

Changes made by the program are detected with `track_changes`. The mode
`auto` is bounded so that it never stalls a run: it does not scan the file
system root, does not enter directories of other file systems, and gives up
when the watched directories hold more than 200 000 entries or one scan takes
longer than 3 s. The program then runs without detection and the report
carries a `detection_scope` note that gives the reason and says what to do:
name the directories the program changes in `watch`, or use
`track_changes: scan`. A tracked run carries a `detection_scope` note that
names the watched directories and the directories of other file systems that
were not entered. The scans before and after the program end at cancellation
and at `timeout`; a scan before the program that reaches `timeout` fails the
run with `E_TIMEOUT` and one that is cancelled with `E_CANCELLED`. The scan
after the program may exceed `timeout` by up to 5 s, so that the changes of a
program ended by the limit are still recorded; a scan that stops early records
no changes and says so in a note. A `run` that changes no file does not report
`nothing_matched`, because the program is not a stage that selects targets.

An exit code other than zero is a result, not an error: the status is `ok`,
`exec.exit_code` holds the code and the report notes `exit_nonzero`. Use
`|> assert exit_code: 0` to fail on it. A program that the console ends
because of `timeout` or `idle_timeout` fails with `E_TIMEOUT`, one ended by
`max_cpu` or `max_memory` with `E_LIMIT`, and one ended by cancellation with
`E_CANCELLED`; the error carries the `exec` record in `details.exec` and
`effect_applied: true`, because the changes made until then remain.

With input records, the `path` of every `entry` or `match` record becomes an
argument after `command`. Without `batch` one process runs per record; with
`batch: n` the arguments are split into batches of up to `n`. `parallel` runs
that many batches at once; results keep the batch order. All batches run to
their end before the call returns, whatever `wait` says. The result is one
`exec` record: its `exit_code` is 0 when every batch exited with 0, otherwise
the code of the first failed batch in batch order; `batches` lists the number,
arguments, exit code and running time of every batch and `failed_batches`
counts the failures. After a failure the remaining batches still run, unless
`bail: true`, which starts no further batch. An empty input starts no
process. When `command` uses fields of the input record, the command is
computed per record and `batch` is not accepted.

A preview (`preview: true`) resolves the program and returns the program, the
arguments as the program receives them (`argv`; for batch files the command
line of the interpreter), the working directory, `launcher`, `env_keys`,
`stdin`, `timeout`, `wait`, `watch` and `track_changes`, without starting
anything.

The command line of a batch file cannot hold a line break: the interpreter
ends the command there. An argument with `\r` or `\n` for a batch file, and an
argument with a NUL character for any program, fails with `E_ARG`;
`details.index` gives the position in `command` and `fix` passes the text on
standard input instead.

Every job of a run, a batch or a `retry` emits `job.started`, then
`job.output` and `job.progress`, then one `job.finished`, also when the job
continues in the background. The command emits no `exec.started` or
`exec.finished`: these events enclose the whole program and come from the
engine.

**Privilege.** `privilege: elevated` runs the program with the rights of the administrator, `as_user: "NAME"` as another account; `sudo`, `doas` and `run0` are not written in the argument list (a list that starts with `sudo` is corrected into the same `run` with `privilege: elevated`). The files that the program changes are reported, but they are not preserved: the entry is irreversible, and the report says so before the change.

```nurt
run ["systemctl", "daemon-reload"] cwd: "/" privilege: elevated
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | `list<text>` | required | Program and arguments; the first element is the program. |
| `cwd` | `path` | required | Working directory of the program. |
| `env` | `map<text>` | none | Environment variables to set. |
| `inherit_env` | `enum(all\|none)` | `all` | Inherit the environment of the console or start with an empty one. |
| `stdin` | `text \| path` | none | Text or file given on standard input; the input is empty otherwise. |
| `timeout` | `duration` | `120s` | Time limit of the program. |
| `idle_timeout` | `duration` | `60s` | Time limit without output. |
| `wait` | `duration \| enum(forever)` | `3s` | Time to wait for the program before it continues as a job; forever waits until timeout. |
| `background` | `bool` | `false` | Start as a job at once, the same as wait: 0s. |
| `merge_stderr` | `bool` | `false` | Merge standard error into standard output. |
| `show` | `enum(auto\|both\|stdout\|stderr\|errors\|summary\|none)` | `auto` | Output returned in the result; the full output is always kept in a file. |
| `head` | `int` | `20` | Number of first output lines returned. |
| `tail` | `int` | `40` | Number of last output lines returned. |
| `max_bytes` | `int` | `4096` | Bytes of output text returned in all streams together; 0 is no limit. |
| `filter` | `regex` | none | Return only output lines that match. |
| `context` | `int` | `0` | Lines of context around lines matching filter. |
| `dedupe` | `bool` | `true` | Collapse repeated output lines, also lines that differ only in numbers. |
| `quiet_on_success` | `bool` | `false` | Return no output when the exit code is 0. |
| `output_encoding` | `text` | `"auto"` | Encoding of the program output; auto detects it. |
| `watch` | `list<path>` | none | Directories in which changes made by the program are detected. |
| `track_changes` | `enum(auto\|scan\|events\|none)` | `auto` | Method of detecting changes made by the program. |
| `max_cpu` | `duration` | none | Limit of processor time. |
| `max_memory` | `size` | none | Limit of memory. |
| `priority` | `enum(low\|normal\|high)` | `normal` | Scheduling priority. |
| `label` | `text` | none | Short name of the job. |
| `description` | `text` | none | Description of the job. |
| `progress` | `regex` | none | Pattern of output lines that report progress. |
| `summary` | `list<regex>` | none | Patterns whose latest matches form the status line. |
| `batch` | `int` | none | Run the program once per batch of this many input arguments. |
| `parallel` | `int` | `1` | Number of batches run at the same time; results keep the batch order. |
| `bail` | `bool` | `false` | Stop starting batches after the first failed batch. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none`, `entry`, `match` | `exec`, `job` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `run` |
| Effect | `process` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `user_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | Changes of files under watch are reversible when their previous content was kept; effects outside the file system are irreversible. |

Changes of files under `watch` are recorded in the journal and are
reversible when their previous content was kept; effects outside the file
system are irreversible. A run that changes no file creates no journal entry.

A command line that matches the built-in table of programs with effects
outside the computer (for example `git push` or `kubectl apply`, also behind
wrappers such as `sudo` or `env`) or a pattern of `run.irreversible_patterns`
lists the matched rules in `exec.external_effect`, and the report marks the
call `irreversible: external_effect`. The classification describes the
effect; it never prevents the run.

## Examples

Run the tests of a project and show only the error lines:

```nurt example
run ["cargo", "test"] cwd: "/home/user/app" show: errors head: 5 tail: 10
```

Start a build in the background with a label:

```nurt example
run ["npm", "run", "build"] cwd: "/home/user/app" background: true label: "build"
```

Format the Go files found in a project, 20 files per process, two processes
at a time:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/app" glob: "**/*.go" |> run ["gofmt", "-w"] batch: 20 parallel: 2 cwd: "/home/user/app"
```

Give text on standard input, with an environment of its own:

```nurt example
run ["sort"] cwd: "/home/user" stdin: "b\na\n" inherit_env: none env: {"LC_ALL": "C", "PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin"}
```

Fail when the program exits with a code other than zero:

```nurt example
run ["go", "build", "./..."] cwd: "/home/user/app" |> assert exit_code: 0
```

A response that leaves lines out ends with the hint "more: next" and carries the field
`continuation`; the command `next` returns the next part without running the
command again.

```text
exit 1  3000 lines  more: next
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND` | The program is not in `PATH` or the named file does not exist; `candidates` lists up to five similar names of the search path. | Accept a candidate, give the full path, or add the directory to `PATH` in `env`. |
| `E_SPAWN` | The program could not be started: the working directory is missing or not a directory, the file is a directory or has no execute permission, or the format is unknown. | Give an existing `cwd`; grant execute permission or start the file through its interpreter. |
| `E_ARG` | An argument or variable cannot be passed without changing its meaning: a NUL character, a line break in an argument of a batch file, `=` in a variable name. | Use the `fix`, which passes the text on standard input. |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | Neither `cwd` nor `base` is given. | Add `cwd`. |
| `E_PATH_RELATIVE` | `cwd` is relative and `base` is not given. | Give an absolute `cwd`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `batch` or `parallel` is below 1, or `batch` is used with a `command` computed per record. | Give a count of 1 or more; remove `batch`. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The `stdin` file does not exist. | Give an existing file or a text. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The program reached `timeout` or `idle_timeout`; `details.exec` holds the record. | Raise the limit or start the program with `background: true`. |
| `E_LIMIT` | The program exceeded `max_cpu` or `max_memory`. | Raise the limit. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The call was cancelled while the program ran. | Run the call again. |

## Related

`jobs`, `stop`, `retry`, `suspend`, `resume`, `assert`, `verify`, `undo`,
`test.run`, `analyze.check`.

title: schedule.create
text:
# schedule.create

## Synopsis

```text
schedule.create <label> action: <pipeline> (cron: <text> | every: <duration> | at: <instant>) [name: value]...
```

## Description

`schedule.create` saves a schedule and returns its `schedule` record. The
schedule runs its action at the run times of exactly one trigger:

- `cron` takes five fields: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31),
  month (1-12 or `jan`-`dec`) and day of week (0-7 or `sun`-`sat`, where 0 and
  7 are Sunday). A field holds `*`, numbers, names, ranges `a-b`, lists `a,b`
  and steps: `*/n` from the lower bound, `a-b/n` within the range and `a/n`
  from `a` to the end of the range. Names are not case sensitive. When neither
  the day of month nor the day of week starts with `*`, a day matches when
  either field matches; otherwise both must match. The shortcuts `@yearly`,
  `@annually`, `@monthly`, `@weekly`, `@daily` and `@hourly` are accepted.
  An expression without a run time within five years is rejected.
- `every` runs at a fixed interval. The first run time is the creation time
  plus the interval. The interval lies between `schedule.min_interval`
  (default `30s`) and `schedule.max_interval` (default `366d`).
- `at` runs once at the given time, which must lie in the future.

Every run time is strictly later than the time it is computed from: a
schedule created at 14:40:00 with `cron: "*/10 * * * *"` first runs at 14:50.

`timezone` applies to the fields of a cron expression and to the times shown
by `schedule.list`. The value `local` is replaced by the IANA name of the
time zone of the device at creation, so a later change of the time zone of
the device does not move the run times. A wall-clock time skipped by the
change to daylight saving time runs at the same distance after the change
(02:30 becomes 03:30); a wall-clock time repeated by the change back runs
once, at its first occurrence.

The action is a pipeline of the language. It is bound and checked when the
schedule is created and saved together with an integrity hash. Each run
executes the pipeline as an operation of the session `schedule:<id>` with the
base directory and the project directories of the creating call, so every run
has its own entry in the operation journal. The environment of the programs
of the action is the environment of the background service with
`run.env_defaults`; variables of the calling session are passed explicitly
with the `env` parameter of `run`. `timeout` limits the whole run and is the
time limit of the `run` stages of the action that set none. A definition
