whose action no longer matches its integrity hash is not run: the run is
recorded with `state: rejected` and `reason: definition_changed`.

Schedules run in the background service of the account. When the service
does not run, the schedule is saved and the record carries `active: false`
and `reason: service_not_running`; the service applies the schedule when it
starts. With `run_now: true` and a running service the action also runs once
at creation, outside the run times and the run limit; the creation does not
wait for that run, and its record appears in `schedule.history`.

A run time reached later than `misfire` after it is not made up one by one:
`on_missed: skip` records one skipped run (`reason: misfire`) and
`on_missed: run_once` makes exactly one run (`trigger: missed`); in both cases
the next run time counts from the present. A single time (`at`) skipped this
way makes the schedule `expired`. A run time reached while a run of the
schedule executes is skipped (`overlap: skip`), waits in a queue of one place
(`overlap: queue`) or runs as well (`overlap: parallel`, within
`schedule.max_parallel`).

The identifiers are `s1`, `s2` and so on. The number of schedules that are
not completed or expired, paused ones included, is limited by
`schedule.max_active` (default 50).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `text` | required | Name of the schedule. |
| `action` | `pipeline` | required | Pipeline to run. |
| `cron` | `text` | one of `trigger` | Five-field cron expression or a shortcut such as @daily. |
| `every` | `duration` | one of `trigger` | Interval between runs; at least the configured minimum. |
| `at` | `instant` | one of `trigger` | Single run at this time. |
| `timezone` | `text` | `"local"` | Time zone of the cron expression and times. |
| `on_missed` | `enum(skip\|run_once)` | `skip` | Behaviour for runs missed while the service was not running. |
| `misfire` | `duration` | `2m` | Maximum delay after which a missed run is not made up. |
| `overlap` | `enum(skip\|queue\|parallel)` | `skip` | Behaviour when a run is due while the previous one is still running. |
| `timeout` | `duration` | `1h` | Time limit of each run. |
| `max_runs` | `int` | none | Number of runs after which the schedule completes. |
| `expires` | `instant \| duration` | none | Time, or time from now, after which the schedule expires. |
| `run_now` | `bool` | `false` | Also run once immediately. |
| `enabled` | `bool` | `true` | Create the schedule active rather than paused. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `schedule` |

The record holds `id`, `label`, `trigger` (`kind`, `expression`, `timezone`),
`next_run`, `state`, `active`, `reason`, `action`, `action_kind`, `runs`,
`max_runs`, `expires`, `on_missed`, `misfire`, `overlap`, `timeout`,
`created` and `session`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

The definition file is written through the operation journal. The run state
(`<state>/schedules/state.json`: next run times, counters and history) is
written only by the background service and is not part of the journal.

## Examples

Run a backup every day at 03:00 in the time zone of the device:

```nurt example
schedule.create "backup" cron: "0 3 * * *" action: (run ["tar", "-czf", "/srv/backup.tgz", "data"] cwd: "/srv")
```

Check a directory every ten minutes and keep at most one waiting run:

```nurt example
schedule.create "inbox" every: 10m overlap: queue action: (run ["./process-inbox.sh"] cwd: "/srv/inbox")
```

Run once at a given time and make up the run if the device sleeps at that
time:

```nurt example
schedule.create "reminder" at: "2026-12-24T18:00:00+01:00" on_missed: run_once action: (run ["notify-send", "Stand-up"] cwd: "/tmp")
```

Run on weekdays between 09:00 and 17:45 every quarter of an hour, for twenty
runs at most:

```nurt example
schedule.create "probe" cron: "*/15 9-17 * * mon-fri" timezone: "Europe/Warsaw" max_runs: 20 action: (run ["./probe"] cwd: "/opt/probe")
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `label` is missing, or none of `cron`, `every` and `at` is given. | Give the label and exactly one trigger. |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | More than one of `cron`, `every` and `at` is given. `expected` lists the parameters of the group. | Keep one trigger. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | The cron expression is invalid or has no run within five years, the interval lies outside the configured bounds, `at` or `expires` has passed, the time zone is unknown, `timeout` exceeds `schedule.max_timeout`, or `max_runs` is below 1. | Correct the value named in the message; `fix` holds a valid form where one exists. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` | `on_missed` or `overlap` has an unknown value. | Use one of the listed values. |
| `E_TYPE` | A parameter has the wrong type, for example a number for `every`. | Give a value of the listed type, such as `10m`. |
| `E_LIMIT` | `schedule.max_active` schedules exist. | Remove schedules with `schedule.remove` or raise the limit. |
| `E_IO` | The schedule store cannot be read or written. | Check the permissions of the state directory. |

## Related

`schedule.list` shows schedules and their next run times, `schedule.run` runs
an action outside its run times, `schedule.pause` and `schedule.resume`
suspend and resume schedules, `schedule.remove` removes them and
`schedule.history` lists past runs.

title: schedule.history
text:
# schedule.history

## Synopsis

```text
schedule.history [<id>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

`schedule.history` returns the runs recorded by the background service, the
newest start first, at most `limit` records. With `id` it returns only the
runs of that schedule; the runs of a removed schedule remain available.

Each record describes one run or one run time that did not run. `exit_state`
holds the outcome: `ok`, `failed` (a non-zero exit code, a refused or failed
run), `timed_out`, `cancelled` (a stopped run), `missed` (a run time skipped
because it was late or no client provided the action) and `skipped_overlap`
(a run time reached while a run was in progress). `trigger_time` is the run
time, or the start for manual runs. `message` names the run, its trigger and
its outcome, for example `#4 schedule ok` or
`#5 schedule skipped (misfire)`. `operation` is the journal operation of the
run.

The service keeps `schedule.history_keep` runs per schedule (default 20).
Manual runs made without the service are not recorded.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `text` | none | Only runs of this schedule. |
| `limit` | `int` | `20` | Maximum number of runs, newest first. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `schedule_run` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

List the last twenty runs of all schedules:

```nurt example
schedule.history
```

List the last five runs of one schedule:

```nurt example
schedule.history "s1" limit: 5
```

List the runs that did not succeed:

```nurt example
schedule.history limit: 100 |> filter exit_state != "ok" |> select schedule_id started message
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | No schedule and no recorded run has the identifier `id`. | List the schedules with `schedule.list`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `limit` is below 1 or `id` is not a schedule identifier. | Give a positive `limit` and an identifier such as `s3`. |
| `E_FORMAT` | `<state>/schedules/state.json` is damaged. | Restart the background service; it rewrites the file. |
| `E_IO` | The schedule store cannot be read. | Check the permissions of the state directory. |

## Related

`schedule.list` shows the last result of each schedule; `schedule.run` runs
a schedule outside its run times.

title: schedule.list
text:
# schedule.list

## Synopsis

```text
schedule.list [<id>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

`schedule.list` returns one `schedule` record per schedule, ordered by
identifier. Without parameters it lists every schedule of the account; `state`
keeps the schedules in one state, and `id` returns one schedule.

The state of a schedule is `paused` while it is paused, `completed` after
`max_runs` runs started by run times, `expired` after its expiry time or after
a missed single time, and `active` otherwise. `active` is `true` only for an
active schedule while the background service runs; otherwise `reason` gives
the cause: `service_not_running`, `paused`, `completed` or `expired`.

`next_run`, `last_run`, `runs` (runs started by run times) and `last_result`
come from the run state kept by the background service. A schedule that the
service has not yet seen shows the next run time computed from its trigger.
Times are instants; the text form shows them with the offset of the time zone
of the schedule.

The command reads the schedule store and changes nothing.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `text` | none | Schedule to show with its last five runs. |
| `state` | `enum(all\|active\|paused\|completed\|expired)` | `all` | Only schedules in this state. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `schedule` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

List all schedules:

```nurt example
schedule.list
```

List the paused schedules:

```nurt example
schedule.list state: paused
```

Show one schedule:

```nurt example
schedule.list "s3"
```

List the labels and next run times of active schedules that do not run:

```nurt example
schedule.list state: active |> filter not active |> select label next_run reason
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | No schedule has the identifier `id`. `actual` lists the identifier. | List the schedules with `schedule.list` and use one of their identifiers. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `id` is not a schedule identifier or `state` is unknown. | Give an identifier such as `s3` and one of the listed states. |
| `E_FORMAT` | `<state>/schedules/state.json` is damaged. | Restart the background service; it rewrites the file. |
| `E_IO` | The schedule store cannot be read. | Check the permissions of the state directory. |

## Related

`schedule.history` lists past runs of the schedules; `schedule.create`,
`schedule.pause`, `schedule.resume` and `schedule.remove` change them.

title: schedule.pause
text:
# schedule.pause

## Synopsis

```text
schedule.pause <id>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

`schedule.pause` marks the selected active schedules as paused in one
operation of the journal and returns one `effect` record per selected
schedule. A paused schedule keeps its definition and history and makes no
runs; run times that pass while it is paused are not made up. A run in
progress is not stopped.

Only schedules in the state `active` change. Paused, completed and expired
schedules are reported with `action: unchanged` and their state in `before`,
and no file is written for them.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `list<text>` | none | Schedules to pause. |
| `all` | `bool` | `false` | Pause all schedules. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

The effect record has `kind: schedule.pause`, `target: schedule:<id>`,
`action` (`pause` or `unchanged`), `before` with the previous state and
`after` with the new state.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Pause one schedule:

```nurt example
schedule.pause "s2"
```

Pause two schedules in one operation:

```nurt example
schedule.pause ["s2", "s4"]
```

Pause every schedule, for example before maintenance of the device:

```nurt example
schedule.pause all: true
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | Neither `id` nor `all: true` is given. | Give the identifiers or `all: true`. |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | `id` and `all: true` are given together. | Keep one of them. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | Some identifiers do not exist; `actual` lists them. Nothing is changed. | Correct the identifiers; `schedule.list` shows the existing ones. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | An identifier contains characters other than letters, digits, `-` and `_`. | Give identifiers such as `s3`. |
| `E_IO` | The schedule store cannot be written. | Check the permissions of the state directory. |

## Related

`schedule.resume` resumes paused schedules; `schedule.list state: paused`
lists them.

title: schedule.remove
text:
# schedule.remove

## Synopsis

```text
schedule.remove <id>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

`schedule.remove` deletes the definitions of the selected schedules in one
operation of the journal and returns one `effect` record per schedule. Either
`id` or `all: true` selects the schedules; every identifier must exist.

Removing a schedule stops its runs in progress: the programs of the action
receive `terminate` and, after `run.kill_grace`, `kill`. A run waiting in the
queue of `overlap: queue` is dropped. The stopped runs are listed in
`after.stopped_jobs` of the effect record, and the effect is marked
irreversible with `process_stopped`, because a stopped program cannot be
resumed.

The run history of a removed schedule stays in the run state and remains
visible in `schedule.history`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `list<text>` | none | Schedules to remove. |
| `all` | `bool` | `false` | Remove all schedules. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

The effect record has `kind: schedule.remove`, `target: schedule:<id>`,
`action: remove`, `before` with the state before the removal and `after` with
`state: removed` and, when runs were stopped, `stopped_jobs`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

After `undo` the restored schedule counts its next run time from the time of
the restoration, so run times that passed while it was removed are not made
up.

## Examples

Remove one schedule:

```nurt example
schedule.remove "s1"
```

Remove two schedules in one operation:

```nurt example
schedule.remove ["s1", "s2"]
```

Remove every schedule:

```nurt example
schedule.remove all: true
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | Neither `id` nor `all: true` is given. | Give the identifiers or `all: true`. |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | `id` and `all: true` are given together. | Keep one of them. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | Some identifiers do not exist; `actual` lists them. Nothing is removed. | Correct the identifiers; `schedule.list` shows the existing ones. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | An identifier contains characters other than letters, digits, `-` and `_`. | Give identifiers such as `s3`. |
| `E_IO` | The schedule store cannot be written. | Check the permissions of the state directory. |

## Related

`schedule.pause` suspends a schedule without removing it. `schedule.list`
shows the schedules and `schedule.history` their past runs.

title: schedule.resume
text:
# schedule.resume

## Synopsis

```text
schedule.resume <id>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

`schedule.resume` makes the selected paused schedules active again in one
operation of the journal and returns one `effect` record per selected
schedule. The next run time counts from the time of the resumption: a
schedule with `every: 10m` resumed at 15:07 next runs at 15:17. A run that
waited in the queue of `overlap: queue` before the pause is dropped. A single
time (`at`) that passed during the pause is handled by `on_missed`.

Only schedules in the state `paused` change. Active, completed and expired
schedules are reported with `action: unchanged` and their state in `before`,
and no file is written for them.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `list<text>` | none | Schedules to resume. |
| `all` | `bool` | `false` | Resume all paused schedules. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

The effect record has `kind: schedule.resume`, `target: schedule:<id>`,
`action` (`resume` or `unchanged`), `before` with the previous state and
`after` with the new state.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Resume one schedule:

```nurt example
schedule.resume "s2"
```

Resume two schedules in one operation:

```nurt example
schedule.resume ["s2", "s4"]
```

Resume every paused schedule and list the next run times:

```nurt example
schedule.resume all: true
schedule.list state: active |> select id label next_run
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | Neither `id` nor `all: true` is given. | Give the identifiers or `all: true`. |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | `id` and `all: true` are given together. | Keep one of them. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | Some identifiers do not exist; `actual` lists them. Nothing is changed. | Correct the identifiers; `schedule.list` shows the existing ones. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | An identifier contains characters other than letters, digits, `-` and `_`. | Give identifiers such as `s3`. |
| `E_IO` | The schedule store cannot be written. | Check the permissions of the state directory. |

## Related

`schedule.pause` pauses schedules; `schedule.list` shows their state and next
run time.

title: schedule.run
text:
# schedule.run

## Synopsis

```text
schedule.run <id>
```

## Description

`schedule.run` runs the action of a schedule once and returns the output
records of the action, for example the `exec` record of a `run` stage. The
run does not change the next run time and does not count against `max_runs`.
Paused, completed and expired schedules can be run as well.

With a running background service, the service executes the run as an
operation of the session `schedule:<id>`, records it in the history with
`trigger: manual` and returns when it ends. A run of the same schedule that
is still in progress, scheduled or manual, makes the command fail with
`E_JOB_STATE`; the lock is shared by the service and every console process.

Without the service, the calling process runs an action of kind `pipeline`
itself, in the current session; such a run is not recorded in the history.
Actions of other kinds run only in the service.

A definition whose action no longer matches its integrity hash is not run.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `text` | required | Schedule to run. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `exec`, `job` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `run` |
| Effect | `process` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | File changes are reversible as for run; effects outside the file system are irreversible. |

## Examples

Run a schedule now:

```nurt example
schedule.run "s1"
```

Run a schedule and keep its exit code and standard output:

```nurt example
schedule.run "s1" |> select exit_code stdout
```

Create a schedule and test its action at once:

```nurt example
schedule.create "report" cron: "0 7 * * mon" action: (run ["./weekly-report.sh"] cwd: "/srv/reports")
schedule.run "s1"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `id` is missing. | Give the identifier of the schedule. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | No schedule has the identifier `id`. | List the schedules with `schedule.list`. |
| `E_JOB_STATE` | A run of the schedule is in progress; `actual` holds its identifier, for example `s1#4`. | Wait until the run ends, or follow it with `schedule.history`. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The action cannot run here: its kind runs only in the service, or its definition was changed outside the schedule commands. | Start the background service, or remove the schedule and create it again. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `id` is not a schedule identifier. | Give an identifier such as `s3`. |

Errors of the action itself, such as `E_TIMEOUT`, are returned as reported by
its stages.

## Related

`schedule.history` lists the runs made by the service; `schedule.create`
with `run_now: true` runs a new schedule at creation.

title: search
text:
# search

## Synopsis

```text
search <pattern> <path>... [name: value]...
entry|content|line |> search <pattern> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`search` finds a pattern in the content of files. The source form walks the
given files and directories: a directory is searched recursively, with the
filters `glob`, `exclude`, `exclude_preset`, `hidden` and `gitignore`, and
with the file types of `file_type` and `exclude_file_type`. The stage form
searches the files of input `entry` records (a directory entry is walked as
in the source form), the text of input `content` records and the text of
input `line` records. Without matches the result is empty.

`glob` and `exclude` compare patterns and paths in Unicode normalization
form C (NFC). A name stored decomposed, as on macOS volumes, matches a
pattern written composed, and a decomposed pattern matches a composed name.

A pattern is text, a regular expression written as `/…/flags`, or a list of
both. With `mode: auto` text is matched literally and `/…/` is a regular
expression; `mode: literal` and `mode: regex` treat every pattern one way.
With a list of patterns every match carries `pattern`, the index of its
pattern from 0, and `output: counts` gives one count per pattern.

Regular expressions use the syntax of the Rust `regex` crate: classes such
as `[a-z]`, `\d`, `\w`, `\s`, Unicode properties `\p{Greek}`, groups `( )`,
`(?:…)`, named groups `(?<name>…)` and `(?P<name>…)`, and the flags `i`,
`m`, `s` and `x`. Classes, `\w`, `\b` and case folding follow Unicode. `^`
and `$` match at the start and end of every line. Look-ahead, look-behind
and back-references are evaluated by a backtracking engine with a step
limit; such matches report `regex_engine: backtracking`, and a line that
exceeds the step limit counts as not matching (notable
`regex_backtracking`). Compared with JavaScript regular expressions, `\d`
and `\w` also match non-ASCII digits and letters, and the flags `g`, `u`
and `y` do not exist.

Every matching line is one `match` record with the position of its first
match. With `only_matching` every match is one record and `line` holds the
matched text. `start` and `end` count bytes from the start of the file as
stored, also in files that are not UTF-8; `column` counts characters from 1.
With `multiline` a match may cross line breaks and reports `end_line` and
`end_column`; a literal pattern that contains a line break implies it.

Binary files are skipped and counted (notable `binary_skipped`) unless
`binary: text` is given. Text in another encoding, such as UTF-16 or
Windows-1250, is decoded before matching. Lines longer than `max_line`
characters are shortened around the first match, with a marker of the
omitted characters (notable `truncated_lines`).

`max_per_file` limits the matches reported for one file; `0`, like leaving it
out, means no limit.

`output: matches` gives `match` records. `output: counts` gives one `match`
record per file, or per file and pattern, with `count`, the number of
matches, and the position of the first match. `output: files` and
`output: unmatched` give `entry` records of the files with and without
matches, with `match_count`.

`sort: path` keeps the order of the walk (roots in the order given, then
depth first by name) or of the input records, and produces records as files
are searched. `sort: modified` puts the most recently modified files first,
`sort: count` the files with the most matches, and `sort: rank` the files
that match the most patterns, then the most matches, then the shallowest
paths; these orders search every file first. With `adaptive: true` and a
limit on the number of records (for example `|> first 50`), files with the
most matches are shown in full while the records fit in the limit, and the
other files are given as one `match` record with `count` and
`summarized: true`.

`scope`, `enclosing` and `mode: syntax` use the code command group. `scope`
keeps the matches in code, comments or string literals; a file of a
language without a grammar counts as code only. `enclosing` adds
`container`, the qualified name, kind and lines of the innermost definition
around each match; without the code group the field is left out. With
`mode: syntax` the pattern is a code pattern of the language with
metavariables such as `$X`; the captured metavariables are in `named`.

Files are searched in parallel within the thread limit of the execution;
the order of the result does not depend on the number of threads.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `text \| regex \| list<text \| regex>` | required | Pattern; with a list, counts are given per pattern. |
| `path` | `list<path>` | required | Files or directories to search in the source form. |
| `glob` | `glob \| list<glob>` | `"**"` | Name patterns of the files to search. |
| `mode` | `enum(auto\|literal\|regex\|syntax)` | `auto` | Pattern mode; auto treats text as literal and /…/ as a regular expression. |
| `case_sensitive` | `bool` | `true` | Match with case sensitivity. |
| `whole_word` | `bool` | `false` | Match whole words only. |
| `multiline` | `bool` | `false` | Allow matches across lines. |
| `invert` | `bool` | `false` | Produce the lines that do not match. |
| `only_matching` | `bool` | `false` | Give only the matched text instead of the whole line. |
| `trim` | `bool` | `false` | Trim leading and trailing whitespace of lines. |
| `dedupe` | `bool` | `false` | Drop repeated identical lines. |
| `scope` | `enum(any\|code\|comments\|strings)` | `any` | Part of source code in which matches count. |
| `enclosing` | `bool` | `false` | Add the enclosing code element of each match. |
| `max_line` | `int` | `500` | Maximum length of a reported line in characters. |
| `exclude` | `list<glob>` | `[]` | Patterns to exclude, in gitignore syntax. |
| `exclude_preset` | `list<enum(vcs\|deps\|build\|cache)>` | `[]` | Predefined exclusions: version control, dependencies, build output, caches. |
| `context` | `int` | `0` | Lines of context before and after each match. |
| `before` | `int` | none | Lines of context before each match. |
| `after` | `int` | none | Lines of context after each match. |
| `output` | `enum(matches\|files\|counts\|unmatched)` | `matches` | Matches, matching files, counts per file, or files without matches. |
| `max_per_file` | `int` | none | Maximum number of matches per file; `0` and no value mean no limit. |
| `binary` | `enum(skip\|text)` | `skip` | Skip binary files or search them as text. |
| `whitespace` | `enum(exact\|trailing\|indent\|normalize)` | `exact` | Tolerance of whitespace differences for literal patterns. |
| `hidden` | `bool` | `true` | Include hidden files. |
| `gitignore` | `bool` | `false` | Apply the rules of .gitignore files. |
| `language` | `text` | none | Programming language of syntax patterns. |
| `file_type` | `list<text>` | `[]` | File types by extension, such as go or ts; applies in every output mode. |
| `exclude_file_type` | `list<text>` | `[]` | File types by extension to leave out. |
| `sort` | `enum(path\|modified\|count\|rank)` | `path` | Sort key of the results; rank orders by relevance. |
| `adaptive` | `bool` | `false` | Fit the result to the limit: full matches for files with most matches, counts for the rest. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `none` | `match`, `entry` |
| `stage` | `entry`, `content`, `line` | `match`, `entry` |

`match` fields: `path`, `no`, `column`, `start`, `end`, `text`, `line`,
`etag`, and when they apply `groups` (group 0 is the whole match), `named`,
`before`, `after`, `count`, `pattern`, `container`, `regex_engine`,
`end_line`, `end_column`, `summarized`. In the stage form the offsets of a
`content` record with a range of lines, and of a `line` record without
`start`, count from the start of the record text; consecutive `line` records
of one file are counted together.

The text form of the result shows the columns `path`, `no`, `column`, `text`
and, when it applies, `count`. All fields stay in the JSON form and appear in
the text with verbosity `detailed` or when the request names them in
`fields`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Find literal text in the files of a directory.

```nurt example
search "fn main" "src"
```

```text expected
src/main.rs:1:1: fn main() {
```

Show the names captured by a regular expression, one record per match.

```nurt example
search /fn (?<name>\w+)/ "src" only_matching: true
```

```text expected
src/lib.rs:1:5: fn run
src/main.rs:1:1: fn main
```

Search a log without regard to case, with one line of context.

```nurt example
search "warning" "logs" case_sensitive: false context: 1
```

```text expected
logs/app.log:2:1: WARNING: disk almost full
```

Count the matches of each pattern of a list per file.

```nurt example
search ["run", "main"] "src" output: counts
```

List the files with matches, the files with the most matches first.

```nurt example
search /\brun\b|\bmain\b/ "." output: files sort: count
```

A response that leaves records out ends with the hint "more: next" and carries the field
`continuation`; the command `next` returns the next part without running the
command again.

```text
matched 212  shown 50  more: next
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | No pattern, or no path in the source form. | Give `pattern` and `path`. |
| `E_REGEX` | The regular expression is not valid; `found` holds the pattern. | Correct the expression at the reported character. |
| `E_LIMIT` | A compiled pattern is too large, more results than `max_records` are held for `sort`, or a file above the text limit is searched with `scope`, `enclosing` or a syntax pattern. | Simplify the pattern, narrow the search, or search the file with a text pattern. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` | A value of an enumeration or a file type is unknown. | Use one of the listed values. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | A count is negative, or the pattern list is empty. | Give 0 or more, or at least one pattern. |
| `E_TYPE` | A parameter or an input record has another type. | Pass text, regular expressions, paths, or `entry`, `content` and `line` records. |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | `invert` is combined with `scope` or `mode: syntax`. | Leave out one of them. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | `scope` or `mode: syntax` is used without the code command group. | Load the code group, or search with `scope: any` and a text pattern. |
| `E_PATH_RELATIVE` | A relative path is given without a base directory. | Give an absolute path or set the `base` option. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | A file or directory of `path` does not exist. | Check the path. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | A root cannot be read. | Check the access rights of the path. |
| `E_IO` | A root cannot be read. | Check the access rights of the path. |

## Related

`find`, `read`, `lines`, `replace`, `help skill: "text-editing"`.

title: select
text:
# select

## Synopsis

```text
any |> select <fields>...
```

## Description

`select` keeps the named fields of each record, in the order written, and
adds computed fields written as `name: expression`. A field path such as
`owner.name` reads a field inside another field and is named after its last
segment.

Records that only keep top-level fields keep their record kind. Records with
a computed field, or with a field read from inside another field, become
`map` records. A field the record does not have stops the program with
`E_UNKNOWN_FIELD`, which lists the fields of the record.

The stage is lazy and keeps the header of the stream. The order declared by
the source and its presentation hint are dropped, because they may name
fields that are no longer present. An empty input gives an empty output.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fields` | `list<field \| named_expression>` | required | Fields to keep and name: expression pairs to compute. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `any` | `any` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `transform` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Keep the path and the size of each file:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> select path size
```

Add a computed field that marks large files:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> select path large: size > 2kb
```

Keep the exit code and the output of a program run:

```nurt example
run ["git", "status", "--short"] cwd: "/home/user/project" |> select exit_code stdout
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | no field is given | name at least one field |
| `E_UNKNOWN_FIELD` | a field is not in the record; `expected` lists the fields | use one of the listed fields |
| `E_TYPE` | an item is neither a field nor `name: expression` | write a field name or `name: expression` |

## Related

`filter`, `sort`, `distinct`, `describe`.

title: services
text:
# services

## Synopsis

```text
services [<name>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

Reading the state of system units needs no rights; `start`, `stop`, `restart`, `enable` and `disable` on system units need the administrator, which `privilege: elevated` on the last stage provides (see those commands).

`services` lists the services of the service manager of the system: systemd
on Linux, the service control manager on Windows and launchd on macOS. It
starts a pipeline and produces one `service` record per service; on Linux the
records are sorted by name.

A text `name` selects one service the way the manager resolves names: on
Linux `nginx` and `nginx.service` name the same unit and template instances
such as `getty@tty1` are accepted; on Windows the comparison ignores case.
When the manager knows no such service, the command fails with `E_NOT_FOUND`.
A regular expression `name` keeps the services whose name matches it.

`state` keeps the services whose state, raw state, or one part of the raw
state separated by `/` equals the text, ignoring case. `state: "failed"`
matches the common state; `state: "exited"` matches the systemd raw state
`active/exited`.

On Linux the command merges the loaded units with the unit files that are
installed but not loaded, so a disabled service that never ran is listed as
`stopped`. Units of other types and unit templates are not listed. The manager
is reached over D-Bus; no external program is run. `scope: user` reads the
manager of the current account on the session bus.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `text \| regex` | none | Service name or pattern. |
| `state` | `text` | none | Only services in this state. |
| `scope` | `enum(system\|user)` | `system` | System services or services of the current account. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `service` |

The `service` record holds `name`, `state` (`running`, `stopped`, `starting`,
`stopping`, `failed`, `paused`, `unknown`), `start_type` (`automatic`,
`manual`, `disabled`, `on_demand`, `static`, `unknown`), `manager`, `scope`,
and where the manager reports them `state_raw`, `description`, `pid`, `path`,
`account` and `os_raw`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| External use | `system_program`: `launchctl`; On macOS the state of services is read through the launchctl component of the operating system. |

## Examples

Show one service:

```nurt example
services name: "cron"
```

List the failed services:

```nurt example
services state: "failed"
```

List the running services of the current account:

```nurt example
services scope: user state: "running"
```

Restart one service:

```nurt example
services name: "nginx" |> restart
```

A response that leaves records out ends with the hint "more: next" and carries the field
`continuation`; the command `next` returns the next part without running the
command again.

```text
matched 230  shown 50  more: next
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | No service has the given name. | List the services with `services` and use a listed name. |
| `E_REGEX` | The pattern of `name` is not a valid regular expression. | Correct the pattern. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `scope` is neither `system` nor `user`. | Use `scope: system` or `scope: user`. |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | The manager refused to show the service; `required` names the privilege. | Run as an account with that privilege. |
| `E_SERVICE` | The manager reported an error or cannot be reached. `os_code` is `no_systemd` when systemd is not the service manager and `no_user_bus` when the account has no session bus. | Use `scope: system`, or run on a system managed by systemd. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | The scope is not available on this system. | Use `scope: system`. |

## Related

`start`, `restart`, `enable` and `disable` act on the records of `services`;
`stop` stops them. `logs unit:` shows the log of a service. The `administration` group
page lists the other commands of the group.

title: set
text:
# set

## Synopsis

```text
set <path> [name: value]...
item |> set <value> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`set` changes the values at key paths of a structured document and keeps
every byte outside the changed values: indentation, quoting, comments, key
order, line endings, encoding and byte order mark. A value is written in the
style of its neighbours; a new key is added at the end of its map.

In the source form the document is the file `path`. `key` with `value` sets
one key path; `values` sets several key paths, in the order of the map. All
key paths of one call are changed in one transaction: when any of them
fails, nothing is written. Two key paths of one file that are equal or nested
(`a` and `a.b`) fail with `E_KEY_CONFLICT`, because the second change would
apply to the result of the first; appends (`list[+]`) never conflict.

In the stage form, after `read … key:` or `query`, every input `item`
record names a file, a key path and the entity tag of the file. The value of
each item is set to `value`, which may be an expression of the item.
Items of one file are changed together, in input order. Items are assigned to
a file by the identity of the file (device and file number), so two names of
one file, such as a symbolic link or a path through a linked directory, are one
file; a file that does not exist yet is identified by its normalised path.

Key paths use the syntax of the `key` type: `a.b`, `list[0]`, `list[-1]`,
`list[+]` to append, `list[*]` for every element, and `#1:` to select a
document of a multi-document YAML stream. An index equal to the length of a
list appends; a larger index fails with `E_KEY_CONFLICT`. A key path that
matches several nodes changes all of them, and `replacements` counts them.
An implicit repetition, such as a repeated XML element or a duplicated key,
without `[*]` fails with `E_KEY_CONFLICT` and lists the candidates `[0]`,
`[1]`, ….

With `create: true` missing keys and intermediate maps are created and the
change reports the notable event `keys_created`. A missing file is created
when every change of the call sets a value; the new document starts empty,
or with the smallest root map of its format (`{}` for JSON, an empty
`<dict>` for property lists, the first key as the root element for XML).
With `create: false` a missing key fails with `E_KEY_NOT_FOUND`, which lists
the closest existing keys as candidates.

Every change passes two guards of the format: the bytes outside the changed
nodes must stay the same, and the changed document must read back as the
original value with the change applied. A construct that cannot be changed
without losing its layout fails with `E_UNSUPPORTED_CONSTRUCT`, naming the
construct; the file is not changed.

`validate` compares the syntax problems of the document before and after the
change. Only an error that the change introduces counts; errors present
before the change are ignored. With `reject` such an error fails the call,
with `warn` the change is written, a warning is logged and the change gets
the flag `validate_warning`, with `off` the check is skipped.

A call that leaves the document unchanged, for example a value equal to the
current one, writes nothing and reports the notable event `unchanged`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | Document to change in the source form. |
| `key` | `key` | none | Key path to set, such as "scripts.test" or "deps[+]" to append to a list. |
| `value` | `any` | none | New value at the key path. |
| `values` | `map<any>` | none | Several key paths and their values, set in one transaction. |
| `create` | `bool` | `true` | Create missing keys and intermediate tables. |
| `format` | `enum(auto\|json\|jsonc\|yaml\|toml\|xml\|ini\|csv\|tsv\|properties\|env\|plist)` | `auto` | Document format; auto selects it from the file extension. |
| `validate` | `enum(off\|warn\|reject)` | `reject` | Roll back the change when it introduces a new syntax error. |
| `if_match` | `text` | none | Expected etag of the document; a different document is not changed. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `none` | `effect` |
| `stage` | `item` | `effect` |

The `effect` record lists one change per written file with `action`
(`modify` or `create`), `size_before`, `size_after`, `hash_before`,
`replacements` and `flags`, and the notable events `keys_created`,
`alias_shared`, `merge_override`, `duplicate_key` and `unchanged` reported by
the formats.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

The operation journal preserves every target file before the first write.
Each file is written with the entity tag read during planning as its
expected state; a file changed in the meantime fails with `E_STALE` and no
file is written. `undo` restores every changed file byte for byte and
removes files that the call created.

## Examples

Set one key of a JSON file:

```nurt example
set "/home/user/app/package.json" key: "scripts.test" value: "vitest run"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/package.json", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "{\n  \"name\": \"app\",\n  \"scripts\": {\n    \"test\": \"jest\"\n  }\n}\n" }
] }
```

```text expected
1 file changed
```

Set two keys of a YAML file in one transaction:

```nurt example
set "/home/user/app/compose.yaml" values: {"services.web.image": "nginx:1.27", "services.web.ports[+]": "8443:443"}
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/compose.yaml", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "services:\n  web:\n    image: nginx:1.25\n    ports:\n      - \"8080:80\"\n" }
] }
```

Change the value read by `read … key:`:

```nurt example
read "/home/user/app/config.toml" key: "server.port" |> set 8081
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app/config.toml", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "# server settings\n[server]\nport = 8080 # public port\n" }
] }
```

Create a missing file with a nested key:

```nurt example
set "/home/user/app/settings.json" key: "editor.tabSize" value: 2
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_KEY_NOT_FOUND` | a key path does not exist and `create` is `false`; `candidates` lists the closest keys | correct the key path or set `create: true` |
| `E_KEY_CONFLICT` | two key paths of one file overlap, an index is past the end of a list, or a key path matches a repetition without `[*]` | change overlapping keys in separate calls, use `[+]`, or select one candidate |
| `E_STALE` | the document differs from `if_match` or from the entity tag of the item, or changed between planning and writing | read the document again and repeat the change |
| `E_DOC_PARSE` | the document cannot be read, or the change introduces a syntax error with `validate: reject` (`problem`: `validate`) | correct the document or the value, or use `validate: warn` |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED_CONSTRUCT` | the change cannot keep the layout of a construct; `found` names the construct | change the construct by hand, or use `replace` |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | the file does not exist and `create` is `false`, or a removal names a missing file | check the path or set `create: true` |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | neither `key` with `value` nor `values` is given | add `key` and `value`, or `values` |
| `E_TYPE` | `values` is not a map, or the input is not `item` records | pass a map of key paths to values |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `if_match` is not an entity tag, or `validate` has another value | pass the `etag` field of a record |
| `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` | `format` names a format that is not available | use one of the listed formats |
| `E_LIMIT` | the file is larger than the document size limit | raise `limits.max_file_bytes_text` |

## Related

`read` with `key:` to read values and their entity tags, `query` to select
values with `jq` filters, `remove` to delete the keys of `item` records,
`undo` to revert a change.

title: skip
text:
# skip

## Synopsis

```text
any |> skip <count>
```

## Description

`skip` drops the first `count` input records and passes on the rest. The
stage is lazy: it reads the dropped records one at a time and then passes on
each further record when the next stage asks for it. An error of the source
among the dropped records still stops the program.

The order, the header and the presentation hint of the stream are kept. An
input with no more than `count` records gives an empty output.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | `int` | required | Number of records to drop. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `any` | `same` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `transform` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Drop the first file of a listing:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> skip 1
```

Drop the header line of a CSV file:

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/data.csv" |> skip 1
```

Dropping more records than the input holds gives no records:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> skip 5
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `count` is missing | write a number after `skip` |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `count` is negative | use 0 or a larger number |

## Related

`first`, `last`.

title: sleep
text:
# sleep

## Synopsis

```text
sleep <duration>
```

## Description

`sleep` blocks the program for the given time and then returns without
output. It starts a pipeline and accepts no input.

The wait is performed on the clock of the execution and is interrupted by
cancellation and by the time limit of the program. A cancelled program
returns `E_CANCELLED` within 100 ms of the signal. A wait of `0s` returns at
once.

A wait that reaches the time limit of the program ends at the limit with
`E_TIMEOUT`. The error carries the requested time in `expected` and the time
waited in `actual`, both in milliseconds. When the program does not set
`timeout`, its time limit is raised to the longest `sleep` it contains, so a
wait longer than the default limit of `run` is not cut short; an explicit
`timeout` of the program always applies.

The command changes nothing. It opens no journal operation and has no entry
in the operation history. The time waited is reported as a progress event with
the waited milliseconds as `done` and the requested milliseconds as `total`.
A check of the program (`nurt_check`) reports `waits: true` and the requested
duration without waiting.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `duration` | `duration` | required | Time to wait. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `none` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `run` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Waits | always blocks the call |

## Examples

Wait for half a second:

```nurt example
sleep 500ms
```

Wait for two seconds:

```nurt example
sleep 2s
```

Create a schedule whose action waits for two seconds, then run the action once
outside its times:

```nurt example
schedule.create "pause" every: 10m action: (sleep 2s)
schedule.run "s1"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | The duration is negative or its end is beyond the range of the clock. | Give a non-negative duration such as `500ms` or `2s`. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The execution was cancelled before or during the wait. | None; the cancellation was requested by the caller. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The time limit of the program ended the wait. `expected` holds the requested milliseconds and `actual` the milliseconds waited. | Set a longer `timeout` for the program or a shorter duration. |

## Related

`schedule.create` and `schedule.run` use `sleep` in the action of a schedule.
`run` starts a program and waits for it with the `wait` parameter. The `system`
group page lists the other commands of the group.

title: sort
text:
# sort

## Synopsis

```text
any |> sort <by>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

`sort` orders the records by one or more keys, the first key first. Keys are
fields or expressions. Values compare by the total order of values: values of
different types order by type (`null` first, then `bool`, numbers, sizes,
durations, instants, text, paths and the other types), so a mixed field sorts
deterministically. Text compares by Unicode code points.

The sort is stable: records with equal keys keep their input order, also with
`order: desc`. `sort` reads the whole input and holds it in memory within the
record limit of the request; a larger input stops the program with `E_LIMIT`.
When the source already produces the records in the requested order, the
stream passes through unchanged. The output declares its order, so a
following `sort` by the same fields does not sort again. An empty input gives
an empty output.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `by` | `list<field>` | required | Fields to sort by, in order of priority. |
| `order` | `enum(asc\|desc)` | `asc` | Sort order. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `any` | `same` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `transform` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Sort files from the largest:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> sort size order: desc
```

Sort by extension, then by size within each extension:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> sort extension size
```

Sort the lines of a file alphabetically:

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/data.txt" |> sort text
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | no key is given | name at least one field |
| `E_UNKNOWN_FIELD` | a key names a field the records do not have; `expected` lists their fields | use one of the listed fields |
| `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` | `order` is neither `asc` nor `desc` | write `order: asc` or `order: desc` |
| `E_LIMIT` | the input holds more records than the limit | narrow the input with `filter` first |

## Related

`first`, `last`, `group`, `distinct`.

title: split
text:
# split

## Synopsis

```text
line |> split <delimiter> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`split` divides the `text` of each `line` record at `delimiter` and gives a
`row` record whose `cells` are the parts, as text. A text delimiter is
matched literally; a regular expression matches any delimiter it describes,
such as `/\s+/` for runs of white space.

Cells are named by `names` in order. Parts beyond the names are named
`c<n>` by their position from 1, and names beyond the parts get `null`.
Without `names` the cells are `c1`, `c2`, and so on. The row keeps the `path`
and the line number `no` of its line. The stage is lazy and keeps the header
of the stream.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `delimiter` | `text \| regex` | required | Delimiter text or pattern. |
| `names` | `list<text>` | none | Names of the columns. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `line` | `row` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `transform` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Split CSV lines into numbered columns:

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/data.csv" |> split ","
```

Split CSV lines after the header into named columns:

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/data.csv" |> skip 1 |> split "," names: ["id", "name"]
```

Split columns separated by white space:

```nurt example
lines "/home/user/table.txt" |> split /\s+/ names: ["user", "shell"]
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | the delimiter is an empty text | give at least one character |
| `E_REGEX` | the delimiter pattern does not compile | correct the pattern |
| `E_TYPE` | the input records are not `line`, or `names` is not a list of text | read the file with `lines`; write names as `["a", "b"]` |

## Related

`parse`, `lines`, `skip`.

title: sql
text:
# sql

## Synopsis

```text
sql <path> <query> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`sql` runs the SQL statements of `query` on the SQLite database file `path`
and produces one `row` record per result row. Statements run in order;
statements without result columns produce no records.

A call whose statements only read (`SELECT`, `VALUES`, `EXPLAIN`, a `WITH`
without `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`, a pragma that only reads) opens the
database read-only and sets the connection to `query_only`. A call with a
statement that changes anything opens the database for writing and is an
effect; no refusal asks for `write: true`. The statements that make a call a
change are every other statement, a pragma that sets a value or acts, and a
call of `load_extension`. A query that is not a literal text is a change.
`write: true` stays as an optional explicit form. `write: false` keeps the
call read-only: a statement that changes the database then fails with
`E_SQL` (`problem`: `write_required`), and the error carries the same call
without `write: false` as `fix`. Every statement of a read is prepared and
checked before the first row is produced.

A change journals the database file and its `-wal`, `-shm` and `-journal`
files before the first statement runs. The statements run in one
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. The transaction is committed when every
statement succeeds and rolled back when one fails; nothing is changed then.
After the commit the write-ahead log of every database is checkpointed into
its file with `TRUNCATE`, so the files hold the new state.

| Statement | Rule |
|---|---|
| `BEGIN`, `COMMIT`, `END` | merged with the transaction of the call; they change nothing |
| `ROLLBACK` | rolls the call back and ends it with `E_ROLLED_BACK`; the database and the journal stay as before |
| `SAVEPOINT`, `RELEASE`, `ROLLBACK TO` | run inside the transaction |
| `ATTACH` | allowed; runs outside the transaction (the transaction is committed before it and opened again for the next change). The file is computed (a literal, a parameter or any expression, evaluated with a `SELECT` first), resolved like every path argument (a relative file needs `base` or `scope.base`, otherwise `E_PATH_RELATIVE`), and journaled before the statement; a `file:` URI is read to its path and `mode=memory` or `:memory:` needs no file. SQLite then receives the resolved name, so it opens the file that the journal preserved. A new file is journaled as created and `undo` removes it. When the file cannot be told (a URI with a host, an expression that gives no text), the call is marked irreversible (`external_effect`) before the change |
| `DETACH` | allowed; runs in its place, after the transaction is committed |
| `VACUUM`, `VACUUM schema` | run outside the transaction automatically, after the other statements; the database file is journaled first |
| `VACUUM INTO` | allowed; runs in its place after the earlier statements are committed, so the copy holds their result. The new file is resolved and journaled as created like the file of `ATTACH`, so `undo` removes it |
| pragmas that set a value or act | run outside the transaction, in their place, so `journal_mode`, `foreign_keys` and `temp_store_directory` work; `temp_store_directory` and `data_store_directory` are allowed and change the state of the whole Nurt process (SQLite keeps them in global variables); the call reports each as an effect that is not undone, and `undo` does not reset them |
| preview | the plan lists the effects of `load_extension` and of the two pragmas as irreversible entries (`external_effect`, "from the text of the statements"); the run reports what the authorizer saw |
| `load_extension` | allowed under any spelling (quoted or in another case); the report marks the call with `external_effect`, because the effects of the extension are unknown and cannot be undone |

A call that changes the database turns the defensive mode of SQLite off, as
the language allows `load_extension`; the schema stays untrusted. A call
with `write: false` keeps the defensive mode and refuses `ATTACH`, `DETACH`, the directory pragmas
(`problem`: `attach`, `pragma`) and `load_extension` (`problem`:
`extension`).

`path` must name an existing file. An empty file is an empty database, as in
SQLite. A file that does not start with the SQLite header, such as an
encrypted database, fails with `E_DOC_PARSE`.

Parameter values bind to the placeholders of the statements. `params` is
either a list or a map.

A list binds in statement order: each statement takes as many values as it
has parameters. Positional (`?`), numbered (`?2`) and named (`:id`, `@id`,
`$id`) placeholders take their value by their parameter index; a named
placeholder has the index of its first occurrence. The number of values must
equal the number of parameters of all statements.

A map binds named placeholders by name. A key is written with or without the
placeholder prefix, so `id` and `:id` both bind `:id`. Every named placeholder
needs an entry and every entry must be used by a placeholder. A positional
placeholder (`?`, `?2`) cannot be bound from a map. A violation fails with
`E_SQL` and the problem `parameter_name`.

| Value type | SQLite value |
|---|---|
| `null` | `NULL` |
| `bool` | `INTEGER` 0 or 1 |
| `int`, `size` (bytes), `duration` (milliseconds) | `INTEGER` |
| `number` | `REAL` |
| `text`, `path`, `glob`, `key`, `enum`, `decimal`, `date` | `TEXT` |
| `instant` | `TEXT` in ISO 8601 form |
| `bytes` | `BLOB` |

| SQLite value | Cell type |
|---|---|
| `INTEGER` | `int` |
| `REAL` | `number`; an infinity is the text `Inf` or `-Inf` |
| `TEXT` | `text`; text that is not UTF-8 is `bytes` |
| `BLOB` | `bytes` |
| `NULL` | `null` |

A read of a database in write-ahead log mode creates the files `-wal` and
`-shm` when they are missing and the directory is writable, as every SQLite
reader does; the database file itself is not changed.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | SQLite database file. |
| `query` | `text` | required | SQL statements. |
| `params` | `list<any> \| map<any>` | `[]` | Values bound to the placeholders of the statements: a list for positional placeholders, a map from names to values for named placeholders. |
| `write` | `bool` | none | Optional: a statement that changes the database opens it for writing without it. write: false keeps the call read-only. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `row` |

Fields of `row`:

Rows are produced while the query runs. A pipeline that uses only the first
rows, or a cancelled execution, interrupts the running statement.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | A call that changes the database copies the database file and its journal files first, and undo restores them; the files of ATTACH and VACUUM INTO are preserved or removed the same way. Without space for the copy, and for the effects of load_extension, the change is irreversible. |

| Action | Effect | Reversibility | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `write` | `local` | `reversible_if_preserved` | Applies when write is true, and without write when a statement changes anything. |

With a change the operation journal preserves the database file and the
files `-wal`, `-shm` and `-journal` next to it before the first statement
runs. `undo` restores the database and these files to their previous bytes
and removes journal files created by the change. Without space for the copy
the change is made and reported as irreversible with `no_space_for_copy`.
The change record of the database file reports the number of rows inserted,
updated or deleted, triggers included, in `rows_changed`.

A lock held by another connection is awaited for `sql.busy_timeout` (5
seconds by default) and then fails with `E_IN_USE`.

## Examples

Create a table in an empty database file and return the inserted row:

```nurt example
sql "/home/user/app.db" "create table users(id integer primary key, name text); insert into users(name) values (?) returning id, name" params: ["ada"]
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app.db", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "" }
] }
```

List the tables of a database:

```nurt example
sql "/home/user/app.db" "select name from sqlite_master where type = 'table' order by name"
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app.db", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "" }
] }
```

Bind named parameters from a map:

```nurt example
sql "/home/user/app.db" "select :low as low, :high as high" params: {"low": 1, "high": 9}
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app.db", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "" }
] }
```

Compute values from bound parameters with numbered placeholders:

```nurt example
sql "/home/user/app.db" "select ?2 - ?1 as span, upper(?3) as label" params: [5, 12, "week"]
```

```json fs-before
{ "format": "nurt-fs-snapshot/1", "entries": [
  { "path": "/home/user/app.db", "type": "file", "content_utf8": "" }
] }
```

A response that leaves records out ends with the hint "more: next" and carries the field
`continuation`; the command `next` returns the next part without running the
command again.

```text
matched 5000  shown 50  more: next
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_SQL` | a statement cannot be prepared or executed, changes the database with `write: false`, is refused with `write: false` (`problem`: `attach`, `extension`, `pragma`), holds no statement (`problem`: `empty_query`), or `params` does not match the statements (`problem`: `parameter_count`, `parameter_name`, `parameter_type`, `parameter_range`); the problem `write_required` marks a statement that changes the database with `write: false`, `VACUUM INTO` included; `details` holds `statement` and `sqlite_code` | correct the statement, remove `write: false`, or pass one value per parameter or one entry per named placeholder |
| `E_ROLLED_BACK` | a statement `ROLLBACK` ended the call; `details.statement` holds its number; the message and `details.irreversible` name effects that were reported earlier and cannot be undone | remove the `ROLLBACK` statement to keep the changes |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `path` or `query` is not given | pass both |
| `E_TYPE` | `path`, `query`, `params` or `write` has another type | pass `params` as a list or a map |
| `E_DOC_PARSE` | the file is not an SQLite database, is encrypted or damaged; `details.format` is `sqlite`, `details.sqlite_code` holds the SQLite code when SQLite reported it | pass an SQLite database file |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | the database file does not exist | check the path; an empty file is an empty database |
| `E_PATH_RELATIVE` | the file of `ATTACH` or `VACUUM INTO` is relative and the call has no `base` | give an absolute file or set `base` |
| `E_IN_USE` | another connection holds a lock longer than `sql.busy_timeout` | retry later or raise `sql.busy_timeout` |
| `E_IO` | the file cannot be read or written for another reason | see the message |
| `E_PERMISSION` | the file or its directory cannot be read or written | check the permissions |
| `E_NO_SPACE` | the volume is full during the change | free space and run the call again |
| `E_LIMIT` | the statements of a change return more rows than one execution may hold | return fewer rows from `RETURNING` or `SELECT` |
| `E_CANCELLED` | the execution was cancelled or its time limit passed; a change is rolled back | run the call again |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | the execution was cancelled or its time limit passed; a change is rolled back | run the call again |

## Related

`query` for JSON and other structured documents, `set` for values at key
paths, `undo` for reverting a change.

title: start
text:
# start

## Synopsis

```text
service |> start [name: value]...
```

## Description

`start` asks the service manager to start each input service and waits up to
`wait` until the service settles. The state is read every 100 ms at first;
the interval grows by 100 ms up to 500 ms, and the wait ends when the state is
neither `starting` nor `stopping`. A service that runs reports
`after: "running"`; a service that ran to completion, such as a systemd
`oneshot` unit, reports `after: "stopped"`. The wait observes cancellation and
the time limit of the program. With `wait: 0s` the command returns at once
and `after` holds the state read right after the request, usually `starting`.

Each input service is read before the action. A service that already runs is
not passed to the manager; its effect record has `before` equal to `after` and
the notable code `unchanged`. For every other service the operation is marked
irreversible with `service_changed` before the manager is asked to act, so the
effect is reported even when the wait fails. Services are processed in input
order; an error stops the processing of the remaining services.

**Privilege.** System units need the administrator: write `privilege: elevated` on the stage. `undo` of the entry stops the services that the command started.

```nurt
services name: "nginx" |> start privilege: elevated
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wait` | `duration` | `10s` | Time to wait for each service to reach the running state. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `service` | `effect` |

Each `effect` record holds `kind: "start"`, `target` (`service:<name>`),
`action`, `before` and `after`. A preview shows the same records with
`status: planned` and the expected `after`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `run` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| External use | `system_program`: `launchctl`; On macOS services are started through the launchctl component of the operating system. |

## Examples

Start one service:

```nurt example
services name: "cron" |> start
```

Start the stopped services of the current account without waiting:

```nurt example
services scope: user state: "stopped" |> start wait: 0s
```

Start a service and give it a minute to come up:

```nurt example
services name: "postgresql" |> start wait: 1m
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The service did not settle within `wait` or the time limit of the program. `expected` holds `running`, `actual` the current state; the effect is already applied. | Give a longer `wait`. |
| `E_SERVICE` | The service entered the `failed` state; `os_code` and `result` hold the reason given by the manager and `next_steps` holds `logs unit: "<name>"`. The manager may also report another error, for example a masked unit, in `os_code` and `os_message`. | Read the log of the service and correct its configuration. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The service no longer exists. | Read the services again with `services`. |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | The manager refused the action; `required` names the privilege, `root` on Linux and `administrator` on Windows. Interactive authorization is never requested. | Run as an account with that privilege. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | The record comes from the manager of another system. | Read the services on this system with `services`. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `wait` is negative. | Give a non-negative duration such as `10s`. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The execution was cancelled. | None; the cancellation was requested by the caller. |

## Related

`services` produces the input records. `restart` restarts services and `stop`
stops them. `logs unit:` shows why a service failed. The `administration` group page
lists the other commands of the group.

title: stop
text:
# stop

## Synopsis

```text
job|process|service |> stop [name: value]...
```

## Description

Stops every input job: the signal `signal` goes to the whole process group
or job object of the program, and after `grace` the remaining processes are
killed. The command returns after the job has ended and its final record,
its detected changes and its journal entry are written.

Only running and suspended jobs can be stopped. Job and process records are
handled by this implementation (the signal goes to the process of a `process`
record); service records are handled by the implementations of the system
commands, selected by the record kind of the input.

On Windows `terminate`, `interrupt` and `hangup` request the end of the
console program group; `kill` ends the job object.

**Privilege.** System units need the administrator: write `privilege: elevated` on the stage. `undo` of the entry starts the services that the command stopped; stopping a process or a job is irreversible.

```nurt
services name: "nginx" |> stop privilege: elevated
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `signal` | `enum(terminate\|kill\|interrupt\|hangup)` | `terminate` | Signal sent first. |
| `grace` | `duration` | `5s` | Time to wait before the process is killed. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `job`, `process`, `service` | `effect` |

Input `job`, `process` or `service` records. Produces one `effect` record per
input record; for a job its `job` field holds the final job record with the
state `stopped`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `run` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Stop job `j7`.

```nurt example
jobs "j7" |> stop
```

```text expected
stopped  job:j7
```

Stop all running jobs at once, without a grace period.

```nurt example
jobs state: running |> stop signal: kill
```

Interrupt job `j3` and kill it after ten seconds.

```nurt example
jobs "j3" |> stop signal: interrupt grace: 10s
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_JOB_STATE` | The job has already ended or lost its supervisor. | Read the job with `jobs "j7"`. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_JOB` | No job has the identifier. | Use one of the identifiers in `candidates`. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The supervisor of the job did not answer. | Read the state with `jobs "j7"`. |

## Related

`jobs`, `suspend`, `resume`, `remove`.

title: summarize
text:
# summarize

## Synopsis

```text
any |> summarize <fields>... [name: value]...
```

## Description

`summarize` gives one `summary` record per field in `fields`, and per group
when `by` is given, with the fields `field`, `count`, `sum`, `min`, `max` and
`average`; with `by`, the record starts with the group value under the name
of the `by` field.

`count` is the number of values other than `null`; `null` values are
skipped. Integers and numbers sum to an integer or a number and average to a
number. Sizes and durations sum and average in their own unit, rounded to
whole bytes and milliseconds. For text and other types, and for fields that
mix types, `sum` and `average` are `null` and `min` and `max` follow the
total order of values.

Without `fields`, each group gives one record with the number of its records
in `count`. Groups are ordered by their value. An empty input without `by`
gives one record per field with `count` 0.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fields` | `list<field>` | none | Numeric fields to summarize. |
| `by` | `field` | none | Field whose value forms the groups. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `any` | `summary` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `transform` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Compute the total and average size of the files of a project:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> summarize size
```

Compute the size statistics per extension:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> summarize size by: extension
```

Count the files per extension:

```nurt example
find "/home/user/project" |> summarize by: extension
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_UNKNOWN_FIELD` | a field is not in the records; `expected` lists their fields | use one of the listed fields |
| `E_LIMIT` | more groups than the limit | group by a field with fewer values |

## Related

`group`, `count`, `distinct`.

title: suspend
text:
# suspend

## Synopsis

```text
job|process |> suspend
```

## Description

Suspends the whole process tree of every input job: `SIGSTOP` to the process
group on Linux and macOS, suspension of the threads of the job object on
Windows. The job state becomes `suspended`. Time spent suspended is not
counted against the time limit of the job and is reported in
`suspended_total` of the final record.

Only running jobs can be suspended. Job and process records are handled by
this implementation.

## Parameters

The command has no parameters.

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `job`, `process` | `effect` |

Input `job` or `process` records. Produces one `effect` record per input
record; its `job` field holds the job record after the change.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `run` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `irreversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Suspend job `j7`.

```nurt example
jobs "j7" |> suspend
```

```text expected
suspended  job:j7
```

Suspend all running jobs.

```nurt example
jobs state: running |> suspend
```

Suspend job `j3` and read its state.

```nurt example
jobs "j3" |> suspend |> select job.state
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_JOB_STATE` | The job is not running, for example already suspended. | Resume it: `jobs "j7" \|> resume`. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_JOB` | No job has the identifier. | Use one of the identifiers in `candidates`. |

## Related

`resume`, `stop`, `jobs`.

title: sysctl.set
text:
# sysctl.set

## Synopsis

```text
sysctl.set <key> <value> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`sysctl.set` sets a kernel parameter with `sysctl -w` on Linux and macOS. The current value is read with `sysctl -n` and recorded; a parameter that already has the value is `unchanged`. With `persistent: true` on Linux the line `key = value` is written to `/etc/sysctl.d/90-nurt.conf` through the journal.

Rights: the command accepts `privilege`; write `privilege: elevated` when the account that runs Nurt is not the administrator. A program that fails for lack of rights ends the command with `E_PERMISSION`, and `privilege: auto` repeats it once elevated. An elevated entry is undone by the same elevated process.

`undo` runs `sysctl.set` with the recorded value; the journal restores the file.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | `text` | required | Name of the parameter, for example net.ipv4.ip_forward. |
| `value` | `text \| int` | required | New value. |
| `persistent` | `bool` | `false` | Also write the value to /etc/sysctl.d/90-nurt.conf (Linux); the file is journaled. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `system_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | Undo sets the recorded value; the file is restored by the journal. |
| Operating systems | `linux`, `macos` |
| External use | `system_program`: `sysctl`; Parameters are read and set with sysctl. |

## Examples

Enable forwarding of packets.

```nurt example
sysctl.set "net.ipv4.ip_forward" 1 privilege: elevated
```

Set a value and keep it after a restart.

```nurt example
sysctl.set "vm.swappiness" 10 persistent: true privilege: elevated
```

Run the change with elevated rights; adding the call parameter `preview: true` shows the effect first.

```nurt example
sysctl.set "vm.swappiness" 10 privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The kernel has no such parameter. | Check the name with `sysctl -a`. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | `persistent` outside Linux. | Omit `persistent`. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The account lacks the rights of the administrator. | Add `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The system program of the command is not installed. | Install the program named in the message. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The system program ended with an error. | Read the end of the error output in the message. |

## Related

`modules.load`, `modules.unload`.

title: test.failed
text:
# test.failed

## Synopsis

```text
test.failed [<run_id>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

Selects the tests with the status `failed` or `error` of an earlier run and
runs only those. The identifiers of the tests are translated to the selectors
of the framework: files and a name pattern for bun, vitest and jest, node
identifiers for pytest, packages and `-run` for go and `--exact` names for
