cargo. The `npm` scripts and custom commands cannot select single tests; the
stored command runs again and the command logs a note.

Without `run_id` the run is the newest run that has failed tests and that no
later run repeated. With `path` only runs of that project directory are
considered, and the repeat runs in it. The new run records the repeated run in
`retry_of`.

When the run has no failed tests, the command returns its `test_run` header
and no results, and starts nothing.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | `text` | the latest run | Earlier test run. |
| `path` | `path` | none | Project directory of the earlier run. |
| `timeout` | `duration` | `30m` | Time limit of the test run. |
| `wait` | `duration` | `3s` | Time to wait before the run continues in the background as a job. |
| `failures` | `int` | `10` | Maximum number of failed tests reported in detail. |
| `message_lines` | `int` | `5` | Maximum number of message lines per failed test. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `test_run`, `test_result`, `job` |

The command takes no input. The output is the same as the output of
`test.run`: a `test_run` header followed by `test_result` records, or a `job`
record.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `run` |
| Effect | `process` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `user_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | Files changed by the test programs are reversible when their previous content was preserved; effects outside the file system are irreversible. |

## Examples

Run again the failures of the latest run.

```nurt example
test.failed
```

Run again the failures of a named run and show the failed results.

```nurt example
test.failed run-3 |> filter status == "failed"
```

Run again the failures of the run of another project directory.

```nurt example
test.failed path: "/work/service"
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_UNKNOWN_RUN` | The run does not exist, or no run has failures. | List the runs with `test.list`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The test program is not installed. | Install it. |
| `E_OUTPUT_PARSE` | The report or the output cannot be read. | Run again with `test.run command:`. |

## Related

`test.run`, `test.show`, `test.list`.

title: test.list
text:
# test.list

## Synopsis

```text
test.list [name: value]...
```

## Description

Returns the `test_run` headers of the stored runs, newest first. The history
keeps the number of runs set by `verify.history_max` (default `50`); older runs
are removed when a new run is stored. A stored run that cannot be read is left
out of the list and reported in the notes of the result as
`source_unavailable`, with the path of its file and the advice to remove the
file; the other runs are listed. `test.show` of that run still fails with the
error of the unreadable entry.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | `int` | `20` | Maximum number of runs, newest first. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `test_run` |

The command takes no input. It produces `test_run` records.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

List the five newest runs.

```nurt example
test.list limit: 5
```

List the runs that failed.

```nurt example
test.list |> filter status == "failed"
```

Show the identifier and the fingerprint of the latest run.

```nurt example
test.list limit: 1 |> select id fingerprint
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `limit` is negative or too large. | Give a count between 0 and 4294967295. |

## Related

`test.run`, `test.show`, `test.failed`.

title: test.run
text:
# test.run

## Synopsis

```text
test.run [<path>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

Runs the test framework of the project in `path` and returns one `test_run`
header and one `test_result` record per test. The framework is started as a
program without a shell. Its machine-readable report is written to the state
directory, not to the project.

With `framework: auto` the framework is detected from the files of the
project in this order: `bun` (`bunfig.toml`, `bun.lock`, a `test` script that
runs `bun test`), `vitest`, `jest`, `npm` (a `test` script other than the
placeholder written by `npm init`), `pytest`, `go` (`go.mod`) and `cargo`
(`Cargo.toml`). A directory that holds `*.test.*` or `*.spec.*` files and no
other marker is run with `bun`. `command` replaces the command of the
framework; without `framework` its output is read as TAP and as lines marked
`(pass)`, `(fail)`, `(skip)` or `(todo)`.

`targets` and `filter` are translated to the options of the framework and
`bail` to its fail-fast option. A target that starts with `-` is rejected;
options of the framework are given through `command`. The `npm` framework is
recorded as `custom` in the `test_run`.

The identifier of a test is stable between runs: the file, the suite and the
name joined by `::`. A repeated identifier receives the suffix `#2`, `#3`.
The run is compared with the earlier runs of the same directory. The header
then carries `baseline` (the run with the most shared tests), `regressions`
(tests that passed and now fail) and `fixed` (tests that failed and now
pass), each only when it applies. With `slowest: n` the header carries
`slowest`, the `n` slowest tests as `id: <time>ms`.

`failures` limits how many failed tests keep their `message`, `stack`,
`stdout` and `stderr` in the output; `message_lines` cuts each of them to
that number of lines. The stored run keeps the complete texts.

With `coverage: true` the framework measures coverage: `--coverage` for bun,
vitest and jest, `pytest-cov` for pytest, `-coverprofile` for go and
`cargo llvm-cov` instead of `cargo test` for cargo. `coverage_file` names a
report that the tests produce themselves; it is read after the run and its
format (LCOV, Cobertura, Istanbul, Go, LLVM) is detected from its content.
The result is the `coverage` field of the `test_run`.

The `fingerprint` of the header is `sha256:` and the digest of the sorted list
of file paths and content hashes. In a git repository the files are the
tracked files and the changed untracked files; otherwise they are the files
found under the ignore rules of the directory. Names in `run.preimage_exclude`
are skipped. At most 20 000 files are covered.

When the run is still going after `wait`, it continues as a job and the
command returns the `job` record. The test run is stored when the job ends.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | none | Project directory. |
| `framework` | `enum(auto\|bun\|vitest\|jest\|npm\|pytest\|go\|cargo)` | `auto` | Test framework; auto detects it from the project. |
| `targets` | `list<text>` | none | Test files, packages or identifiers to run. |
| `filter` | `text` | none | Only tests whose name matches this filter. |
| `bail` | `bool` | `false` | Stop at the first failing test. |
| `command` | `list<text>` | none | Test command run instead of the detected framework command. |
| `coverage` | `bool` | `false` | Collect code coverage and return it with the run. |
| `coverage_file` | `path` | none | Coverage report in LCOV, Cobertura or Go format produced by the tests; detected from the framework when omitted. |
| `timeout` | `duration` | `30m` | Time limit of the test run. |
| `wait` | `duration` | `3s` | Time to wait before the run continues in the background as a job. |
| `slowest` | `int` | `0` | Number of slowest tests reported. |
| `failures` | `int` | `10` | Maximum number of failed tests reported in detail. |
| `message_lines` | `int` | `5` | Maximum number of message lines per failed test. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `test_run`, `test_result`, `job` |

The command takes no input. It produces a `test_run` header followed by
`test_result` records, or a `job` record when the run continues in the
background.

The status of the run is `passed`, `failed`, `error` (the framework did not
start or the code did not compile), `timed_out` or `no_tests`. When the run
ends with an error and no test results, a result with the identifier `(run)`
carries the end of the output. A test file that cannot be loaded and a Go
package that does not build are reported as results with the status `error`.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `run` |
| Effect | `process` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `user_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | Files changed by the test programs are reversible when their previous content was preserved; effects outside the file system are irreversible. |

## Examples

Run the tests of the current project and show only the failed ones.

```nurt example
test.run |> filter status == "failed"
```

Run one file with the first failure stopping the run.

```nurt example
test.run framework: bun targets: ["src/sum.test.ts"] bail: true
```

Run a Go project with coverage and show the coverage of the run.

```nurt example
test.run framework: go coverage: true |> select coverage
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_TEST_NO_FRAMEWORK` | No framework was recognised. | Name the framework or give `command:`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The test program is not installed. | Install it or give `command:`. |
| `E_OUTPUT_PARSE` | The report or the output cannot be read. | Run with `command:` to see the output; the error carries the execution record. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | A target looks like an option. | Pass options through `command:`. |

## Related

`test.failed`, `test.show`, `test.list`, `run`, `jobs`.

title: test.show
text:
# test.show

## Synopsis

```text
test.show [<run_id>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

Reads a stored run and returns its `test_run` header and the `test_result`
records that match the filters. Without `status` every result is returned.
`failed` selects the results with the status `failed` and `error`; `skipped`
selects the results with the status `skipped` and `todo`.

`test` keeps the results whose identifier or name contains the text, ignoring
case. `failures` limits how many failed results keep their message, stack and
output, and `message_lines` cuts each of those texts to that number of lines.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | `text` | the latest run | Earlier test run. |
| `test` | `text` | none | Only the test with this identifier or name. |
| `status` | `enum(failed\|passed\|skipped)` | none | Only tests with this status. |
| `failures` | `int` | `10` | Maximum number of failed tests reported in detail. |
| `message_lines` | `int` | `5` | Maximum number of message lines per failed test. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `test_result` |

The command takes no input. It produces the `test_run` header of the run and
its `test_result` records in the order of the run.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `source` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Show the failures of the latest run with three message lines each.

```nurt example
test.show status: failed message_lines: 3
```

Show the results of one run whose identifier contains a name.

```nurt example
test.show run-2 test: "parse"
```

Show only the passed tests of the latest run.

```nurt example
test.show status: passed
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_UNKNOWN_RUN` | The run does not exist; the error lists known runs. | Use one of the listed runs or run `test.run`. |

## Related

`test.run`, `test.failed`, `test.list`.

title: undo
text:
# undo

## Synopsis

```text
undo [<id>] [name: value]...
```

## Description

`undo` restores the state that preceded one or more operations recorded in
the journal. It repairs a mistake; it does not replace checking the result of
an operation before relying on it.

Exactly one form selects the operations:

| Form | Operations undone | Scope recorded |
|---|---|---|
| no selection | the latest available operation of the session (of the account without a session) that is not itself an undo | `op` |
| `id` | operation `id`, all its items; a bulk operation is undone as a whole | `op` |
| `to` | every available operation newer than `to` in the session, latest first, as one transaction | `to` |
| `file` | every available operation that changed the file, newer than `since` or all of them, for that file only; the file returns to its state before the oldest of them | `file` |
| `id` with `paths` | the listed items of operation `id` only | `paths` |

An undo of an undo is applied again with `redo`; the default selection never
picks an undo. Operations of other sessions inside a `to` range are skipped
and listed in `skipped` unless `all_sessions` is true.

Reports name the operation `op`, while the parameter that selects it is `id`.
A call written `undo op: N` or `undo operation: N` is corrected to `undo id: N`
(rule L06) and runs; the correction is listed in the result.

Before anything is written, every item of the whole selection is compared
with the state the journal recorded after the operation: content hash, kind,
size and permission bits, absence of deleted entries, the content preserved
for overwritten and deleted files, and later operations that changed the same
items. A difference changes nothing and consumes no operation number;
`on_conflict` decides what happens instead:

| `on_conflict` | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `report` | fails with `E_JOURNAL_CONFLICT` listing every difference; fails with `E_JOURNAL_PARTIAL` when an operation has items released for space |
| `force` | undoes anyway; the current content of every item is kept in the new journal entry; differences are listed in `forced`; released items are skipped as with `partial` |
| `include_later` | also undoes, latest first, the later operations that changed the same items, and the later operations of those, until no later change remains; fails with `E_JOURNAL_EXPIRED` when one of them expired; with `to` it behaves as `report`, since a range is already undone latest first |
| `partial` | undoes the remaining items of operations with items released for space and lists the released items in `unavailable`; differences are reported as with `report` |
| `abort` | fails with `E_JOURNAL_CONFLICT` reporting only the number of differences, or with `E_JOURNAL_PARTIAL` |

An operation is in the state `partial` when some of its items were released
to free disk space or were undone individually with `file` or `paths`; the
items still kept remain undoable. Items undone individually are restored only
once; an operation whose items are all undone becomes `undone`.

Inside a `to` or `file` range, an undo whose operation lies in the same range
cancels it, and neither is undone; a `redo` of such an undo is undone.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `int` | the latest operation | Operation to undo. |
| `to` | `int` | none | Undo every operation newer than this one, latest first, in one transaction. |
| `file` | `path` | none | Undo every change of this file since the given point. |
| `since` | `int \| instant` | none | Operation or time from which changes of file are undone. |
| `paths` | `list<path>` | none | Undo only the changes of these paths within the operation. |
| `all_sessions` | `bool` | `false` | Include operations of other sessions; only with to. |
| `on_conflict` | `enum(report\|force\|include_later\|partial\|abort)` | `report` | Behaviour when later changes touch the same files. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

A preview of `undo id` and `undo id paths:` lists the items the undo would
restore; the other forms are previewed without items.

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `journal` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | An undo can be reversed with redo. |

## Examples

Undo the latest operation of the session:

```nurt example
undo
```

Undo operation 18 together with the later operations that changed the same
files:

```nurt example
undo 18 on_conflict: include_later
```

Return a file to its state before operation 12:

```nurt example
undo file: "/home/user/app/config.toml" since: 12
```

Undo two items of a bulk removal:

```nurt example
undo 21 paths: ["/home/user/app/a.go", "/home/user/app/b.go"]
```

Undo everything done after operation 30 in this session:

```nurt example
undo to: 30
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_JOURNAL_NOOP` | the operation does not exist, is already undone or still in progress, a path is not an item of the operation, or nothing is left to undo | list operations with `history` |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | the arguments mix forms: more than one of `id`, `to` and `file`, `since` without `file`, `paths` without `id`, an empty `paths`, or `all_sessions` without `to` | use one form of the synopsis |
| `E_JOURNAL_EXPIRED` | an operation of the selection expired; nothing changed; `expired` lists them | select later operations |
| `E_JOURNAL_CONFLICT` | items changed after the operation; nothing changed; `conflicts` lists every difference | use one of the programs in `fix`, or `on_conflict: force` or `include_later` |
| `E_JOURNAL_PARTIAL` | items of the operation were released for space; nothing changed | `on_conflict: partial` |
| `E_JOURNAL_CORRUPT` | an operation failed its integrity check; its data is kept for salvage | `nurt journal salvage` |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | an item cannot be restored by the journal (a rename across volumes or over an existing entry); nothing changed | restore the item from the data listed by `history N details: true`, or undo the other items with `paths` |
| `E_STALE` | an item changed while the undo ran; the undo was rolled back | repeat the undo |
| `E_ROLLBACK_FAILED` | an undo that failed could not restore every item; `failed` lists them | restore the listed paths |

## Related

`redo`, `history`, `journal.pin`, `journal.status`, `help skill: "journal"`.

title: unmount
text:
# unmount

## Synopsis

```text
unmount <target> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`unmount` unmounts a mount point with `umount` on Linux and macOS and `mountvol /D` on Windows. The device, the type and the options are read first. With `persistent: true` on Linux the line of the mount point is removed from `/etc/fstab` through the journal.

Rights: the command accepts `privilege`; write `privilege: elevated` when the account that runs Nurt is not the administrator. A program that fails for lack of rights ends the command with `E_PERMISSION`, and `privilege: auto` repeats it once elevated. An elevated entry is undone by the same elevated process.

`undo` runs `mount` with the recorded device, type and options.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | `text` | required | Mount point. |
| `persistent` | `bool` | `false` | Also remove the mount from /etc/fstab (Linux); the file is journaled. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `external` |
| Reversibility | `reversible_if_preserved` |
| Implementation | `system_program` |
| Reversibility conditions | Undo mounts the recorded device with its type and options. |
| External use | `system_program`: `umount`, `mountvol`; Unmounts use umount on Linux and macOS and mountvol on Windows. |

## Examples

Unmount a directory.

```nurt example
unmount "/srv/data" privilege: elevated
```

Unmount and remove the line of `/etc/fstab`.

```nurt example
unmount "/srv/data" persistent: true privilege: elevated
```

Run the unmount with elevated rights; adding the call parameter `preview: true` shows the effect first.

```nurt example
unmount "/srv/data" privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | Nothing is mounted at the mount point. | Check the mount point with `disks`. |
| `E_IN_USE` | A process uses the mount. | Stop the processes listed by `open_files`. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The account lacks the rights of the administrator. | Add `privilege: elevated`. |
| `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` | The system program of the command is not installed. | Install the program named in the message. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The system program ended with an error. | Read the end of the error output in the message. |

## Related

`mount`, `disks`.

title: verify
text:
# verify

## Synopsis

```text
effect |> verify <check>
```

## Description

`verify` runs the pipeline `check` after the effect of the program, with the
`effect` records as its input, and reads its whole output. When the check
succeeds, the `effect` records pass on unchanged. When any stage of the check
fails, for example an `assert` inside it, the change is rolled back from the
journal and the program ends with `E_ROLLED_BACK`, which carries the error of
the check; when the rollback cannot restore every file, the error is
`E_ROLLBACK_FAILED` with the files concerned.

The check usually runs a build or a test (`run … |> assert exit_code: 0`) or
reads the changed files again. It runs in stage `6`, after the stages that
read the records of the effect.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `check` | `pipeline` | required | Pipeline that checks the result of the change. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `effect` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `check` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | A failed check rolls back the preceding change from the journal. |

## Examples

Replace a call and keep the change only when the project still builds:

```nurt example
search /oldName\(/ "/home/user/project/src" |> replace "newName(" |> verify (run ["go", "build", "./..."] cwd: "/home/user/project" |> assert exit_code: 0)
```

Roll a write back when the file no longer contains a required key:

```nurt example
write "/home/user/project/config.toml" text: "name = 1" mode: overwrite |> verify (lines "/home/user/project/config.toml" |> assert contains: "version")
```

Keep a version change only when the tests pass:

```nurt example
write "/home/user/project/VERSION" text: "1.4.0" mode: overwrite |> verify (run ["make", "test"] cwd: "/home/user/project" |> assert exit_code: 0)
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_ROLLED_BACK` | the check failed and the change was rolled back; the cause holds the error of the check | fix the change or the check and run the program again |
| `E_ROLLBACK_FAILED` | the rollback could not restore every file; the files are listed | restore the listed files with `undo` or by hand |
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | the check pipeline is missing | write the pipeline in parentheses after `verify` |
| `E_TYPE` | `check` is not a pipeline | enclose the check pipeline in parentheses |

## Related

`assert`, `undo`, `history`.

title: windows.cim
text:
# windows.cim

## Synopsis

```text
windows.cim <class> [name: value]...
```

## Description

`windows.cim` reads instances of a CIM class from the local Windows
Management Instrumentation service and returns one `cim_object` record per
instance. The command builds the WQL statement
`SELECT <properties> FROM <class> [WHERE <where>]` from its parameters; all
properties are read when `properties` is omitted or empty.

`class` and every element of `properties` must be CIM names
(`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`), so they cannot change the statement. `where` is a
WQL condition on the properties of the class. It must be one line with
balanced `'` and `"` string literals and must not contain the association
query forms `ASSOCIATORS OF` or `REFERENCES OF`. `namespace` is written with
`/` separators, for example `root/Microsoft/Windows/Storage`.

Property values are converted to language values by their CIM type:

| CIM type | Value |
|---|---|
| `string`, `char16`, `reference` | `text` |
| `sint8` to `uint64` | `int`; values of `uint64` above the range of `int` keep all digits |
| `real32`, `real64` | `number` |
| `boolean` | `bool` |
| `datetime`, point in time | `instant` in UTC; the offset of the value is applied |
| `datetime`, interval | `duration` |
| arrays | `list` |
| embedded objects | `map` with the field `__class`, up to four levels deep |

Properties without a value are left out of `properties`. A `datetime` value
with unknown fields (`*`) is returned as `text`.

`path` holds the object path reported by WMI. When `properties` leaves out
the key properties of the class, WMI does not report the object path and
`path` is empty.

The rest of the pipeline may limit the number of records, for example with
`first`; the query then stops reading after that number of instances.


## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `class` | `text` | required | CIM class name, for example Win32_Process. |
| `where` | `text` | none | WQL condition on instance properties. |
| `namespace` | `text` | `"root/cimv2"` | CIM namespace. |
| `properties` | `list<text>` | none | Properties to return; all when omitted. |
| `invoke` | `text` | none | Method to call on every selected instance, or on the class when where is omitted (static methods such as Win32_Process.Create). |
| `arguments` | `map<any>` | none | Input parameters of the method by name: text, int or bool values. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none` | `cim_object`, `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `read` |
| Reversibility | `read` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |
| Reversibility conditions | A query only reads. A call with invoke is irreversible unless the method has a documented opposite (StartService and StopService, Enable and Disable, Pause and Resume), which undo calls on the same instances. |
| Operating systems | `windows` |

| Action | Effect | Reversibility | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `invoke` | `external` | `irreversible` | Applies when invoke is given. |

## Examples

Read the name and version of the operating system.

```nurt example
windows.cim "Win32_OperatingSystem" properties: ["Caption", "Version"]
```

List the running services.

```nurt example
windows.cim "Win32_Service" where: "State = 'Running'" properties: ["Name", "ProcessId"]
```

List the disks known to the storage management provider.

```nurt example
windows.cim "MSFT_Disk" namespace: "root/Microsoft/Windows/Storage"
```

Find processes by name and keep the command lines.

```nurt example
windows.cim "Win32_Process" where: "Name = 'svchost.exe'" properties: ["ProcessId", "CommandLine"] |> first 5
```

Stop a service; `undo` starts it again.

```nurt example
windows.cim "Win32_Service" where: "Name = 'Spooler'" invoke: "StopService" privilege: elevated
```

Start a process through the static method of the class.

```nurt example
windows.cim "Win32_Process" invoke: "Create" arguments: {"CommandLine": "notepad.exe"} privilege: elevated
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_OS_ONLY` | The command runs only on Windows. | Use `host`, `processes` or `services` on other systems. |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | A class, property or namespace is not a CIM name, the condition is malformed, or WMI rejected the query. | Correct the name or the condition. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | The class or the namespace does not exist. | Check the class name and the namespace. |
| `E_PRIVILEGE` | Reading the namespace requires the `administrator` privilege. | Run the console as an administrator. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The method returned a `ReturnValue` other than 0; `return_value` holds it. | Read the documentation of the method for the code. |
| `E_LIMIT` | The query returns more instances than a stage may hold. | Narrow the query with `where`. |
| `E_IO` | WMI or COM failed; `os_error` holds the `HRESULT`. | Check that the WMI service is running. |

## Related

`services`, `host`, `processes`, `disks`.

## Notes

With `invoke` the command calls the method of the class instead of reading.
`where` selects the instances that receive the call; without `where` the
method of the class is called, as for the static method `Create` of
`Win32_Process`. `arguments` holds the input parameters of the method by name;
a value is text, an integer or a boolean. `invoke` and the names in
`arguments` must be CIM names. The call is an effect of the program: a preview
reads the selected instances and shows the call without making it, and a
method that returns a `ReturnValue` other than 0 ends the call with
`E_STAGE_FAILED`; the effect record holds `return_value`.

A call is a change of the target `cim:<class>.<method>`. The call is
irreversible unless the class documents an opposite method, which `undo` calls
on the same instances; a call without `where` has no instances to repeat the
opposite on, so it stays irreversible.

| Class | Method | Opposite |
|---|---|---|
| `Win32_Service` | `StartService`, `StopService` | each other |
| `Win32_NetworkAdapter`, `Win32_PnPEntity` | `Enable`, `Disable` | each other |
| `Win32_Printer` | `Pause`, `Resume` | each other |

title: write
text:
# write

## Synopsis

```text
write [<path>] [<text>] mode: <enum(create|overwrite|append|prepend)> (path: <path> | files: <list<map<any>>>) [name: value]...
```

## Description

`write` writes one file, or a batch of files given in `files` in one
transaction: all files are written or none. The content is `text`, the
content named by `from`, the bytes of `data`, or the input records. `size`
truncates or extends the file without content; `data` with `offset` writes
bytes in place.

`mode` has no default. `create` fails with `E_EXISTS` when the file exists;
`overwrite` replaces the content; `append` adds the text at the end;
`prepend` adds it at the start. Every mode creates a missing file.

A new file is UTF-8 without a byte order mark, with the line endings of the
configuration key `text.new_file_line_ending` (`lf` by default). An existing
file keeps its encoding, its byte order mark and its line endings, unless
`encoding`, `bom` or `line_ending` give other values; text is appended in the
encoding and line endings of the file. A character the encoding cannot
represent fails with `E_ENCODING` at its line and column before anything is
written, with a `convert` call as the fix.

A link in the last component of `path` is followed: the file it names is
written and the link stays a link. A directory is never written. Missing
parent directories are created unless `parents` is `false`; each one is a
target of its own. Content identical to the file is not written and is
reported as `unchanged`.

Input records are written in `format`; `auto` follows the extension of the
file (`.json`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.toml`, `.csv`, `.tsv`), otherwise `text`.
`json` writes an indented array of objects; `csv` and `tsv` write a header
row with every field name followed by one row per record; `text` writes one
line per record, the `text` field when the record has one, otherwise the
record as compact JSON. `yaml` and `toml` need the documents group.

A `registry:/` path writes a registry value on Windows, of the type
`value_type` (`string` by default); `mode` is `create` or `overwrite`.

Text written to a file of a known format is checked after the write: a
document format of the documents group, otherwise a language of the code
group. Only syntax errors that the previous content did not have count.
With `validate: reject` such an error rolls the whole write back with
`E_ROLLED_BACK`; with `warn` it is reported as a warning and the write is
kept; `off` skips the check. Bytes, sizes and registry values are not
checked, and without the documents and code groups nothing is checked.

**Privilege.** Files that the account may not change (`/etc/hosts`, files of other accounts) are written with `privilege: elevated`. The entry is in the journal of the account with the owner, group, mode and access control of the previous content, the account has access to the copy, and `undo` restores them through the same backend.

```nurt
write "/etc/hosts" "127.0.0.1 localhost\n" mode: append privilege: elevated
```

With `privilege: auto` the stage runs with the account and is repeated once with `elevated` when a target fails with `E_PERMISSION` or `E_PRIVILEGE`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `enum(create\|overwrite\|append\|prepend)` | required | Write mode; there is no default. |
| `path` | `path` | one of `target` | File to write. |
| `text` | `text` | none | Text to write. |
| `from` | `pipeline \| stream<any> \| path` | none | Pipeline, named result or file whose content is written. |
| `encoding` | `text` | `"auto"` | Text encoding; auto keeps the encoding of an existing file. |
| `line_ending` | `enum(lf\|crlf\|cr\|keep)` | `keep` | Line endings of the written text. |
| `bom` | `bool` | as in the existing file | Write a byte order mark. |
| `parents` | `bool` | `true` | Create missing parent directories. |
| `ensure_newline` | `bool` | `false` | End the file with a line ending. |
| `format` | `enum(auto\|json\|yaml\|toml\|csv\|tsv\|text)` | `auto` | Serialization of written records; auto follows the file extension. |
| `files` | `list<map<any>>` | one of `target` | Batch of files written in one transaction, each with path, text and optional mode. |
| `value_type` | `enum(string\|dword\|qword\|multi_string\|expand_string\|binary)` | none | Type of a registry value; only for registry: paths. |
| `file_mode` | `text` | none | Permissions of a new file, such as "0644". |
| `size` | `size` | none | Truncate or extend the file to this size. |
| `data` | `bytes` | none | Bytes to write. |
| `offset` | `int` | none | Byte offset at which data is written. |
| `validate` | `enum(off\|warn\|reject)` | `reject` | Roll back a write that adds a new syntax error to a known format. |
| `if_match` | `text \| map<text>` | none | Expected etag of the file, or a map from path to etag for files. |

## Input and output

| Form | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| default | `none`, `any` | `effect` |

## Effect

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | `change` |
| Effect | `local` |
| Reversibility | `reversible` |
| Implementation | `builtin` |

## Examples

Create a file with three lines:

```nurt example
write "/home/user/app/Dockerfile" "FROM alpine:3.20\nRUN apk add --no-cache curl\nCMD [\"sh\"]\n" mode: create
```

```text expected
+ /home/user/app/Dockerfile
```

Append a line to an existing file of 120 bytes:

```nurt example
write "/home/user/app/.gitignore" "dist/\n" mode: append
```

```text expected
120b → 126b
```

Replace a file that uses CRLF line endings; the new text keeps them:

```nurt example
write "/home/user/app/config.ini" "[main]\nport = 8080\n" mode: overwrite
```

Write two files in one transaction; the missing directory `docs` is created:

```nurt example
write files: [{path: "/home/user/app/a.txt", text: "a\n"}, {path: "/home/user/app/docs/b.txt", text: "b\n"}] mode: create
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|
| `E_MISSING_PARAM` | `mode`, or both `path` and `files`, are missing | give `mode: create`, `overwrite`, `append` or `prepend` |
| `E_EXISTS` | `mode: create` and the file exists | use `mode: overwrite` or `mode: append` |
| `E_PARAM_CONFLICT` | two sources of content, `path` with `files`, or `offset` without `data` | give one source of content |
| `E_ENCODING` | a character the encoding of the file cannot represent | `convert` the file to UTF-8 first, or give `encoding` |
| `E_STALE` | the file changed after its etag was read, or after the plan | read the file again and use the new etag |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | a parent directory is missing and `parents` is `false`, or a link names a missing entry | set `parents: true` or create the target |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | the path is a directory, `file_mode` is not octal, or `value_type` is given for a file | correct the value |
| `E_ROLLED_BACK` | the written text adds a syntax error and `validate` is `reject` | correct the text or pass `validate: warn` |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | `format: yaml` or `toml` without the documents group | load the group or use `format: json` |
| `E_OS_ONLY` | a `registry:/` path outside Windows | write files instead |
| `E_LIMIT` | a file read for the change is larger than the text limit | write with `data` and `offset`, or `size` |

## Related

`create`, `replace`, `insert`, `edit`, `convert`, `read`, `undo`.

title: Group administration
text:
# Group administration

## Scope

The group lists and controls services of the operating system and queries
Windows management objects. Services have one model on all systems: the
service manager of the system (systemd, the Windows service control manager
or launchd) is hidden behind the `service` record, and the commands that
change a service take `service` records as input.

The Windows registry is not a command of this group. It is a provider of
paths: `registry:/HKCU/Software/Example` addresses a key and
`registry:/HKCU/Software/Example/Mode` a value, and the file commands of the
core group (`list`, `find`, `read`, `write`, `remove`, `copy`, `move`) work on
them. The previous value is preserved in the operation journal, so a registry
change made with `write` can be undone.

| Task | Command | Group |
|---|---|---|
| Stop a service | `stop` | core |
| Suspend or resume a process | `suspend`, `resume` | system |
| Read and change registry values | `read`, `write`, `remove` | core |
| Undo a registry change | `undo` | core |

## Commands

| Command | Category | Input and output | Reversibility | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `services` | source | none to `service` | read | [services](../commands/services.md) |
| `start` | run | `service` to `effect` | irreversible | [start](../commands/start.md) |
| `restart` | run | `service` to `effect` | irreversible | [restart](../commands/restart.md) |
| `enable` | change | `service` to `effect` | irreversible | [enable](../commands/enable.md) |
| `disable` | change | `service` to `effect` | irreversible | [disable](../commands/disable.md) |
| `windows.cim` | change | none to `cim_object`, `effect` | read | [windows.cim](../commands/windows.cim.md) |
| `firewall.rules` | source | none to `map` | read | [firewall.rules](../commands/firewall.rules.md) |
| `firewall.allow` | change | none to `effect` | reversible | [firewall.allow](../commands/firewall.allow.md) |
| `firewall.deny` | change | none to `effect` | reversible | [firewall.deny](../commands/firewall.deny.md) |
| `firewall.remove` | change | none to `effect` | reversible | [firewall.remove](../commands/firewall.remove.md) |
| `network.route_add` | change | none to `effect` | reversible | [network.route_add](../commands/network.route_add.md) |
| `network.route_remove` | change | none to `effect` | reversible | [network.route_remove](../commands/network.route_remove.md) |
| `network.dns_set` | change | none to `effect` | reversible | [network.dns_set](../commands/network.dns_set.md) |
| `clock.timezone_set` | change | none to `effect` | reversible | [clock.timezone_set](../commands/clock.timezone_set.md) |
| `clock.set` | change | none to `effect` | irreversible | [clock.set](../commands/clock.set.md) |
| `clock.ntp` | change | none to `effect` | reversible | [clock.ntp](../commands/clock.ntp.md) |
| `accounts.create` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [accounts.create](../commands/accounts.create.md) |
| `accounts.modify` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [accounts.modify](../commands/accounts.modify.md) |
| `accounts.remove` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [accounts.remove](../commands/accounts.remove.md) |
| `accounts.password` | change | none to `effect` | irreversible | [accounts.password](../commands/accounts.password.md) |
| `groups.create` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [groups.create](../commands/groups.create.md) |
| `groups.remove` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [groups.remove](../commands/groups.remove.md) |
| `groups.add_member` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [groups.add_member](../commands/groups.add_member.md) |
| `groups.remove_member` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [groups.remove_member](../commands/groups.remove_member.md) |
| `mount` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [mount](../commands/mount.md) |
| `unmount` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [unmount](../commands/unmount.md) |
| `sysctl.set` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [sysctl.set](../commands/sysctl.set.md) |
| `modules.load` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [modules.load](../commands/modules.load.md) |
| `modules.unload` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [modules.unload](../commands/modules.unload.md) |
| `power.restart` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [power.restart](../commands/power.restart.md) |
| `power.shutdown` | change | none to `effect` | reversible_if_preserved | [power.shutdown](../commands/power.shutdown.md) |
| `power.cancel` | change | none to `effect` | irreversible | [power.cancel](../commands/power.cancel.md) |
| `disks.partition` | change | none to `effect` | irreversible | [disks.partition](../commands/disks.partition.md) |
| `disks.format` | change | none to `effect` | irreversible | [disks.format](../commands/disks.format.md) |

## Records

| Record | Required fields |
|---|---|
| `service` | `name`, `state`, `start_type`, `manager` |
| `cim_object` | `class`, `path`, `properties` |
| `effect` | `status`, `kind` |

The values of `service.state` are `running`, `stopped`, `starting`,
`stopping`, `failed`, `paused` and `unknown`. The values of
`service.start_type` are `automatic`, `manual`, `disabled`, `on_demand`,
`static` and `unknown`. The field `manager` is `systemd`, `windows` or
`launchd`. The field `state_raw` keeps the state as the service manager
reports it.

The `effect` record of `start`, `restart`, `enable` and `disable` names the
service in `target` (for example `service:nginx`), the action in `action`, and
the state of the service in `before` and `after`.

## Service model

`services` selects services by `name` (text or regular expression), by
`state` and by `scope`. `scope` selects the instance of the service manager:

| Scope | Service manager instance |
|---|---|
| `system` | services of the computer; default |
| `user` | services of the account that runs the program |

`scope` of `services` is not the `scope` of `environment`; the values and the
meaning differ, see the group `system`.

`start` and `restart` take the services of the input and wait up to `wait`
(default `10s`) for the requested state. `enable` makes the services start at
boot, or at login for the scope `user`. `disable` removes that start. A
program has one stage that changes the world, so `start`, `restart`, `enable`
and `disable` are the last stage that changes anything: `services name: "nginx"
|> restart` selects in the read step and restarts in the apply step.

Changing the state of a service is an effect outside the file system. The
operation journal records it as irreversible, `undo` does not reverse it, and
the effect report lists it among the irreversible effects. A preview shows the
services that would be changed and changes nothing.

## Firewall, routes, DNS and the clock

`firewall.rules`, `firewall.allow`, `firewall.deny` and `firewall.remove` read
and change the rules of the firewall of the system: nftables, firewalld or ufw
on Linux, pf on macOS and the Windows Defender Firewall. `network.route_add`,
`network.route_remove` and `network.dns_set` change the routing table and the
name servers. `clock.timezone_set`, `clock.ntp` and `clock.set` change the time
zone, network time and the clock.

Every one of these commands changes the system and accepts `privilege`; they
need the administrator, so a call is written with `privilege: elevated`. The
stage never starts `sudo` itself: the executor runs the stage with the
elevated process, and a program that reports missing rights ends the call with
`E_PRIVILEGE`.

The report of a change holds a change of the action `state` for one target
with the value before and after: `firewall:<rule>` (`absent` or `present`),
`route:<destination>`, `dns:<interface>`, `clock:timezone` and `clock:ntp`.
From these values the engine derives the program that `undo` runs, with the
rights of the original call:

| Command | `undo` runs |
|---|---|
| `firewall.allow`, `firewall.deny` | `firewall.remove` of the rule |
| `firewall.remove` | `firewall.allow` or `firewall.deny` of every removed rule |
| `network.route_add` | `network.route_remove` of the route |
| `network.route_remove` | `network.route_add` of every removed route |
| `network.dns_set` | `network.dns_set` with the previous servers and domains; a change of `/etc/resolv.conf` is restored by the journal |
| `clock.timezone_set` | `clock.timezone_set` with the previous zone |
| `clock.ntp` | `clock.ntp` with the previous state |
| `clock.set` | irreversible |

A change that the system already holds (a rule that exists, the same zone) is
reported as `unchanged`, opens no journal entry and runs no program. A preview
reads the system and lists the effects without changing anything.

## Platform differences

| Aspect | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Service manager | systemd, through its D-Bus interface | launchd | service control manager |
| `manager` value | `systemd` | `launchd` | `windows` |
| Reading services | D-Bus | property list files and `launchctl` | service control manager API |
| Changing services | D-Bus | `launchctl` | service control manager API |
| `scope: user` | systemd user instance of the account | launchd user jobs of the account | services of the account, when the system provides them |
| `windows.cim` | `E_OS_ONLY` | `E_OS_ONLY` | WMI over COM |

Changing a service of the scope `system` requires a privilege. Without it the
command fails with `E_PRIVILEGE`, and `fix` names the privilege. An error of
the service manager is reported as `E_SERVICE`.

`windows.cim` queries instances of a CIM class in `namespace` (default
`root/cimv2`) with an optional WQL `where` condition and a list of
`properties`. On Linux and macOS it fails with `E_OS_ONLY`.

## External programs

| Command | Marker | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| `services` | [X] | macOS only: the state of services is read through `launchctl` |
| `start` | [X] | macOS only: services are started through `launchctl` |
| `restart` | [X] | macOS only: services are restarted through `launchctl` |
| `enable` | [X] | macOS only: services are enabled through `launchctl` |
| `disable` | [X] | macOS only: services are disabled through `launchctl` |
| `firewall.rules` | [X] | `nft`, `firewall-cmd`, `ufw` or `pfctl` read the rules; Windows uses PowerShell |
| `firewall.allow` | [X] | the same programs change the rules |
| `firewall.deny` | [X] | the same programs change the rules |
| `firewall.remove` | [X] | the same programs change the rules |
| `network.route_add` | [X] | `ip`, `route` or PowerShell |
| `network.route_remove` | [X] | `ip`, `route` or PowerShell |
| `network.dns_set` | [X] | `resolvectl`, `networksetup` or PowerShell; `/etc/resolv.conf` is written without a program |
| `clock.timezone_set` | [X] | `timedatectl`, `systemsetup` or `tzutil` |
| `clock.set` | [X] | `date` or PowerShell |
| `clock.ntp` | [X] | `timedatectl`, `systemsetup` or PowerShell |
| `accounts.create` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `accounts.modify` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `accounts.remove` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `accounts.password` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `groups.create` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `groups.remove` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `groups.add_member` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `groups.remove_member` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `mount` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `unmount` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `sysctl.set` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `modules.load` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `modules.unload` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `power.restart` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `power.shutdown` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `power.cancel` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `disks.partition` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |
| `disks.format` | [X] | the system program of the operating system named on the page of the command |

The [X] marker names a component of the operating system that a command
starts as a program. The commands for accounts, groups, mounts, kernel
parameters, power and disks start the programs of the operating system on
every system; the page of each command names them. macOS offers no public interface for these operations, so `launchctl` is the
one component of the operating system that the commands of this group start. They start it through the process interface and report it in the check of
the program. Linux and Windows use system interfaces and start no program. When `launchctl` is missing on macOS, the
command fails with `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING`.

## Examples

Restart the service `nginx`:

```nurt example
services name: "nginx" |> restart
```

List the running services that start automatically:

```nurt example
services state: "running" |> filter start_type == "automatic" |> select name state
```

Restart a service and wait up to 30 seconds for it to run:

```nurt example
services "nginx" |> restart wait: 30s
```

Stop a service from starting at boot:

```nurt example
services name: "cups" |> disable
```

Read a registry value and then change it; the previous value stays in the
journal:

```nurt example
read "registry:/HKCU/Software/Example/Mode"
write "registry:/HKCU/Software/Example/Mode" "3" value_type: dword mode: overwrite
```

Read two properties of the operating system on Windows:

```nurt example
windows.cim "Win32_OperatingSystem" properties: ["Caption", "Version"]
```

## Related

[Group system](system.md) lists processes and ports. [Group schedule](schedule.md)
runs programs at set times. `stop` of the core group stops services.

## Accounts, groups, mounts, kernel, power and disks

The commands `accounts.create`, `accounts.modify`, `accounts.remove`,
`accounts.password`, `groups.create`, `groups.remove`, `groups.add_member`,
`groups.remove_member`, `mount`, `unmount`, `sysctl.set`, `modules.load`,
`modules.unload`, `power.restart`, `power.shutdown`, `power.cancel`,
`disks.partition` and `disks.format` change the system through its own
programs and are sources of one `effect` record per changed target. Every one
of them reads the state it changes first, reports `unchanged` when the system
already has the requested state, and records the state before and after as
JSON documents in `before` and `after` of the target (`account:<name>`,
`group:<name>`, `mount:<path>`, `sysctl:<key>`, `module:<name>`,
`power:schedule`, `disk:<device>`). `undo` derives the inverse command from
those states:

| Command | Undo |
|---|---|
| `accounts.create` | `accounts.remove` with `keep_home: true` |
| `accounts.remove` | `accounts.create` with the recorded values; the home directory returns with the journal |
| `accounts.modify` | `accounts.modify` with the recorded values |
| `accounts.password` | irreversible |
| `groups.create`, `groups.remove` | pairwise; a removed group returns with its members |
| `groups.add_member`, `groups.remove_member` | pairwise |
| `mount`, `unmount` | pairwise; `/etc/fstab` is restored by the journal |
| `sysctl.set` | `sysctl.set` with the previous value; the file of `persistent` is restored by the journal |
| `modules.load`, `modules.unload` | pairwise |
| `power.restart`, `power.shutdown` | `power.cancel` when scheduled; irreversible when immediate |
| `power.cancel`, `disks.partition`, `disks.format` | irreversible |

The commands accept `privilege` like every changing command; the executor
runs a call with `privilege: elevated` in the elevated process, and `undo`
runs the inverse through the same backend. `disks.partition` and
`disks.format` refuse a mounted partition and list in their preview the
partitions, file systems, mount points and the size of the data that is lost.

title: Group git
text:
# Group git

## Scope

The commands of the `git` group read and change Git repositories in the
console process. No `git` program, credential helper, SSH client or other
program named by the repository configuration is started. Repository hooks
and filter drivers are the only programs of the user that these commands
run, and they run under the rules of `run`.

Every change of the working tree and of the repository directory is one
operation of the journal and can be undone with `undo`. Objects added to the
object store are kept by `undo`; `git gc` removes those that become
unreachable.

## Repository

The first parameter of every command is `repo: path`. It accepts the root of
a working tree, any directory below it, a linked working tree, a `.git`
directory or file, and a bare repository. The search for the repository
stops below every directory listed in `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`.

A repository owned by another account is opened only when `safe.directory`
lists it, as in `git`; the error offers the entry to add. A repository that
uses `extensions.refStorage=reftable` or an extension that is not
implemented fails with `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED` before anything is read.
`core.fsmonitor` is not used: the files are checked directly and the report
notes `fsmonitor_ignored`.

## Paths

Paths in parameters are relative to the root of the working tree, whatever
the current directory is. An absolute path below the root is accepted; a path
outside it fails with `E_INVALID_VALUE` (problem `outside_repository`).

| Form | Selects |
|---|---|
| `src` | the file `src`, or every path below the directory `src` |
| `src/*.rs` | paths matching the glob; `*` also matches `/` |
| `.` | every path |

`exclude: list<glob>` removes paths from the selection with the syntax of
`.gitignore`: a pattern without `/` matches a name at any depth, a pattern
with `/` is anchored at the root, `**` matches any number of directories, and
an excluded directory excludes everything below it.

## Configuration

The configuration is read in the order of `git`; a later layer overrides an
earlier one.

| Layer | Source |
|---|---|
| system | `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`, or the system file of the `git` distribution (`/etc/gitconfig`; on Windows `C:/Program Files/Git/etc/gitconfig`); none when `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` is true |
| global | `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config` followed by `~/.gitconfig` |
| repository | `config` of the repository directory |
| working tree | `config.worktree`, when `extensions.worktreeConfig` is set |
| environment | `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>` |

`include` and `includeIf` are followed. Environment variables are those of
the console session. A leading `~` in `core.excludesFile`,
`core.attributesFile`, `core.hooksPath` and `commit.template` is the home
directory of the session.

## Content filters

Content is converted between the working tree and the object store as `git`
converts it: `core.autocrlf`, `core.eol`, and the attributes `text`, `eol`,
`crlf`, `binary`, `ident` and `working-tree-encoding`.

A driver named by the attribute `filter` and configured as
`filter.<name>.clean`, `filter.<name>.smudge` or `filter.<name>.process` runs
as a program of the user through `sh -c`, with `%f` replaced by the quoted
path. When no program service is available, or a driver that is not
`filter.<name>.required` fails, the content passes unfiltered and the report
notes `filter_not_applied` with the number of files. A failing required
driver fails the command with `E_EXTERNAL_FAILED`. A Git LFS pointer file
that is not converted stays a pointer file in the working tree.

## Revisions

Revisions follow the syntax of `git rev-parse`.

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `main`, `v1.0`, `origin/main` | branch, tag or remote-tracking branch |
| `3f2a9c1` | abbreviated object identifier |
| `HEAD~2`, `HEAD^2` | ancestor, parent |
| `main@{1}`, `@{upstream}`, `@{push}` | reflog entry, upstream, push destination |
| `:/fix parser` | newest commit whose message matches |
| `HEAD:src/main.rs` | object at a path of a tree |
| `v1.0^{}`, `HEAD^{tree}` | peeled object |

A revision that cannot be resolved fails with `E_GIT_REVISION`. Its problem
is `not_found`, with the references of nearest name as candidates,
`ambiguous`, with the matching objects as candidates, `invalid_syntax`, or
`not_a_commit` where a commit is required. Abbreviated identifiers in
results have the length of `core.abbrev` and are extended until they are
unique.

## Remote addresses

| Address | Transport |
|---|---|
| `https://host/path`, `http://host/path` | smart HTTP |
| `ssh://user@host/path`, `user@host:path` | SSH |
| `file:///path`, `/path`, `../path` | local repository, served in process |

`url.<base>.insteadOf` rewrites addresses with the longest matching prefix;
for a push, `url.<base>.pushInsteadOf` takes precedence. `git://` and
`ext::` addresses fail with `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED`.

## Locks

A file of the repository directory is not changed while its lock file
`<file>.lock` exists, which means that a `git` process is changing it or
ended without removing the lock. The command fails with `E_GIT_LOCKED` and
offers the removal of the lock as a fix.

## Errors

| Code | Problem | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `E_GIT_NOT_REPOSITORY` | `not_repository`, `path_not_found`, `unsafe_repository` | the path is not in a repository, does not exist, or belongs to another account |
| `E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED` | `unsupported_feature`, `unsupported_transport` | repository extension or address scheme without implementation |
| `E_GIT_REVISION` | `not_found`, `ambiguous`, `invalid_syntax`, `not_a_commit` | revision that cannot be resolved |
| `E_GIT_LOCKED` | `lock_exists` | lock file of `git` present |
| `E_INVALID_VALUE` | `outside_repository`, `invalid_url` | path outside the working tree, address that cannot be parsed |
| `E_EXTERNAL_FAILED` | `filter_failed` | required filter driver failed |
| `E_STALE` | | a file changed between reading and writing |
| `E_IO` | `corrupt_repository`, `repository_error`, `filter_failed` | repository data that cannot be read or converted |

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`git.status`](../commands/git.status.md) | state of the working tree and the index |
| [`git.diff`](../commands/git.diff.md) | differences with hunk identifiers |
| [`git.log`](../commands/git.log.md) | history |
| [`git.show`](../commands/git.show.md) | commit, tag or file at a revision |
| [`git.blame`](../commands/git.blame.md) | origin of lines |
| [`git.branch`](../commands/git.branch.md) | branches |
| [`git.tag`](../commands/git.tag.md) | tags |
| [`git.stage`](../commands/git.stage.md) | index: files, hunks and lines |
| [`git.commit`](../commands/git.commit.md) | commits |
| [`git.review`](../commands/git.review.md) | checks of changes before a commit |
| [`git.checkpoint`](../commands/git.checkpoint.md) | snapshots of the working tree |
| [`git.worktree`](../commands/git.worktree.md) | linked working trees |
| [`git.clone`](../commands/git.clone.md) | copy of a repository |
| [`git.fetch`](../commands/git.fetch.md) | download from a remote |
| [`git.switch`](../commands/git.switch.md) | change of the current branch |
| [`git.restore`](../commands/git.restore.md) | restore files from a revision or the index |
| [`git.reset`](../commands/git.reset.md) | move the current branch |
| [`git.stash`](../commands/git.stash.md) | set changes aside |
| [`git.merge`](../commands/git.merge.md) | merge histories |
| [`git.rebase`](../commands/git.rebase.md) | replay commits |
| [`git.push`](../commands/git.push.md) | upload to a remote |
| [`git.pull`](../commands/git.pull.md) | fetch and integrate |

## Examples

Status of the repository that contains a subdirectory:

```nurt
git.status "/work/app/src/net"
```

Previous position of a branch from its reflog:

```nurt
git.log "/work/app" revision: "main@{1}" count: 1
```

Staging a directory without lock files:

```nurt
git.stage "/work/app" action: add paths: ["docs"] exclude: ["*.lock"]
```

History of the upstream of the current branch:

```nurt
git.log "/work/app" revision: "@{upstream}" count: 5
```

title: Group network
text:
# Group network

## Scope

The group sends HTTP requests, downloads files, resolves DNS names, measures
round-trip times and lists the network interfaces of the host. All commands
are part of Danaco Nurt; none of them starts a program.

| Task | Command | Group |
|---|---|---|
| Read or write a local file | `read`, `write` | core |
| Extract a downloaded archive | `archive.extract` | archive |
| Undo a download | `undo` | core |
| Check which hosts a program contacts | `nurt_check` | all groups |

The check of a program (`nurt_check`) lists the network targets of
`http.request` and `http.download` before the program runs, so an embedding
application can apply its own rules.

## Commands

| Command | Category | Input and output | Reversibility | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `http.request` | change | none to `response` | read, by method | [http.request](../commands/http.request.md) |
| `http.download` | change | none to `effect` | reversible | [http.download](../commands/http.download.md) |
| `network.ping` | source | none to `ping_result` | read | [network.ping](../commands/network.ping.md) |
| `network.resolve` | source | none to `dns_record` | read | [network.resolve](../commands/network.resolve.md) |
| `network.interfaces` | source | none to `network_interface` | read | [network.interfaces](../commands/network.interfaces.md) |

## Records

| Record | Required fields |
|---|---|
| `response` | `url`, `status`, `headers`, `body`, `bytes`, `elapsed`, `final_url` |
| `ping_result` | `host`, `address`, `sent`, `received`, `loss` |
| `dns_record` | `name`, `type`, `value`, `ttl` |
| `network_interface` | `name`, `addresses`, `up` |
| `effect` | `status`, `kind` |

Round-trip times of `ping_result` (`rtt_min`, `rtt_avg`, `rtt_max`,
`rtt_stddev`) are in milliseconds. `loss` is a percentage.

## HTTP requests

The status of the HTTP response is data. A response with the status 404 or
503 is a successful result of `http.request`; the status is the field `status`
of the record, and a program checks it with `filter` or `assert`. Only a
failure to obtain a response is an error.

The parameter `as` selects the form of the body: `raw` (default), `text`, or
`markdown` for a page converted from HTML. The parameter `extract` selects
what is returned from a page: `content`, `headers`, `links`, `headings`,
`meta` or `tables`. With several addresses in `url`, the command produces one
record per address.

The reversibility of `http.request` depends on the method:

| Method | Effect | Reversibility |
|---|---|---|
| `get`, `head`, `options` | read | read |
| `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete` | external | irreversible |
| any, with `save` | file written | reversible, restored by `undo` |

An irreversible request is listed among the irreversible effects of the
effect report.

`http.download` writes the response body to the path in `to` and resumes a
partial download when the server supports it (`resume: true`). With `hash`,
the downloaded file is verified against the given digest, for example
`sha256:` followed by the digest. A file with a different digest is not kept,
and the command fails with `E_HASH_MISMATCH`. The file write goes through the
operation journal, so `undo` removes the downloaded file or restores the file
that it replaced.

## Platform differences

| Command | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `http.request`, `http.download` | identical behavior | identical behavior | identical behavior |
| `network.ping` | ICMP echo through the system | ICMP echo through the system | ICMP echo through the system API |
| `network.resolve` | resolver of the system, or the host in `server` | same | same |
| `network.interfaces` | interfaces of the system | interfaces of the system | adapters of the system |

The commands report these errors:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_NETWORK` | Name resolution, connection, TLS, proxy, redirect or protocol failure. |
| `E_HASH_MISMATCH` | The digest of a download differs from `hash`. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The `timeout` of the command or of the program elapsed. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | The execution was cancelled. |

The default `timeout` of `http.download` is `300s`, longer than the default
time limit of a program. When the program does not set `timeout`, its limit is
raised to the longest explicit limit of its commands.

## External programs

No command of the group starts a program. The group has no [X], [P] or [U]
marker.

## Examples

Send a request and check that exactly one response arrived:

```nurt example
http.request "https://api.example.com/health" |> assert count: 1
```

Check that the status is a success. A status of 400 or above fails the
`assert` and not the request:

```nurt example
http.request "https://example.com/health" |> assert all: status < 400
```

Read a page as Markdown:

```nurt example
http.request "https://example.com/docs" as: markdown
```

Send JSON with the method `post`:

```nurt example
http.request "https://example.com/api/items" method: post json: {name: "demo"}
```

Download a file and verify its digest:

```nurt example
http.download "https://example.com/a.tar.gz" "/home/user/dl/a.tar.gz" hash: "sha256:e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"
```

Measure three round trips to a host:

```nurt example
network.ping "example.com" count: 3
```

Resolve the mail exchangers of a domain:

```nurt example
network.resolve "example.com" type: mx
```

List the interfaces that are up:

```nurt example
network.interfaces |> filter up |> select name addresses
```

## Related

[Group schedule](schedule.md) runs requests and downloads at set times.
[Group system](system.md) lists ports and the processes that hold them.

title: Group package
text:
# Group package

## Scope

The group lists, searches, installs, removes and upgrades packages through the
package manager of the system and returns the result as `package` records. The
commands do not replace the package manager: it carries out every operation,
and the group gives its output a typed form and records the change in the
operation journal.

| Task | Command | Group |
|---|---|---|
| Find an installed program by name | `program.find` | program |
| Describe an installed program | `program.describe` | program |
| Search programs of all sources, including packages | `program.search` | program |
| Run a program | `run` | core |

`package.search` queries the repositories of the package manager.
`program.search` reads the package databases of the system and needs no
package manager.

## Commands

| Command | Category | Input and output | Reversibility | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `package.list` | source | none to `package` | read | [package.list](../commands/package.list.md) |
| `package.search` | source | none to `package` | read | [package.search](../commands/package.search.md) |
| `package.install` | change | none to `effect` | irreversible | [package.install](../commands/package.install.md) |
| `package.remove` | change | none to `effect` | irreversible | [package.remove](../commands/package.remove.md) |
| `package.upgrade` | change | none to `effect` | irreversible | [package.upgrade](../commands/package.upgrade.md) |

## Records

| Record | Required fields |
|---|---|
| `package` | `name`, `version`, `manager`, `installed` |
| `effect` | `status`, `kind` |

`package.version` is the installed version, or the offered version in the
result of a search. With `outdated: true` the field `available_version` holds
the newer version. Optional fields are `description`, `architecture`, `size`,
`source` and `files_count`.

## Package managers

The parameter `manager` selects the package manager. The default is `auto`:
the manager that the host uses is detected from the operating system and the
programs found in the search path.

| Value | System |
|---|---|
| `apt` | Debian and Ubuntu |
| `dnf` | Fedora and Red Hat family |
| `pacman` | Arch Linux |
| `zypper` | openSUSE and SUSE |
| `brew` | macOS and Linux with Homebrew |
| `winget` | Windows |
| `choco` | Windows with Chocolatey |
| `scoop` | Windows with Scoop |

The record field `manager` also accepts `dpkg`, `rpm` and `other` for packages
that the manager reports with another origin. A value of `manager` that the
host does not have fails with `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING`.

Installation, removal and upgrade change the system outside the file system.
The operation journal records them as irreversible: `undo` does not restore a
removed package and does not remove an installed one.
## Platform differences

| Aspect | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Managers | `apt`, `dnf`, `pacman`, `zypper`, `brew` | `brew` | `winget`, `choco`, `scoop` |
| Privilege for `install`, `remove`, `upgrade` | the privilege that the manager requires | the privilege that the manager requires | the privilege that the manager requires |
| Missing privilege | `E_PRIVILEGE` | `E_PRIVILEGE` | `E_PRIVILEGE` |

A command whose manager is not installed fails with `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING`, and
`fix` shows how to install it.

## External programs

The catalog marks the implementation of every command of the group as a
package manager program [P]:

| Command | Marker | Program |
|---|---|---|
| `package.list` | [P] | the selected manager |
| `package.search` | [P] | the selected manager |
| `package.install` | [P] | the selected manager |
| `package.remove` | [P] | the selected manager |
| `package.upgrade` | [P] | the selected manager |

The check of the program reports the program before execution.

## Examples

List the installed packages named `git`:

```nurt example
package.list name: "git"
```

Count the packages that have a newer version:

```nurt example
package.list outdated: true |> count
```

Show the installed and the available version of outdated packages:

```nurt example
package.list outdated: true |> select name version available_version
```

Search the repositories of the manager:

```nurt example
package.search "ripgrep"
```

Install two packages with the manager `apt`:

```nurt example
package.install ["git", "curl"] manager: apt
```

Upgrade one package:

```nurt example
package.upgrade ["openssl"]
```

## Related

[Group program](program.md) describes installed programs without a package
manager. [Group system](system.md) reports the host on which `manager: auto`
decides.

title: Group program
text:
# Group program

## Scope

The group answers which programs exist on the computer and how to use them.
It locates programs in the search path, searches installed programs and the
program catalogs, describes a program with its version and usage guide, and
browses programs by category.

The group works on every computer from the first call and needs no
configuration. External catalogs are optional and add descriptions, categories
and usage guides to the programs that the system already reports.

| Task | Command | Group |
|---|---|---|
| Run a program | `run` | core |
| List, install and remove packages | `package.*` | package |
| Describe the host and its operating system | `host` | system |
| Read the manual page of a program as a file | `read` | core |

`package.search` queries the repositories of a package manager and needs the
manager. The commands of this group read the databases of the package managers
and never start the manager.

## Commands

| Command | Category | Input and output | Reversibility | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `program.find` | source | none to `program_location` | read | [program.find](../commands/program.find.md) |
| `program.search` | source | none to `program_card` | read | [program.search](../commands/program.search.md) |
| `program.describe` | source | none to `program_card` | read | [program.describe](../commands/program.describe.md) |
| `program.catalog` | source | none to `program_category` or `program_card` | read | [program.catalog](../commands/program.catalog.md) |

## Records

| Record | Required fields |
|---|---|
| `program_location` | `name`, `found` |
| `program_card` | `name`, `summary`, `source`, `installed`, `guide_optional`, `sources` |
| `program_category` | `name`, `count`, `source` |

`program_location` reports the path that a name resolves to; `all_paths` lists
every match in the order the system resolves them. `program_card` carries the
description in `description` and the usage guide in `guide`. The field `source`
names the main source (`path`, `package`, `app` or `catalog`) and `sources`
lists every source from which the card was assembled, so the origin of each
text is known.

## Sources of data

| Source | Value of `source` | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Search path | `path` | name, path and version of executable files; `PATHEXT` is honored on Windows |
| Package databases | `package` | name, version, description and executables of installed packages |
| System applications | `app` | name, path, version and publisher of applications |
| Program catalogs | `catalog` | descriptions, categories and usage guides |
| Descriptions | | manual pages and `whatis` entries, package metadata |

The package databases are read from files, without starting the manager:

| System | Databases |
|---|---|
| Linux | dpkg, rpm, pacman |
| macOS | Homebrew |
| Windows | winget, Scoop, Chocolatey |

Applications come from the registry and the Start menu on Windows, from
application bundles on macOS and from desktop entries on Linux.

## External catalogs

A catalog is a directory in the format `nurt-program-catalog/1`:

```text
catalog.json        index: format, categories and programs
guides/<name>.md    usage guide of a program, Markdown with a front matter
```

The index lists categories (`id`, `title`, `description`, `parent`) and
programs (`name`, `category`, `summary`, `aliases`, `platforms`, `guide`,
`verified`, `tags`). The reader treats a catalog as data: it executes no field
and no file of the catalog and fetches no address.

The setting `programs.catalogs` lists the catalogs: paths or tables with
`path`, `priority` and `enabled`. The default is an empty list, and the product
names no catalog. Without catalogs the commands describe the installed programs.
A catalog that is configured explicitly and cannot be read fails with
`E_CATALOG`. The setting `programs.sources_disabled` excludes sources
(`path`, `package`, `app`, `man`, `catalog`) from the index.

## Platform differences

| Aspect | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Executable files | files with the execute permission | files with the execute permission | extensions of `PATHEXT` |
| Application source | desktop entries | application bundles | registry and Start menu |
| Package databases | dpkg, rpm, pacman | Homebrew | winget, Scoop, Chocolatey |
| Version of an executable | package version | bundle version | version resource of the file |

`E_OS_ONLY` is not reported by this group: every command works on all
three systems and a source that does not exist on the system is skipped.

## External programs

| Command | Marker | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| `program.describe` | [U] | runs the program once with `--help`, within a time limit, when `help` is used |

The time limit of reading the help is the setting `programs.help_timeout`
(default `3s`). No other command of the group starts a program, and the
index is never built by starting programs. The [U] marker names a program of
the user.

## Examples

Locate two programs and report their versions:

```nurt example
program.find ["git", "python3"] versions: true
```

Search installed programs and catalogs, and keep the installed ones:

```nurt example
program.search "convert images" limit: 10 |> filter installed |> select name path summary
```

Search only the search path and the package databases:

```nurt example
program.search "pdf" source: [path, package] limit: 5
```

Describe a program without its usage guide:

```nurt example
program.describe "ffmpeg" include_guide: false
```

List the categories with the most programs:

```nurt example
program.catalog |> sort count order: desc |> first 5
```

## Related

[Group package](package.md) installs the programs that this group finds.
[Group system](system.md) reports the host on which the search runs.

title: Group schedule
text:
# Group schedule

## Scope

The group creates and manages schedules: programs that run at set times
without a caller. One syntax replaces cron, systemd timers, launchd jobs and
the Windows Task Scheduler. The action of a schedule is a program in the
syntax of Danaco Nurt, given as a pipeline in the parameter `action`.

Schedules run in the background service of the instance (`nurt-service`). A
run is an ordinary operation: it has an entry in the operation journal and
the effects of its program are reported like those of a program run by a
caller. The group only defines and queries schedules; the service executes
them.

| Task | Command | Group |
|---|---|---|
| Start or stop the background service | `nurt service` | command line |
| Run a program once, now | `run` | core |
| Undo the effect of a scheduled run | `undo` | core |
| List the operations of the journal | `history` | core |

## Commands

| Command | Category | Input and output | Reversibility | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `schedule.create` | change | none to `schedule` | reversible | [schedule.create](../commands/schedule.create.md) |
| `schedule.list` | source | none to `schedule` | read | [schedule.list](../commands/schedule.list.md) |
| `schedule.remove` | change | none to `effect` | reversible | [schedule.remove](../commands/schedule.remove.md) |
| `schedule.pause` | change | none to `effect` | reversible | [schedule.pause](../commands/schedule.pause.md) |
| `schedule.resume` | change | none to `effect` | reversible | [schedule.resume](../commands/schedule.resume.md) |
