| `schedule.run` | run | none to `exec` or `job` | reversible if preserved | [schedule.run](../commands/schedule.run.md) |
| `schedule.history` | source | none to `schedule_run` | read | [schedule.history](../commands/schedule.history.md) |

## Records

| Record | Required fields |
|---|---|
| `schedule` | `id`, `trigger`, `next_run`, `active`, `action` |
| `schedule_run` | `schedule_id`, `started`, `exit_state`, `trigger_time` |
| `effect` | `status`, `kind` |
| `exec` | `command`, `program`, `cwd`, `pid`, `exit_code`, `started`, `elapsed` |

The field `trigger` is an object with `kind` (`cron`, `every` or `at`),
`expression` (the trigger as written) and `timezone`. The field `action` holds
the canonical text of the program. The values of `exit_state` are `ok`,
`failed`, `timed_out`, `skipped_overlap`, `missed` and `cancelled`; the field
`operation` of a run is the number of its journal operation.

## Triggers and time

`schedule.create` takes the label as the first argument and exactly one
trigger:

| Parameter | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `cron` | five-field cron expression or `@daily` |
| `every` | interval from `30s` to 366 days |
| `at` | one point in time |

The first run of an interval is one interval after creation. A later run is
one interval after the previous planned time; when that time has passed, it is
one interval after the current time. A planned time is always later than the
reference time.

`timezone` defaults to `local`, the zone of the computer at the moment of
creation stored as an IANA name. A later change of the zone of the system
does not move the schedule. A time that does not exist in a transition to
summer time runs at the first existing moment after the transition. A time
that occurs twice in a transition to winter time runs once, at the first
occurrence.

## Missed runs and overlap

The background service runs only while the computer and the service run. A
planned time that passed while they did not is handled by `on_missed`:

| Value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `skip` | The run is skipped when the delay exceeds `misfire` (default `2m`); the next run is planned from the current time. |
| `run_once` | Exactly one run is made, regardless of the number of missed times. |

`overlap` decides what happens when a planned time arrives while the previous
run still runs:

| Value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `skip` | The run is skipped and counted as skipped; default. |
| `queue` | One run is kept for later; further times count as skipped. |
| `parallel` | The run starts at once, alongside the previous one. |

`max_runs` ends the schedule after that many runs, and `expires` ends it at a
time or after a duration. A finished schedule has the state `completed` or
`expired`.

`timeout` (default `1h`) limits the whole program of the action and is the
default `timeout` of its `run` stages that do not set one. Without this rule
the default limit of `run` would stop an action earlier than the schedule
allows.

`schedule.run` starts the action at once, outside the planned times. It does
not change `next_run` and does not count against `max_runs`.

## Platform differences

The schedule is the same on all systems. The service differs:

| Aspect | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Service manager of the background service | systemd | launchd | service control manager |
| Service in user mode | runs for the account; it keeps running after logout only when linger is enabled for the account | runs for the account | runs for the account |
| Service in system mode | runs for the computer | runs for the computer | runs for the computer |

The installation mode of the service is the setting `service.mode`, `user` by
default and `system` for servers. Without a running service a schedule is
stored but does not run: `schedule.create` returns the record with
`active: false` and `reason: service_not_running`; the failure is reported
and not hidden.

## External programs

No command of the group starts a program. The group has no [X], [P] or [U]
marker. On macOS the service is registered with launchd by `nurt service`,
outside these commands.

## Examples

Create a schedule that runs a backup program every night at 02:00:

```nurt example
schedule.create "backup" cron: "0 2 * * *" action: (run ["backup"] cwd: "/home/user")
```

Check an address every five minutes and keep the run limited to one minute:

```nurt example
schedule.create "health" every: 5m timeout: 1m action: (http.request "https://example.com/health" |> assert all: status < 400)
```

List the active schedules with their next run:

```nurt example
schedule.list state: active |> select id label next_run
```

Create a schedule, pause it and resume it:

```nurt example
schedule.create "report" every: 1h action: (run ["report"] cwd: "/home/user")
schedule.pause "s1"
schedule.resume "s1"
```

Create a schedule and run its action once at once:

```nurt example
schedule.create "pause" every: 10m action: (sleep 2s)
schedule.run "s1"
```

Show the failed runs of all schedules:

```nurt example
schedule.history limit: 10 |> filter exit_state == "failed"
```

## Related

[Group network](network.md) provides the requests that schedules commonly run.
[Group system](system.md) provides `sleep`.

title: Group system
text:
# Group system

## Scope

The group reports the state of the computer: running processes, network ports,
mounted volumes, facts about the host, environment variables, accounts, files
held open by processes and the system log. `sleep` belongs to the group
because it waits on the clock of the program and reads nothing.

Commands that act on the state reported here belong to other groups:

| Task | Command | Group |
|---|---|---|
| Stop a process, job or service | `stop` | core |
| Read the operation journal of Danaco Nurt | `journal.*` | journal |
| Read and change files, including `registry:` paths | `read`, `write`, `list` | core |
| Manage services | `services`, `start`, `restart` | administration |

`suspend` and `resume` are listed at the end of the command table. Their
pages are maintained with the commands that run and control programs.

## Commands

Every source command takes no input and produces records of one kind.

| Command | Category | Input and output | Reversibility | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `processes` | source | none to `process` | read | [processes](../commands/processes.md) |
| `ports` | source | none to `port` | read | [ports](../commands/ports.md) |
| `disks` | source | none to `disk` | read | [disks](../commands/disks.md) |
| `host` | source | none to `host` | read | [host](../commands/host.md) |
| `environment` | source | none to `environment_variable` | read | [environment](../commands/environment.md) |
| `open_files` | source | none to `process` | read | [open_files](../commands/open_files.md) |
| `accounts` | source | none to `account` | read | [accounts](../commands/accounts.md) |
| `sleep` | run | none to none | read | [sleep](../commands/sleep.md) |
| `logs` | source | none to `log_event` | read | [logs](../commands/logs.md) |

Commands of the group described by other pages:

| Command | Category | Input and output | Reversibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| `suspend` | run | `job` or `process` to `effect` | irreversible |
| `resume` | run | `job` or `process` to `effect` | irreversible |

## Records

Fields that every record of the kind carries. Optional fields are listed on
the page of the command.

| Record | Required fields |
|---|---|
| `process` | `pid`, `parent_pid`, `name`, `command`, `user`, `memory`, `started`, `state` |
| `port` | `protocol`, `local`, `address`, `port`, `state` |
| `disk` | `mount`, `device`, `filesystem`, `total`, `free`, `used`, `type`, `case_sensitive`, `readonly` |
| `host` | `os`, `os_version`, `architecture`, `cpus`, `memory_total`, `hostname`, `user`, `home`, `temp`, `timezone`, `path_style`, `nurt_version`, `features` |
| `environment_variable` | `name`, `value`, `scope` |
| `account` | `name`, `kind`, `id` |
| `log_event` | `time`, `source`, `level`, `message` |

`open_files` produces `process` records of the processes that hold the path.
Environment values are never masked. The raw attributes of the system are
kept in `os_raw` on the kinds that have the field and are outside the
stability guarantee of the record.

## Scope of environment variables

The parameter `scope` of `environment` selects where the variables are read:

| Value | Source |
|---|---|
| `process` | environment of the process that runs the program; default |
| `user` | persistent variables of the account; Windows only |
| `machine` | persistent variables of the computer; Windows only |

`scope` of `environment` and `scope` of `services` have different values and
different meaning. For `services` it selects the service manager instance
(`system` or `user`), see the group `administration`.

The environment is read through the `env:` provider of the file commands or
through `environment`. The provider addresses one variable as a path and
returns text. `environment` returns records that can be filtered and sorted,
and it reads the persistent scopes.

## Platform differences

| Command | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `processes` | process table of the kernel | process table of the kernel | process snapshot of the system |
| `ports` | socket tables of the kernel | socket tables of the system | IP Helper tables |
| `disks` | mount table | mount table | volumes with drive letters |
| `host` | kernel version in `kernel` | kernel version in `kernel` | `os_version` is the build number |
| `environment` | `process` scope | `process` scope | `process`, `user` and `machine` scopes |
| `accounts` | account and group databases | local directory | local accounts and groups; `id` is a SID |
| `logs` | systemd journal read by a native reader | unified log | Event Log |

Accounts report `uid` as UID on Linux and macOS and as SID on Windows.

Reading data that belongs to other accounts can require a privilege.
Processes, sockets and open files of other accounts are reported with the
fields that the system discloses; optional fields such as `pid`, `process`,
`cwd` or `executable` are absent when it hides them. A command that cannot
read its source at all fails with `E_PRIVILEGE`; `fix` names the required
privilege. A source read partially is reported as the warning
`permission_denied_skipped`, which does not interrupt the program.

### The command logs

`logs` returns events from the log of the operating system without starting a
program. The newest events come first. `level` is a threshold: the events of
that importance and the more important ones are returned.

| Parameter | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | program that logged the event | process | provider |
| `unit` | systemd unit | subsystem | channel; default `System` and `Application` |
| `since`, `until` | time of the event | time of the event | `TimeCreated` |

Linux reads the journal files of systemd with a reader of the file format of
Danaco Nurt. On Linux without a journal the command fails with `E_NOT_FOUND`.
On Windows the `Security` channel requires a privilege and fails with
`E_PRIVILEGE` without it. Each event carries a `cursor` field that marks its position in the log.

## External programs

| Command | Marker | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| `host` | [U] | `versions: true` runs every located program once with `--version` |

No other command of the group starts a program. A [U] marker names a program
of the user that the command starts only on request.

## Examples

Show the five busiest processes named `node`:

```nurt example
processes name: "node" |> sort cpu order: desc |> first 5
```

List the listening port 8080 and the process that holds it:

```nurt example
ports state: listen |> filter port == 8080
```

List the fixed disks with less than 10 GB free:

```nurt example
disks type: fixed |> filter free < 10gb |> select mount free
```

Read the warnings of one service from the system log:

```nurt example
logs unit: "nginx.service" level: warning limit: 20
```

List the processes that hold a file open:

```nurt example
open_files "/home/user/app/data.db"
```

Report the versions of programs found in the search path:

```nurt example
host programs: ["git", "python3"] versions: true
```

Wait for two seconds:

```nurt example
sleep 2s
```

## Related

[Group administration](administration.md) manages the services that `processes` and `ports`
report. [Group program](program.md) describes installed programs. The page of
the command `sleep` is [sleep](../commands/sleep.md).

title: Nurt for bash users
text:
# Nurt for bash users

Every row pairs a Bash command with its form in Nurt. The last column states whether Nurt corrects the habit automatically, rejects it with an error that carries the fix, or rejects it with an error that carries no program and asks for the program of the row.

The paths are those of a Linux host, and the call parameter `base` is `/home/user/app`.

## Files and directories

| Rule | Bash | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| B01 | `rm -rf /home/user/app/build` | `remove "/home/user/app/build"` | corrected automatically: recursion is implicit and a missing path is skipped |
| B02 | `rm /home/user/app/build/*.tmp` | `find "/home/user/app/build" glob: "*.tmp" depth: 1 hidden: false \|> remove on_missing: error` | corrected automatically: the glob is expanded as bash would, without recursion |
| B03 | `mv /home/user/a.txt /home/user/archive` | `move "/home/user/a.txt" to: "/home/user/archive"` | corrected automatically |
| B04 | `cp -r /home/user/app /home/user/backup` | `copy "/home/user/app" to: "/home/user/backup" preserve: false` | corrected automatically |
| B05 | `mkdir -p /home/user/app/out` | `create "/home/user/app/out" type: directory` | corrected automatically |
| B06 | `touch /home/user/app/a.txt` | `create "/home/user/app/a.txt" type: file on_exists: touch` | corrected automatically |
| B07 | `chmod -R 755 /home/user/app/bin` | `attributes "/home/user/app/bin" mode: "755" recursive: true` | corrected automatically |
| B09 | `ln -s /home/user/app/src /home/user/link` | `create "/home/user/link" type: link target: "/home/user/app/src"` | corrected automatically |
| B13 | `ls -la /home/user/app` | `list "/home/user/app"` | corrected automatically |
| B14 | `find /home/user/app -name '*.go' -type f` | `find "/home/user/app" glob: "**/*.go" type: file` | corrected automatically |
| B37 | `stat /home/user/app/a.txt` | `info "/home/user/app/a.txt"` | corrected automatically |

## Reading and searching text

| Rule | Bash | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| B10 | `cat /home/user/app/a.txt` | `read "/home/user/app/a.txt"` | corrected automatically |
| B11 | `tail -n 20 /home/user/app/a.log` | `read "/home/user/app/a.log" last: 20` | corrected automatically |
| B12 | `wc -l /home/user/app/a.txt` | `lines "/home/user/app/a.txt" \|> count` | corrected automatically |
| B15 | `grep -rni 'todo' /home/user/app/src` | `search /todo/ "/home/user/app/src" case_sensitive: false` | corrected automatically: a pattern in basic regular expression syntax is converted with an assumption that the report names |
| B16 | `sed -i 's/oldName/newName/g' /home/user/app/a.go` | `replace /oldName/ "newName" in: ["/home/user/app/a.go"]` | corrected automatically |
| B17 | `sed -n '10,20p' /home/user/app/a.go` | `read "/home/user/app/a.go" lines: 10..20` | corrected automatically |
| B37b | `sha256sum /home/user/app/a.tar.gz` | `hash "/home/user/app/a.tar.gz"` | corrected automatically |
| B37c | `diff /home/user/a.txt /home/user/b.txt` | `diff "/home/user/a.txt" "/home/user/b.txt"` | corrected automatically |

## Writing text

| Rule | Bash | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| B19 | `echo "dist/" >> /home/user/app/.gitignore` | `write "/home/user/app/.gitignore" "dist/\n" mode: append` | corrected automatically |

## Archives

| Rule | Bash | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| B34 | `tar -xzf /home/user/dl/data.tar.gz -C /home/user/data` | `archive.extract "/home/user/dl/data.tar.gz" into: "/home/user/data"` | corrected automatically |
| B34b | `gzip /home/user/app/a.log` | `compress "/home/user/app/a.log" keep: false` | corrected automatically |

## Processes and system

| Rule | Bash | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| B35a | `ps aux` | `processes` | corrected automatically |
| B35b | `df -h` | `disks` | corrected automatically |
| B35c | `ss -ltnp` | `ports protocol: tcp` | corrected automatically |
| B35d | `printenv` | `environment` | corrected automatically |
| B35e | `which git` | `program.find "git"` | corrected automatically |
| B36 | `kill -9 4132` | `processes pid: 4132 \|> stop signal: kill` | corrected automatically |

## Running programs

| Rule | Bash | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| B29 | `npm run build &` | `run ["npm", "run", "build"] cwd: "/home/user/app" background: true` | error without fix: `&` is not part of the language; write the program with background: true and the directory as cwd |
| B30 | `timeout 60 make test` | `run ["make", "test"] cwd: "/home/user/app" timeout: 60s` | error with fix: there is no current directory; the fix passes the directory as cwd or base |
| B20 | `cd /home/user/app && make` | `run ["make"] cwd: "/home/user/app"` | corrected automatically: only a change to an absolute directory in the same line is converted |
| B31 | `CI=1 npm test` | `run ["npm", "test"] cwd: "/home/user/app" env: {"CI": "1"}` | error with fix: there is no current directory; the fix passes the directory as cwd or base |

## Network

| Rule | Bash | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| B32 | `curl -s https://example.com/health` | `http.request "https://example.com/health" follow_redirects: false` | corrected automatically |
| B32b | `wget -O /home/user/a.tar.gz https://example.com/a.tar.gz` | `http.download "https://example.com/a.tar.gz" "/home/user/a.tar.gz"` | corrected automatically |

## Git

| Rule | Bash | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| B38 | `git -C /home/user/app status` | `git.status "/home/user/app"` | corrected automatically |

## Services and packages

| Rule | Bash | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| B40 | `systemctl restart nginx` | `services name: "nginx" \|> restart` | corrected automatically |
| B40b | `apt install -y ripgrep` | `package.install ["ripgrep"] manager: apt` | corrected automatically |

## Control flow

| Rule | Bash | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| B22 | `mkdir /home/user/out && cp /home/user/a.txt /home/user/out` | `create "/home/user/out" type: directory parents: false` | error with fix: two changing commands are not run in one program; the fix is one call per change, this is the first |
| B25 | `rm -rf "$BUILD"/*` | `find "/home/user/app/build" glob: "*" depth: 1 \|> remove` | error without fix: there are no variables in text; write the directory |
| B28 | `sudo systemctl restart nginx` | `services name: "nginx" \|> restart privilege: elevated` | corrected automatically: the program runs with the call parameter privilege: elevated; sudo -u NAME gives as_user |

title: Nurt for PowerShell users
text:
# Nurt for PowerShell users

Every row pairs a PowerShell command with its form in Nurt. The last column states whether Nurt corrects the habit automatically, rejects it with an error that carries the fix, or rejects it with an error that carries no program and asks for the program of the row.

The paths are those of a Windows host, and the call parameter `base` is `C:/Users/user`.

## Files and directories

| Rule | PowerShell | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | `Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users\user\app` | `list "C:/Users/user/app" hidden: false` | corrected automatically |
| P02 | `Get-ChildItem C:\Users\user\app -Recurse -Filter *.go` | `find "C:/Users/user/app" glob: "**/*.go" type: any hidden: false` | corrected automatically |
| P06 | `Copy-Item C:\Users\user\app C:\Users\user\backup -Recurse` | `copy "C:/Users/user/app" to: "C:/Users/user/backup"` | corrected automatically |
| P07 | `Move-Item C:\Users\user\a.txt C:\Users\user\archive` | `move "C:/Users/user/a.txt" to: "C:/Users/user/archive" on_conflict: error` | corrected automatically |
| P08 | `Remove-Item C:\Users\user\app\build -Recurse -Force` | `remove "C:/Users/user/app/build"` | corrected automatically |
| P09 | `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path C:\Users\user\app\out` | `create "C:/Users/user/app/out" type: directory` | corrected automatically |
| P10 | `Rename-Item C:\Users\user\a.txt -NewName b.txt` | `rename path: "C:/Users/user/a.txt" to: "b.txt"` | corrected automatically |
| P11 | `Test-Path C:\Users\user\a.txt` | `info "C:/Users/user/a.txt"` | corrected automatically |

## Reading and searching text

| Rule | PowerShell | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| P03 | `Get-Content C:\Users\user\a.log -Tail 20` | `read "C:/Users/user/a.log" last: 20` | corrected automatically |
| P05 | `Select-String -Pattern todo -Path C:\Users\user\app\a.go` | `search /todo/ "C:/Users/user/app/a.go" case_sensitive: false` | corrected automatically: Select-String ignores letter case by default, so the pattern is case-insensitive |
| P21 | `Get-FileHash C:\Users\user\a.zip -Algorithm SHA256` | `hash "C:/Users/user/a.zip" algorithm: sha256` | corrected automatically |
| P20 | `Compare-Object (Get-Content a.txt) (Get-Content b.txt)` | `diff "C:/Users/user/a.txt" "C:/Users/user/b.txt"` | corrected automatically: only files are compared; relative paths are resolved against the call parameter base |

## Writing text

| Rule | PowerShell | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| P04 | `Add-Content C:\Users\user\app\.gitignore -Value dist/` | `write "C:/Users/user/app/.gitignore" "dist/\n" mode: append` | corrected automatically |

## Registry

| Rule | PowerShell | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| P12 | `Get-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Example -Name Mode` | `read "registry:/HKCU/Software/Example/Mode"` | corrected automatically |
| P13 | `Set-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Example -Name Mode -Value 3 -Type DWord` | `write "registry:/HKCU/Software/Example/Mode" "3" value_type: dword mode: overwrite` | corrected automatically |

## Pipelines

| Rule | PowerShell | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| P15 | `Get-ChildItem C:\Users\user\app -Recurse \| Where-Object { $_.Length -gt 1MB }` | `find "C:/Users/user/app" type: any hidden: false \|> filter size > 1mib` | corrected automatically |
| P16 | `Get-Process \| Select-Object -First 5` | `processes \|> first 5` | corrected automatically |
| P17 | `Get-Process \| Sort-Object WorkingSet -Descending` | `processes \|> sort memory order: desc` | corrected automatically |
| P18 | `Get-Process \| Measure-Object` | `processes \|> count` | corrected automatically |
| P19 | `Get-Process \| ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_.Name }` | `processes \|> select name` | error without fix: loops are replaced by pipelines; write the pipeline that selects the field |

## Processes and services

| Rule | PowerShell | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| P22 | `Stop-Process -Id 8120 -Force` | `processes pid: 8120 \|> stop signal: kill` | corrected automatically |
| P23 | `Start-Process npm -ArgumentList 'test' -WorkingDirectory C:\Users\user\app -Wait` | `run ["npm", "test"] cwd: "C:/Users/user/app" wait: forever` | corrected automatically |
| P24 | `Restart-Service nginx` | `services name: "nginx" \|> restart` | corrected automatically |
| P31 | `$env:PATH` | `environment name: "PATH"` | corrected automatically |
| P40 | `Get-Volume` | `disks` | corrected automatically |
| P37 | `Get-WinEvent -LogName System -MaxEvents 50` | `logs source: "System" limit: 50` | corrected automatically |
| P39 | `Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_OperatingSystem` | `windows.cim "Win32_OperatingSystem"` | corrected automatically |

## Network

| Rule | PowerShell | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| P25 | `Invoke-WebRequest https://example.com/a.zip -OutFile C:\Users\user\a.zip` | `http.download "https://example.com/a.zip" "C:/Users/user/a.zip"` | corrected automatically |
| P38 | `Test-Connection example.com` | `network.ping "example.com"` | corrected automatically |
| P38b | `Resolve-DnsName example.com` | `network.resolve "example.com"` | corrected automatically |

## Archives

| Rule | PowerShell | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| P29 | `Expand-Archive -Path C:\Users\user\a.zip -DestinationPath C:\Users\user\data` | `archive.extract "C:/Users/user/a.zip" into: "C:/Users/user/data" on_conflict: error` | corrected automatically |

## Other

| Rule | PowerShell | Nurt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| P26 | `Start-Sleep -Seconds 5` | `sleep 5s` | corrected automatically |
| P30 | `Set-Location C:\Users\user\app` | `run ["make"] cwd: "C:/Users/user/app"` | error without fix: there is no current directory; pass the directory of the next program as cwd or base |
| P42 | `Invoke-Expression $command` | `run ["pwsh", "-Command", "Get-Date"] cwd: "C:/Users/user"` | error without fix: the language has no eval; run the program explicitly |

title: C interface (libnurt)
text:
# C interface (libnurt)

The library `libnurt` exposes the engine to C and to every language with a C
foreign function interface. The interface is declared in
`crates/nurt-ffi/include/nurt.h`; the exported symbols are listed in
`crates/nurt-ffi/nurt.symbols`. The crate `nurt-ffi` builds a shared library
(`libnurt_ffi.so`, `libnurt_ffi.dylib`, `nurt_ffi.dll`) and a static library.
The release publishes the shared library in its own archive `nurt-lib-<version>-<target>`, as `libnurt.so.1`,
`libnurt.1.dylib` and `nurt.dll`, with `nurt.h` and `nurt.pc`; the program archive does not hold it. The packages
install the library as `libnurt.so` (also `libnurt.so.1`) and `libnurt.dylib`. The bindings for .NET and Java look for the name of the
package first and for the name of the build second, so both are found; a path given in the
options or in `NURT_LIBRARY` is used as given, whatever its name.

On musl targets (`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`) the library of the release is static: the archive `nurt-lib-<version>-<target>`
holds `libnurt.a`, `nurt.h` and `nurt.pc`, and `pkg-config --static --libs nurt` returns every library that a static link needs. On musl the library is
static (`libnurt.a`) and must not be linked into one program with another static library written in Rust.
The program `examples/c/hello.c` calls `nurt_abi_check` and `nurt_version`; the release checks build and run it against the library archive.

## Versioning

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| `NURT_ABI_MAJOR` | `1` |
| `NURT_ABI_MINOR` | `0` |
| `NURT_ABI_VERSION` | `(NURT_ABI_MAJOR << 16) \| NURT_ABI_MINOR` |

Within one major version the interface only grows: functions, status codes
and JSON members are added, never removed or changed. A caller passes
`NURT_ABI_VERSION` of its header to `nurt_abi_check` once after loading the
library; the call returns `NURT_OK` when the major versions are equal and the
minor version of the library is not lower, otherwise `NURT_E_ABI`.

## Conventions

- Strings passed to the library are UTF-8 and terminated by `\0`.
- Complex values are JSON documents: request envelopes `nurt-request/1`,
  responses `nurt-response/1`, syntax trees `nurt-ast/1`, configuration
  `nurt-config/1`, errors and events.
- Handles (`nurt_engine`, `nurt_exec`) are opaque.
- Every function is thread-safe unless its description says otherwise.
- After `fork()` without `exec()`, an engine opened in the parent process is
  not usable in the child; its functions return `NURT_E_INTERNAL`.

## Status codes

| Code | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `NURT_OK` | 0 | The call succeeded. A language error, if any, is in the JSON result. |
| `NURT_E_TIMEOUT` | 1 | `nurt_exec_wait`: the execution is still running after the timeout. |
| `NURT_E_CANCELLED` | 2 | `nurt_exec_wait`: the execution ended because it was cancelled. |
| `NURT_E_ARG` | 3 | A null pointer where a value is required, text that is not UTF-8, or JSON that is not valid for the argument. |
| `NURT_E_ABI` | 4 | Incompatible interface version (`nurt_abi_check`, `nurt_ext_load`). |
| `NURT_E_IO` | 5 | A configuration file, the journal, the state directory or an extension cannot be opened or read. |
| `NURT_E_INTERNAL` | 6 | Internal failure, including a panic caught at the boundary. |

Errors of the language (syntax, binding, assertions, stale targets, journal
errors) are not call failures. The call returns `NURT_OK` and the response
carries `report.error` with a stable `E_*` code. A request envelope that is
not JSON or does not match the schema `nurt-request/1` is `NURT_E_ARG`; an
envelope that matches the schema but breaks a rule of the envelope (no input,
two inputs, `variant` without `program`, a `limit` out of range) returns
`NURT_OK` and a response with the language error `E_ARG`; a relative path
option (`base`, `save_to`) gives `E_PATH_RELATIVE`.

### Language errors in other results

| Result | Form of a language error |
|---|---|
| Response (`nurt_run_json`, `nurt_exec_wait`, `nurt_page`) | `report.error` of the response. |
| One JSON document (`nurt_correct`, `nurt_catalog`, `nurt_history`, `nurt_space`) | The document is `{"error": {...}}`. |
| Two JSON documents (`nurt_parse`, `nurt_check`) | The first document is `null`; the diagnostics are `{"diagnostics": [], "error": {...}}`. |
| Text (`nurt_print`, `nurt_describe`, `nurt_help`) and no result (`nurt_session_end`, `nurt_ext_load`) | The call fails with the status of the error code when the function may return it (`E_ARG`, `E_UNSUPPORTED`, `E_UNKNOWN_NAME`: `NURT_E_ARG`; `E_IO`: `NURT_E_IO` for `nurt_session_end` and `nurt_ext_load`), otherwise with `NURT_E_INTERNAL`. `nurt_last_error` holds the error object under `detail.error`. |

The error object has the members of the error of the effect report
(`spec/schemas/nurt-report-1.schema.json`): `code`, `message`, `at` (the position, with
`stage`, `line`, `column` and `length`), `found`, `fix`, `help`, `details`. The execution
stage is `at.stage`.

A caller treats any unknown non-zero status as a failure; a later minor
version may add codes.

### Status codes of each function

| Function | OK | TIMEOUT | CANCELLED | ARG | ABI | IO | INTERNAL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nurt_abi_check` | x | | | | x | | |
| `nurt_info` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_engine_open` | x | | | x | | x | x |
| `nurt_engine_config_get` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_parse` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_print` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_correct` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_check` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_run_json` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_exec_start` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_exec_wait` | x | x | x | x | | | x |
| `nurt_exec_cancel` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_page` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_catalog` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_describe` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_help` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_schema` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_history` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_space` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_session_end` | x | | | x | | x | x |
| `nurt_ext_load` | x | | | x | x | x | x |
| `nurt_ext_list` | x | | | x | | | x |
| `nurt_last_error` | x | | | x | | | |

`nurt_abi_version`, `nurt_version`, `nurt_engine_close`, `nurt_exec_free`,
`nurt_buf_free` and `nurt_set_log_callback` do not return a status. The table
is verified by the interface tests in C, Python, Node and Rust, which produce
every marked status.

## Last error

`nurt_last_error(e, out_json)` returns the last failure of the calling thread:

```json
{"status": 3, "code": "NURT_E_ARG", "message": "`program` must not be null", "detail": {"function": "nurt_parse", "argument": "program"}}
```

| Member | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | integer | Value of the status code. |
| `code` | string | Name of the status code. |
| `message` | string | What failed and how to correct it. |
| `detail` | object | `function`: the exported function that failed; further members depend on the failure (`argument`, `path`, `expected`, `error`). |

The record is kept per thread, like `errno`, and is replaced only by the next
failing call of the same thread; `NURT_OK`, `NURT_E_TIMEOUT` and
`NURT_E_CANCELLED` leave it unchanged. `e` may be null, for example after a
failed `nurt_engine_open`. Without a recorded failure the buffer is empty.

## Memory

| Rule | Description |
|---|---|
| Ownership | Memory returned by the library is held in a `nurt_buf` and released with `nurt_buf_free`. The string returned by `nurt_version` is static. |
| Empty buffer | `ptr` is `NULL` exactly when `len` is 0. |
| Terminator | A `\0` byte follows the last byte and is not counted in `len`; `ptr` can be used as a C string. |
| `cap` | Belongs to the library; callers do not read it. |
| Output buffers | An output buffer is overwritten without being released: pass a buffer initialised to zero or already released. |
| Failure | When a call returns a status other than `NURT_OK`, its output buffers are empty. The response of `nurt_exec_wait` with `NURT_E_CANCELLED` is the only exception. |
| Release | `nurt_buf_free` sets the buffer to zero; it accepts `NULL` and zero buffers, so releasing twice is safe. |
| Handles | An engine is released with `nurt_engine_close`, an execution with `nurt_exec_free`; both accept `NULL`. An execution keeps the engine data it needs, so it may be released after its engine. |

## Engine

`nurt_engine_open` opens the engine with the clock and the host of the
process. The configuration is assembled from the built-in defaults, the
system and user files, the project file, the file named by `NURT_CONFIG`,
the `NURT_*` variables and run-time settings; `config_json` is applied at the
level of the `NURT_CONFIG` file, after that file. The state directory is
`state.dir` or the directory of the platform.

| Failure | Status |
|---|---|
| `config_json` is not JSON or not an object `nurt-config/1` | `NURT_E_ARG` |
| A value does not match its key, for example a relative `state.dir` | `NURT_E_ARG`; `detail.error.code` is `E_CONFIG` or `E_PATH_RELATIVE` |
| A configuration file or the state directory cannot be read or created | `NURT_E_IO` |

| Function | Result |
|---|---|
| `nurt_engine_config_get` | The effective configuration `nurt-config/1`. |
| `nurt_parse` | The syntax tree and `{"diagnostics": []}`. |
| `nurt_correct` | `{"program": text, "ast": tree, "corrections": [...]}`; `program` is the corrected text, or the given text when nothing was corrected. |
| `nurt_check` | The check document `nurt-check/1` (`format`, `effect`, `reversibility`, `operations`, `waits`, `paths`, `network`, `programs`, `groups`, `corrections`, `details`) with the member `bound` holding the bound tree, and `{"diagnostics": []}`. |
| `nurt_page` | The response of the page; `limit` 0 keeps the limit of the original request. |
| `nurt_describe` | Text of the subject `name`, else `layer`, else `core`, in `language` or the configured language. Members other than `layer`, `name` and `language` are `NURT_E_ARG`. |
| `nurt_help` | Text of the topic; `NULL` asks for the index of topics (the empty topic). |
| `nurt_history` | `{"operations": [...]}`; `query_json` holds the parameters of the command `history` (`id`, `limit`, `state`, `before`, `since`, `path`, `deleted_only`); an unknown member is `NURT_E_ARG`. |
| `nurt_space` | `{"volumes": [...]}`; a relative `volume` is the language error `E_PATH_RELATIVE`. |
| `nurt_session_end` | Removes the run-time settings of the session. An identifier that is empty, longer than the limit or with control characters is `NURT_E_ARG`. |
| `nurt_ext_list` | `{"extensions": [...]}`. |
| `nurt_ext_load` | `E_UNSUPPORTED` (`NURT_E_ARG`) when the library has no extension host. |
| `nurt_catalog` | The command catalog, or `{"error": ...}` with `E_UNSUPPORTED` while the engine has no catalog. `what_json` is `null`, `{"group": name}` for the commands of a group or `{"command": name}` for the specification of a command; another member is `NURT_E_ARG`, an unknown name is `{"error": ...}`. |

## Information

`nurt_info` needs no engine and returns:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `version` | Version of the library. |
| `abi` | `major`, `minor` and `version` of the interface. |
| `formats` | Versions of the formats `ast`, `bound`, `report`, `request`, `response`. |
| `schemas` | Names accepted by `nurt_schema`. |
| `catalog_rev` | Revision of the command catalog built into the library: `sha256:` and the digest of its canonical JSON; `null` when the catalog cannot be loaded. |
| `features` | Cargo features compiled into the library, for example `stub`. |
| `target` | `arch`, `os`, `family`, `pointer_width`, `endian`. |
| `build` | `profile`: `debug` or `release`. |

## Panics

Every exported function runs inside a panic boundary. A panic is caught,
reported as `NURT_E_INTERNAL` with the panic message in the last error, and
sent to the log receiver at level `NURT_LOG_ERROR`. The engine stays usable.
The boundary relies on unwinding: the library is built with
`panic = "unwind"`.

## Threads

| Item | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Engine | One engine may be used from several threads at once. Several engines may exist in one process. |
| Synchronous calls | `nurt_run_json` and the other functions with a result run on the calling thread. |
| Execution | `nurt_exec_start` runs the request on a thread of the engine and returns at once. |
| Events | Each execution has one delivery thread. The event callback is called from that thread only, one event at a time. Events are buffered, so a slow callback does not slow the execution. |
| Log receiver | `nurt_set_log_callback` sets one receiver for the whole process; it may be called from any thread. Passing `NULL` stops logging. |
| Last error | Kept per thread. |

### Events of an execution

Each event is one JSON object passed to the callback as `event_json`, valid
only during the call:

```json
{"seq": 1, "time": "2026-11-21T09:12:00Z", "request": "r1", "t": "exec.started"}
{"seq": 2, "time": "2026-11-21T09:12:00Z", "request": "r1", "t": "progress", "command": "find", "phase": "scan", "done": 64, "total": 148, "bytes": null, "message": null}
{"seq": 3, "time": "2026-11-21T09:12:00Z", "request": "r1", "t": "exec.finished", "status": "ok", "error": null}
```

The members are those of `spec/schemas/nurt-event-1.schema.json`, the same document that
`nurt serve` sends in the notifications `nurt/event`.

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seq` | Sequence number, from 1, increasing by 1 within the execution. |
| `time` | Time of the event as text, RFC 3339 in UTC. |
| `request` | Identifier of the request as text, the same for every event of the execution; `null` when the request has none. |
| `t` | Event type: `exec.started`, `progress`, `job.started`, `job.output`, `job.progress`, `job.finished`, `log`, `exec.finished`. |
| `id` | `job.*` events only: the identifier of the background job. |
| `status` | `exec.finished` only: the status of the report (`ok`, `failed` and the other values of `report.status`). An execution that ends without a response has `failed`. |
| `error` | `exec.finished` only: the code of the error that ended the execution, or `null`. |

The first event is `exec.started` and the last is `exec.finished`. No callback
follows `exec.finished`, and none follows `nurt_exec_free`. The callback may
call other functions of the library; it does not call `nurt_exec_free` for its
own execution, `nurt_engine_close` for its engine, or `nurt_exec_wait` for its
own execution with a timeout other than 0.

## Waiting and cancellation

| Call | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `nurt_exec_wait(x, 0, out)` | Checks without waiting: `NURT_E_TIMEOUT` and an empty buffer while the execution runs. |
| `nurt_exec_wait(x, ms, out)` | Waits for no longer than `ms` milliseconds. |
| `nurt_exec_wait(x, NURT_WAIT_FOREVER, out)` | Waits without limit. |
| After completion | Every call returns the same status and the same response. |
| `nurt_exec_cancel(x)` | Requests cancellation and returns `NURT_OK`. Repeated calls have no further effect. |
| Cancellation of a running execution | The execution stops at the next cancellation point. `nurt_exec_wait` returns `NURT_E_CANCELLED` and a response with status `failed` and the error `E_CANCELLED`. Changes already committed stay in the journal and can be undone. |
| Cancellation after completion | Has no effect: the result stays `NURT_OK` or the failure status the execution ended with. |
| `nurt_exec_free(x)` | Cancels a running execution, waits for its threads and releases the handle. |
| `nurt_engine_close(e)` | Cancels the running executions of the engine and waits until they complete. |

An execution is complete once `exec.finished` has been delivered, so after
`nurt_exec_wait` returns a result no event callback runs for the execution.
`nurt_exec_wait` returns `NURT_E_CANCELLED` exactly when the response reports
`E_CANCELLED`; an execution that ended before the cancellation point keeps its
response and `NURT_OK`.

## Test engine

With the cargo feature `stub` the engine is replaced by a test double that
answers from recorded cases; its events have the same members as the events
of the engine. The feature is never enabled in a release
build. Each case is a JSON file in the directory named by `NURT_STUB_DIR`
(by default `crates/nurt-ffi/tests/fixtures/stub`); a call is answered by
the case whose key equals the SHA-256 digest of the canonical JSON form
(RFC 8785) of `{"function": ..., "input": ...}`. `NURT_STUB_PANIC` holds a
comma-separated list of exported functions that panic inside their boundary,
for tests of `NURT_E_INTERNAL`.

## Examples

Running a request:

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include "nurt.h"

int main(void) {
    nurt_engine *engine = NULL;
    nurt_buf response = {0};
    if (nurt_abi_check(NURT_ABI_VERSION) != NURT_OK ||
        nurt_engine_open(NULL, &engine) != NURT_OK) {
        nurt_buf error = {0};
        nurt_last_error(NULL, &error);
        fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", error.ptr ? (const char *)error.ptr : "unknown failure");
        nurt_buf_free(&error);
        return 1;
    }
    if (nurt_run_json(engine, "{\"nurt\":\"1.0\",\"program\":\"find \\\"/srv/app\\\"\"}",
                      &response) == NURT_OK) {
        printf("%s\n", (const char *)response.ptr);
    }
    nurt_buf_free(&response);
    nurt_engine_close(engine);
    return 0;
}
```

Waiting for an execution with a deadline:

```c
nurt_exec *exec = NULL;
nurt_buf response = {0};
nurt_exec_start(engine, request_json, on_event, &state, &exec);
if (nurt_exec_wait(exec, 5000, &response) == NURT_E_TIMEOUT) {
    nurt_exec_cancel(exec);
    nurt_exec_wait(exec, NURT_WAIT_FOREVER, &response);
}
nurt_buf_free(&response);
nurt_exec_free(exec);
```

title: Extensions
text:
# Extensions

Extensions add commands, document formats and grammars to Danaco Nurt without
changing the program. An extension is a directory with a manifest
`nurt-ext.toml` and a WebAssembly component, or, when the configuration allows
it, a native library.

## Extension directory

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Configuration key | `ext.dir` (string, path) |
| Environment variable | `NURT_EXT_DIR` |
| Default | `ext` in the configuration directory |
| Relative value | resolved against the configuration directory |
| Layout | one subdirectory per extension, named after the extension |

The key `ext.native` (boolean, default `false`) allows native extension
libraries. Native libraries are available only in builds with the `native`
feature.

## Installation, removal and listing

| Operation | Behaviour | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| install | Reads and checks the manifest of a source directory, checks that every file it names exists, copies the directory to `<ext.dir>/<name>` through a staging directory and switches it in by rename. An installed version is replaced only on request. | `E_CATALOG` (rejected manifest), `E_NOT_FOUND` (manifest or named file missing), `E_EXISTS` (installed, replacement not requested), `E_UNSUPPORTED` (symbolic link or special file in the source, native extension not allowed), `E_INVALID_VALUE` (the source directory holds `<ext.dir>`), `E_IO` |
| remove | Deletes `<ext.dir>/<name>`, usable or not. | `E_INVALID_VALUE` (malformed name), `E_NOT_FOUND`, `E_IO` |
| list | Lists every subdirectory of `ext.dir` in name order with name, directory, version, API version, kind and full command names. An unusable extension is listed with the member `problem`. | `E_IO` |

An interrupted installation leaves the previous version in place. Directories
whose names start with `.` are staging areas and are not listed; every
installation uses a staging directory of its own, so installations of one
extension do not overwrite each other's copies.

### Trust

Installation does not verify a signature or a checksum of the source: the
account that installs an extension trusts its source directory. A WebAssembly
extension runs in a sandbox and reaches files only through the host calls
below, within `permissions.read` and `permissions.write`; the grants are
checked when the extension asks for a path and again when its writes are
applied. A native extension runs in the process of the engine without such
restrictions, which is why `ext.native` is off by default.

## Manifest

```toml
[ext]
name = "acme"
version = "1.2.0"
api = "nurt:ext@1.0"
kind = "wasm"
wasm = "acme.wasm"
description = "Checks of acme files"

[[stage]]
name = "lint"
summary = "Reports problems of acme files."
input = ["entry"]
output = ["finding"]

[[stage.param]]
name = "strict"
type = "bool"
summary = "Reports style problems too."

[[format]]
id = "acme-conf"
extensions = ["acmeconf"]

[[grammar]]
language = "acme"
extensions = ["acme"]
wasm = "grammar/acme.wasm"

[permissions]
read = ["${project}"]
write = []
network = []
```

Unknown keys are rejected.

### Section `[ext]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | Extension name and command prefix: lowercase ASCII letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter, at most 64 bytes. Must not be a group, command or command prefix of the core. |
| `version` | string | required | Version of the extension, Semantic Versioning 2.0.0. |
| `api` | string | required | Required interface version, `nurt:ext@MAJOR.MINOR`; a patch number is accepted and ignored. |
| `kind` | `"wasm"` \| `"native"` | required | Distribution form. |
| `wasm` | string | none | Component file; required for `kind = "wasm"`. |
| `library` | string | none | Library file; required for `kind = "native"`. |
| `description` | string | none | One-line description; the summary of the command group. |

File names are relative paths inside the extension directory; `..`, absolute
paths and root prefixes are rejected.

### Entries `[[stage]]`

Each entry declares the command `<ext.name>.<name>`.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | Command name without the prefix; same rules as `ext.name`. |
| `summary` | string | generated | One-line description. |
| `input` | array of strings | `[]` | Accepted record kinds; `any` accepts every kind. |
| `output` | array of strings | `[]` (any kind) | Produced record kinds. |
| `source` | boolean | `false` | The command can start a pipeline. A command with an empty `input` must be a source. |
| `writes` | boolean | `false` | The command changes files; requires a non-empty `permissions.write`. |
| `network` | boolean | `false` | The command contacts the network; requires a non-empty `permissions.network`. |
| `param` | array of tables | `[]` | Parameters, with the keys of a parameter of the command catalog. |

A command without `writes` is a read stage of category `transform` (or
`source` without input). A command with `writes` is a change stage with a
reversible local effect.

### Entries `[[format]]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required | Format identifier: lowercase ASCII letters, digits, `_` and `-`. |
| `extensions` | array of strings | `[]` | File name extensions without the leading period. |
| `editable` | boolean | `false` | Keys can be changed with the layout preserved. |

### Entries `[[grammar]]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `language` | string | required | Language identifier; same rules as `format.id`. |
| `extensions` | array of strings | `[]` | File name extensions without the leading period. |
| `wasm` | string | required | Grammar component file. |
| `tags` | string | none | Tag query file. |
| `locals` | string | none | Local scope query file. |

### Section `[permissions]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `read` | array of strings | `[]` | Directories the extension may read. |
| `write` | array of strings | `[]` | Directories the extension may change; also readable. |
| `network` | array of strings | `[]` | Hosts the extension may contact. |

A directory is absolute or starts with a placeholder:

| Placeholder | Value during an execution |
|---|---|
| `${project}` | Base directory of the request. |
| `${home}` | Home directory of the account. |
| `${temp}` | Temporary directory. |
| `${ext}` | Directory of the extension. |

An entry whose placeholder has no value grants nothing. A path is granted when
it lies below a granted directory both as written and with symbolic links
resolved. Paths with `..` components and relative paths are refused.

## Interface versions

The host implements `nurt:ext@1.0`. A manifest is accepted when its major
version equals the major version of the host and its minor version is not
newer. Any other version fails installation with `E_CATALOG` and the message
names both versions.

## WebAssembly interface

The component implements the world `extension` of the package
`nurt:ext@1.0.0`:

```wit
package nurt:ext@1.0.0;

interface host {
    record failure {
        code: string,
        message: string,
    }

    enum log-level {
        error,
        warn,
        info,
        debug,
        trace,
    }

    read-file: func(path: string) -> result<list<u8>, failure>;
    list-dir: func(path: string) -> result<list<string>, failure>;
    write-file: func(path: string, content: list<u8>) -> result<_, failure>;
    log: func(level: log-level, message: string);
}

interface stage {
    run: func(command: string, args: string, input: list<string>) -> result<list<string>, string>;
}

world extension {
    import host;
    export stage;
}
```

### Function `stage.run`

| Parameter | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | string | Full command name, `<extension>.<name>`. |
| `args` | string | JSON object from parameter name to value; parameters without a value are left out. Per-record expressions are evaluated once, without a record. |
| `input` | list of strings | Input records, one JSON document each. |

Result: the output records, one JSON document each, or a message describing
why the command failed.

A record has the JSON form `{"kind": "<record kind>", "fields": {...}}` with
field values in plain JSON (texts, numbers, booleans, lists and objects).
Members other than `kind` and `fields` are rejected.

### Host calls

| Call | Access | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `read-file` | below `permissions.read` or `permissions.write` | Whole file content, at most `limits.max_file_bytes_text` bytes. |
| `list-dir` | below `permissions.read` or `permissions.write` | Entry names in byte order. |
| `write-file` | below `permissions.write`, commands with `writes = true` | The write is recorded, not performed. The preview shows it as a change; the apply step writes it through the journal, so the change can be undone. The recorded writes of one call hold at most `limits.max_file_bytes_text` bytes together; a further write is refused with `E_LIMIT`. |
| `log` | always | Adds a `log` event with the command as source. |

A refused call returns `failure` with the code `E_PERMISSION`, `E_PATH_RELATIVE`,
`E_NOT_FOUND`, `E_LIMIT` or `E_IO`. When the command then fails, the error of
the command is the refused call.

### Limits

| Limit | Value | Error |
|---|---|---|
| Execution fuel per call | 10 000 000 000 units, about one per instruction | `E_LIMIT` |
| Linear memory per instance | 512 MiB | `E_STAGE_FAILED` |

Every call runs in a new instance; no state survives between calls.

## Native libraries

A native extension is a shared library exporting three C functions:

```c
uint32_t nurt_ext_api(void);
int32_t nurt_ext_run(const uint8_t *request, size_t request_len,
                     uint8_t **response, size_t *response_len);
void nurt_ext_free(uint8_t *response, size_t response_len);
```

| Function | Contract |
|---|---|
| `nurt_ext_api` | Returns the interface version as `MAJOR << 16 \| MINOR`. |
| `nurt_ext_run` | Receives the JSON object `{"command", "args", "input"}` and stores a response allocated by the library. Status 0 with `{"records": [...]}`; any other status with `{"error": "<message>"}`. |
| `nurt_ext_free` | Releases a response; called exactly once per response. |

Native code runs with the rights of the process, so the host cannot restrict
the paths it reaches. Native extensions load only with `ext.native = true` and
cannot declare commands with `writes = true`.

## Errors

| Code | Condition |
|---|---|
| `E_CATALOG` | Rejected manifest, interface version mismatch, core name, unusable component or library, missing export `nurt:ext/stage@1.0.0`, name taken in the registry. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | A host call reached a path outside the permissions. |
| `E_STAGE_FAILED` | The command returned a failure, trapped, returned an invalid record, or planned writes without `writes = true`. |
| `E_LIMIT` | The command used up its execution fuel. |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | Native extension not allowed or not built, or a native command declares `writes = true`. |
| `E_NOT_FOUND`, `E_EXISTS`, `E_IO` | Installation, removal and listing. |

## Examples

A read command of an extension in a pipeline:

```
find src -name '*.acme' |> acme.lint strict=true
```

Manifest of a command that changes files:

```toml
[ext]
name = "fmt"
version = "0.3.0"
api = "nurt:ext@1.0"
kind = "wasm"
wasm = "fmt.wasm"

[[stage]]
name = "apply"
input = ["entry"]
writes = true

[permissions]
write = ["${project}"]
```

title: Report output
text:
# Report output

The result of a program is the report `nurt-report/1`. The crate `nurt-report`
reduces the report to the requested level of detail and renders it in one of
four formats. The response envelope `nurt-response/1` carries the reduced
report and the rendered text.

## Call options

| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | `text`, `json`, `markdown`, `compact` | `text` | Format of the rendered result. |
| `verbosity` | `quiet`, `normal`, `detailed` | `normal` | Level of detail of the report. |
| `limit` | integer, 1 to 5000 | `50` | Number of changes or records per page. |
| `diff` | `none`, `stat`, `unified` | `unified` | Form of differences. |
| `diff_context` | integer | `3` | Context lines of a difference; fixed when the hunks are produced, not changed by the renderer. |
| `max_chars` | integer | `0` | Largest number of characters of one text field; `0` means no limit. |
| `fields` | list of names | all fields | Fields kept in the rows of a reading program. |
| `save_to` | absolute path | none | File that receives the full result; the report gives `result_file`. |

Configuration keys `report.diff_max_hunks` (default `20`) and
`report.diff_max_lines` (default `200`) bound the differences at verbosity
`normal`.

The terminal width and the colors apply to the format `text` of the command
line only. The text of a response contains no ANSI sequences and is not
shortened to a terminal width.

## Verbosity

| Level | Kept | Removed |
|---|---|---|
| `quiet` | status, `op`, targets, summary, `notable`, `irreversible`, `error`, `result_file`, records of a reading program | changes, differences, `bulk`, `timing` |
| `normal` | everything of `quiet`, changes up to `limit`, differences up to `report.diff_max_hunks` hunks and `report.diff_max_lines` lines, `bulk` | `timing` |
| `detailed` | everything of `normal`, all differences, `timing` | none |

The number of changes left out is written as a line `… N more changes`; the
header of the differences gives the total number of hunks. A diff mode other
than `unified` removes the differences; the numbers of added and removed lines
stay in the changes.

## Limits

- Changes beyond `limit` are counted, not listed. `targets.listed` is set to
  the number of listed changes.
- Rows of a reading program beyond `limit` are counted, not listed. The cursor
  of the next page is `next_cursor`, set by the engine. The field
  `continuation` (`id`, `unit`, `shown`, `remaining`, `cut_lines`) names the
  kept remainder and the text of the response ends with `more: next`; the
  command `next` reads the next part from it.
- Differences are limited as given under Verbosity.

## Field shortening

A text field longer than `max_chars` characters is cut at a character
boundary. The record that holds the field gets `truncated: true`. The rule
applies to the records `exec`, `job`, `test`, `analysis`, `git` and to the
header and rows of a reading program, including nested lists, maps and
records.

## Field selection

`fields` keeps only the named fields in each row of a reading program, in the
order of the option. Unknown names are ignored. The header record and the
other records of the report are not affected.

## Formats

### text

One block per part of the report, in a fixed order: corrections, `ran`,
header, targets, program or job block, records, changes, differences, bulk
summary, test, analysis and git records, `notable`, `irreversible`, error,
next cursor, result file, timing. Counts are grouped by a space every three
digits. Sizes use binary units (`b`, `kib`, `mib`, `gib`, `tib`).

```
op 18  replace  ok
targets 3 files · replacements 7 · lines +7 −7 · 41.2kib → 41.3kib
  /srv/app/src/a.go    3 repl  1.1kib → 1.1kib    1a2b3c4d → 9f8e7d6c
diff (3 hunks)
  /srv/app/src/a.go:12
    - func oldName(x int) {
    + func newName(x int) {
notable
  ! many_per_file  /srv/app/src/c/d.go  2  many replacements in one file
next cursor c_5d2e
```

A line of `notable` has the code, the target, the count and the detail of the
entry. An entry without a detail shows the standard message of its code.

A reading program writes the header `<kind>  matched N · shown N · next cursor
C` and a table of the rows. The table of the records `operation` (`history`),
`match` (`search`) and `response` (`http.request`) has the essential columns
only; verbosity `detailed` or the option `fields` shows the others, and the
JSON form always holds all fields. A failed program without an operation number
starts with the line `error <code>`. A report with status `ok` and an error
(failure after the effect) writes the effect first and the error block with
the line `effect applied` after it.

The line `result file <path>` appears when the result was written to a file.

The headings and labels of the formats `text`, `markdown` and `compact` are
keywords and stay English whatever the call parameter `language` is; `language`
changes the messages that the producer of the report puts into its data.

A control character in a line of a difference, such as the carriage return of
a file with CRLF line endings, is written as an escape sequence (`\r`) in the
formats `text` and `compact`; the tab stays as it is.

### json

The reduced report as one line of JSON that validates against
`nurt-report/1`. The order of fields is fixed. The response has no `rendered`
member for this format, because the report is the result.

### markdown

Headings, pipe tables and fenced blocks for differences and trees. The parts
are the same as in the format `text`. The result file is written as
``result file `<path>` ``.

### compact

One record per line, without headings. The first line is
`report kind=<kind> status=<status>` with `op` and `ran` when present. The
following lines start with the name of the part: `correction`, `targets`,
`summary`, a change line, `diff <path>:<line> <text>`, `bulk`, `notable`,
`irreversible`, `error`, `next cursor=<cursor>`, `result file=<path>`,
`timing`. A value is written as `key=value`; a value that is empty or contains
a space, a quote or `=` is written as a JSON string.

## Tree view

Rows of kind `entry` that all carry an integer `depth` are drawn as a tree in
the formats `text` and `markdown`. A row of depth 0 is a root. A row of depth
`d` is a child of the nearest preceding row of depth `d - 1`. The connectors
are `|-- `, `` `-- `` and `|   `. A directory is written with a trailing `/`,
a file with its size. A directory above a row that is not in the list, as
when `find` returns only the matches, is derived from the `path` of the row
and drawn at its depth; a value with a line break is written on one line with
the break as `\n`.

```
src/
|-- a.go  1.1kib
`-- b.go  8.0kib
```

The formats `json` and `compact` keep the flat list of rows with their
`depth`.

## Line breaks and control characters

A report is shown line by line, so a value that comes from outside the report
(a file name, a path, a cell of a record, a message) is written on one line in
the formats `text`, `markdown` and `compact`. A line feed is written as `\n`, a
carriage return as `\r`, a tab as `\t` and any other control character as a
Rust escape such as `\u{1}`. A backslash is not doubled, so a name with the two
characters `\n` and a name with a line feed look alike; the format `json` tells
them apart.

| Place | Rule |
|---|---|
| table cell of the format `text` | escaped as above |
| tree view | the label of a row is escaped; a directory derived from a `path` is escaped the same way |
| table cell of the format `markdown` | escaped as above, then `\|` for a pipe |
| inline code and list item of the format `markdown` | escaped as above; the code delimiter is longer than every run of backticks in the text |
| value of the format `compact` | a value with a space, a control character, a quote or `=` is written as a JSON string |
| path of a `diff` line of the format `compact` | escaped as above |

The text of a file shown by `read` is one value like any other: in a table it
is written on one line with `\n` for each line break, and the format `json`
keeps the lines.

## Paths that are not valid Unicode

A path or a name with bytes that are not valid Unicode (on Linux, for example,
the byte `0xFF`) is shown in every format with the invalid bytes replaced by
U+FFFD. The format `json` adds the raw form next to the display form: a field
`raw_<field>` of type `bytes` (standard base64) that holds the native bytes of
the path, for example `raw_path` next to `path` in a `change`, a `hunk`, an
`entry`, a `match` and an entry of `notable` or `irreversible`, `raw_directory`
in the directories of a bulk summary and `raw_sample_head` and
`raw_sample_tail` in its sample. The raw field is absent when the path is
valid Unicode. The raw form is also what the commands read from the records
they receive, so `find ... |> remove` acts on the entry that `find` listed. The
journal keeps the raw form of every target, so `undo` restores the entry under
its name. In the formats `text`, `markdown` and `compact` a record shows the
raw field as the number of its bytes, `<N bytes>`.

## Response envelope

| Member | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `nurt` | string | `nurt-response/1` |
| `report` | object | the report after reduction |
| `rendered` | object | `format` and `text` of the rendered report; absent for the format `json` |

`report.next_cursor` is the cursor of the next page.

## Errors

The error of a report is written with the fields `code`, `at`, `fix`, `help`,
`expected`, `actual`, `sample`, `candidates`, `next_steps` and `cause`. Every
code of the error enumeration produces a report that validates against
`nurt-report/1` and renders in all four formats.

title: nurt serve` protocol reference (`nurt-rpc/1`)
text:
# `nurt serve` protocol reference (`nurt-rpc/1`)

`nurt serve` runs the engine behind a JSON-RPC 2.0 server on standard input
and standard output. Embedding applications that cannot load the C library
(`docs/reference/c-abi.md`) use this protocol; both interfaces return the same
JSON documents and map failures to the same status codes.

## Synopsis

```
nurt serve [--framing ndjson|content-length]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--framing` | `ndjson` \| `content-length` | `ndjson` | Delimiting of messages on both streams. |

Standard output carries protocol messages only. Diagnostics of the process
go to standard error or, after `initialize` with events enabled, to `log`
events.

## Framing

| Framing | Form of one message |
|---|---|
| `ndjson` | One JSON document per line, UTF-8, terminated by `\n`. A `\r` before the `\n` and empty lines are ignored. The server never writes a line feed inside a message. |
| `content-length` | Header lines terminated by `\r\n`, an empty line, then exactly `Content-Length` bytes of JSON. Other headers are ignored. The server writes only the `Content-Length` header. |

A received message longer than the size limit (16 MiB unless the server was
configured otherwise; reported in `initialize` as `limits.max_message_bytes`)
is skipped and answered with `-32600` and `id: null`. A broken header block of
the `content-length` framing is answered with `-32700` and ends the
connection with exit code 1.

## Messages

Every message is a JSON-RPC 2.0 object with `"jsonrpc": "2.0"`.

| Message | Members | Server behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Request | `id` (string, number or `null`), `method`, `params` (object, array or absent) | Answered with exactly one reply carrying the same `id`. |
| Notification | `method`, `params`, no `id` | Executed; never answered, also on error. |
| Reply sent by the client | `id`, `result` or `error` | Ignored. The server sends no requests. |
| Batch (array) | | Rejected with `-32600`; send one request per message. |

## Connection lifecycle

1. The client sends `initialize`. Before it, every method except
   `initialize` and `shutdown` is answered with `-32600`.
2. The client sends requests. Several requests may be in flight; replies
   arrive in the order the requests complete and are matched by `id`.
3. The client sends `shutdown`, or closes the input. The server stops
   reading, waits until every request in flight has been answered, answers
   `shutdown` with `null` and exits. Messages after `shutdown` are not read.

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | `shutdown` was received or the input ended. |
| `1` | The input could not be read, the framing was broken, or the output could not be written. |

When a write to the output fails, the server cancels the requests in flight and
reads no further message: it exits with code 1 before the next read, or, when a
read is already waiting, as soon as that read returns; the message it returned
is not processed. The server never waits for the end of the input.

## Methods

| Method | Parameters | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `initialize` | see [`initialize`](#initialize) | see [`initialize`](#initialize) |
| `run` | request envelope `nurt-request/1` | response `nurt-response/1`; a request whose only fault is an `ast` that is not a tree `nurt-ast/1` is answered with the language error `E_AST_SCHEMA` (report status `failed`), not with `-32602` |
| `check` | request envelope `nurt-request/1` | check document `nurt-check/1` with the members `bound` (the bound tree), `ast_hash` (hash of the bound tree in `bound`, as in `spec/syntax-tree.md` section 6, `sha256:<hex>`; absent only when the tree is not known, never for a program given as text) and `diagnostics` |
| `parse` | `{program: string, variant?: "a" \| "b" \| "c"}` | `{ast: nurt-ast/1, diagnostics: []}` |
| `print` | `{ast: nurt-ast/1, variant?: "a" \| "b" \| "c"}` | `{text: string}` |
| `correct` | `{program: string, variant?: "a" \| "b" \| "c"}` | `{ast: nurt-ast/1, corrections?: [...], ran?: string}`; `ran` is the corrected program text when the engine corrected it |
| `page` | `{cursor: string, limit?: integer}` | response `nurt-response/1` with the next page |
| `describe` | `{subject?: string, language?: string}` | `{description: {text: string, tokens: integer, estimate: boolean}}`; the description of the subject is the field `text` |
| `help` | `{topic?: string, language?: string}` | `{text: string}` |
| `schema` | `{name: string}` | the published JSON Schema `name` |
| `catalog` | `{what?: object \| null}` or absent | command catalog `nurt-catalog-result/1` |
| `history` | `{query?: object \| string \| null}` or absent | `{operations: [...]}` |
| `space` | `{volume?: absolute path}` | `{volumes: [...]}` |
| `info` | absent | engine description: version, formats, features, system |
| `cancel` | `{request_id}` or `{job_id}` | `{cancelled: boolean}` |
| `shutdown` | absent | `null` |

`variant` defaults to the variant of the configuration; `subject` and
`topic` default to `core`. `schema` accepts `ast`, `bound`, `report`, `request`,
`response`, `config`, `catalog`, `catalog-result`, `value`, `tool`,
`fs-snapshot`, `check`, `rpc` and `event`. `what` selects
`{"group": name}` (the commands of a group) or `{"command": name}` (the
specification of a command); `null` or absent returns the groups. `query`
is the query of `history` as an object or as the text of an object; an
object without `query` is itself the query. A selection or a query of another
shape is the JSON-RPC error `-32602`. A language error of any
method is part of the result, not a JSON-RPC error: the result is then a
response `nurt-response/1` whose report has the status `failed`, the error in
`report.error` and, as `report.kind`, the name of the method (for `run`, the
kind of the program).

### `initialize`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `protocol` | string | yes | `nurt-rpc/<major>[.<minor>]`; the major version must be `1`. |
| `client` | object `{name, version}` | no | Name and version of the client; informational. |
| `abi` | integer | no | Expected C interface version `(major << 16) \| minor`; compared by major version when the server embeds the C interface. |
| `language` | string | no | Expected language version; informational. |
| `ast` | string | no | Expected version of `nurt-ast/1`; the major version must match. |
| `session` | string | no | Session used by `run`, `check` and `page` requests whose `options.session` is absent. |
| `config_overrides` | object | no | Must be absent or empty; the configuration is fixed when the server starts. |
| `capabilities.events` | boolean | no, `false` | Send `nurt/event` notifications for executions. |

Unknown members are ignored.

| Result member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `protocol` | string | `nurt-rpc/1`. |
| `version` | string | Version of Danaco Nurt. |
| `abi` | integer \| `null` | Version of the embedded C interface; `null` when the server does not embed it. |
| `language` | `null` | The engine does not report a language version. |
| `ast` | string | Version of `nurt-ast/1`. |
| `report` | string | Version of `nurt-report/1`. |
| `catalog_rev` | `null` | The engine does not report a catalog revision. |
| `features` | array of string | Features of the build, for example `stub`. |
| `groups` | array of string | Command groups whose services the engine provides. |
| `limits.max_inflight` | integer | Requests executed at the same time (default 16). |
| `limits.max_message_bytes` | integer | Size limit of one received message (default 16777216). |

Errors: `-32602` for invalid parameters or non-empty `config_overrides`,
`-32004` (`NURT_E_ABI`) for another major version of `protocol`, `abi` or
`ast` (`data.supported` names the supported version), `-32600` when the
connection is already initialized.

### `cancel`

Exactly one of the members is given.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `request_id` | string \| number | `id` of a request in flight on this connection. The comparison keeps the JSON type: `1` and `"1"` differ. |
| `job_id` | string | Identifier of a background job. Not available in this server: the result is a `failed` response with `E_UNSUPPORTED`. |

`cancelled` is `true` when the request was in flight. Cancelling is
idempotent; a finished or unknown request gives `false` and no error. A
cancelled `run` is answered with `-32002` (`NURT_E_CANCELLED`) whose
`data.response` is the `failed` response with `E_CANCELLED`, and its last
event is `exec.finished` with `error: "E_CANCELLED"`. Methods other than `run`
complete normally.

## Errors

The `error` object of a reply is used only for errors of the protocol and of
the call. Language errors are part of the result.

| Code | Name | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `-32700` | Parse error | The message is not JSON, or the framing is broken. |
| `-32600` | Invalid request | The message is not a request object; a batch; the message is too long; the connection is not initialized or already initialized; the limit of requests in flight is reached; a request with the same `id` is in flight. |
| `-32601` | Method not found | The method is unknown; the message lists the known methods. |
| `-32602` | Invalid params | The parameters do not match the method. |
| `-32603` | Internal error | The server failed to serialise a result. |
| `-32000 - s` | Application error | Status `s` of the C interface; `data.status` names it. |

| Code | `nurt_status` | Cause in the server |
|---|---|---|
| `-32001` | `NURT_E_TIMEOUT` | Not used by the server. |
| `-32002` | `NURT_E_CANCELLED` | A `run` was cancelled; `data.response` holds the response. |
| `-32003` | `NURT_E_ARG` | A recorded stub case fails with this status. |
| `-32004` | `NURT_E_ABI` | Version mismatch in `initialize`. |
| `-32005` | `NURT_E_IO` | A recorded stub case fails with this status. |
| `-32006` | `NURT_E_INTERNAL` | The execution of a request panicked (`data.panic`), or no stub case answers the call. |

## Concurrency

Each request runs on its own thread; `initialize`, `cancel` and `shutdown`
are answered by the reading thread, so a cancellation is never queued behind
the request it cancels. At most `limits.max_inflight` requests and
notifications run at the same time; a request above the limit is answered
with `-32600`. An `id` may be reused once the reply to the previous request
with that `id` was sent.

## Events

After `initialize` with `capabilities.events = true`, each execution of `run`
sends notifications with the method `nurt/event`. The parameters are the
delivered event of the contract:

| Member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `seq` | integer | Number of the event within the execution, from 1. |
| `time` | string | Time of emission, RFC 3339 UTC. |
| `request` | string \| `null` | `id` of the request as text; `null` for a notification. |
| `t` | string | Event type. |

| `t` | Further members |
|---|---|
| `exec.started` | `ast_hash`, `effect` (`effect` is absent when the engine does not report it) |
| `progress` | `command`, `phase`, `done`, `total`, `bytes`, `message` |
| `job.started` | `id`, `label`, `command`, `cwd`, `pid`, `started` |
| `job.output` | `id`, `stream`, `cursor`, `lines`, `bytes` |
| `job.progress` | `id`, `percent`, `line` |
| `job.finished` | `id`, `state`, `exit_code`, `signal`, `elapsed`, `output_file`, `changes` |
| `log` | `level`, `message`, `source` |
| `exec.finished` | `status`, `error` (the code of the error of the report, `null` when the report has none; also for a program that failed before it was planned, for example `E_SYNTAX`) |

The events of one execution are sent in the order of `seq`; `exec.started`
is the first and `exec.finished` the last, and all of them precede the reply
to the request.

## Stub mode

A build with the feature `stub` can answer from the recorded cases of the
C library stub (`crates/nurt-ffi/tests/fixtures/stub/`) instead of an engine,
for tests of bindings before an engine is available. A call is answered by
the case whose key, the SHA-256 digest of the canonical JSON of
`{"function", "input"}`, equals the key of the call; the input of a call is
built as in the C interface. `initialize` and `info` report the feature
`stub`. A call without a case is answered with `-32006` and `data.key`.

## Examples

Newline-delimited session (`>` sent by the client, `<` sent by the server):

```
> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocol":"nurt-rpc/1","capabilities":{"events":true}}}
< {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocol":"nurt-rpc/1","version":"0.1.2","abi":null,"language":null,"ast":"1.1","report":"1.0","catalog_rev":null,"features":[],"groups":[],"limits":{"max_inflight":16,"max_message_bytes":16777216}}}
> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"run","params":{"nurt":"1.0","program":"find \"/srv/app\" glob: \"*.go\""}}
< {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"nurt/event","params":{"seq":1,"time":"2026-11-21T09:12:00Z","request":"2","t":"exec.started"}}
< {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"nurt/event","params":{"seq":2,"time":"2026-11-21T09:12:00Z","request":"2","t":"exec.finished","status":"ok","error":null}}
< {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"nurt":"1.0","report":{"nurt":"1.0","status":"ok","kind":"find"}}}
> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"shutdown"}
< {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"result":null}
```

Cancelling a request in flight:

```
> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"scan","method":"run","params":{"nurt":"1.0","program":"find \"/srv/archive\""}}
> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"cancel","params":{"request_id":"scan"}}
< {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"result":{"cancelled":true}}
< {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"scan","error":{"code":-32002,"message":"the request was cancelled","data":{"status":"NURT_E_CANCELLED","response":{"nurt":"1.0","report":{"nurt":"1.0","status":"failed","kind":"find","error":{"code":"E_CANCELLED","message":"the execution was cancelled"}}}}}}
```

The same request with the `content-length` framing:

```
Content-Length: 44\r\n
\r\n
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"shutdown"}
```

title: Integrator guide
text:
# Integrator guide

Reference for hosts that give an AI agent the `nurt` tool: agent runtimes, SDK integrations, editors and services that run Danaco Nurt on behalf of a model.

| Page | Content |
|---|---|
| [Interfaces](#interfaces) | `nurt serve`, the C ABI and the MCP server |
| [Tool definition](tool-definition.md) | `nurt schema tool`, formats, rules per platform, command groups loaded on demand |
| [Tool calls](tool-calls.md) | arguments and requests, corrections and `accept`, pages and cursors |
| [Policy](policy.md) | host policy with `check` and `preview`: forbidden commands, allowed directories, HTTP targets |
| [Remote instances and events](remote-and-events.md) | sending syntax trees to another device, events of background jobs |
| [Versions and compatibility](versioning.md) | format versions, protocol negotiation, compatibility rules |

Examples for model SDKs and agent frameworks: `integrations/examples/`.

## Interfaces

| Interface | Transport | Use | Events | Isolation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nurt serve --stdio` | JSON-RPC 2.0 (`nurt-rpc/1`) over standard input and output of a child process | agent runtimes and services; one process per session or workspace | notifications `nurt/event` in the same stream | separate process; a crash of the console does not stop the host |
| `nurt serve --socket <path>` | as above, over a Unix domain socket or a named pipe | a console shared by several host processes | as above | as above; reported as unavailable by builds that do not link the transport |
