| `libnurt` (`nurt.h`) | C ABI in the host process | short calls without effects: `nurt_check`, `nurt_describe`, `nurt_correct`; hosts without child processes | callback `nurt_event_cb` | none; a fault in the library stops the host |
| `nurt mcp --stdio` | Model Context Protocol over standard input and output | MCP clients: desktop and editor assistants, frameworks with MCP support | MCP notifications | separate process |
| `nurt mcp --http <address>` | Model Context Protocol, streamable HTTP | a server shared over the network | MCP notifications | separate process |

The `nurt mcp` subcommand is present in builds that link the feature `mcp`; a build without it reports the subcommand as unavailable. `nurt serve` is present in every build. Framing, methods, lifecycle, events and error codes of `nurt serve` are defined in [`docs/reference/serve-protocol.md`](../reference/serve-protocol.md); this guide does not repeat them.

Selection:

1. A host that runs its own agent loop uses `nurt serve --stdio`. It supervises the child process: it restarts the process after an exit and fails the requests in progress with a call error. The journal is on disk, so a restarted console recovers completed operations.
2. A host that only analyses programs (policy, highlighting, correction) can call `libnurt` in process.
3. A host that already speaks MCP starts `nurt mcp`; no code is needed.

The language bindings (`bindings/`) wrap `nurt serve` and `libnurt` with the same API in Python, TypeScript, Go, Java and .NET.

Every interface accepts the request envelope `nurt-request/1` and returns the response `nurt-response/1` with the effect report `nurt-report/1`. Errors of the language (an unknown command, a failed assertion) are part of the report; call errors (malformed JSON, an unknown method, a stopped process) are errors of the interface.

## Calls to `nurt serve`

A request is a JSON-RPC 2.0 message of `nurt-rpc/1`; `check` takes the same parameters as `run`. Methods, parameters and results are listed in the [protocol reference](../reference/serve-protocol.md):


```json
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "check", "params": {"nurt": "1.0", "program": "list \"/home/user/app\""}}
```

A call error replaces the result with the `error` object; the codes and their mapping to the statuses of the C ABI (`-32000` minus the status) are defined in the protocol reference:


```json
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "error": {"code": -32002, "message": "the call was cancelled", "data": {"status": "NURT_E_CANCELLED"}}}
```

title: Policy
text:
# Policy

The console runs the programs it receives; it does not decide which programs an agent may run. The host enforces its policy before `run`, on data that the console computes without any effect:

| Call | Effect | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `check` (`nurt serve`), `nurt_check` (C ABI) | none; parse, correction, binding and plan | the strongest effect, the weakest reversibility, the paths named by the program, the network targets, the programs to run, the command groups, the corrections |
| `run` with `preview: true` | none; stages up to the plan of the effect | the targets the program would change, with differences, `notable` and `irreversible` effects known in advance |

The answer of `check` is the document `nurt-check/1`:

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `format` | `nurt-check/1` |
| `effect` | strongest effect of the plan: `read`, `local` (changes local files), `external` (acts outside the local file system, for example `git.push` or a `POST` request) or `process` (starts programs) |
| `reversibility` | weakest reversibility: `read`, `reversible`, `reversible_if_preserved` or `irreversible` |
| `operations` | number of operations; more than one for a script |
| `waits` | `true` when a stage blocks the call by waiting |
| `paths` | paths named by literals of the program, in order of appearance |
| `network` | one entry per endpoint: `command`, `param`, `source` (`literal`, `record`, `remote`, `catalog`, `implementation`), `target` (`scheme`, `host`, `port`, `url`; `null` when unknown before the run) and `remote` |
| `programs` | one entry per external program: `command`, `program`, `implementation`, `launcher`, `source` |
| `groups` | command groups the plan uses, in order of first use |
| `corrections` | corrections applied to the program text before binding: `id`, `rule`, `class`, `at`, `from`, `to`, `kind`, `alternatives` |
| `details` | facts reported by the static check of the commands of the program: `command`, `index`, `details` |

The method `check` of `nurt serve` returns this document with the member `diagnostics` (the diagnostics of parsing and binding); both parts are required in the result. `nurt_check` of the C ABI returns the document `nurt-check/1`.

The examples use the Python binding, where `CheckResult.raw` holds the document.

Policy decisions are made on the corrected and bound program and on the actual targets, never on the program text.

An example of the document for a program that pushes a branch:


```json
{
  "format": "nurt-check/1",
  "effect": "external",
  "reversibility": "irreversible",
  "operations": 1,
  "waits": false,
  "paths": ["/home/user/app"],
  "network": [
    {"command": "git.push", "param": null, "source": "remote", "target": null, "remote": "origin"}
  ],
  "programs": [],
  "groups": ["git"],
  "corrections": [],
  "details": []
}
```

The reply of `nurt serve` to `check` for the program above:


```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "result": {
    "format": "nurt-check/1",
    "effect": "external",
    "reversibility": "irreversible",
    "operations": 1,
    "waits": false,
    "paths": ["/home/user/app"],
    "network": [
      {"command": "git.push", "param": null, "source": "remote", "target": null, "remote": "origin"}
    ],
    "programs": [],
    "groups": ["git"],
    "corrections": [],
    "details": [],
    "diagnostics": []
  }
}
```

## Forbidding a command: `git.push`

```python
check = nurt.check(program)
commands = {use["command"] for use in check.raw["network"]}
commands |= {facts["command"] for facts in check.raw["details"]}
if "git.push" in commands:
    return tool_error("git.push is not allowed in this session")
response = nurt.run(program)
```

`check` runs after correction and binding and names every command with its full name, so an alias, a different notation or a corrected spelling of a command that only reads is caught. A misspelt name of a command that changes something is not corrected: `check` answers `E_AMBIGUOUS` and the first candidate is the program with the name written right, so a forbidden command cannot be reached by a typing error either. A host that allows no effect outside the local file system compares `effect` with `external` instead.

## Allowed directories

```python
ALLOWED = ("/home/user/app/",)

check = nurt.check(program, base="/home/user/app")
outside = [path for path in check.raw["paths"] if not path.startswith(ALLOWED)]
if outside:
    return tool_error(f"paths outside the workspace: {outside}")
preview = nurt.run(program, base="/home/user/app", preview=True)
targets = [change["path"] for change in preview.report.get("changes", [])]
if any(not path.startswith(ALLOWED) for path in targets):
    return tool_error("the program changes files outside the workspace")
```

`check` lists the paths written in the program; `preview` lists the files that the program would change (`report.changes`) after glob expansion and filtering. Both are needed: a pattern inside an allowed directory can still reach a symbolic link that leads outside.

## Network targets of `http.*`

For the commands that use the network, `check` returns every endpoint the program contacts: the command, the origin of the target and, when it is known before the run, the scheme, host, port and URL. A host that allows access to one service:

```python
check = nurt.check(program)
for use in check.raw["network"]:
    target = use["target"]
    if target is None or target["host"] != "api.example.com" or target["scheme"] != "https":
        return tool_error(f"network target not allowed: {use['command']}")
```

Targets computed at run time (a URL read from a file) have `source: "record"` and `target: null`; a strict policy rejects such programs or runs them with `preview: true` first. A host that must allow reads only compares `effect` of the document with `read`.

## Programs started by `run`

`programs` of the document lists the external programs that the plan would start, with the command that starts each one and the origin of the program name. The policy of a host for shell commands applies to this list. Programs known to change remote state (publishing, deployment, remote shells) are reported in `irreversible` with the reason `external_effect`.

## Confirmation by the user

A host that asks the user before a change runs the program with `preview: true`, shows the targets and differences of the report, and then runs the same program without `preview`. The journal records every change; `undo` reverts an operation by its number `op`.

title: Remote instances and events
text:
# Remote instances and events

## Syntax trees for another device

A host that runs programs on another machine (a server, a container, a device) parses the program locally and sends the syntax tree:

1. `parse` on the local console returns the tree `nurt-ast/1` after correction.
2. The host applies its policy with `check` on the same program.
3. The host sends a request with `ast` to the remote instance over its own transport (SSH, a socket, a message queue) to `nurt serve` running there:


```json
{
  "nurt": "1.0",
  "ast": {
    "nurt": "1.0",
    "program": {
      "statements": [
        {
          "t": "pipeline",
          "head": {
            "t": "stage",
            "name": "list",
            "args": [{"value": {"t": "text", "v": "/srv/app"}}]
          },
          "stages": []
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "options": {"base": "/srv/app", "session": "s-17"}
}
```

The remote instance does not correct the tree again, so the program that runs is the one the policy checked. A tree with a newer version than the instance supports is rejected with `E_AST_VERSION`, which lists the unknown nodes. The connection, authentication and the choice of the device belong to the host.

## Events

`nurt serve` sends notifications `nurt/event` without an `id`; the parameters are the document `nurt-event/1`, which `libnurt` also passes to `nurt_event_cb`. Each event has `t` (type), `seq` (from 1, within the execution), `time` and, when the request has an identifier, `request`.

| Type | Content |
|---|---|
| `exec.started` | `ast_hash`, `effect` |
| `exec.finished` | `status`, `error` |
| `progress` | `command`, `phase`, `done`, `total`, `bytes`, `message` |
| `job.started` | `id`, `label`, `command` (list of strings), `cwd`, `pid`, `started` |
| `job.output` | `id`, `stream` (`stdout`, `stderr`), `cursor`, `lines`, `bytes` |
| `job.progress` | `id`, `percent`, `line` |
| `job.finished` | `id`, `state` (`exited`, `failed`, `stopped`, `timed_out`), `exit_code`, `signal`, `elapsed`, `output_file`, `changes` |
| `log` | `level`, `message`, `source` |

A notification in the stream of `nurt serve`:


```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "nurt/event",
  "params": {
    "seq": 3,
    "time": "2026-11-22T10:15:02Z",
    "request": "7",
    "t": "job.output",
    "id": "j-4",
    "stream": "stdout",
    "cursor": "o-120",
    "lines": ["compiling", "linking"],
    "bytes": 17
  }
}
```

The same event as the parameter of `nurt_event_cb`:


```json
{"seq": 4, "time": "2026-11-22T10:15:09Z", "request": "7", "t": "exec.finished", "status": "ok", "error": null}
```

A program started with `run ... background: true` returns a `job` record at once. The host follows the job through the events or reads its output incrementally with `jobs <id> since: <cursor>`; `stop`, `retry` and `remove` act on the job. Subscriptions, filtering of output lines and delivery of events to the context of the model belong to the host.

title: Tool calls
text:
# Tool calls

## Arguments and request

A tool call is turned into a request by placing `program`, `ast`, `cursor` and `accept` at the top level and every other argument in `options`:


```json
{"program": "find \"/home/user/app\" glob: \"**/*.go\" |> count", "limit": 20}
```


```json
{"nurt": "1.0", "program": "find \"/home/user/app\" glob: \"**/*.go\" |> count", "options": {"limit": 20}}
```

An unknown argument is a call error: the host returns it to the model as a tool error naming the argument. A request with two inputs, a relative `base` or a `limit` out of range is answered with the language error `E_ARG` in the report, with a fix.

## Result

The host returns `rendered.text` of the response to the model; for `format: "json"`, where `rendered` is absent, it returns the report as JSON. A report with `error` (`report.error`) is returned as a tool error (`is_error: true` for Anthropic, an error response for MCP), so that the model reads `fix` and corrects the call. Language errors never raise exceptions in the bindings; `raise_on_error` changes this per call.

## Corrections and `accept`

The console corrects common mistakes of notation before binding. A correction that touches a target of a change is not applied; the report carries `E_AMBIGUOUS` with ranked candidates. This holds for a misspelt name of a command that changes the file system or a remote state or runs a program: `remvoe "/home/user/app/build"` does not run, and the first candidate is `remove "/home/user/app/build"`. A misspelt name of a command that only reads (`fnid`) is corrected and the program runs. The same holds for a text with an unknown escape that a place reads as a regular expression or a Windows path (`"\d+"`, `"C:\temp\new"`): a reading program runs with the correction shown, a changing program is offered as a candidate.


```json
{
  "nurt": "1.0",
  "report": {
    "nurt": "1.0",
    "status": "failed",
    "kind": "remove",
    "error": {
      "code": "E_AMBIGUOUS",
      "message": "the target of the change is ambiguous",
      "candidates": [
        {"rank": 1, "ref": "c1", "program": "remove \"/home/user/app/build\"", "why": "the directory is named by the program"},
        {"rank": 2, "ref": "c2", "program": "remove \"/home/user/app/build/*\"", "why": "the contents of the directory only"}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

The model, or the host on behalf of the user, accepts one candidate with a call that has only `accept`:


```json
{"accept": "c1"}
```

The candidate runs exactly as listed. A candidate that expired or is unknown gives `E_EXPIRED_CANDIDATE`; the program is sent again. A host that asks the user for confirmation shows `program` and `why` of each candidate.

## Pages

A result longer than `limit` records ends with `report.next_cursor`. The next page is read with a call that has only `cursor` (and optionally `limit`):


```json
{"cursor": "p-7f3a-2", "limit": 100}
```

Reading a page never runs a changing program again. A host that collects all pages calls `page` (`nurt serve`) or repeats the call until `next_cursor` is absent. `max_chars` limits the length of single text fields; `save_to` writes the full result to a file instead of the response.

title: Tool definition
text:
# Tool definition

## Syntax

```
nurt schema tool [--format <format>] [--language en|pl] [--groups core|all|<group>,<group>...]
```

`nurt schema tool` without options prints the published schema `nurt-tool/1` (the schema of the `json-schema` format below), like every other name of `nurt schema`. With at least one option it prints the definition of the tool; an option that is not given takes its default. The description texts and the catalog version come from the installed engine.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--format` | enum | `json-schema` | output format, see below |
| `--language` | `en`, `pl` | `en` | language of the description; also the default of the `language` argument |
| `--groups` | text | `core` | command groups described in addition to the core group |

The value follows the option as a separate argument or after `=`. An unknown format, language or group is the error `E_UNKNOWN_VALUE` with the accepted values; an unknown option or a missing value is a usage error (exit code 2).

The Rust crate `nurt-tooldef` produces the same output: `render(ToolFormat, &RenderOptions)`. The output is deterministic for the same inputs.

## Result

One JSON object: the element of the tool list of the platform.

| Format | Platform | Object |
|---|---|---|
| `anthropic` | Anthropic Messages API | `{name, description, input_schema}` |
| `openai` | OpenAI Chat Completions | `{type: "function", function: {name, description, parameters, strict: false}}` |
| `openai-strict` | OpenAI Chat Completions, structured outputs | as `openai`, `strict: true` |
| `openai-responses` | OpenAI Responses API | `{type: "function", name, description, parameters, strict: false}` |
| `openai-responses-strict` | OpenAI Responses API, structured outputs | as `openai-responses`, `strict: true` |
| `gemini` | Gemini API | element of `functionDeclarations`: `{name, description, parameters}` |
| `mcp` | Model Context Protocol | element of `tools/list`: `{name, description, inputSchema, _meta}` |
| `json-schema` | any | `{name, description, input_schema, catalog_version}`; the input schema is JSON Schema 2020-12 |

The tool name is `nurt` in every format. The arguments are the inputs and the call options of `nurt-request/1`:

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `program` | text | program text |
| `ast` | object | syntax tree `nurt-ast/1`, equivalent to `program` |
| `cursor` | text | cursor of a further page of an earlier result |
| `accept` | text | identifier of a candidate of an earlier `E_AMBIGUOUS` error |
| `preview`, `base`, `limit`, `fields`, `format`, `verbosity`, `diff`, `diff_context`, `max_chars`, `save_to`, `timeout`, `session`, `language`, `script` | as in `nurt-request/1` | call options |

Exactly one of `program`, `ast`, `cursor` and `accept` is given. The envelope fields `nurt` (format version) and `variant` (notation variant, detected by the console) are not arguments.

## Rules per platform

The definition is generated from one source. Constructs that a platform does not accept are rewritten so that every format accepts the same calls; a constraint moved into a description is still checked by the console against `nurt-request/1`.

| Rule | Formats |
|---|---|
| the exclusive choice of `program`, `ast`, `cursor` and `accept` (`oneOf` at the root of the request schema) is stated in the root `description` | all |
| `additionalProperties: false` is removed | `gemini` |
| `default` is written into the description of the argument | `openai-strict`, `openai-responses-strict`, `gemini` |
| `minLength` is written into the description | `openai-strict`, `openai-responses-strict` |
| every argument is required and has `null` in its type; `null` means an absent argument | `openai-strict`, `openai-responses-strict` |
| `ast` is passed as JSON text | `openai-strict`, `openai-responses-strict`, `gemini` |
| enumerations carry `type: string`; type names are `STRING`, `INTEGER`, `OBJECT`, ... with `format: enum` | `gemini` (both), strict formats (first only) |

A host that receives arguments in a strict format or in `gemini` removes `null` values and parses `ast` text before it builds the request. The language bindings and `nurt_tooldef::request_from_arguments` do this.

## Description and command groups

The description holds the core description of the language, then the description of every selected group. The core group is always present. Other groups are loaded on demand:

1. Start with `--groups core`.
2. When the model needs a group, for example after `help group: "git"` or after `E_UNKNOWN_COMMAND` with a command of an optional group, render the definition again with the group added (`--groups git`), or append the text of `describe` for the group to the context.
3. MCP servers send `notifications/tools/list_changed` after the set of groups changes; clients read the tool list again.

`catalog_version` (`json-schema`) and `_meta["pl.danaco-group/nurt-catalog"]` (`mcp`) carry the version of the command catalog the description was produced from. A host that caches definitions uses the format, the language, the groups and this version as the cache key.

## Examples

```sh
nurt schema tool --format anthropic
nurt schema tool --format openai-responses-strict --groups core,git
nurt schema tool --format mcp --language pl --groups all
```

title: Versions and compatibility
text:
# Versions and compatibility

| Item | Version form | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| request, response, report, syntax trees | `nurt: "MAJOR.MINOR"` in each document | a minor version adds optional fields and new values of enumerations marked as extensible; a reader ignores unknown optional fields |
| protocol `nurt-rpc/1` | `initialize` returns the protocol and the features | the host checks the major version and reads the feature list instead of comparing program versions |
| C ABI | `nurt_abi_version()` | the major version must match; the minor version must be at least the one the host was built against |
| tool definition | follows `nurt-request/1` | a new option becomes a new optional argument; tool names and existing arguments do not change within a major version |
| command catalog | `catalog_version` | new commands and parameters are added within a major version; descriptions may change between minor versions |

A host that sends a document with a newer minor version than the console supports receives a language error naming the unsupported field; a newer major version is rejected as unsupported. Hosts pin the major version of the formats they use and test with the conformance suite `nurt-conformance`.

Implementations and integrations that pass the mandatory tests of `nurt-conformance` may use the name "Danaco Nurt Compatible".

The first request of a session is `initialize`; the result lists the protocol, the versions of the formats, the features and the limits:


```json
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 0, "method": "initialize", "params": {"protocol": "nurt-rpc/1", "client": {"name": "example-host", "version": "1.0.0"}, "capabilities": {"events": true}}}
```


```json
{
  "protocol": "nurt-rpc/1",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "abi": 65536,
  "language": "1.0",
  "ast": "1.0",
  "report": "1.0",
  "catalog_rev": "1.0",
  "features": ["events", "preview"],
  "groups": ["core"],
  "limits": {"max_inflight": 4, "max_message_bytes": 16777216}
}
```

title: Command catalog `nurt-catalog/1
text:
# Command catalog `nurt-catalog/1`

The command catalog is the single source of command signatures. The binder,
the built-in help, the model description, the reference documentation, the
tool definitions and the conformance suite all read it. It consists of:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `catalog/_index.toml` | the index `nurt-catalog-index/1`: catalog files and the expected number of commands |
| `catalog/core.toml` | the core commands, always described to the model |
| `catalog/<group>.toml` | one file per optional group, described on request |
| `spec/schemas/nurt-catalog-1.schema.json` | the JSON schema of a catalog file, generated from the Rust types |

The Rust types are in the module `nurt_contracts::spec`: `CatalogFile`,
`CatalogIndex`, `StageSpec`, `ParamSpec`, `ParamType`, `DefaultValue`,
`IoSpec`, `FormSpec`, `ActionEffect`, `ExternalUse`.

## 1. Catalog file

```toml
format = "nurt-catalog/1"
group = "documents"
summary = "Structured documents and SQLite."

[[command]]
name = "set"
category = "change"
reversibility = "reversible"
effect = "local"
implementation = "builtin"
input = ["none", "entry"]
output = ["effect"]
summary = "Set values at key paths, preserving layout."

[[command.param]]
name = "path"
type = "path | list<path>"
position = 1
required = true
summary = "Document to change."
```

### 1.1 File keys

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | text | yes | always `nurt-catalog/1` |
| `group` | identifier | yes | `core` or the group name; equal to the file name without `.toml` |
| `summary` | text | yes | one sentence ending with a full stop |
| `command` | array of tables | no | the commands of the group |

### 1.2 Command keys (`[[command]]`)

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | yes | full command name: an identifier or two identifiers joined by a dot (`git.status`); unique in the whole catalog |
| `group` | identifier | no | normally omitted; when present, equal to the file group |
| `category` | enum | yes | `source`, `transform`, `check`, `change`, `run`, `system`, `journal`, `help` |
| `reversibility` | enum | yes | `read`, `reversible`, `reversible_if_preserved`, `irreversible` |
| `effect` | enum | yes | default effect: `read`, `local`, `external`, `process` |
| `implementation` | enum | yes | `builtin`, `user_program`, `language_server`, `package_manager`, `system_program` |
| `input` | list of kinds | yes | accepted input kinds (section 4) |
| `output` | list of kinds | yes | produced output kinds (section 4) |
| `summary` | text | yes | one sentence ending with a full stop |
| `reversibility_note` | text | no | conditions of reversibility; omitted when there are none |
| `effects` | list of tables | no | actions whose effect differs from the default (section 7) |
| `waits` | bool | no | the command always blocks the call by waiting (`sleep`); default `false` |
| `os` | list of enum | no | operating systems the command is limited to: `linux`, `macos`, `windows`; empty means all; on other systems binding fails with `E_OS_ONLY` |
| `external` | table | no | use of an external program or system component beyond `implementation` (section 8) |
| `fallback` | enum | no | implementation used when the primary one is unavailable, such as `builtin` syntax analysis for a `language_server` command without an installed server; the result states which one ran |
| `required_groups` | list of identifiers | no | exclusive groups of which exactly one parameter must be given (section 6) |
| `param` | array of tables | no | parameters (section 2) |
| `form` | array of tables | no | input-dependent forms of a polymorphic command (section 5) |

### 1.3 Parameter keys (`[[command.param]]`)

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | identifier | yes | parameter name, unique in the command |
| `type` | type expression | yes | section 3 |
| `position` | integer ≥ 1 | no | position among positional arguments of the primary form; the positions of a command form the sequence `1..n` |
| `required` | bool | no | required in the primary form; default `false`; a required parameter has no `default`; with `default_from` it is missing only when its source has no value either |
| `repeated` | bool | no | a positional parameter that collects several arguments into a list; its type accepts a list; at most one per command |
| `per_record` | bool | no | the value may be an expression evaluated on each input record (`to: "/dst/" + name`) |
| `default` | text | no | default value as a literal of the language in variant A: `"1"`, `"true"`, `'"**"'`, `"asc"`, `"120s"`, `"10mb"`, `"[]"`; absent means no value (`null`) |
| `unbounded_default` | bool | no | the default is "no limit"; excludes `default` |
| `default_from` | identifier | no | the default is the value of another parameter of the command or of the call parameter `base`, converted to the type of this parameter (a path becomes a one-element list): `run cwd` defaults to `base`, `run watch` to `cwd`; excludes `default` and `unbounded_default` |
| `default_note` | text | no | description of a computed default ("the latest operation") |
| `values` | list of identifiers | conditional | the enumeration values of the type, repeated for readability; required and equal to the values of the type, in order, when the type contains `enum(…)` |
| `summary` | text | yes | short description |
| `exclusive_group` | identifier | no | parameters with the same group name are mutually exclusive (section 6) |
| `waits` | bool | no | a value of this parameter greater than its default, or the value `forever`, marks the stage `waits: true` in the bound tree (`run wait:` above `3s`, `jobs wait:` above `0s`) |
| `secret` | bool | no | the value is confidential (credentials in an address or a header); it is masked in the journal, the report and the printed bound tree |

A bare-word default (`asc`, `auto`) is one of `values`; the word `all` is also
accepted for parameters whose type contains `range` (the whole range).

## 2. Call parameters are not command parameters

The following parameters belong to the call envelope (`nurt-request/1`,
`options`) and to the `--name` options of the command line, not to any
command. They apply to every command and are never listed in catalog files.

| Parameter | Type and default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `preview` | `bool = false` | compute targets and effect only, without changing anything |
| `base` | `path` | directory against which relative paths are resolved; not a current directory |
| `limit` | `int = 50` (at most 5000) | records or changes per page of the result |
| `cursor` | `text` | cursor of the next page; reading a page again does not run a changing program again |
| `fields` | `list<text>` | fields of the result, like a final `select` |
| `format` | `enum(text\|json\|markdown\|compact) = text` | form of the result |
| `verbosity` | `enum(quiet\|normal\|detailed) = normal` | detail level of the effect report |
| `diff` | `enum(none\|stat\|unified) = unified` | form of differences in the report of a change |
| `diff_context` | `int = 3` | context lines of differences |
| `max_chars` | `int = 0` (no limit) | limit of a single text field of the result; truncated fields carry `truncated: true` |
| `save_to` | `path` | write the full result to a file (UTF-8) instead of returning it |
| `timeout` | `duration = 120s` | time limit of the whole program (`run timeout:` limits one program) |
| `session` | `text` | session identifier recorded in the journal |
| `language` | `enum(en\|pl) = en` | language of help and hints; codes, fields and keywords are always English |
| `script` | `bool = false` | script mode: several pipelines, each a separate operation |
| `privilege` | `enum(account\|elevated\|auto) = account` | rights of the operation: the account that runs Nurt; the administrator (`root` on Linux and macOS, `LocalSystem` on Windows); or `auto`, which runs with the account and repeats the whole stage once with `elevated` when a target fails with `E_PERMISSION` or `E_PRIVILEGE` before any change is kept. The default comes from the configuration key `privilege.default`. Valid on every changing command, on `run` and on reading commands. No command is marked "never elevated" |
| `as_user` | `text` | account that runs the operation (equivalent of `sudo -u NAME`; Linux and macOS); implies elevation for the switch; ends with `E_UNSUPPORTED` on Windows |

A command may have a parameter with the name of a call parameter when its
meaning is narrower and stated in the catalog: `run timeout:` limits one
program, while the call parameter `timeout` limits the whole program;
`write format:` is the serialization of written records, while the call
parameter `format` is the form of the result. The two never collide, because
call parameters are not part of the program text.

The two call parameters `privilege` and `as_user` are the exception: they may
also be written on a stage, as named arguments, on every command that does not
declare a parameter of the same name (`write "/etc/hosts" "..." privilege:
elevated`, `package.install ["jq"] privilege: elevated`, `run [...] cwd: "/"
as_user: "deploy"`). The binder takes them out of the signature, checks the
value (`privilege` is `account`, `elevated` or `auto`, written as a word or a
text; `as_user` is a non-empty word or text; each at most once per stage) and
appends them to the arguments of the stage (`privilege` as an `enum` value, `as_user` as `text`) after the
parameters of the signature, with `default: false`. A value written on a stage
replaces the option of the request and the configuration key
`privilege.default` for the whole call.

Rule of `privilege: auto`: the call first runs with the rights of the account. When it ends with `E_PERMISSION` or `E_PRIVILEGE` and has left no operation (`op` absent: nothing was kept), the whole call is repeated once with `elevated`; the report states `elevated: true` and `elevation_reason: permission_denied`. A call that already changed something is never repeated, and a second denial is returned as it is. A stage reads the effective value from
the options of its context: `ctx.options().privilege()` and
`ctx.options().effective_privilege()`; the executor has already run the call
with the rights that value names, so a stage never needs to elevate itself.
### 2.0 `preview` on a stage and the boolean shorthand

A stage that has no parameter named `preview` accepts `preview` as its last
argument: `remove preview`, `remove preview: true` and `remove preview: @dry`
compute the effect of that stage without applying it. The binder keeps the
value in the bound stage as the argument `preview`; the executor plans the
stage and reports status `planned` for its part. The call parameter `preview`
of the envelope previews the whole program.

A parameter of type `bool` written without a value is `true`: a word that
names a `bool` parameter of the command, that is not written otherwise and
that is not a value of an enumeration parameter of the command stands for
`name: true`. `false` is always written out (`hidden: false`). The long form
stays valid. The rule applies to commands, to the call of a function and to
the parameters of a script (`nurt run file.nurt dry`). A parameter of a
function or of a script that is not `bool`, written without a value, is
`E_MISSING_PARAM` with the expected type.

### 2.1 Shared command parameters

Parameters with the same name have the same meaning and type in every command
that has them. The default may differ per command and is always written in
the catalog.

| Parameter | Type and usual default |
|---|---|
| `case_sensitive` | `bool = true` |
| `whole_word` | `bool = false` |
| `whitespace` | `enum(exact\|trailing\|indent\|normalize)`; `exact` for searching, `normalize` for `replace` and `edit` |
| `encoding` | `text = "auto"` |
| `line_ending` | `enum(lf\|crlf\|cr\|keep) = keep` |
| `hidden` | `bool = true` |
| `gitignore` | `bool = false` |
| `on_missing` | `enum(skip\|error) = skip` |
| `on_conflict` | `enum(overwrite\|skip\|error)`, default per command |
| `expect` | `range` |
| `if_match` | `text` (etag), or `text \| map<text>` (path to etag) for commands with several target files |
| `validate` | `enum(off\|warn\|reject) = reject` |
| `depth` | `int` |
| `type` | `enum(file\|directory\|link\|any)` for entry kinds |
| `order` | `enum(asc\|desc) = asc` |
| `file_type` | `list<text> = []`, file types by extension (`go`, `ts`); applies in every output mode |
| `hash` | `enum(none\|sha256\|sha512\|sha1\|md5\|blake3\|crc32)`; the algorithm list is the same wherever a hash algorithm is chosen |

## 3. Type expressions

The `type` key holds a type expression. The parser is part of the contract
(`ParamType::parse`); an invalid expression makes the catalog file invalid.

```text
type        = alternative { "|" alternative } ;
alternative = scalar
            | "list" [ "<" type ">" ]
            | "map"  [ "<" type ">" ]
            | "stream" "<" identifier ">"
            | "enum" "(" identifier { "|" identifier } ")" ;
scalar      = "text" | "int" | "number" | "bool" | "path" | "glob" | "regex"
            | "size" | "duration" | "percent" | "instant" | "key" | "bytes" | "range"
            | "expression" | "pipeline" | "field" | "named_expression" | "any" ;
identifier  = lowercase letter { lowercase letter | digit | "_" } ;
```

Spaces and tabs between tokens are ignored. Inside `list<…>` and `map<…>` the
full grammar applies, so `list<text | regex>` is a list whose elements are
text or regular expressions.

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `text`, `int`, `number`, `bool` | basic values |
| `path`, `glob`, `regex`, `key`, `instant`, `size`, `duration` | values with literal forms of the language; a quoted text is converted implicitly to `path`, `glob`, `instant`, `key`, `size` and `duration` in a place of that type |
| `percent` | share of a capacity, written as a quoted text: `"10%"`; a command may also accept `"10%free"`, a share of the free space, and says so in the parameter summary; there is no separate literal, the text is converted in a place of this type like `size` and `duration` |
| `bytes` | raw bytes (base64 in JSON) |
| `range` | `5`, `1..5`, `40..`, `..9`, `all`; lines count from 1, bounds inclusive |
| `expression` | expression evaluated on each input record (`filter`, `assert all:`) |
| `pipeline` | nested pipeline in parentheses (`verify (…)`, `write from: (…)`) |
| `field` | name of a record field (`sort size`) |
| `named_expression` | pair `name: expression` computing a new field (`select total: size * 2`) |
| `any` | any value |
| `enum(a\|b)` | one of the bare words |
| `list<T>`, `map<T>` | list; map from text keys; bare `list` and `map` mean `list<any>` and `map<any>` |
| `stream<R>` | result of a named pipeline `@name` with records of kind `R` (`any` for any kind) |
| `A \| B` | any of the alternatives |

The canonical text of a type (used in serialization, help and JSON) writes
alternatives separated by `" | "`, enumeration values separated by `|`
without spaces, and bare `list` and `map` as `list<any>` and `map<any>`.
Parsing the canonical text gives the same type.

Errors are typed (`TypeParseError`): `empty`, `unexpected_end`,
`unexpected_char`, `unknown_type`, `invalid_enum_value`,
`duplicate_enum_value`, `duplicate_alternative`, `too_deep` (nesting deeper
than 16 levels), each with the byte offset of the problem.

## 4. Input and output kinds

`input` and `output` list kinds (`IoSpec`):

| Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `none` | input only: the command starts a pipeline (source form) |
| `any` | records of any kind |
| `same` | output only: the records of the input, unchanged in kind (`filter`, `sort`) |
| scalar keyword (`int`, `text`) | a single value (`count` produces `int`, `help` produces `text`) |
| record kind (`entry`, `match`, `effect`, …) | records of that kind |

The kind `effect` is the effect report of a changing or running stage seen as
a record; the stages after an effect (`assert`, `filter`, `select`, `first`,
`last`, `skip`, `count`, `sort`, `verify`) consume it.

## 5. Forms of polymorphic commands

Some commands accept different parameters depending on their input: the
source form of `replace` takes `pattern`, `with` and `in`, while the stage
form after `search` takes only `with`. Such commands list forms:

```toml
[[command.form]]
name = "source"
input = ["none"]
positional = ["pattern", "with"]
required = ["pattern", "with", "in"]
summary = "Replace a pattern in the given files."

[[command.form]]
name = "matches"
input = ["match", "node", "item"]
positional = ["with"]
required = ["with"]
params = ["with", "occurrence", "template", "expect", "if_match", "validate"]
summary = "Replace the text of the input matches."
```

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | form name, unique in the command |
| `input` | yes | input kinds of the form; every input kind of the command belongs to exactly one form |
| `output` | no | output kinds of the form; empty means the output of the command |
| `positional` | no | positional parameters of the form, in order |
| `required` | no | required parameters of the form; a name of an exclusive group means "exactly one of the group" |
| `params` | no | parameters accepted by the form; empty means all |
| `expand` | no | in a source form: the parameter that names the entries the command works on; the binder expands the form (section 5.2) |
| `summary` | yes | one sentence |

The binder selects the form whose `input` contains the kind of the input
records (`none` for a source). The first form is the primary form: the
`position` and `required` keys of the parameters and the command key
`required_groups` describe it, and the catalog check verifies that they agree.
A command without forms has a single form described by its parameters.

### 5.1 Repeated positional parameters

A repeated parameter (`repeated = true`) collects positional arguments into a
list. When positional parameters follow it (`copy FROM… TO`), the later
positions take the last arguments and the repeated parameter takes the rest,
as in `copy "/a" "/b" "/dst"` (`from: ["/a", "/b"]`, `to: "/dst"`). With a
single positional argument the repeated parameter takes it.

### 5.2 Expanded source forms

A source form with the key `expand` is not bound as written. The binder
expands it to an `info` head whose `path` is the value of the named
parameter, followed by the command bound in its form for `entry` input:

```toml
[[command.form]]
name = "source"
input = ["none"]
positional = ["path"]
required = ["path"]
expand = "path"
summary = "Remove the given files and directories."
```

`remove "/a" "/b"` binds to `info ["/a", "/b"] |> remove`, so the two programs
have the same bound tree. `info` accepts a list of paths, does not descend
into directories and reports a missing path as an entry with `exists: false`,
which the command handles according to its `on_missing` parameter. The core
catalog expands the source forms of `copy` and `move` (`from`) and of
`remove`, `rename` and `attributes` (`path`). The named parameter accepts a
path, the form takes no input, and the form for `entry` input does not accept
the parameter. Source forms without `expand` (`replace`, `insert`) are bound
as written.

## 6. Exclusive and required groups

Parameters that share `exclusive_group` exclude each other: at most one of
them may be given. A group listed in the command key `required_groups` (or in
the `required` list of a form) requires exactly one. A group has at least two
members, and its name is not the name of a parameter.

```toml
required_groups = ["condition"]
[[command.param]]
name = "count"
type = "range"
exclusive_group = "condition"
summary = "Expected number of records."
```

## 7. Effects of actions

`effects` lists actions whose effect or reversibility differs from the
command default:

```toml
effects = [
  { action = "push", effect = "external", reversibility = "irreversible" },
]
```

`action` is an identifier naming one of:

| Meaning | Example |
|---|---|
| a value of the `action` parameter of the command | `git.stash` `action: drop` |
| a value of another enumeration parameter | `http.request` `method: post` (`action = "post"`) |
| the name of a parameter whose use changes the effect | `http.request` `save:` (`action = "save"`) |
| the input record kind, for commands whose effect depends on it | `remove` on `job` (`action = "job"`) |

`note` states the condition when it is not obvious from the identifier.

## 8. External use

`external` marks the use of a program or system component outside the
executable, as required for every such operation:

```toml
external = { kind = "system_program", programs = ["launchctl"], note = "Services on macOS." }
```

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | yes | `user_program`, `language_server`, `package_manager` or `system_program` |
| `programs` | no | program names |
| `when` | no | parameter whose use triggers the external use; absent when unconditional |
| `note` | no | remark shown in the description and in the report |

## 9. Index

```toml
format = "nurt-catalog-index/1"
total = 148

[[file]]
name = "core"
file = "core.toml"
summary = "Core commands for files, text, records, programs, the journal and help."
commands = 33
```

The first entry is `core`; every entry names `<name>.toml`; the sum of
`commands` equals `total`.

### 9.1 Catalog revision

The catalog revision identifies the exact catalog used for binding and is
recorded as `catalog_rev` in every bound tree:

```
catalog_rev = "sha256:" + lowercase_hex(SHA-256(UTF-8(JCS(files))))
```

`files` is the JSON array of the catalog files in the order of the index, each
serialized from `CatalogFile` (the form validated by
`nurt-catalog-1.schema.json`), and JCS is the canonical JSON of RFC 8785. Any
change of a command, a parameter or a description therefore changes the
revision. The command registry of the engine reports the same value as
`catalog_rev` in the result of a catalog query and in `nurt_info`. The groups
of registered extensions follow the files of the index as files of the same
form, so a registry with extensions reports a different revision from the one
recorded in a bound tree, which names the built-in catalog used for binding.
The revision of the correction tables, `corr_rev`, has the same
form.

### 9.2 The command `next`

`next` is a core command of category `source` that reads the next part of a
shortened result (`spec/report.md`, section 2.1). Its parameters:
`id` (position 1, text: `c3`, a count or the words `all` and `full`),
`count` (position 2, int), `all` (bool) and `full_lines` (bool). The short
forms are `next`, `next c3`, `next 200`, `next c3 200`, `next all` and
`next full`; every short form has the same result as its long form, and
`next |> filter …` continues the part as a pipeline. The command changes
nothing, writes no journal entry and costs no effect in `E_ONE_EFFECT`.

### 9.3 The group `administration`

The file `administration.toml` holds the commands that change the system
outside the file system, the service commands and the Windows management
calls. Every changing command accepts `privilege` (section 2.1) and records
the state before and after in its report, from which `undo` derives the
inverse; a command marked `irreversible` has no inverse, and its preview
lists what is lost. The tool description loads the group on demand under the
name `administration`.

| Command | Category | Effect | Reversibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| `services` | source | read | read |
| `start` | run | external | irreversible |
| `restart` | run | external | irreversible |
| `enable` | change | external | irreversible |
| `disable` | change | external | irreversible |
| `windows.cim` | change | read | read |
| `firewall.rules` | source | read | read |
| `firewall.allow` | change | external | reversible |
| `firewall.deny` | change | external | reversible |
| `firewall.remove` | change | external | reversible |
| `network.route_add` | change | external | reversible |
| `network.route_remove` | change | external | reversible |
| `network.dns_set` | change | external | reversible |
| `clock.timezone_set` | change | external | reversible |
| `clock.set` | change | external | irreversible |
| `clock.ntp` | change | external | reversible |
| `accounts.create` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `accounts.modify` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `accounts.remove` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `accounts.password` | change | external | irreversible |
| `groups.create` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `groups.remove` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `groups.add_member` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `groups.remove_member` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `mount` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `unmount` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `sysctl.set` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `modules.load` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `modules.unload` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `power.restart` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `power.shutdown` | change | external | reversible_if_preserved |
| `power.cancel` | change | external | irreversible |
| `disks.partition` | change | external | irreversible |
| `disks.format` | change | external | irreversible |

## 10. Checks

`CatalogFile::check`, `CatalogIndex::check` and `check_catalog` return the list
of problems; the test suite requires an empty list for every file in
`catalog/`:

1. every file parses into `CatalogFile` (unknown keys are rejected), has the
   format `nurt-catalog/1` and a group equal to its file name;
2. command names are valid and unique in the whole catalog;
3. every type expression parses; every `default` is non-empty; a required
   parameter has no default; `values` repeat the enumeration values of the
   type; a bare-word default is one of the values; `default_from` names
   another parameter of the command or `base` and excludes `default`;
4. the positions of each command form the sequence `1..n`; a repeated
   parameter is positional and accepts a list;
5. exclusive groups have at least two members; required groups exist;
6. forms are consistent with the parameters and cover every input kind once;
   `expand` stands only in a source form, names a parameter that accepts a
   path, and that parameter is not accepted by the form for `entry` input;
7. the index lists every file with its number of commands, and when every
   listed file is present the number of commands equals `total`.

## 11. Compatibility

Within `nurt-catalog/1` the catalog only grows: new commands, new optional
parameters whose default keeps the previous behaviour, new enumeration values
and new optional keys. Removing or renaming a command or a parameter, changing
a type incompatibly, or changing a default is a change of the major version.

title: Configuration `nurt-config/1
text:
# Configuration `nurt-config/1`

Danaco Nurt reads its configuration from TOML files, environment variables
and run-time settings at seven levels of precedence. The machine-readable form
of the format is the JSON Schema `spec/schemas/nurt-config-1.schema.json`,
generated from the Rust type `nurt_contracts::config::Config`. Example files are in `spec/golden/config/`;
`spec/golden/config/defaults.toml` lists every key with its default.

## 1. Files

A configuration file is a TOML document. Tables correspond to the sections
below, and every key is optional: an empty file is the built-in
configuration.

| System | System file | User file | State directory |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linux | `/etc/nurt/nurt.toml` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nurt/nurt.toml` (by default `~/.config/nurt/nurt.toml`) | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/nurt/` |
| macOS | `/Library/Application Support/Nurt/nurt.toml` | `~/Library/Application Support/Nurt/nurt.toml` | `~/Library/Application Support/Nurt/` |
| Windows | `%PROGRAMDATA%\Nurt\nurt.toml` | `%APPDATA%\Nurt\nurt.toml` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Nurt\` |

A project file is named `.nurt.toml` and lies in the project directory. The
variable `NURT_CONFIG` names one more file. An application that embeds the
library may pass a configuration in JSON when it opens the engine
(`nurt_engine_open`); it is applied at the level of the `NURT_CONFIG` file,
after that file.

## 2. Levels and precedence

| Level | Identifier | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `builtin` | built-in defaults |
| 2 | `system` | system file |
| 3 | `user` | user file |
| 4 | `project` | `.nurt.toml` of the project |
| 5 | `config_file` | file named by `NURT_CONFIG`; configuration of an embedding application |
| 6 | `environment` | `NURT_*` variables, read when the process starts |
| 7 | `runtime` | invocation parameters, request options, `journal.limits` |

A higher level overrides a lower one, key by key:

- tables merge: a key set at a higher level replaces only that key;
- scalars and arrays are replaced as a whole (an array is never appended);
- layers of the same level are applied in the order in which they are read.

The level that set each key is recorded. It is reported, for example, by
`journal.status` for the effective journal limits.

A key that the format does not define is ignored and reported to the
caller; a value that does not match the type of its key is an error that
names the key, the level and the file.

## 3. Project files and trust

A project file comes from a repository and is not trusted. It may set only:

| Keys | Condition |
|---|---|
| `scope.base`, `scope.project_roots` | always |
| `report.*`, `run.*` | always |
| `journal.*` | only for a trusted project |

A project is trusted when its directory is listed in `scope.trusted_projects`.
The list can be set in the system file, the user file, the `NURT_CONFIG` file
(or the configuration of an embedding application) and the variable
`NURT_TRUSTED_PROJECTS`. It cannot be set in a project file or at run time,
so that neither a repository nor a request can grant trust.

Keys that are not applied are reported with these notable codes:

| Key | Level | Notable code |
|---|---|---|
| `scope.trust*` | project, runtime | `trust_config_ignored` |
| `service.*` | project | `trust_config_ignored` |
| `privilege.*` | project | `trust_config_ignored` |
| `journal.*` | project that is not trusted | `journal_config_ignored` |
| any other key outside the list above | project | `project_config_ignored` |

The rule is available to implementations as the pure function
`nurt_contracts::config::allowed_at(level, key)`.

## 4. Protection floors

`journal.floor.max_ops` and `journal.floor.max_age` are the lowest step and
age limits of the journal. A lower effective value, from any level, is raised
to the floor and the change is noted in `journal.status`; `unlimited` is
above every floor. Values that come from a project file are raised to at
least 10 steps and 5 minutes even when no floor is set. Floors are normally
set by an administrator (system file) or by an embedding application when it
opens the engine; a floor can only raise protection: when several levels set
the same floor, the highest value wins, whatever the precedence of the levels,
so that a user file cannot lower a floor set in the system file.

## 5. Values

| Type | Syntax | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| duration | digits followed by `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, `d` or `w`, also combined; no bare numbers | `"1500ms"`, `"30m"`, `"1h30m"` |
| size | number with `b`, `kb`, `mb`, `gb`, `tb` (powers of 1000) or `kib`, `mib`, `gib`, `tib` (powers of 1024); a fraction is allowed; an integer means bytes | `"256mib"`, `"1.5tb"`, `4096` |
| percentage | number with up to two decimal places followed by `%` | `"15%"`, `"12.5%"` |
| step limit | integer `1` to `100000`, or `"unlimited"`; `0` is not accepted | `30`, `"unlimited"` |
| age limit | duration from `10s` to `365d`, or `"unlimited"` | `"30m"` |
| size budget | size of at least `1mib`, percentage of the volume capacity (`1%` to `90%`), percentage of the free space including journal data (`1%free` to `100%free`), or `"unlimited"` | `"20gib"`, `"10%"`, `"50%free"` |
| byte limit | size or `"unlimited"` | `"unlimited"` |
| size or percentage | size, or percentage of the volume capacity | `"5gib"`, `"15%"` |

Units are written in lower case. When the configuration is written back (for
example by `nurt_engine_config_get`), durations and sizes use the largest
unit that represents the value exactly: `"120s"` is written as `"2m"`,
`"24h"` as `"1d"`.

## 6. Environment variables

| Variable | Key | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `NURT_CONFIG` | — | path of an additional configuration file |
| `NURT_SYNTAX` | `syntax.variant` | text |
| `NURT_SYNTAX_TOLERANT` | `syntax.tolerant` | boolean |
| `NURT_CORRECTION` | `correction.enabled` | boolean |
| `NURT_BASE` | `scope.base` | text |
| `NURT_PROJECT_ROOTS` | `scope.project_roots` | list |
| `NURT_TRUSTED_PROJECTS` | `scope.trusted_projects` | list |
| `NURT_JOURNAL` | `journal.enabled` | boolean |
| `NURT_JOURNAL_MAX_OPS` | `journal.max_ops` | text |
| `NURT_JOURNAL_MAX_AGE` | `journal.max_age` | text |
| `NURT_JOURNAL_MAX_SIZE` | `journal.max_size` | text |
| `NURT_JOURNAL_MAX_OP_SIZE` | `journal.max_op_size` | text |
| `NURT_JOURNAL_OVERSIZE` | `journal.oversize` | text |
| `NURT_JOURNAL_OVERWRITE` | `journal.overwrite` | text |
| `NURT_JOURNAL_NETWORK` | `journal.volumes.network` | boolean |
| `NURT_JOURNAL_REMOVABLE` | `journal.volumes.removable` | boolean |
| `NURT_SPACE_RESERVE` | `space.reserve` | text |
| `NURT_SPACE_SOFT` | `space.soft` | text |
| `NURT_SPACE_POLL_MS` | `space.poll_ms` | integer |
| `NURT_RUN_TIMEOUT` | `run.timeout` | text |
| `NURT_RUN_WAIT` | `run.wait` | text |
| `NURT_LANGUAGE` | `output.language` | text |
| `NURT_COLOR` | `output.color` | text |
| `NURT_RESULTS_DIR` | `output.results_dir` | text |
| `NURT_MAX_RECORDS` | `limits.max_records` | integer |
| `NURT_THREADS` | `limits.threads` | integer |
| `NURT_PROGRAMS_CATALOGS` | `programs.catalogs` | list |
| `NURT_HTTP_PROXY` | `http.proxy` | text |
| `NURT_EXT_DIR` | `ext.dir` | text |
| `NURT_STATE_DIR` | `state.dir` | text |
| `NURT_LOG` | `log.level` | text |
| `NURT_SESSION` | `session.id` | text |

Booleans are `1`, `true`, `yes`, `on`, `0`, `false`, `no` or `off` (in any
case). Lists are separated by `:` (`;` on Windows); empty items are skipped.
Text is converted by the type of the key, so `NURT_JOURNAL_MAX_OPS=unlimited`
and `NURT_JOURNAL_MAX_OPS=30` are both valid. The HTTP client also honours
the standard variables `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY`. Other
variables are ignored.

## 7. Keys

"None" in the default column means that the key is not set and the
behaviour in the meaning column applies.

### 7.1 `[syntax]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `syntax.variant` | `a`, `b`, `c` | `a` | notation variant of the text form |
| `syntax.tolerant` | boolean | `true` | also accept the notation of the other variants |

### 7.2 `[correction]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `correction.enabled` | boolean | `true` | correction of the written form of programs |
| `correction.max_read` | integer | `8` | correction budget of programs that only read |
| `correction.max_effect` | integer | `4` | correction budget of programs that change something |
| `correction.require_first_char` | boolean | `true` | fuzzy correction of names keeps the first character |
| `correction.candidates_ttl` | duration | `10m` | lifetime of candidates that can be accepted after an ambiguous program |

### 7.3 `[scope]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scope.base` | path | none | absolute directory for relative paths |
| `scope.project_roots` | list of paths | `[]` | project directories; changes outside them are reported as `outside_project` |
| `scope.trusted_projects` | list of paths | `[]` | projects whose `.nurt.toml` may change `journal.*` (section 3) |

### 7.4 `[journal]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `journal.enabled` | boolean | `true` | record changes in the journal |
| `journal.max_ops` | step limit | `30` | number of recent changing operations that can be undone |
| `journal.max_age` | age limit | `30m` | how long previous content is kept |
| `journal.max_size` | size budget | `unlimited` | size budget per volume; the space reserve always applies |
| `journal.max_size_min` | size | `2gib` | lower clamp of percentage budgets |
| `journal.max_size_max` | size | `50gib` | upper clamp of percentage budgets |
| `journal.max_size_total` | byte limit | `unlimited` | budget summed over all volumes |
| `journal.max_op_size` | byte limit | `unlimited` | limit of a single operation |
| `journal.oversize` | `skip`, `keep` | `skip` | operation larger than the budget: done without keeping previous content (reported as irreversible), or kept above the budget |
| `journal.age_clock` | `wall`, `active` | `wall` | entries age in wall-clock time, or only while the computer runs |
| `journal.floor.max_ops` | step limit | none | lowest step limit (section 4) |
| `journal.floor.max_age` | age limit | none | lowest age limit (section 4) |
| `journal.pin_max_age` | duration | `24h` | default duration of `journal.pin` |
| `journal.overwrite` | `exchange`, `clone_or_copy` | `exchange` | keeping overwritten files |
| `journal.count_undo_as_op` | boolean | `true` | an undo counts as a step |
| `journal.history_keep` | integer | `1000` | expired entries whose metrics are kept for `history` |
| `journal.dir_name` | text | `.nurt-journal` | name of the journal directory on each volume |
| `journal.volumes.network` | boolean | `false` | keep a journal on network volumes |
| `journal.volumes.removable` | boolean | `false` | keep a journal on removable volumes |
| `journal.volume` | table by mount point | empty | settings of one volume: `enabled`, `reserve`, `soft`, `max_ops`, `max_age`, `max_size`; absent keys are inherited |

### 7.5 `[space]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `space.reserve` | size or percentage | `15%` | free space that the journal never takes |
| `space.reserve_min` | size | `5gib` | lower clamp of a percentage reserve |
| `space.reserve_max` | size | `50gib` | upper clamp of a percentage reserve |
| `space.soft` | size or percentage | none: reserve plus the larger of 5 % and 2 GiB, no more than reserve plus 20 GiB | threshold at which the service starts releasing journal data |
| `space.margin` | size or percentage | none: the smaller of 1 % and 1 GiB | margin above the reserve |
| `space.poll_ms` | integer | `250` | period of free space measurement, in milliseconds |
| `space.poll_fast_ms` | integer | `50` | measurement period near a threshold, in milliseconds |
| `space.heartbeat_ms` | integer | `500` | heartbeat period of the service, in milliseconds |
| `space.heartbeat_max_age_ms` | integer | `2000` | age after which a heartbeat is stale, in milliseconds |
| `space.sync_budget_ms` | integer | `1500` | budget of synchronous release before a write, in milliseconds |
| `space.settle_ms` | integer | `1000` | wait for free space to grow after a release, in milliseconds |
| `space.quota_aware` | boolean | `true` | take quotas of the account into account |

### 7.6 `[run]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run.timeout` | duration | `120s` | time limit of a program |
| `run.wait` | duration | `3s` | time to wait in the foreground before a program continues in the background |
| `run.idle_timeout` | duration | `60s` | time without output and processor activity after which a program is reported as stalled |
| `run.kill_grace` | duration | `5s` | time between the termination request and killing the process group |
| `run.env_defaults` | table of text | `PYTHONUTF8="1"`, `PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8"`, `NO_COLOR="1"`, `TERM="dumb"`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT="0"`, `PAGER="cat"`, `GIT_PAGER="cat"`, `DEBIAN_FRONTEND="noninteractive"` | variables added to the environment of every program |
| `run.track_changes` | `auto`, `scan`, `events`, `none` | `auto` | detection of file changes made by a program |
| `run.track_ignore` | list of names | `[".git"]` | names excluded from change detection |
| `run.preimage` | `auto`, `off` | `auto` | keep previous content of declared and watched files before a program runs |
| `run.preimage_budget` | duration | `1500ms` | time budget of keeping previous content |
| `run.preimage_max_entries` | integer | `20000` | largest number of files kept |
| `run.preimage_copy_max` | size | `256mib` | largest amount copied when cloning is not available |
| `run.preimage_exclude` | list of names | `node_modules`, `.git`, `target`, `build`, `dist`, `.venv`, `__pycache__` | names never kept |
| `run.irreversible_patterns` | list of patterns | `[]` | argument patterns added to the built-in table of programs with effects outside the computer; tokens are separated by spaces, `*` matches any token, `a\|b` matches alternatives; the built-in table cannot be removed |
| `run.parallel` | integer | `1` | default number of batches run at the same time |
| `run.spool_max` | byte limit | `1gib` | largest output kept per program: its first part and, up to a quarter of the limit (at most 64 MiB), its last part; the bytes between them are omitted, marked with a line `[... N bytes omitted ...]` in the spool file and reported with the note `spool_limit`; the counters and the hash cover all output; `unlimited` keeps everything and can be set at any level, including the run-time level for one run |
| `run.supervisor` | `auto`, `none` | `auto` | supervision of programs that continue in the background after the command line exits; `none` allows background programs only inside a long-lived process |
| `run.waits_threshold` | duration | `3s` | waiting time above which a program is listed among the waits of a checked program |

### 7.7 `[output]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `output.language` | `en`, `pl` | `en` | language of messages and help |
| `output.color` | `auto`, `always`, `never` | `auto` | colours for people |
| `output.head` | integer | `20` | first lines of program output shown in a response |
| `output.tail` | integer | `40` | last lines of program output shown in a response |
| `output.max_bytes` | integer | `4096` | bytes of text of one program output stream shown in a response; `0` is no limit |
| `output.spool_ttl` | duration | `1h` | lifetime of files with complete program output |
| `output.results_dir` | path | none: `results` in the state directory | directory of complete results saved to files |

### 7.8 `[report]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `report.mass_threshold` | integer | `200` | targets from which an operation is reported as a bulk operation |
| `report.diff_max_hunks` | integer | `20` | hunks in the sample of differences |
| `report.diff_max_lines` | integer | `200` | lines in the sample of differences |
| `report.notable.mass_files` | integer | `100` | deleted files from which `mass_delete` is reported |
| `report.notable.mass_bytes` | size | `1gib` | deleted bytes from which `mass_delete` is reported |
| `report.notable.mass_ratio` | number | `0.8` | share of a directory deleted from which `mass_delete` is reported |
| `report.notable.shrink_ratio` | number | `0.5` | share of its size by which a file of at least 1 KiB shrinks from which `size_shrunk` is reported |
| `report.notable.per_file_repl` | integer | `100` | replacements in one file from which `many_per_file` is reported |
| `report.notable.targets_high` | integer | `500` | targets from which `target_count_high` is reported |

### 7.8a `[continuation]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `continuation.max_age` | duration | `1h` | a continuation older than this expires |
| `continuation.max_count` | integer | `50` | most continuations kept; the oldest is removed first |
| `continuation.max_size` | size | `256mib` | most space of all kept results; the oldest is removed first |

Kept results live in the `results` area of the state directory, outside the
journal, and are removed at the end of the session of the console or by these
limits.

### 7.9 `[text]`, `[limits]`, `[fs]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text.legacy_encodings` | list | `windows-1250`, `ibm852`, `iso-8859-2`, `windows-1252` | legacy encodings considered, in order, when a file is not valid UTF-8 |
| `text.new_file_line_ending` | `lf`, `crlf` | `lf` | line ending of new files |
| `limits.max_records` | integer | `5000000` | largest number of records held in memory by one stage; more is an error (`E_LIMIT`), never a silent cut |
| `limits.max_file_bytes_text` | size | `1gib` | largest file read as text |
| `limits.threads` | integer | none: number of processor cores | worker threads |
| `fs.sharing_retry_ms` | integer | `2000` | time of retries after a sharing violation (Windows), in milliseconds |

### 7.9a `[loop]`, `[function]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `loop.max_iterations` | integer | `10000` | largest number of iterations of a `repeat` or `while` without `limit` (an explicit `limit` replaces both loop keys); reaching it ends `repeat` with `E_LIMIT` and `while` normally, and the report says so |
| `loop.max_time` | duration | `10m` | longest time of a `repeat` or `while` without `limit`, with the same outcome |
| `function.max_depth` | integer, 1 to 1024 | `64` | deepest nesting of calls of functions defined with `define`; deeper recursion ends with `E_LIMIT` |

### 7.10 `[code]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code.servers` | table by language | `python`: `pyright-langserver --stdio`; `typescript`, `javascript`: `typescript-language-server --stdio`; `go`: `gopls`; `rust`: `rust-analyzer`; `c`, `cpp`: `clangd` | language servers; each entry has `command` (program and arguments, found in `PATH`) and optional `init` (initialization options) |
| `code.servers_allow` | `all`, `off` or list of languages | `all` | servers that may be started |
| `code.server_idle` | duration | `10m` | time after which an unused server stops |
| `code.server_retry` | duration | `5m` | time before a failed server is started again |
| `code.max_servers` | integer | `4` | servers running at the same time |
| `code.timeout` | duration | `20s` | time limit of a server request |
| `code.timeout_max` | duration | `2m` | largest time limit a command may request |
| `code.index_max_files` | integer | `20000` | largest number of files indexed for syntax analysis |
| `code.file_bytes_max` | size | `1mib` | largest file analysed |
| `code.diagnostics_quiet` | duration | `1500ms` | time without new diagnostics after which diagnostics are complete (at least `50ms`) |

### 7.11 `[documents]`, `[sql]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `documents.max_bytes` | size | `256mib` | largest structured document read |
| `documents.yaml_version` | `1.1`, `1.2` | `1.2` | YAML version of documents without a directive |
| `documents.xml_external_entities` | boolean | `false` | resolve external entities of XML documents |
| `sql.busy_timeout` | duration | `5s` | wait for a locked SQLite database |

### 7.12 `[programs]`, `[http]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `programs.catalogs` | list of paths or tables `{ path, priority, enabled }` | `[]` | external catalogs of programs in the format `nurt-program-catalog/1`; without them the commands describe installed programs |
| `programs.index_dir` | path | none: cache directory of the user | directory of the program index |
| `programs.help_timeout` | duration | `3s` | time limit of reading the help of a program on request |
| `programs.sources_disabled` | list of `path`, `package`, `app`, `man`, `catalog` | `[]` | sources of program information that are not used |
| `http.proxy` | URL | none: system setting | proxy of HTTP requests and Git fetches |

### 7.13 `[git]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `git.trash_refs` | boolean | `false` | keep deleted branches under `refs/nurt/trash/` |
| `git.hooks.timeout` | duration | `10m` | time limit of a repository hook |
| `git.ssh.known_hosts` | `strict`, `accept_new` | `strict` | verification of SSH host keys |
| `git.ssh.identity_files` | list of paths | `[]`: standard identity files | private key files |
| `git.signing.key_file` | path | none | OpenPGP secret key file, imported into a temporary GnuPG home directory for signing commits when the repository configuration does not name a key held by `gpg-agent` |
| `git.signing.openpgp_source` | `gpg_agent`, `key_file` | none: gpg-agent, then the key file | the only holder of the secret key used for OpenPGP signatures; GnuPG (`gpg.openpgp.program` or `gpg.program`) makes the signature in both cases |
| `git.checkpoint.keep` | integer | `50` | checkpoints kept per repository |
| `git.status.limit` | integer | `200` | entries listed by `git.status` before paging |
| `git.network.timeout` | duration | `5m` | time limit of a network operation |

The configuration of a Git repository (for example `user.signingKey`,
`commit.gpgSign`, `http.proxy`, `core.*`) applies as in Git; the keys above
cover only what Git does not define.

### 7.14 `[verify]`, `[ext]`, `[service]`, `[state]`, `[log]`, `[session]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `verify.history_max` | integer | `50` | test runs kept for comparison |
| `ext.dir` | path | none: `ext` in the configuration directory | directory of extensions |
| `ext.native` | boolean | `false` | allow native extension libraries besides WebAssembly |
| `service.mode` | `user`, `system` | `user` | installation mode of the background service; `user` runs for the account (on Linux with lingering enabled), `system` is recommended for servers |
| `state.dir` | path | none: state directory of the operating system | state directory |
| `log.level` | `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace` | `warn` | level of diagnostic logs |
| `session.id` | text | none | session identifier recorded in the journal |
| `session.ttl` | duration | `24h` | time without calls after which session settings (for example limits set by `journal.limits` for a session) expire |

### 7.15 `[privilege]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `privilege.default` | `account`, `elevated`, `auto` | `account` | value of the call parameter `privilege` when a call does not give it; the embedding engine may set it |
| `privilege.allowed` | boolean | `true` | when `false`, `elevated` and `auto` end with `E_PRIVILEGE` and the reason `disabled_by_configuration`; the switch with which the embedding engine applies its policy |
| `privilege.backends` | list of `self`, `broker`, `sudo`, `doas`, `run0` | none: the list of the system | allowed backends in order of trial; the list of the system is `["self", "broker", "sudo", "doas", "run0"]` on Linux, `["self", "broker", "sudo"]` on macOS and `["self", "broker"]` on Windows; `broker` is reported as `not_installed` until the service `nurt-elevation` exists |
| `privilege.group` | text | none: `sudo` or `wheel` (Linux), `admin` (macOS) | group allowed to connect to the service `nurt-elevation` |

A project file cannot set `privilege.*`.

## 8. Interface for implementations

The module `nurt_contracts::config` provides:

| Item | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Config` and its sections | typed configuration with built-in defaults (`Default`) and TOML or JSON deserialization |
| `ConfigLevel` | the seven levels, in increasing precedence |
| `allowed_at(level, key)` | the rule of section 3 as a pure function |
| `ConfigLayer`, `resolve(layers, project_trusted)` | merging of levels with admission, notes and the level of each key |
| `trusted_projects(layers)` | trusted projects from the levels that may declare trust |
| `env_layer(vars, separator)` | the environment level built from process variables |
| `known_keys()`, `ENV_VARS` | every key and every variable of the format |
| `PROJECT_FLOOR_MAX_OPS`, `PROJECT_FLOOR_MAX_AGE` | floors of values from project files |

The conformance tests in `crates/nurt-contracts/tests/config_*.rs` check the
defaults against `spec/golden/config/defaults.toml`, the generated schema
against the approved file, every golden file against the schema, the
precedence of the seven levels for the three retention limits, the trust
rules and the environment level.

title: Error codes
text:
# Error codes

Every error of the language has a stable code written in upper case with the prefix `E_`, a message and, where known, the stage, the position in the program and ready replacements of the program text. Errors of the stages `parse` and `bind` have no effect on the world: they describe a mistake in the program and how to correct it, never a refusal. Codes are only added within a major version of the language; the meaning of a code never changes.

The list of codes below, the enumeration `ErrorCode` of the crate `nurt-contracts` and the definition `ErrorCode` of the schema `nurt-value-1.schema.json` are the same; a test of the crate compares them, and another test checks that every code mentioned in the specification and in the documentation is in the list.

## Error object

The error is the member `error` of the effect report. Members other than `code` and `message` are present only when they have a value.

| Member | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | text | Stable code from the table below. |
| `message` | text | Message in English, one or two sentences. |
| `at` | object | Position of the error: `stage`, the stage in which the error occurred (`0` to `7` or `5a`), and the place in the program, `line`, `column` and `length`, counted in Unicode scalar values from 1. Errors raised while a stage runs carry `stage` without a place in the program. |
| `location` | object | Position in a data file: `path`, `line`, `column`, `end_line`, `end_column`, `byte`. |
| `found` | text | The fragment that was found, for example the name of an unsupported construct. |
| `problem` | text | Short name of the specific problem, for example `not_merged`. |
| `fix` | list of text | Ready replacements of the program text, best first. |
| `help` | text | Help topic with the rules that apply. |
| `expected` | any | What was expected: names, types, counts or hashes; up to eight nearest names for unknown names. |
| `actual` | any | What was found instead. |
| `sample` | list of text | Sample of the records or paths concerned. |
| `candidates` | list of objects | Ranked ready programs: `rank`, `ref` (identifier for `accept`), `program`, `why`. |
| `next_steps` | list of text | Further calls that complete the task, for example the parts of a split program. |
| `effect_applied` | bool | The effect of the program is in the world despite the error, as after a failed assertion in stage `5a` or a merge with conflicts; absent when false. |
| `details` | object | Data specific to the code, for example `path`, `os_error`, `holders` of a file in use, `partial_read` of a failed stage, `released` items of a partial journal entry. |
| `cause` | object | Error that caused this one, in the same form. |

## Stages

| Stage | Name | Effect in the world |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | `parse` | none |
| `1` | `bind` | none |
| `2` | `read` | reads only |
| `3` | `check` | none; a failed assertion changes nothing |
| `4` | `plan` | none; a preview ends here |
| `5` | `apply` | the change, recorded in the journal |
| `5a` | `after` | none; stages on the records of the effect, the effect stays |
| `6` | `verify` | a failed verification rolls the effect back |
| `7` | `report` | none |

## Status of the C interface

Functions of the C interface that return a response document (`nurt_run_json`, `nurt_check`, `nurt_parse`, `nurt_correct`, `nurt_exec_wait`, `nurt_page`, `nurt_history`, `nurt_space`) return `NURT_OK` for every language error and carry the error in the document. Functions without a response document, such as `nurt_engine_open`, `nurt_print` and `nurt_ext_load`, return the status in the column `C status` and give the error object through `nurt_last_error`. `NURT_E_ABI` is reserved for a mismatch of interface versions; no language error maps to it. Codes with the status `NURT_OK` occur only in calls that return a response document.

## Codes

| Code | Stages | C status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `E_LEXICAL` | 0 | `NURT_E_ARG` | A token is not valid: an unknown character, an unterminated text or a malformed number, size or duration. |
| `E_ESCAPE` | 0 | `NURT_E_ARG` | An escape sequence in a text is not valid; the help shows the accepted escapes and the raw text form. |
| `E_SYNTAX` | 0 | `NURT_E_ARG` | The program does not follow the grammar. |
| `E_AMBIGUOUS` | 0, 1 | `NURT_E_ARG` | A correction is possible but touches a target of a change; `candidates` lists ranked ready programs. |
