title: Effect report and request envelope
text:
# Effect report and request envelope

| Format | Schema | Rust types |
|---|---|---|
| `nurt-report/1`, the effect report of one program | `schemas/nurt-report-1.schema.json` | `nurt_contracts::report` |
| `nurt-request/1`, the request envelope | `schemas/nurt-request-1.schema.json` | `nurt_contracts::envelope::Request` |
| `nurt-response/1`, the response to a request | `$defs/response` of the request schema | `nurt_contracts::envelope::Response` |

All three are JSON documents in UTF-8; CBOR is an equivalent encoding. Each
carries a version `"nurt": "MAJOR.MINOR"`, currently `"1.0"`. Within major
version 1 the formats only gain optional fields and new values of the code
enumerations; a reader ignores report fields it does not know. The product
name never appears in the output of a program.

## 1. Principles of the report

1. The report shows the effect, not the fact that something ran: targets,
   changed and deleted files with their number and total size, sizes and
   hashes before and after, a sample of differences, a summary of bulk
   operations, and unusual effects.
2. The report carries the operation number `op` and nothing else about the
   journal. No field, flag or sentence of the report states whether, how or
   until when an operation can be undone; there is no journal state and no
   expiry. The state of journal entries is shown only by an explicit
   `history` query. The report of `undo` and `redo` is an ordinary effect
   report.
3. `irreversible` is present only when an effect is irreversible. Its absence
   carries no information about undo.
4. `notable` describes unusual effects. It never blocks anything; policy
   belongs to the caller.
5. Lists are omitted when empty and optional fields when absent, so that the
   report of an ordinary effect stays short.

## 2. Report fields

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `nurt` | text, required | format version `1.<minor>` |
| `status` | code, required | outcome, section 3 |
| `kind` | text, required | the changing command, or the source command of a reading program (`replace`, `remove`, `run`, `find`); `request` for envelope errors detected before any program is known |
| `op` | integer from 1 | journal entry of the operation; absent for reading programs, previews and changing programs without targets |
| `ran` | text | canonical text of the program that ran; present only when corrections were applied |
| `elevated` | `true` | present only when the operation ran with elevated rights |
| `backend` | `self`, `broker`, `sudo`, `doas`, `run0` | elevation backend that ran the operation; present only with `elevated` |
| `as_user` | text | account the operation ran as, when the call gave `as_user` |
| `elevation_reason` | `permission_denied`, `elevated_entry` | why the operation was elevated without being asked to: `privilege: auto` repeated the stage after a denial, or `undo` or `redo` of an elevated entry was sent to a backend |
| `ast_hash` | `sha256:<64 hex>` | hash of the syntax tree, see `syntax-tree.md` |
| `result_file` | path | file holding the full result (UTF-8) when the result was written to a file (`save_to` or `output.results_dir`) |
| `corrections` | list | corrections applied to the program text: `id`, `rule` (`L`, `T`, `V`, `B` or `P` and two digits), `class` (`C`, `S`, `F`, `P`), `at` (`line`, `column`, `length`), `from`, `to`, `kind`, `alternatives` |
| `targets` | object | `count` (required), `files`, `directories`, `bytes`, `listed` (number of entries of `changes` on this page) |
| `summary` | object | `files_created`, `files_modified`, `files_deleted`, `files_renamed`, `directories_created`, `directories_deleted`, `replacements`, `lines_added`, `lines_removed`, `bytes_before`, `bytes_after`, `bytes_freed` |
| `changes` | list | changed targets on this page, section 5 |
| `diff` | list | hunks of unified differences: `path`, `raw_path`, `old_start`, `old_len`, `new_start`, `new_len`, `lines` (prefix `+`, `-` or space, or the marker line `\ No newline at end of file`), `header` |
| `bulk` | object | summary of a bulk operation: `by_directory` and `by_extension` (largest first, with `count` and `bytes`; a directory that is not valid Unicode also has `raw_directory`), `sample_head`, `sample_tail` (and `raw_sample_head`, `raw_sample_tail` when a sampled target is not valid Unicode) |
| `exec` | record `exec` | a program that ran |
| `job` | record `job` | a program that continues in the background; present when the status is `running` |
| `test` | record `test_run` | a test run |
| `analysis` | record `analysis` | an analysis verdict |
| `git` | record `git_effect` | the effect on a repository |
| `records` | object | result of a reading program: `type` (record type), `matched`, `header` (header record of a stream), `rows` |
| `notable` | list | unusual effects in descending order of severity, section 6 |
| `irreversible` | non-empty list | irreversible effects, section 7 |
| `error` | object | error of the language, section 8 |
| `next_cursor` | text | cursor of the next page; absent on the last page |
| `continuation` | object | what a shortened response leaves out and how `next` reads it, section 2.1 |
| `timing` | object | `parse_ms`, `read_ms`, `plan_ms`, `apply_ms` (verbosity `detailed`) |
| `parts` | list | the parts of a control construct in order, section 2.1 |
| `parts_total` | integer | number of parts when `parts` is shortened to the first 200 |

### 2.1 Parts of a control construct

A program that holds a control construct (`when`, `each`, `repeat`, `while`,
`steps`, a call of a function) is one operation and one journal entry; `op`
is the number of the entry and `kind` the word of the construct. The report
lists the parts in order in `parts`, each with:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `at` | place of the part: `when`, `when.branch[2]`, `each.iteration[3]`, `steps.step[1]`, `call rotate.step[2]` |
| `kind` | `branch` (the chosen branch), `iteration`, `step`, `loop` (the totals of a loop) |
| `condition` | value of the condition of the chosen branch; `false` when no branch ran |
| `branch` | number of the chosen branch from 1; the `otherwise` branch is one past the last condition |
| `command` | command whose effect the step reports |
| `targets` | number of targets the part changed |
| `ok` | `false` for the part that failed |
| `rolled_back` | the effects of the part were rolled back (parts that failed or were undone by the failure of a later part) |
| `irreversible` | the effects of the part cannot be rolled back; they are listed in `irreversible` |
| `error` | code of the error that ended the part |
| `iterations` | number of iterations of a `loop` part |
| `op` | journal entry of an iteration of a loop with `atomic: false` |
| `note` | remark: the limit ended the loop, a preview plans one iteration |

When a part fails the whole construct is rolled back: the status is
`rolled_back`, `error.details.restored` lists what was restored and
`error.details.not_rolled_back` lists the parts the catalog marks irreversible.
`parallel: N` of `each` reads every iteration twice, once to find its targets and once to run it, and compares paths by components, both separators and without regard to case; only the reading and planning of the iterations run at the same time, their changes are applied one at a time inside the one transaction. It runs iterations at the same time only when their targets are disjoint, found by planning every iteration before the start; otherwise the iterations run in order and the `loop` part says so in `note`. With `preview: true` a `repeat` or a `while` plans one iteration (the number of iterations is known only by running, `note` says so) and an `each` plans every iteration; the status is `planned`, `changes` lists the effects of
every part and nothing is changed. A loop with `atomic: false` keeps the
iterations completed before a failure, each in its own entry (`op` of the
part); the report names the failed iteration.

Records (`exec`, `job`, `test`, `analysis`, `git`, `records.header` and
`records.rows`) appear in their JSON form defined by the value and record
formats; the report schema does not restrict their fields. Domain results that
do not fit the common fields are carried by a record in a named optional
field; a new domain adds a new optional field of the same kind.

Fields marked `x-nurt-volatile` in the schema (`op`, `result_file`,
`next_cursor`, `timing`) differ between runs of the same program and are
ignored when reports are compared.

### 2.1 Continuation of a shortened response

Every response that leaves out lines, records, bytes or the end of long lines
carries the field `continuation`:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | short identifier, `c1`, `c2`, … within the session of the console |
| `unit` | `lines`, `records`, `bytes` | unit of the parts |
| `shown` | int | units in the responses given so far |
| `remaining` | int | units not yet given; `-1` when not known in advance (a query that continues after a cursor, such as `logs`) |
| `cut_lines` | int | lines of the shown part that were shortened by `max_line` or `max_chars` |

The one-line text of the response ends with `more: next` when the
continuation is the latest one and with `more: next c3` otherwise. The
command `next` returns the next part and never computes the result again.
The notices `truncated_lines` and `limit_reached` stay and gain the optional
field `continuation`: the identifier (`c3`) of the continuation of the
response, absent when nothing continues. The sentence `read_hint` of
the record `exec` no longer exists: the spool file of a run stays, its path
stays in the record (`output_file`, `stdout_file`, `stderr_file`) and the
continuation reads the lines left out of that file. A result that is a
selection of lines (`show: errors`) is continued from the first line of the
file. Kept results are bound by the keys `continuation.max_age`,
`continuation.max_count` and `continuation.max_size`; a continuation that
expired ends with `E_CONTINUATION_EXPIRED`.

## 3. Status

| Status | Meaning | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | the program finished; a changing program applied its effect | may carry `error` for a check that failed after the effect was applied; the effect remains |
| `planned` | preview (`preview: true`): targets and effect computed, nothing changed | no `op` |
| `running` | a program started in the background is still running | `job` required |
| `partial` | the effect was applied to part of the targets, for example the undo of a bulk entry whose preserved content was partly released to free disk space | `op` required; `irreversible` or `error` lists the rest |
| `rolled_back` | the effect was applied and reverted because a later check failed | `error` required (`E_ROLLED_BACK` with `cause`) |
| `failed` | the program stopped with an error | `error` required |

A program stopped by its time limit, by a resource limit or by cancellation
ends with `failed` and the error `E_TIMEOUT`, `E_LIMIT` or `E_CANCELLED`.

## 4. Verbosity

| Level | Content |
|---|---|
| `quiet` | `status`, `op`, `targets`, `summary`, `notable`, `irreversible`; no changes and no differences |
| `normal` (default) | `summary`, changes up to `limit` (default 50), a sample of differences up to `report.diff_max_hunks` (20) hunks and `report.diff_max_lines` (200) lines, `bulk` for bulk operations |
| `detailed` | all changes and differences, paged through the cursor, and `timing` |

An operation is a bulk operation from `report.mass_threshold` (200) targets.
At level `normal` it shows the totals, the ten largest directories and
extensions, five targets from the start and two from the end, and `notable`.
The full list of targets is always available through the cursor; nothing is
hidden.

## 5. Changes

| `action` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `create` | target created |
| `modify` | content changed |
| `delete` | target deleted |
| `rename` | target renamed or moved; `path` is the path after the change, `from` is the previous path (required) and `to` repeats `path` |
| `attributes` | mode, ownership or access control changed |
| `link` | link created or changed |
| `truncate` | target truncated |
| `state` | state of a target outside the file system changed; `path` is `<provider>:<name>` (for example `service:nginx`), `before` and `after` hold the states |

`flags` carries additional markers of a change, for example `crlf` or
`keys_created`.

A path that is not valid Unicode is written with U+FFFD in `path`, `from` and
`to`; the change then also has the native bytes in `raw_path`, `raw_from` and
`raw_to` (standard base64), as described for paths in `records.md`.

## 6. Unusual effects (`notable`)

Each entry is `{code, severity, path?, raw_path?, count?, detail?}`; `raw_path`
holds the native bytes of `path` when it is not valid Unicode; entries are sorted
by severity, `alert` first. Severities in increasing order: `info`, `notice`,
`warning`, `alert`. The table gives the default severity; thresholds are
configured under `report.notable.*`. Codes with source "report" are derived by
the report builder from the changes; all other codes are emitted by the
command that observed the condition.

| Code | Default | Source | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outside_project` | alert | report | target outside every directory of `scope.project_roots` (when set) |
| `system_path` | alert | report | target in a system directory |
| `home_config` | warning | report | configuration in the home directory (`~/.ssh`, `~/.config`, shell profiles) |
| `mass_delete` | warning, alert at ten times the threshold | report | deleted files from `mass_files` (100), bytes from `mass_bytes` (1 GiB) or share from `mass_ratio` (80%) |
| `delete_tree` | notice | report | recursive deletion of a non-empty directory |
| `overwrote_existing` | warning | report | existing files replaced by a write, move or copy |
| `file_emptied` | warning | report | a file with content became empty |
| `size_shrunk` | warning | report | size shrank by `shrink_ratio` (50%, files from 1 KiB) or more |
| `many_per_file` | notice | report | `per_file_repl` (100) or more replacements in one file |
| `target_count_high` | notice | report | `targets_high` (500) or more targets |
| `nothing_matched` | notice | report | a changing stage received no targets; never for `run`, which has no targets to select |
| `unchanged` | info | command | a write produced identical content |
| `binary_target` | warning | command | a binary file was changed |
| `binary_skipped` | notice | command | binary files were skipped (`count`) |
| `special_file` | warning | command | a device, pipe, socket or pseudo file was written |
| `symlink_followed` | warning | command | a change went through a symbolic link to a target outside its directory |
| `hardlink_broken` | notice | command | a file with several hard links was replaced, separating the links |
| `hardlink_set_preserved` | info | command | a file with several hard links was written in place, keeping the links |
| `attributes_changed` | notice | command | mode, ownership or access control changed |
| `encoding_preserved`, `line_ending_preserved` | info | command | the file kept an encoding other than UTF-8 or line endings other than `lf` |
| `line_ending_mixed` | notice | command | mixed line endings |
| `encoding_changed`, `line_ending_changed`, `bom_changed` | notice | command | the encoding, the line endings or the byte order mark was converted |
| `truncated_lines` | notice | command | long lines were shortened in the output |
| `regex_backtracking` | warning | command | a regular expression hit the backtracking limit |
| `decompressed` | info | command | compressed content was decompressed transparently |
| `cross_device` | notice | command | a move between volumes, performed as copy and delete |
| `to_is_dir` | notice | command | the destination of a move or copy is an existing directory |
| `case_collision`, `case_alias`, `nfd_name` | notice | command | names differing in letter case collide; a name matched in another letter case or normalization form |
| `portability` | notice | command | a name not portable between systems |
| `external_volume` | notice | command | a target on a network or removable volume |
| `archive_path_escape` | warning | command | archive entries outside the destination were skipped |
| `permission_denied_skipped` | warning | command | files without read permission were skipped |
| `link_loop_skipped` | notice | command | a symbolic link leading back to one of its parent directories was not followed |
| `ignored` | info | command | changes in paths excluded from tracking (`run.track_ignore`) |
| `alias_shared` | warning | command | a node referenced by aliases was changed |
| `keys_created` | info | command | intermediate keys were created |
| `duplicate_key` | warning | command | a repeated key; the last occurrence was changed |
| `semantic_fallback` | notice | command | a code operation fell back to syntax analysis |
| `references_left` | notice | command | textual references to the old name remain |
| `rename_incomplete` | warning | command | a rename did not reach every reference |
| `detection_scope` | info | command | after `run`: changes outside `watch` are not detected; with `track_changes: auto` the note also names the directories of other file systems that were not entered, or, when detection was skipped (file system root, more than 200 000 entries, a scan longer than 3 s), the reason and what to do |
| `exit_nonzero` | notice | command | a program exited with a code other than zero; `count` holds the code |
| `post_stages_deferred` | info | command | stages after the effect were skipped because the program moved to the background |
| `rollback_partial` | warning | command | a rollback restored only part of the changes |
| `output_binary` | notice | command | a program wrote binary output |
| `spool_limit` | warning | command | program output exceeded the spool limit |
| `stdin_closed_early` | info | command | a program closed its input early |
| `job_lost` | warning | command | a background job lost its supervisor |
| `tool_missing` | notice | command | a requested analysis tool is not installed |
| `tests_none` | notice | command | no tests were found or run |
| `trust_config_ignored` | warning | command | trust settings in a project configuration file were ignored; a project cannot make itself trusted |
| `project_config_ignored` | notice | command | keys of a project configuration file outside the keys allowed for projects were ignored |
| `journal_config_ignored` | notice | command | journal settings of an untrusted project were ignored |
| `journal_oversize` | warning | command | the operation exceeds the journal size limit; shown by the preview before the change |
| `source_unavailable` | warning | command | a data source of the operating system was unavailable; results are incomplete |
| `settings_broadcast` | notice | command | a settings change was broadcast to running programs |
| `hooks_skipped` | notice | command | repository hooks were not run |
| `history_rewritten` | warning | command | repository history was rewritten |
| `force_push` | alert | command | a remote branch was overwritten |
| `detached_head` | notice | command | detached head state |
| `branch_deleted_unmerged` | warning | command | an unmerged branch was deleted |
| `fast_forward` | info | command | a branch was updated by fast-forward |
| `conflicts` | warning | command | the operation stopped with conflicts (`count`) |
| `untracked_removed` | warning | command | untracked files were removed |
| `local_changes_carried` | info | command | uncommitted changes were carried to another branch |
| `filter_not_applied` | warning | command | a content filter of the repository was not applied |
| `credential_helper_ignored`, `ssh_command_ignored`, `fsmonitor_ignored`, `signing_program_ignored` | notice | command | a program named by the repository configuration was not run |
| `submodules_not_updated` | notice | command | submodules were not updated |
| `sparse_checkout`, `shallow_repository` | info | command | the repository uses sparse checkout or shallow history |
| `line_endings_converted` | info | command | line endings converted by repository settings |
| `upstream_set` | info | command | an upstream branch was set |
| `stash_kept` | notice | command | a stash entry was kept after a conflict |
| `signed` | info | command | a commit or tag was signed |
| `amend_published` | alert | command | the amended commit is reachable from a remote-tracking branch |
| `commit_detached_head` | warning | command | a commit was created on a detached `HEAD` |
| `operation_in_progress` | warning | command | a commit was created while a rebase, cherry-pick, revert or bisection is in progress |
| `excluded` | info | command | files matched by `exclude` were skipped (`count`) |
| `review_skipped` | notice | command | files were not reviewed: untracked files over the size limit, binary files or files over the count limit |
| `checkpoint_without_index` | notice | command | a checkpoint was created without the index because the index has conflicts |
| `tls_verification_disabled` | warning | command | verification of TLS certificates is disabled by the repository configuration |
| `http_option_ignored` | notice | command | an unsupported HTTP setting of the repository configuration was ignored |
| `pack_without_deltas` | info | command | a push sent objects without new delta compression |
| `push_status_unknown` | warning | command | the remote did not report the outcome of a reference update |
| `host_key_unverified` | warning | command | the host key of a remote was accepted without verification |
| `match_exec_ignored` | notice | command | a `Match exec` condition of the SSH configuration was not run |
| `credentials_in_url` | warning | command | credentials written in the URL of a remote were used |
| `limit_reached` | info | command | the output stopped at the number of entries given by `limit` (`count` holds the number of entries left out) |
| `interactive_program` | notice | command | a program classified as interactive was run (editor, pager, terminal monitor, interpreter without a script); it can wait for terminal input |
| `opaque_script` | notice | command | a program ran a script given in its arguments (`bash -c`, `python -c`); the effects of the script are not classified |

## 7. Irreversible effects (`irreversible`)

Each entry is `{reason, path?, raw_path?, count?, detail?}`; `raw_path` holds the
native bytes of `path` when it is not valid Unicode.

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `external_effect` | a program with an effect outside the local file system was run (publishing, deployment, remote shells) |
| `remote_ref_updated` | references of a remote repository were updated or fetched |
| `network` | a network request that changes remote state was sent |
| `database` | a database was changed without a preserved copy |
| `process_stopped` | a process or job was stopped |
| `service_changed` | a system service was started, restarted, enabled, disabled or stopped |
| `package_changed` | system packages were installed, removed or upgraded |
| `previous_content_not_kept` | a program changed a file whose previous content was not preserved; `detail` gives the cause, for example the time budget or a file system without block sharing |
| `no_space_for_copy` | no space for a copy of the previous content; the change was made directly |
| `journal_inactive` | the journal is disabled or its space service is not running |
| `network_volume`, `removable_volume` | the target is on such a volume, which has no journal by default |
| `purged` | journal entries were purged |
| `special_file` | a device, pipe, socket or pseudo file was written |
| `too_large_for_journal` | the operation is larger than the limit for one journal entry |
| `released_for_space` | preserved content of part of a bulk operation was released to free disk space |
| `job_output_removed` | the kept output of a background job was removed together with the job |
| `process_state_changed` | the state of a running process was changed: suspended, resumed, signalled or given another priority |
| `journal_entries_expired` | journal entries of earlier operations expired because of this operation, for example when the journal limits were lowered |
| `journal_error` | the journal failed while recording the operation; the change was made without preserved previous content |

## 8. Errors

`error` is `{code, message, at?, location?, found?, problem?, fix?, help?,
expected?, actual?, sample?, candidates?, next_steps?, effect_applied?,
details?, cause?}`. `at` is `{line?, column?, length?, stage?}`: `stage` is the
execution stage as text (`"0"` to `"7"`, `"5a"`), and `line`, `column` and
`length` give the place in the program text when the error has one. The list of
codes is part of the schema (`$defs/error_code`); every code defined by the
error contract is listed there, and a test keeps the two in step. The error
structure itself is specified together with the error codes; the report
schema allows additional error fields.

Errors before any effect leave the world unchanged and come with a ready fix.
A check that fails after the effect was applied, for example `assert
exit_code: 0` after `run`, is reported with status `ok` and the error; the
effect remains.

## 9. Request envelope (`nurt-request/1`)

```json
{
  "nurt": "1.0",
  "program": "find \"/srv/app/src\" glob: \"**/*.go\"",
  "variant": "a",
  "options": { "limit": 20, "verbosity": "normal" }
}
```

Exactly one input is given:

| Input | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `program`, with optional `variant` | program text in notation `a`, `b` or `c`; without `variant` the configured variant applies |
| `ast` | surface syntax tree `nurt-ast/1` |
| `cursor` | cursor of a further page of an earlier result; reading a page never runs a changing program again |
| `accept` | identifier of a candidate from an earlier `E_AMBIGUOUS` error |

The member `params` accompanies `program` or `ast`: an object with the values of the parameters declared by the program with `params { … }`. A value is typed JSON or, as the command line passes it, text that the declared type reads (`"7"` for `int`, `"10mb"` for `size`). A name that is not declared is `E_UNKNOWN_PARAM` with the nearest names, a missing required parameter is `E_MISSING_PARAM` and a value of the wrong type is `E_TYPE`; every error lists the declaration and nothing has run.

A condition of a construct is checked at binding against the types declared by the output record of the source command: a use of a field that no value of its type satisfies is `E_TYPE` with `effect_applied: false`. Fields typed `any` or `json` are the only exception and are checked when the condition is evaluated. A stage that may change the world (`may_affect`) and takes its action from a value that is not a literal is `E_TYPE` at binding in a condition.

Options (`options`) are shared by every command. An absent option takes its
value from the configuration, and without a configured value from the default
below. Options of the call override the configuration.

| Option | Type and default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `preview` | bool, `false` | compute targets and effect only; change nothing |
| `base` | absolute path | directory against which relative paths are resolved; not a current directory |
| `limit` | 1 to 5000, `50` | records or changes per page |
| `fields` | list of text | fields of the result to keep |
| `format` | `text`, `json`, `markdown` or `compact`, `text` | form of the result |
| `verbosity` | `quiet`, `normal` or `detailed`, `normal` | level of detail of the report |
| `diff` | `none`, `stat` or `unified`, `unified` | form of differences |
| `diff_context` | int, `3` | context lines of differences |
| `max_chars` | int, `0` | largest number of characters of one text field; `0` means no limit; shortened fields are marked `truncated: true` |
| `save_to` | absolute path | file that receives the full result; the report gives `result_file` |
| `timeout` | duration, `120s` | time limit of the whole program, for example `250ms`, `30s`, `5m`, `1h30m` or `7d` |
| `session` | text | session identifier recorded in the journal |
| `language` | `en` or `pl`, `en` | language of messages and help; codes, fields and keywords are always English |
| `script` | bool, `false` | several pipelines, each its own operation |

Unknown fields are rejected in the envelope and in `options`: a misspelt
option is never ignored. Paths are absolute in canonical notation: `/srv/app`,
`C:/proj`, `//server/share` or a provider path such as `registry:/HKCU`.

An envelope that is not valid JSON or does not match the schema is a call
error of the interface (`NURT_E_ARG` of the C interface). An envelope that
matches the schema but breaks a rule of the envelope, for example two inputs
at once, is answered with a report of status `failed` and the error `E_ARG`.

## 10. Response (`nurt-response/1`)

```json
{
  "nurt": "1.0",
  "report": { "nurt": "1.0", "status": "ok", "kind": "remove", "op": 21 },
  "rendered": { "format": "text", "text": "op 21  remove  ok\n" }
}
```

The report is always present. `rendered` holds the text in the requested
format for `text`, `markdown` and `compact`; it is absent for `json`, where
the report is the result. A further page exists when `report.next_cursor` is
present. `nurt_run_json`, the `run` and `page` methods of `nurt serve` and the
`nurt` tool of the integrations return this document.

### 10.1 Script with several pipelines

A script (option `script`) whose execution ran more than one operation keeps
the result of every pipeline. The response then holds `reports`, an array
with one report per executed pipeline, in program order:

```json
{
  "nurt": "1.0",
  "report": { "nurt": "1.0", "status": "ok", "kind": "remove", "op": 21 },
  "reports": [
    { "nurt": "1.0", "status": "ok", "kind": "find",
      "records": { "type": "row", "rows": [ { "value": 3 } ] } },
    { "nurt": "1.0", "status": "ok", "kind": "remove", "op": 21,
      "changes": [] }
  ]
}
```

- Each report of `reports` carries the `kind` of its own pipeline (the last
  effect command of the pipeline, else its source command), the status and the
  error of its own operation, and its own changes, notable and irreversible
  effects, `op` and records.
- `report` is the report of the whole program. Its `kind` is the last effect
  command of the program, else the source command of the first pipeline. It
  carries the changes, notable and irreversible effects and the error of every
  operation, but no records, because the records belong to the report of their
  pipeline.
- A script stops at the first operation that ends with an error; `reports`
  then ends with the report of that operation.
- `rendered` holds the text of `report` followed by the text of every report
  of `reports`, each starting on a new line.
- The reports of `reports` are not paged and carry no `next_cursor`; the
  paging and the result file (`save_to`) apply to `report`.
- A program with a single operation has no `reports`; its `report` carries the
  records as before.

## 11. Conformance

The directory `golden/report/` holds reports for every status, for every group
of error codes, for a bulk operation and for reports with unusual and
irreversible effects; `golden/request/` holds envelopes for every input and
`golden/request/response/` holds responses. Every golden file validates
against the published schema and against the schema generated from the Rust
types, and survives JSON and CBOR round trips unchanged. The generated schemas
are kept as approved snapshots in `golden/report/schema/` and
`golden/request/schema/`.

title: Shared services
text:
# Shared services

Command crates depend only on `nurt-contracts`. When a command of one group
needs a capability implemented by another group, it calls a service trait
from `nurt_contracts::services`. The engine registers the implementations
once, in a `Services` registry carried by the execution context. An engine
configured for the running process (`EngineConfig::system`) registers the
services of every group of the build that the embedding application did not
supply itself: documents, source code, the process host, the file listing
(when the engine has a file system), repository queries, the text codec and
the file holders. The review rule provider has no implementation of its own.

A missing service is never an error by itself. It means the group that
provides it is not loaded; the calling command applies the fallback listed
below and, where the result is affected, reports it in the effect report.

## Services

| Trait | Provided by | Used by | Without the service |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DocService` | documents group | `read key:`, `write format:`, `validate` on documents, test and analysis commands that read configuration files | `read key:` and `write format:` fail with `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING`; `validate` is skipped with a note |
| `CodeService` | code group | `read symbol:`, `read view: outline \| symbols`, `search mode: syntax`, `search scope:`, `search enclosing:`, `validate` on source code, reference checks of `remove`, `rename` and `replace`, `info details: symbols`, `git.diff symbol:`, `git.log symbol:`, `analyze.check checks: complexity, duplication` | `view:` falls back to the full content with a note; `scope:` other than `any`, `symbol:` and `mode: syntax` fail with `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING`; reference checks are textual; git commands use the function context rules of git |
| `ProcessHost` | run group | language server client, git hooks, service and package managers | the language server client reports `source: syntax`; hooks and managers fail with `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` |
| `FileListService` | file commands | repository-wide code commands (`code.symbols`, `code.references`, `code.profile`) | the code group walks the tree with the same exclusions on its own |
| `GitQueryService` | git group | `code.profile` hot spots, `code.diagnostics changed:`, `info details: git`, `analyze.* changed_only` | the dependent fields are empty; `changed: true` fails with `E_EXTERNAL_MISSING` |
| `TextCodecService` | text group | document and code commands that decode or encode files | UTF-8 and UTF-16 with a byte order mark only |
| `FileHolderService` | system group | the file layer (`E_IN_USE` lists holders), `open_files` | `E_IN_USE` without holders |
| `ReviewRuleProvider` | engine or extension | `git.review checks: [secrets]` | built-in rules only |

## Common rules

1. Every trait is object safe, `Send` and `Sync`, and is used as
   `&dyn Trait`. Handles of running processes (`ServiceChild`) are `Send`
   only: they have one user at a time.
2. Methods are synchronous. Long work is bounded by the caller: the process
   host takes the cancellation token of the stage; the other services work on
   bytes that are already in memory.
3. The document and code services never read files. The caller reads the file
   through the file layer and passes the bytes, so the same methods check
   content that is not yet written (`validate`) and run on virtual file
   systems in tests.
4. Errors use the contract error type. A service never returns an error for an
   ordinary negative answer: a key that selects nothing is an empty list, a
   program that exits with a non-zero code is an outcome.
5. Positions are given twice: as byte ranges (zero-based, end exclusive) for
   editing, and as one-based lines and columns counted in Unicode scalar
   values for records.

## Document service

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `formats()` | formats with their file name extensions and whether keys can be changed with layout preserved |
| `detect_format(path, bytes)` | format from the file name and content; `None` for unstructured content |
| `read_keys(bytes, format, key, depth)` | values selected by a key path, as `DocItem` (canonical concrete key, value, region, comment, document index, YAML anchor, alias and tag) |
| `check_syntax(bytes, format)` | syntax issues; an empty list means the content parses |
| `serialize_records(records, format, options)` | records written as a document (`write format: json \| yaml \| toml \| csv \| tsv`) |

Format identifiers are lowercase (`json`, `jsonc`, `yaml`, `toml`, `xml`,
`ini`, `csv`, `tsv`, `properties`, `env`, `plist`); extensions may add more.
Changing documents is not part of the service: `set`, and `remove` or
`replace` on `item` records, belong to the documents group and are dispatched
by record type.

## Code service

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `languages()` | languages with a grammar |
| `language_of(path, bytes)` | language from the file name and content |
| `outline(bytes, language, depth)` | symbols in source order with nesting depth |
| `find_symbol(bytes, language, name)` | definitions of a name; `Container.name` narrows the container; several results mean the name is ambiguous |
| `enclosing(bytes, language, offset)` | innermost symbol containing a byte |
| `classify_spans(bytes, language)` | comment and string regions; the rest is code |
| `check_syntax(bytes, language)` | syntax errors |
| `compile_pattern(pattern, language)` | structural pattern with metavariables `$X` and `$$$X`, as an opaque `SyntaxPattern` |
| `syntax_search(bytes, pattern)` | matches with captures |
| `render_template(match, template)` | replacement text with captures substituted |
| `references(bytes, language, name)` | occurrences of an identifier with role and lexical class |
| `function_metrics(bytes, language)` | lines, parameters, cyclomatic complexity and nesting per function |
| `tokens(bytes, language)` | tokens for duplicate detection |

A language without a grammar fails with `E_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE`; a pattern
that does not parse in the language fails with `E_PATTERN_SYNTAX`. Searches
across a repository combine `FileListService` with per-file calls.

## Process host

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `resolve_program(program, cwd)` | program file as `run` would find it |
| `run_program(spec, cancel)` | run to completion with captured output, time limit, cancellation and optional detection of changed files |
| `spawn_service(spec)` | long-running helper with piped standard streams in its own process group or job object |

Programs follow the rules of `run`: arguments as a list without a shell,
lookup in `PATH` (and `PATHEXT` on Windows), batch files started through the
command interpreter with every argument quoted, no terminal, and the whole
process tree stopped on timeout, cancellation or `kill_tree`.

## File listing

`walk(spec)` lists entries under a root with the parameters and defaults of
`find`: globs (default `**`), entry kind (default files), depth, hidden
entries (default included), symbolic links (default not followed), ignore
files (default off), exclusions in gitignore syntax and named exclusion groups
`vcs`, `deps`, `build`, `cache`. `WalkSpec::source_tree` is the request used by
repository-wide code analysis: ignore files on and `vcs`, `deps`, `cache`
excluded.

## Registry

`Services` is built with `with_doc`, `with_code`, `with_process_host`,
`with_file_list`, `with_git_query`, `with_text_codec`, `with_file_holders` and
`with_review_rules`. The accessors of the same names (`doc()`, `code()`, …)
return `Option<&dyn Trait>`; `available()` lists the registered services by
their stable names (`doc`, `code`, `process_host`, `file_list`, `git_query`,
`text_codec`, `file_holders`, `review_rules`).

title: Stage interface
text:
# Stage interface

This document specifies how a command of the Nurt language is implemented
and executed. The Rust form of the contract is the module `stage` of the crate
`nurt-contracts`; clock and host facts are in the module `env`. An
implementation of the language in another programming language follows the
same steps and the same rules.

## 1. Execution steps

A pipeline is executed in fixed steps. Steps 0 to 4 have no effect in the
world. The step number appears in error positions as text.

| Step | Name | What happens | Effect in the world |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0` | parse | text is corrected and parsed into the surface tree | none |
| `1` | bind | the surface tree is bound to the catalog; static checks of every stage | none |
| `2` | read | sources and transforms produce records; file records carry `etag` | reads only |
| `3` | check | checks before the effect (`assert`) | none; failure changes nothing |
| `4` | plan | the effect stage computes its targets and the planned effect; `preview` ends here | reads only |
| `5` | apply | the effect stage changes the world through a journal transaction | change |
| `5a` | after | stages after the effect read the records of the effect | none |
| `6` | verify | the `verify` pipeline runs; failure rolls the effect back | rollback |
| `7` | report | the effect report is built | none |

## 2. Dispatch by phase

The binder assigns every bound stage a phase. The phase selects the interface
the executor calls:

| Phase | Step | Interface |
|---|---|---|
| `source`, `transform` | 2 | `ReadStage::execute` |
| `check` | 3 | `ReadStage::execute` |
| `mutate`, `run` | 4 | `EffectStage::plan` |
| `mutate`, `run` | 5 | `EffectStage::apply` |
| `after` | 5a | `ReadStage::execute` |
| `verify` | 6 | executor |

A command implementation (`StageImpl`) provides the read interface, the
effect interface or both. A command whose effect depends on an argument (one
action reads, another changes) provides both; the binder assigns the phase
from the arguments.

`StageImpl::check` runs in step 1, after binding, with access to the catalog
specification, the host facts and the configuration only. It may reject
arguments that the catalog types cannot express and reports static facts
(`StaticInfo`): whether the stage waits, network endpoints it will contact,
external programs it will start, paths it names, and command-specific
details. These facts are returned by the check of a program without executing
it, so that an embedding application can apply its own rules before
execution.

## 3. Registry

One command may have several implementations, for example `remove` for file
entries, for document items and for jobs, supplied by different crates. Each
implementation describes itself with a `StageDescriptor`: the command name,
whether it can start a pipeline, and the record kinds it accepts. The registry
selects the implementation by command name and by the record kind declared by
the catalog for the output of the previous stage. When no implementation
accepts that kind, binding fails with `E_TYPE` and the list of accepted kinds.
A stream whose records have kinds handled by different implementations fails
with `E_TYPE` when the first record of another kind reaches the stage; the
program is split by the caller.

## 4. Records and streams

Records flow between stages in a `RecordStream`, a lazy iterator of
`Result<Record>`:

* A stage pulls records from its input only as needed. A pipeline therefore
  holds the whole input in memory only when a stage must (for example `sort`,
  `last`, `group`); such a stage collects with a bound, and exceeding
  `limits.max_records` fails with `E_LIMIT`. Records are never dropped
  silently.
* An error item ends the program. A stream yields nothing after its first
  error.
* Items skipped without an error (an unreadable entry during a listing, an
  unavailable log channel) are recorded as notable entries of the report
  through the context; they do not end the program.
* The output of a stage is records, a single value (for example the result of
  `count`) or nothing. It may carry a header record describing the whole
  stream (for example `test_run` in front of `test_result` records), the order
  of the stream known to its producer (so that a following `sort` by the same
  keys does not collect the stream) and a presentation hint for the text
  renderer (`tree`, `sizes`). Pass-through stages keep the header, order and
  hint.

## 5. Arguments

A stage receives its bound arguments in signature order. Every parameter of
the signature is present; defaults inserted by the binder are marked.
Literal values, defaults and references to named results are evaluated before
the stage runs. Per-record expressions are evaluated by the stage for each
input record through the evaluator of the context. Pipeline arguments (the
check of `verify`, `write from:`) are run through the pipeline runner of the
context.

## 6. Effect stages

An effect stage (a change, an external action or a launched program) has two
steps.

### Plan (step 4)

The stage consumes its input, records the entity tag of
every target as read, and returns an effect plan: the planned changes with
differences, notable effects and irreversible effects known in advance,
records describing an effect without file targets (for example the command
line and directory of a program), whether the operation is bulk, and private
state of the implementation. The plan step may read the world, including
read-only network requests needed to compute the plan; it creates, changes,
sends and starts nothing. A preview reports the plan and stops. The same plan
is used by the apply step, so a preview shows exactly the targets that an
execution changes. The private state holds what is needed to produce new
content, not the content itself.

### Apply (step 5)

The executor admits the operation and opens a journal
transaction. The stage receives the plan and the transaction; every change of
user data goes through the transaction: all targets are declared and their
previous state is preserved before the first change, then the changes are
applied and the journal checks entity tags (`E_STALE` on mismatch). Effects
outside the file system are marked irreversible on the transaction. The stage
never commits; the executor commits on success and rolls back on failure or
cancellation. The stage returns the records of the effect (`effect`, `exec`,
`job`, …), the changes as applied and the notable and irreversible effects
observed. The returned records do not borrow the transaction.

When a launched program continues in the background after its `wait`, the
outcome is marked detached and holds a `job` record; the stages after the
effect are not run.

## 7. Stages after the effect

The stages allowed after the effect (`assert`, `filter`, `select`, `first`,
`last`, `skip`, `count`, `sort`, `group`) are read stages executed in step 5a
on the records of the effect. They never change the world. A failed `assert`
in step 5a reports `E_ASSERT` with step `5a` next to the full effect report;
the effect is not rolled back. Only `verify` (step 6) rolls back.

## 8. Execution context

A stage reaches the world only through its execution context:

| Facility | Purpose |
|---|---|
| file system | read-only access to files; writes go through the transaction only |
| journal store | the journal commands (`history`, `undo`, `redo`, `journal.*`) |
| clock | wall time, monotonic time, waiting |
| host | host facts and the environment of the engine process |
| configuration, request options | effective settings and options of the call |
| cancellation, deadline | cooperative cancellation and the time limit of the program |
| limits | records held in memory, size of text files, threads |
| state directory | spool, jobs and caches of the engine |
| evaluator, pipeline runner | per-record expressions and pipeline arguments |
| services | registry of the services of other command groups (documents, source code, programs, file listing, repository queries, text codecs, file holders, review rules); a service is absent when its group is not loaded |
| extensions | further shared objects registered by type |
| frame | index, command and step of the running stage, and the demand of the rest of the pipeline |
| events | progress and output of launched programs |
| notes | notable entries of the report |

### Demand

The context tells a stage what the rest of the pipeline needs:
the fields used later (expensive fields that are not used may be left out),
whether records of files must carry `etag` (an effect stage or an entity-tag
check follows), and how many records are used later (the stage may stop
early). The output must be correct for any demand.

### Services

When a service is absent, the stage degrades as its command
documentation describes (for example a plain view instead of an outline) and
records a notable entry; it does not fail.

### Environment

Stages read environment variables only through the host of
the context, never from the process directly, so that an embedding
application can give each execution its own environment and tests can
substitute it.

## 9. Cancellation and limits

Cancellation is cooperative. The context holds a cancellation token shared by
all stages of one execution; child tokens are cancelled with their parent and
can also be cancelled on their own (for example one background job). The first
reason wins:

| Reason | Error |
|---|---|
| requested by the caller | `E_CANCELLED` |
| time limit of the program | `E_TIMEOUT` |
| resource limit | `E_LIMIT` |
| engine shutdown | `E_CANCELLED` |

A stage calls the checkpoint of the context in long loops and before blocking
work; the checkpoint fails when the token is cancelled or the deadline has
passed (and then cancels the token with the time-limit reason). Wrapping a
stream with the checked adapter performs the checkpoint before every pull.
Waiting uses the clock of the context and never extends past the deadline. A
virtual clock completes waits immediately, which makes time limits testable
without waiting.

Cancellation during step 5 rolls the transaction back. Cancellation before
step 5 has no effect in the world.

## 10. Events

Events are delivered while a program executes. Every event has its type in
the member `t`:

| `t` | Content |
|---|---|
| `progress` | `command`, `phase`, `done`, `total`, `bytes`, `message` |
| `job.started` | `id`, `label`, `command`, `cwd`, `pid`, `started` |
| `job.output` | `id`, `stream` (`stdout`, `stderr`), `cursor`, `lines`, `bytes` |
| `job.progress` | `id`, `percent`, `line` |
| `job.finished` | `id`, `state` (`exited`, `failed`, `stopped`, `timed_out`), `exit_code`, `signal`, `elapsed`, `output_file`, `changes` |
| `log` | `level`, `message`, `source` |

Every launched program has a job identifier from its start, so the same
events describe a program that finishes in the foreground and one that
continues in the background. The engine adds a sequence number, the time and
the request identifier when it delivers an event to the embedding
application. Emitting an event never blocks the execution for long; event
sinks buffer and deliver events in order.

## 11. Clock and host

The clock provides wall time (nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, UTC), a
monotonic time that includes suspend and never decreases, the readings of all
clocks at one moment (wall time, boot identifier, monotonic time with and
without suspend, used by the journal to measure the age of entries) and
cancellable waiting.

The host provides stable facts (operating system, version, architecture, host
name, account, home and temporary directories, path notation, local time
rules, locale, number of processors) and the environment variables of the
engine process. Values that change while the program runs are read by the
commands that report them.

## 12. Concurrency

The interface is synchronous. Every interface is safe to share between
threads; record streams can be moved between threads. A stage may use up to
`limits.threads` threads for parallel work and must produce its records in a
deterministic order regardless of scheduling.

title: Job supervisor protocol
text:
# Job supervisor protocol

A run that continues in the background after the command line exits is
supervised by a process that outlives the command line. The command line and
the supervisor exchange files in the state directory; there is no socket and no
other channel. The Rust implementation is in `crates/nurt-proc/src/jobs`.
The protocol version is `1` (`PROTOCOL` in `jobs/table.rs`); every message file
carries it in the field `protocol`, and a file of another version is dropped.

## 1. Files of `<state>/jobs`

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `sequence`, `sequence.lock` | last job number; identifiers `j<number>` are never reused |
| `<id>.json` | job file: public record, request without environment, result |
| `<id>.input.json` | environment and standard input; readable by the account of the engine only |
| `<id>.lock` | locked by the process that supervises the job; a job recorded as running whose lock is free has lost its supervisor |
| `<id>.control/` | control requests to the supervising process and their replies |
| `host.lock` | locked by the detached supervisor |
| `inbox/` | start requests, their replies and cancel notices |

Files are replaced atomically by renaming a complete temporary file, so a
reader never sees a partial file and takes no lock.

## 2. Start of a run

1. The client writes `inbox/<name>.request.json`, where `<name>` is
   `<process id>-<counter>`; requests are served in the order of the counters.
   The file holds `protocol`, `command_name`, the bound `program`, the `request`
   (the run with its environment and standard input) and `wait`, the time the
   run may take before it moves to the background.
2. When `host.lock` is free the client starts the supervisor with the command
   registered by the host application, and starts it again when the lock is
   still free after 3 s. A supervisor that has been started tries the lock
   up to 10 times, 10 ms apart, so that the instant in which a client probes the
   lock does not make it give up.
3. The supervisor takes a request by removing its file. Whoever removes the file
   owns the request: a client that removes it first has withdrawn the request and
   the supervisor does not run it.
4. The supervisor runs the preparation of the run (journal transaction, change
   detection, spool), starts the program, records the process in the job file and
   writes `inbox/<name>.reply.json`: `started` with the job identifier, or
   `failed` with the error. The client waits up to 30 s for the reply, removes
   it and follows the job.

## 3. Cancellation

Cancellation is a state of the call, not an event that can be missed. It is
delivered in three ways, according to how far the run has advanced:

| Moment | How the cancellation reaches the run |
|---|---|
| The supervisor has not taken the request | the client removes the request file; the call ends with `E_CANCELLED` and nothing was started |
| The supervisor took the request and the program has not started | the client writes `inbox/<name>.cancel.json` (`{"protocol": 1}`); the supervisor gives each run a cancellation token of its own and cancels it when the file appears; the preparation ends at its next check, the supervisor checks the token again immediately before it starts the program, and the request is answered with `failed` (`E_CANCELLED`); the journal entry is rolled back with the reason `cancelled` and no job is recorded |
| The program has started | the client writes the control request `cancel` into `<id>.control/`; the supervisor checks the cancellation again right after it recorded the process and, when it is set, ends the whole process tree at once |

The process tree is ended as a group: `kill(-pgid)` on Unix systems, the job
object on Windows, the same calls as at a time limit. The result of a started
program that was cancelled has `killed_by: cancel`.

Cancelling a job that has ended, or cancelling a job twice, is not an error: the
answer is the record of the job in its current state. A client removes its cancel
notice after it has read the reply; a supervisor removes every cancel notice
found at its start.

## 4. Control requests

A requester writes `<id>.control/<name>.request.json` with the action `stop`
(with `signal` and `grace`), `suspend`, `resume` or `cancel`. The job thread of
the supervising process reads the directory at each poll (every 50 ms), removes
the request file, acts and writes `<name>.reply.json` with `done` (the job record)
or `failed` (the error). `cancel` needs no reply. A requester that can no longer
remove its request waits for the reply, which the supervising process writes
after the final state of a stopped job; the waiting time is the grace time plus
60 s for `stop` and 10 s for the other actions.

## 5. Compatibility

The cancel notice is an additional file; the protocol version stays `1`.

| Client | Supervisor | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| older | newer | the client never writes a cancel notice; a cancellation after the supervisor took the request reaches the program as before, by the control request once the program has started, and the supervisor ends the tree at once when it finds the request after it recorded the process |
| newer | older | the older supervisor ignores `*.cancel.json` files (it reads only `*.request.json`); the client removes the notice after the reply, and the cancellation reaches the program by the control request |

title: Syntax trees: `nurt-ast/1` and `nurt-bound/1
text:
# Syntax trees: `nurt-ast/1` and `nurt-bound/1`

Nurt executes and records a syntax tree, never program text. Program text in
any syntax variant is corrected and parsed into a **surface tree**
(`nurt-ast/1`). Binding the surface tree with the command catalog produces a
**bound tree** (`nurt-bound/1`). An instance on a remote device receives a
surface tree encoded as JSON or CBOR and binds it with its own catalog, so a
program never passes through another interpreter and no quoting layers are
involved. The journal and the effect report store the bound tree.

The normative definitions are the JSON Schemas
[`schemas/nurt-ast-1.schema.json`](schemas/nurt-ast-1.schema.json) and
[`schemas/nurt-bound-1.schema.json`](schemas/nurt-bound-1.schema.json). The
Rust types of the modules `nurt_contracts::ast` and `nurt_contracts::bound`
serialize to exactly these documents.

## 1. Identifiers and versions

| Item | Surface tree | Bound tree |
|---|---|---|
| Format name | `nurt-ast/1` | `nurt-bound/1` |
| Version member | `"nurt": "1.1"` | `"nurt": "1.1"` and `"bound": "1.1"` |
| Media type | `application/vnd.nurt.ast+json; v=1`, `application/vnd.nurt.ast+cbor; v=1` | `application/vnd.nurt.bound+json; v=1`, `application/vnd.nurt.bound+cbor; v=1` |
| File extension | `.nurt.json` (tree), `.nurt` (program text, UTF-8) | — |
| Schema | `nurt-ast-1.schema.json` | `nurt-bound-1.schema.json` |
| Canonical encoding | JSON according to RFC 8785 (JCS); deterministic CBOR (RFC 8949, section 4.2) | same |

Versions are written `MAJOR.MINOR`. Within one major version only optional
members and new node kinds are added; new commands and parameters are catalog
data and never change the schema. A reader accepts a document of its own major
version whose minor version is not greater than its own; a newer minor version
is rejected with `E_AST_VERSION` and the list of unknown node kinds. The node
kinds a reader knows are listed by `nurt_contracts::ast::SURFACE_KINDS` and
`nurt_contracts::bound::BOUND_KINDS`. After a change of the major version,
readers accept the previous major version for at least 24 months.

The two documents are distinct: the surface schema rejects the root members
`bound`, `catalog_rev` and `corr_rev`, the stage member `effect` and the
argument member `default`; the bound schema requires them.

## 2. Common conventions

* Every node object carries its kind in the member `"t"`. Argument objects and
  map entries are not nodes and have no `"t"`.
* Optional members are omitted when absent. An empty field path of a
  reference is omitted. Arrays that are part of a node (`args`, `stages`,
  `items`, `entries`) are always present, possibly empty.
* User data never appears as a member name: map entries are objects
  `{"k": key, "v": value}`.
* A reader rejects an unknown member of any object with `E_AST_SCHEMA`.
* Identifiers match `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*` and have at most 64 bytes; command names
  have at most 129 bytes. The reserved words `let`, `true`, `false`, `null`,
  `and`, `or`, `not` and `in` are not admissible as the name of a `let` result,
  as the name of a reference or as an `ident` node; they remain admissible as
  parameter names and map keys.
* `meta` is an object at the root with the optional members `source` (program
  text), `variant` (`a`, `b` or `c`) and `comments` (objects `{span, text}`,
  the text without the leading `#`); other members are preserved. Comments are
  not part of the program; a formatter restores them from `meta.comments`.
* A document is at most 128 levels deep: the nesting depth is the number of
  JSON values on the path from the root to the deepest value, the root being at
  depth 1. The parser measures the same depth on the tree it builds and rejects
  a deeper program with `E_SYNTAX` (`nesting_too_deep`), so a program the parser
  accepts always encodes to a surface document that the decoders accept.
* `span` is `[line, column, end_line, end_column]`. Lines and columns start at
  1, columns count Unicode scalar values and the end position is exclusive (the
  position directly after the last character). Positions do not exceed
  2^32 - 1. Spans are informative.

### Spans of the surface tree

| Node | Covers |
|---|---|
| `let` | from `let` to the end of the pipeline |
| `pipeline` | from the start of the head to the end of the last stage |
| `stage` | from the command name to its last token: the end of the last argument, or, when the arguments are written in parentheses (notation B), the closing parenthesis |
| argument | a named argument from its name to the end of its value; a positional argument equals its value |
| literal, identifier | the token, including quotes, the `r#` delimiters of raw text and the regular expression flags |
| `ref` | from `@` to the end of the last field |
| `list`, `map`, `call`, `sub` | from the opening bracket or name to the closing bracket |
| map entry | from the key to the end of the value |
| `bin` | from the start of the left operand to the end of the right operand |
| `un`, `spread` | from the operator to the end of the operand |
| `field` | from the start of the record expression to the end of the field name |
| `range` | from the first to the last bound written |
| parenthesized expression | the node of the inner expression; its span includes the parentheses |

## 3. Surface tree

Root members: `nurt` (required), `program` (required), `meta`.
`program.statements` holds at least one statement.

| `t` | Members | Text form (word notation) |
|---|---|---|
| `let` | `name`, `value: pipeline` | `let recent = find …` |
| `pipeline` | `head: stage \| ref`, `stages: [stage]` | `find … \|> filter … \|> first 20` |
| `stage` | `name`, `args: [argument]` | `filter size > 1mb` |
| argument | `name?`, `value` | `glob: "**/*.go"`, `20` |
| `text` | `v` | `"abc"`, `r"abc"`, `r#"…"#` |
| `ident` | `v` | `desc`, `size` |
| `regex` | `v`, `flags` (`imsx`, in this order) | `/oldName\(/i` |
| `int`, `num` | `v` (non-negative) | `40`, `3.5` |
| `size` | `v` (bytes) | `10mb` = 10 000 000, `1kib` = 1 024 |
| `dur` | `v` (milliseconds) | `30s`, `1h30m` |
| `bool`, `null` | `v` / — | `true`, `null` |
| `list` | `items` | `["a", "b"]` |
| `map` | `entries: [{k, v, span?}]` | `{replace: "a", with: "b"}` |
| `ref` | `name`, `fields?` | `@recent`, `@recent.path` |
| `spread` | `x` | `...@recent.path` (list elements only) |
| `field` | `name`, `of?` | `file.size` |
| `call` | `fn`, `args` | `ago(1h)` |
| `un` | `op` (`not`, `neg`), `x` | `not hidden`, `-1` |
| `bin` | `op`, `l`, `r` | `size > 1mb` |
| `range` | `lo?`, `hi?` | `10..12`, `40..`, `..9` |
| `sub` | `p: pipeline` | `(run […] \|> assert exit_code: 0)` |
| `key` | `segs` | structured key: names, indexes, `{"wild": "*" \| "**" \| "+"}`, `{"filter": expr}` |

### Control constructs (version 1.1)

Version 1.1 adds the statements below. A block is an array of at least one
statement; a reader of version 1.0 rejects a document that holds one with
`E_AST_VERSION`, naming the node kinds it does not know. A document of version
1.0 is read unchanged. The words that start a construct are reserved only at
the start of a statement, so `steps`, `params` and the other words stay
admissible as parameter names and map keys.

| `t` | Members | Text form |
|---|---|---|
| `when` | `branches: [{cond, body, span?}]`, `otherwise?: block` | `when COND { … } otherwise when COND { … } otherwise { … }` |
| `each` | `source`, `name`, `options?: [{name, value}]`, `body` | `each (find "/d") as f parallel: 4 { … }` |
| `repeat` | `options: [{name, value}]` (`until` required), `body` | `repeat until: COND every: 5s limit: 2m { … }` |
| `while` | `cond`, `options?`, `body` | `while COND limit: 20 { … }` |
| `break`, `continue` | — | `break` |
| `steps` | `body` | `steps { … }` |
| `define` | `name`, `params?: [{name, type, default?}]`, `body` | `define rotate(dir: path, keep: int = 7) { … }` |
| `params` | `params: [{name, type, default?}]` | `params { dir: path  days: int = 30 }` |

Rules of the constructs:

1. A call of a function is a `stage` whose name is the function; the parser
   reads `name(…)` as the notation of a call for every name defined earlier in
   the program, in all three variants.
2. `type` is written as in the catalog: `path`, `int`, `list<text>`,
   `enum(a, b)`. A parameter name is declared once.
3. Options are named; a bare option name is `true` (`atomic`). The options of
   `each` are `parallel` and `atomic`, of `repeat` `until`, `every`, `limit`
   and `atomic`, of `while` `limit` and `atomic`.
4. In a condition `exists <operand>` is a `call` of `exists`.
5. The spans of a construct cover it from its first word to the closing brace.
   The formatter keeps the comments of a construct before it.

Rules of the surface tree:

1. The tree does not depend on the catalog. Positional arguments keep their
   order and have no name; no default is added.
2. The parser produces `text` for every quoted string and `ident` for every
   bare identifier. Paths, globs, instants and keys are `text` nodes; the
   binder types them by their place in the signature. The structured `key`
   node is an alternative to a key written as text for producers that build
   trees directly. A printer writes a `key` node as a text literal in
   canonical key notation, so parsing the printed program yields a `text`
   node; both bind to the same `key` value of the bound tree.
3. Text values are stored after escape processing. In a regular expression
   `\/` is stored as `/`; every other escape is stored unchanged. The pattern
   is not empty. Flags are drawn from `imsx` and written in this order.
4. Numeric literals are non-negative: `-1` is `un` with `op: "neg"` applied to
   `int` 1. Every integer of a tree lies within ±(2^53 - 1), the range that
   canonical JSON represents exactly; a larger literal is a lexical error.
5. `spread` appears only as an element of a list.
6. An identifier directly followed by `:` always starts a named argument, even
   when it is an operator word (`replace "a" "b" in: ["/srv/a.txt"]`).
7. The binary operators, in increasing binding strength: `or`; `and`; `not`
   (unary); `== != < <= > >= ~ !~ in` (non-associative); `+ -`; `* /`;
   unary `-`; field access `.` and calls.
8. Syntax variant B produces the same surface tree as variant A. Variant C
   writes every argument by name, and the parser keeps the names because it
   does not read the catalog; the surface tree of a variant C program
   therefore differs from variant A, and the bound trees of all three variants
   are equal.

Example: `ports state: listen |> filter port == 8080`

```json
{"nurt": "1.1", "program": {"statements": [{"t": "pipeline",
  "head": {"t": "stage", "name": "ports", "args": [
    {"name": "state", "value": {"t": "ident", "v": "listen", "span": [1, 14, 1, 20]}, "span": [1, 7, 1, 20]}],
    "span": [1, 1, 1, 20]},
  "stages": [{"t": "stage", "name": "filter", "args": [
    {"value": {"t": "bin", "op": "==",
      "l": {"t": "ident", "v": "port", "span": [1, 31, 1, 35]},
      "r": {"t": "int", "v": 8080, "span": [1, 39, 1, 43]}, "span": [1, 31, 1, 43]},
     "span": [1, 31, 1, 43]}], "span": [1, 24, 1, 43]}],
  "span": [1, 1, 1, 43]}]}}
```

## 4. Bound tree

Root members: `nurt`, `bound`, `catalog_rev`, `corr_rev`, `program` (all
required) and `meta`. `catalog_rev` identifies the command catalog and
`corr_rev` the correction tables used to produce the tree. Both are revision
strings matching `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9:._-]*`, at most 128 bytes long. A
binder writes `catalog_rev` as the catalog revision defined in
[`catalog.md`](catalog.md) (`sha256:` followed by a lowercase hex digest) and
`corr_rev` in the same form, computed over the correction tables.

Statements, `let` and `pipeline` have the same shape as in the surface tree.
A stage has the members:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | canonical command name from the catalog: one identifier or a group and an identifier joined by `.` |
| `effect` | effect kind from the catalog: `read`, `local`, `external`, `process` |
| `phase` | execution phase (section 5); required |
| `waits` | `true` when the stage blocks the call by waiting; omitted when `false`. The catalog marks the command `waits`, or a parameter marked `waits` has a value greater than its default or the value `forever` |
| `args` | every parameter of the signature, in signature order, followed by the call parameters `privilege` and `as_user` when they were written on the stage (`catalog.md`, section 2) |
| `span` | source range of the surface stage |

An argument has `name`, `value`, `default` (`true` when the value comes from
the catalog default; omitted when `false`) and `span` (absent for defaults).

Value nodes carry no span. Kinds: `null`; `bool`, `int`, `num`; `text`,
`path`, `glob`, `key`, `enum`, `instant` with a text `v`; `size` and `dur`
with a non-negative integer `v`; `regex` with `v` and `flags` from `imsx`;
`list`; `map`; `range`; `ref`; `sub`; and the expression kinds `field`,
`call`, `un`, `bin`, `spread`. Integers lie within ±(2^53 - 1); constant
negation is folded, so `-1` binds to `int` -1.

| Kind | Form of `v` |
|---|---|
| `path` | canonical absolute path: `/a/b`, `C:/a/b`, `//server/share/a` or `provider:/a/b`; forward slashes, no empty, `.` or `..` segment, no trailing `/` except at the root |
| `instant` | RFC 3339 in UTC with the suffix `Z`; fractional seconds without trailing zeros (`2026-03-01T12:00:00Z`) |
| `glob`, `key` | non-empty text |
| `enum` | identifier |
| `regex` | non-empty pattern |

Binding rules:

1. Every parameter of the signature appears once, in signature order,
   whether it was written positionally, by name or not at all.
2. A parameter that was not written receives its catalog default with
   `default: true`. A parameter without a default, a parameter whose default
   is unbounded, a parameter of an exclusive group that was not written (as
   in `assert`) and a parameter of the source form when the command is bound
   as a stage receive `null` with `default: true`.
3. Literals are cast to the type of their place: text to `path`, `glob`,
   `instant`, `key`; identifiers to `enum`; a single path to a one-element list
   where the place is a list of paths; an integer `n` to the range `n..n` where
   the place is a range.
4. In expressions evaluated on records (`filter`, `select`, `sort`,
   per-record parameters), a bare identifier is the field of the current record
   and binds to `field`.
5. Values derived from other parameters are written explicitly: the `mode` of
   a pattern resolves to `literal` or `regex`, and a parameter with
   `default_from` in the catalog receives the value of its source converted to
   its type (`run cwd` defaults to the call parameter `base`, and the default
   `watch` list of `run` is the list holding `cwd`).
6. Short source forms of change commands are expanded to their single
   pipeline. The source form names in `expand` the parameter that holds the
   entries; its value becomes the `path` of an `info` head, followed by the
   command bound in its form for `entry` input. `remove "/a"` binds to
   `info ["/a"] |> remove`, so both programs have the same bound tree. `info`
   accepts a list of paths, does not descend into directories and reports a
   missing path as an entry with `exists: false`, which the command handles
   according to its `on_missing` parameter.
7. The pipeline checked by `verify` is the `sub` value of its parameter
   `check`.
8. `effect` always comes from the catalog, never from the program. Stages of
   the phases `source`, `transform`, `check`, `after` and `verify` have the
   effect `read`.

### Control constructs of the bound tree (version 1.1)

The statements `when`, `each`, `repeat`, `while`, `break`, `continue`,
`steps`, `define` and `params` have the same names and blocks as in the
surface tree, with these differences: a condition and a source are bound
expressions of type `bool` and of a list; the options of a loop are members
(`parallel`, `atomic` (omitted when `true`), `every_ms`, `limit`); a limit is
`{"kind": "iterations", "n": N}` or `{"kind": "time", "ms": N}`; a parameter
has a canonical `type` and a bound `default`. A function call is a pipeline
head `{"t": "call", "name", "args"}` whose `args` list every parameter by name,
with `default: true` on the values that come from the declaration. A reading
pipeline inside an expression is a `sub` value and `exists` is a `call`.
Binding checks, before any effect: conditions are not statically another type
than `bool`; options have their names and types; `break` and `continue` stand
inside a loop; `params` is the first statement; functions are defined before
their first call, the body of a function sees only its parameters, and a call
names every required parameter with a value of its type.

## 5. Phases

| `phase` | Stage | Effect in the world |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | the head stage that produces records | read only |
| `transform` | record transformations before the effect | none |
| `check` | `assert` before the effect; failure changes nothing | none |
| `mutate` | the single change stage | change, journaled |
| `run` | the single program-running stage | program effects, tracked |
| `after` | `assert`, `filter`, `select`, `first`, `last`, `skip`, `count`, `sort`, `group` on the records produced by the effect | none; a failed `assert` reports `E_ASSERT` without rolling the effect back |
| `verify` | `verify (…)`; failure rolls the effect back | rollback |

A pipeline has at most one stage of phase `mutate` or `run`. Stages of phase
`after` stand only after it, and `verify`, when present, is the last stage.
Any other stage after the effect is rejected with `E_ONE_EFFECT`. The pipeline
of a `let` has no stage of phase `mutate` or `run`. A decoded bound tree that
breaks these rules is rejected with `E_AST_SCHEMA`.

## 6. `ast_hash`

```
ast_hash = "sha256:" + lowercase_hex(SHA-256(UTF-8(JCS(hash_form(document)))))
```

The hash form of a document is the document without the member `meta` of the
root object and without the member `span` of every object
(`nurt_contracts::ast::strip_for_hash`). It is taken from the JSON produced by
serializing the decoded, typed tree, so omitted optional members and members
written with their default value (`"waits": false`, `"default": false`) never
change the hash. Programs that differ only in layout or comments, or are
written in syntax variants A and B, have the same surface `ast_hash`; programs
in every syntax variant have the same bound tree. The report and the journal
use `ast_hash` of the bound tree, which includes every default; a later change
of a default value never changes the hash or the meaning of a recorded
program. The member `ast_hash` of the result of `check` is the hash of the
bound tree; it may be absent only when the tree is not known, never for a
program given as text (`docs/reference/serve-protocol.md`).

## 7. Conformance files

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `golden/ast/<name>.nurt` | program text, word notation |
| `golden/ast/<name>.json` | surface tree of the program, with spans; trees without program text use structured nodes and metadata |
| `golden/ast/<name>.hash` | `ast_hash` of the surface tree |
| `golden/ast/<name>.b.nurt` | the same program in variant B; its surface tree is `<name>.json` |
| `golden/ast/<name>.c.nurt`, `<name>.c.json`, `<name>.c.hash` | the same program in variant C, its surface tree and its `ast_hash` |
| `golden/bound/<name>.json` | bound tree of the same program against the reference catalog |
| `golden/bound/<name>.hash` | `ast_hash` of the bound tree |
| `golden/<format>/invalid/<case>.json` | document that a reader rejects |
| `golden/<format>/invalid/expected.tsv` | error code and layer of every rejected document: `schema` (the published schema rejects it), `types` (the schema and the Rust types reject it) or `rules` (the phase rules of section 5 reject it) |
| `golden/<format>/schema.generated.json` | schema generated from the Rust types |

Golden bound trees use the fixed revisions `cat-1` and `corr-1`.

A golden program has a bound tree only when the reference catalog `cat-1` binds it on every
system. `example-41-windows-registry` does not: its paths belong to the Windows registry
(`registry:/HKCU/...`), so binding fails with `E_PATH_FOREIGN` on other systems, and a golden tree
does not depend on the system that produced it. Its surface tree is checked and no bound tree is
recorded. The same holds for `example-48-preview-and-program-search` and for `structured-key`,
whose key syntax is exercised as a surface tree only.
Conformance tests check that every tree is valid under the published schema
and under the generated schema, deserializes into the Rust types and
serializes back to the same JSON value, survives a CBOR round trip unchanged
and has the recorded `ast_hash`, and that every invalid document is rejected
at its layer. Setting `NURT_BLESS=1` regenerates the generated schemas and the
recorded hashes after a reviewed change.
